## BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-MODELO-1 -- the whole-day verdict for a `ventana.tipo == "dia"` experiment

`BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-1-INV` slice 4, on the tables `BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-ESQUEMA-1-M` merged
(`d54a4da`). The first real use is Carlos's cold-shower week (2026-11-09..13, afternoon-shift days
not after a night; verdict due 2026-11-14). An intraday window is a later slice
(`BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-INTRADIA-MODELO-1`) -- `veredicto` answers it honestly with `'aun_no'` on every
metric, never an error.

**`body/experimentos.py`** (new), pure reads over a connection and a person id, the style of
`body/turnos_costo.py` and `body/baselines.py`:

- `dias_que_cuentan(conn, person_id, filtro_dias, desde, hasta)`: a day matches when its shift kind
  is in `turno_en` (if set) and not in `turno_fuera` (if set), and, with `excluir_tras_noche`, is
  not in the post-night recovery window. A day with no shift row has no kind: it never matches
  `turno_en` (which requires a kind), and it never matches `turno_fuera` either (it is not any of
  the listed kinds) -- the same thing `turnos_costo.bloques_noche` does, since it only ever looks
  at rows with kind='night'.
- **The post-night window is reused, not redefined**: `body/turnos_costo.py` gains a public
  `dias_post_noche(conn, person_id, desde, hasta)`, pulled out of the private `_dias_excluidos`
  (now `_post_noche_de_bloques` + `dias_post_noche`, called from both) -- same days, same order of
  computation; `tests/test_turnos_costo.py` passes unchanged. `dias_que_cuentan` buffers its own
  `desde` backward by `ventana_post` before calling it, the same reason `_dias_excluidos` already
  buffers its own window: a block whose last night falls just before `desde` can still have its
  recovery tail bleed into it.
- **Occurrence**: with `habito_id`, a test day is one with `habit_check.done = 1`; without, one
  with `experimento_registro.ocurrio = 1`. A matching day in the test period that did not happen is
  excluded from both sides (`dias_excluidos_no_ocurrio`).
- **Day offset per metric** (`OFFSET_DIA`, ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1 decision (b)):
  `body/garmin_adapter.py`'s `parse_day(day, raw)` reads a calendar day's sleep/hrv/wake fields from
  Garmin's own sleep/hrv endpoints for that day, and Garmin keys those endpoints by the morning the
  sleep session ENDED -- so `day`'s sleep/hrv/wake value is really about the night from day-1 into
  day. A practice meant to affect that night's sleep therefore shows up at day+1:

  | offset +1 (the following night) | offset 0 (default, the practice day's own daytime, or a multi-day figure) |
  |---|---|
  | sleep_minutes, sleep_score, sleep_deep_min, sleep_light_min, sleep_rem_min, sleep_awake_min, sleep_need_min, body_battery_sleep_charge, sleep_spo2_avg, sleep_respiration_avg/low/high, hrv_last_night, body_battery_wake, resting_hr (same per-day user_summary call, lowest reading set in that night's small hours), snoring_min (self-measured, same nighttime convention) | readiness, hrv_weekly_avg (7-day rolling, not one night), stress_avg, steps, active_kcal, body_battery_high/low, intensity_minutes, respiration_awake, high_stress_min, vo2max(_cycling), fitness_age, flex_alcance_cm, and any metric_def key not listed here |

- **Baseline**: matched days (same filter) in `BASE_DIAS = 120` days before `fecha_inicio`,
  excluding days inside any OTHER of the person's experiments' own `[fecha_inicio, fecha_fin or
  hoy]` span (`_dias_de_otros_experimentos`); one value per day, same offset applied.
- **Verdict per metric** (`_veredicto_metrica`): `n_prueba >= MIN_PRUEBA = 3` and
  `n_base >= MIN_BASE = baselines.MIN_DAYS` (imported, not copied) or else `'pocos_dias'`; sd of the
  baseline 0 (or the n floors unmet) -> `'pocos_dias'`, never a division. Otherwise
  `diferencia = media_prueba - media_base`, `ee = sd_base * sqrt(1/n_prueba + 1/n_base)`, and
  `resultado` is `'mas_bajo'` (`diferencia <= -UMBRAL * ee`), `'mas_alto'` (`>= UMBRAL * ee`) or
  `'sin_cambio'`, with `UMBRAL = 2.0` -- ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1 decision (a): the noise test
  is on the standard error of the DIFFERENCE of two means, not a single day's z, because a multi-day
  test mean is far less noisy than one day. Direction only -- whether lower is better is not this
  module's call.
- **`veredicto(conn, person_id, experimento_id, hoy=None)`**: raises `ValueError` for an
  `experimento_id` that is not this person's own (same style as `db.registrar_dia_experimento`).

**Tests** (`tests/test_experimentos_modelo.py`, 16 new, invented demo data only): the cold-shower
shape (`'mas_bajo'`) and a change inside the noise (`'sin_cambio'`), both against a 120-day noisy
baseline with an exact known mean and pstdev; a skipped day excluded from both sides with an
outlier value that never entered the mean; a night metric (`hrv_last_night`) read from the day
after, never from the practice day itself; `turno_en`/`turno_fuera`/`excluir_tras_noche` each
respected, including a day with no shift row; another experiment's test days kept out of the
baseline (an outlier value on those days that never entered this experiment's mean); habit-linked
vs. registro-based occurrence; too few test days and too short a baseline both reading
`'pocos_dias'`; a zero-variance baseline reading `'pocos_dias'` rather than dividing; an intradia
window reading `'aun_no'` on every metric; person isolation.

## BODY-VIVO-TAREA-NUEVA-1 -- refresh before refusing an unknown task

**Defect, as measured by the orchestrator on Carlos's PC, 2026-11-09**: `main()` in
`body/vivo.py` checked `argv[0] not in TAREAS` against the RUNNING process's own `TAREAS` and
returned usage + exit 2 BEFORE `refrescar()` ran, so a task name added on `main` could never
start through the live-tree launcher until some OTHER task happened to refresh the tree first.
After `BODY-MOMENTOS-PULL-1` merged (adding task `intradia`), `python -m body.vivo intradia
--dias 130` in the live tree answered `uso: ... tareas: manana, pull, ...` and exit 2 because the
live tree was still at an older commit; running `vida_dia` first refreshed it, and `intradia` then
started. The same happened again with `vida_dia` itself, worked around with `vida_export
--current`. A scheduled task registered for a brand-new name would fail every run this way,
silently, since a scheduled task's stderr goes nowhere.

**Fix**: an unknown task name now runs the exact same refresh path a known task runs -- the same
`_modulos_body_inesperados` guard, the same `refrescar(vivo)`, the same status file written with
the task name as given. What happens next depends on the outcome:
- if the refresh moved the tree (`"actualizado"`) AND the refreshed tree's own `body.vivo` turns
  out to know the name, the launcher relaunches itself as ONE child process --
  `_relanzar_en_arbol_nuevo`, running `sys.executable -m body.vivo <the same argv>` with `cwd` set
  to the live tree -- and returns that child's exit code. The child refreshes again, finds the
  tree already current, and runs the task in-process itself.
- otherwise (not moved, refresh refused, or the refreshed tree doesn't know the name either):
  usage + exit 2, same as before, with the status file already recording the attempt.

**Why a child only here, and never for a known task**: the PID rule in the module's own
docstring is about a task Task Scheduler launches under a name the running code ALREADY knows --
staying in-process keeps the same PID the scheduler is watching for `web`'s restart policy. A
name the running code does not know cannot have that problem solved by staying in-process: the
running code literally cannot execute code it never imported, no matter how it is called. The
child is the only way to run code newer than what this process holds.

**Telling "the new tree knows the task" without importing it here**: `_tareas_conocidas_por_el_arbol`
spawns `python -m body.vivo --tareas` (a new flag, handled first in `main()`, that just prints
`",".join(sorted(TAREAS))` and returns 0) in the refreshed tree and parses its stdout. Importing
the new `body.vivo` into THIS process instead was rejected on purpose: `_modulos_body_inesperados`
exists precisely because a previous task's stale import surviving in this same process is a
correctness hazard, and reading the new module's `TAREAS` here would be exactly that hazard,
deliberately invited.

**Tests** (`tests/test_vivo.py`, all against the existing throwaway-repo/worktree fixtures, no
real git state touched): `--tareas` prints exactly `TAREAS`'s names; an unknown task on a stale
tree whose refreshed `main` knows it -> refreshed, child launched with the same argv and the live
tree as `cwd` (asserted), its exit code returned; an unknown task the refreshed tree does not know
either -> exit 2 after one refresh, no child; an unknown task when the refresh itself is refused
(dirty tree) -> exit 2, no child, and `_tareas_conocidas_por_el_arbol` never even called
(short-circuited); a known task -> unchanged, in-process, no child (asserted); empty argv -> exit
2 with no refresh. Existing tests stay green unchanged, including the one unknown-task test that
calls `main()` against the real repository with no mocking -- `refrescar` there still answers
`"sin_cambio:no_es_arbol_vivo"` (the main working tree is not a linked worktree), so no git
mutation happens and the path falls through to the same exit 2 it always returned.

**Gate**, once, foreground, on the branch tip: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover
tests -t .` -> `Ran 1732 tests in 372.350s ... OK (skipped=1)`. 6 more than the prior recorded
floor (1726, `BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-MODELO-1`): exactly the 6 new tests above (`--tareas`, the three
unknown-task cases, the known-task no-child assertion, empty-argv); `skipped=1` carries over
unchanged.

**Merge** (no schema change, no customer-facing bytes -- a scheduled-task launcher with no screen
and no string a person reads -- no cross-repo/DTO change -- Merge Policy A applies, and the
spec's own approval-reason authorizes the merge in words): `git checkout main` (tip `d6e45a2`),
`git merge --no-ff feat/body-vivo-tarea-nueva-1` (branch tip
`1fd6dadcabf16b3712cbd16870ac7bd60995fb17`) -> `94bb2891d7c074a2f72ab4df9ff1e501c3ba58db`. The
merge commit's tree (`09f04ce7e3328ed468136d54309032cfb62b872c`) is identical to the branch tip's
own tree -- `main` had not moved since the branch was cut, so the merge introduced nothing beyond
the branch's own content and the gate above was not re-run.

## BODY-MOMENTOS-DIA-COMPLETO-1 -- a day's intraday pull is "stored" only once it is complete

**Defect, as measured** (BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-1-INV, continued): BODY-MOMENTOS-PULL-1 (merged
`562f806`) treated a day as stored once ANY intraday row existed (`db.intradia_almacenado`), and
`pull.traer_intradia` then skipped it for good unless `forzar=True`. The orchestrator measured this
on Carlos's PC, 2026-11-09: the first backfill (`body.vivo intradia --dias 130`, counts only -- 130
fetched, 0 already stored, 0 empty, 2026-07-03..2026-11-09) ran in the evening, so 2026-11-09 was
stored with only the hours fetched up to that run, and every later run would have skipped it for
good. The same gap hits a day fetched in the early morning before the watch had synced the night
to Garmin -- the watch syncs to the phone in batches, so a day's last hours can reach Garmin's
servers hours after that day's local midnight.

**The rule**: `db.intradia_almacenado` now compares the stored `fetched_at` (UTC, written by
`guardar_intradia`) against a threshold computed from `day` and the person's own zone -- the next
local midnight, converted to UTC, plus a new named constant `db.INTRADIA_MARGEN_CIERRE_H = 6`
(hours). A day fetched before that threshold reads as NOT stored, the same as a day never fetched
at all, including the out-of-retention empty marker (`payload=None`) fetched too early. The zone
comes from `db.person(conn, person_id)["timezone"]`, read inside `intradia_almacenado` itself --
the adapter (`garmin_adapter`) still never reads the DB; this is `db.py` reading its own table.

**Pull side**: `pull.traer_intradia` needed no logic change -- `db.guardar_intradia`'s `INSERT OR
REPLACE` already overwrites a day's earlier, partial row when `intradia_almacenado` now says no,
and the function already returns `"fetched"`/`"empty"` (never `"already_stored"`) whenever a
Garmin call was actually made, so `traer_intradia_rango`'s counts already count a re-fetched
partial day as fetched. Only the docstrings were corrected to say so. No scheduled path calls
either function (`pull_all`/`pull_hosted`/`pull_backfill_hosted` are unchanged, and
`IntradiaNotCalledByAnyJobTest` still asserts it).

**Tests added** (`tests/test_momentos_pull.py`, invented payloads, `fetched_at` set directly by SQL
instead of patching the wall clock -- the margin rule compares two fixed instants, so the real
clock at test-run time is irrelevant): `AlmacenadoCierreTest` -- fetched before the day ends, within
the margin after midnight, and after the margin, for both a real payload and the empty marker (6
cases), plus a same-UTC-instant case where America/Bogota (UTC-5) reads as not yet complete while
Europe/Madrid (UTC+1 in November) reads as complete. `TraerIntradiaRefetchTest` -- a day stored
before its close is re-fetched and returns `"fetched"`; within the margin is re-fetched; after the
margin is skipped and returns `"already_stored"`; a re-fetched partial day is counted as fetched by
`traer_intradia_rango`. Existing tests (`forzar=True`, person isolation, the no-scheduled-caller
guard) were left unchanged and still pass, since every day they exercise is fetched at the real
`datetime.now()`, always well past its own closing margin.

**Gate**, once, foreground, on the branch tip: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover
tests -t .` -> `Ran 1743 tests in 458.400s ... OK (skipped=1)`.

**Merge** (no schema change -- `raw_payload`'s columns and the rule for `fetched_at` already there
are unchanged, only how one value already written is read; no customer-facing bytes -- this is
`pull.traer_intradia`/`db.intradia_almacenado`, not called from any route or scheduled job yet; no
cross-repo/DTO change -- Merge Policy A applies, and the spec's own approval-reason authorizes the

## BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-PANTALLA-1-M2 -- four corrections from the 375 px re-measure

Continues BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-PANTALLA-1 (+ -M, commit `d218828`, on
`feat/body-experimentos-pantalla-1`). Four things the orchestrator's own 375 px measurement found
wrong, approved by ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1; the verdict model (`body/experimentos.py`) is
untouched, as that approval says -- every count below is read from `experimento_registro` /
`habit_check`, the verdict itself still from `experimentos.veredicto`.

1. **The progress line now counts what the person marked, not what they didn't.** It used to read
   `len(dias_excluidos_no_ocurrio)` as "sin hacer" -- a day with no mark at all read exactly like
   one explicitly marked false, so a just-started experiment showed "0 días hechos, 1 sin hacer" on
   its first morning. `_progreso_txt` (`body/rutas/experimentos.py`) now takes `hechos` from
   `ver["dias_prueba"]` (reused from the verdict, not re-derived) and splits
   `ver["dias_excluidos_no_ocurrio"]` by whether `_dias_marcados` (the same
   `experimento_registro`/`habit_check` source `veredicto`'s own `_ocurrio_por_dia` reads) carries a
   mark for that day: marked false -> `no_hechos`, no mark at all -> `sin_marcar`. TODAY, unmarked,
   counts for neither (the day is not over). Es "{hechos} hechos · {no_hechos} no · {sin_marcar} sin
   marcar", en "{hechos} done · {no_hechos} not done · {sin_marcar} not marked" -- a zero part is
   left out, and nothing marked reads es "todavía ningún día marcado" / en "no days marked yet". New
   keys: `experimentos.progreso_hechos`, `experimentos.progreso_no_hechos`,
   `experimentos.progreso_sin_marcar`, `experimentos.progreso_vacio`, replacing the old
   `experimentos.progreso`. Same line on the card and the detail page (`_tarjeta_desde_veredicto` now
   threads `conn`, `person_id` and `today` through to build it).
2. **Hoy's two buttons sit side by side on the left.** `body/templates/today.html`'s button row
   gains the existing `justify-start` utility class alongside `.row gap-8` (`.row` itself untouched,
   per the approval's own instruction) so the floating assistant button never covers "Hoy no" / "Not
   today" while scrolling. Once today is marked, the chosen button carries `aria-pressed="true"`
   plus the `.btn.on` selected style already used elsewhere for a primary/active action (an existing
   accent token, not a new colour, not a grading one); the other stays `aria-pressed="false"`, and
   posting it still changes the mark. `hoy_contexto` now returns a `marcado` field ("1" / "0" /
   `None`) instead of baking the mark into the line text; the "· hecho" suffix is gone -- one signal,
   not two -- and `aria-pressed` is the screen-reader cue. Removed keys:
   `today.experimento_linea_marcado`, `experimentos.marca.hecho`, `experimentos.marca.no_hecho`
   (their only caller was this line).
3. **A closed card on Metas now shows its date range and day-filter line**, like an active card:
   `body/templates/goals.html`'s closed-card loop gains the `{{ e.dias_txt }} · {{ e.fecha_txt }}`
   line the active loop already had -- both fields were already on the card dict, just never
   rendered for a closed one.
4. **The detail page's two means say what they count.** `experimentos.media_linea` was "{etiqueta}
   ({n} días): {valor}" with `n` = days WITH A FIGURE (a night without a reading drops out), which
   read as test days. Now es "{etiqueta} ({n} con dato): {valor}", en "{etiqueta} ({n} with a
   reading): {valor}" -- one key, so both the test-days and the baseline lines pick it up.

`tests/test_i18n_paridad.py` and `tests/test_registro_tu.py` needed no table edits: both scan
generically (literal `t()` keys, `su/sus/tiene/puede`) and passed unchanged against the new/removed
keys above. `tests/test_accesibilidad.py` and `tests/test_rendimiento.py` likewise passed unchanged.
`tests/test_experimentos_pantalla.py` gains: a fresh experiment's empty sentence (es, en); hecho/no/
sin-marcar each counted separately, including a habit-linked experiment reading `habit_check`; zero
parts left out; `aria-pressed` before and after marking on Hoy, and that posting the other button
still flips the mark; the closed card's date range and day-filter line; the "con dato" / "with a
reading" wording (es, en).

## BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-INTRADIA-MODELO-1 -- intraday verdict, same whole-day rule on a per-day window

`experimentos.veredicto` for `ventana.tipo == 'intradia'` no longer returns `'aun_no'` for every
metric (BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-MODELO-1's own stub). It now feeds `_veredicto_metrica`'s same whole-day
rule (MIN_PRUEBA, MIN_BASE, UMBRAL) a per-day WINDOW mean instead of a whole day's own figure --
ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1, carrying out BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-1-INV slice 8 (Carlos's morning-
grounding experiment, his Personal desk's own `vida/experimento-manana.md`, aimed at Sat
2026-11-14).

**The window.** Each counting day's window is `[anchor - antes_min, anchor + despues_min]`.
`ancla: 'despertar'` anchors at that day's own `sleep_session.end_local` -- measured: body/db.py's
`save_day` files a sleep row under the morning the session ENDED (the schema's own comment: "the
day Garmin files the sleep under (wake day)"), so a day's own row IS that day's own wake time, no
`OFFSET_DIA` shift needed (unlike a whole-day metric's own night-after reading). `ancla: 'momento'`
anchors at `experimento_registro.momento_id` -> `moment.ts_local`. A day with no sleep row, or
whose registro has no momento_id, has no anchor at all for that day.

**The baseline's own moment, a judgement call.** A baseline day never has a moment of its own --
nothing was logged on an ordinary day -- so a `'momento'` baseline is anchored at the MEDIAN local
clock time of the test days' own moments, applied to each baseline day's own date
(`_anclas_base_momento`). This is the closest honest stand-in for "when this would have happened on
an ordinary day"; {} (no baseline anchor at all) when no test day has a moment yet to take the
median from.

**The coverage floor.** A day's value per metric is the mean of `db.intradia`'s samples inside its
window, using only valid samples (the parser already drops a "no reading" code). A window holding
fewer than `COBERTURA_MIN` (0.5, named in `body/experimentos.py`) of the samples its OWN observed
spacing implies -- the median gap between that window's merged samples' own consecutive
timestamps, never a fixed Garmin constant, since a watch not worn drops samples without changing
the device's nominal interval -- is a day WITHOUT DATA, same as a day `db.intradia` returns `[]`
for (never fetched). A window spanning midnight pulls samples from BOTH calendar days `db.intradia`
stores under their own `day` key, filtered by each sample's own parsed local timestamp, never by
which day it was filed under.

**The result's shape.** Unchanged (`metricas` -> `resultado`/`n_prueba`/`n_base`/`media_prueba`/
`media_base`/`diferencia`; `dias_prueba`; `dias_excluidos_no_ocurrio`; `estado`), plus
`dias_sin_dato` (`{"prueba": [...], "base": [...]}`, test/base days dropped for a missing anchor or
thin coverage) -- for a later job to find what intraday days an active experiment is still missing.
The whole-day (`ventana.tipo == 'dia'`) path is untouched and keeps its own shape, without
`dias_sin_dato`.

**`'aun_no'` stays a valid code -- the screens and the assistant still recognise it -- but nothing
produces it any more, for either window type.** A day never marked occurred now reads `'pocos_dias'`
for an intraday experiment too, the same as a whole-day experiment's own unmarked day (both go
through the same `dias_que_cuentan` / `_ocurrio_por_dia` filter before any window is even built).

**The assistant's `leer_experimentos` description** stops saying an intraday verdict is "not
available"; it says what the window compares (the minutes around a wake time or a logged moment, on
test days against the person's own ordinary days).

**Tests.** `tests/test_experimentos_intradia.py` (new): despertar windows from invented
`sleep_session` rows; momento windows from invented moments, including the median-clock baseline;
coverage below and above the floor (a watch-not-worn gap inside an otherwise dense day); a day never
fetched; `mas_bajo`/`mas_alto`/`sin_cambio`/`pocos_dias` each reached; person isolation (another
person's intraday series never enters this person's verdict); a window crossing midnight, pulling
real in-window samples from both calendar days' own stored payloads while excluding out-of-window
junk values stored right next to them. `tests/test_experimentos_modelo.py`'s own
`test_intradia_window_reads_aun_no_for_every_metric` is replaced, not deleted, by
`test_intradia_window_with_no_registered_days_reads_pocos_dias`, asserting the real outcome for the
same fixture.

**Gate**, once, foreground, from the repository root, on branch tip `e3050098cf1076d8795f2b599d4989a8ede01429`:
`.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .` -> `Ran 1819 tests in 318.737s ...
FAILED (failures=1, skipped=1)`.

**Stops GATE_RED, committed on the branch (`e3050098cf1076d8795f2b599d4989a8ede01429`), not
merged.** The one failure is outside this slice's `touches:`:
`tests/test_experimentos_pantalla.py::VerdictWordsTest::test_aun_no_for_an_intraday_window`, which
built a fresh intraday experiment with zero registered days specifically to assert the OLD blanket
`'aun_no'` text ("todavía sin veredicto"); that fixture now reads `'pocos_dias'` ("muy pocos días
todavía") instead, by the same rule a whole-day experiment already uses for zero occurred days.
Fixing it means editing a file this slice was not approved to touch, so it is named here instead,

## BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-INTRADIA-DIAS-FALTANTES-1 -- wires the on-demand intraday fetch into the
scheduled pull, closing the gap BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-1-INV named: the intraday window verdict reads
minute data from `raw_payload`, but nothing fetched it after the one-time backfill -- every new
test morning stayed "sin dato" until someone re-ran the backfill by hand.

**The rule**: `experimentos.dias_intradia_necesarios(conn, person_id, hoy) -> list[str]` (new, pure
read) -- for every one of this person's ACTIVE experiments with `ventana.tipo == 'intradia'`, the
counting days (`dias_que_cuentan`) in its test window (`fecha_inicio`..yesterday, the same `fin_
prueba` bound `_veredicto_intradia` already uses, since today's own window cannot be complete yet)
and its baseline window (`fecha_inicio - BASE_DIAS`..`fecha_inicio - 1`, same as `veredicto`'s own
`base_desde`/`base_hasta`), kept only inside Garmin's intraday reach (`pull.INTRADIA_ALCANCE_DIAS`
back from `hoy`, boundary inclusive -- the same boundary `traer_intradia_rango`'s own refusal
uses) and not already `db.intradia_almacenado`. Newest first, de-duplicated across experiments. Not
filtered by whether the habit actually happened that day -- that is decided later by the verdict,
and this function must not skip fetching a day that might still turn out to count. A whole-day
experiment (`ventana.tipo == 'dia'`) and a person with no active intraday experiment both
contribute nothing.

**The wiring and its bound**: `pull._pull_intradia_pendientes(conn, person_id, hoy, token_str=None)`
(new, `body/pull.py:367`) fetches up to `INTRADIA_MAX_POR_CORRIDA = 14` of those days (newest
first) through the existing on-demand `traer_intradia` -- a new experiment's test mornings come
first, its baseline fills in over a few runs. Called only on the implicit "today" sweep (no
explicit `--date`/`fecha`), from two call sites: the local default/`--days` path in `pull._run`
(the shape both `manana`'s own `--days 1` and the plain scheduled daily sync use), and
`pull_hosted`'s per-person loop, once per connected person, re-reading and persisting the token the
same way `_pull_one_person` does. `--all`, `--recompute`, `--backfill` and `pull_backfill_hosted`
are untouched -- `tests/test_momentos_pull.py`'s `IntradiaNotCalledByAnyJobTest` still holds (no
active experiment in its fixtures, so the new call sites make zero Garmin calls there too). A
failure on one day is logged (`intradia: fetch failed for <day>: <exception type>`, via
`errores.texto_seguro`) and does not stop the others or fail the run; prints `intradia: N días
traídos, M pendientes` (counts and dates only) whenever at least one day was needed, `M` counting
every day still missing after this run (capped-out or errored alike).

**Tests**: `tests/test_pull_intradia_experimentos.py` (new) -- `dias_intradia_necesarios` itself:
no active experiment -> `[]`; a whole-day experiment contributes nothing; another person's
experiment never fetches for this person; a closed (`estado='cerrado'`) experiment contributes
nothing; missing counting days across test and baseline windows, newest first; a day already
`db.intradia_almacenado` is skipped; a day outside `pull.INTRADIA_ALCANCE_DIAS` (patched small,
5, for a tractable fixture) is dropped; days shared by two experiments are not repeated.
`tests/test_pull.py` (new) -- the wiring itself: `_pull_intradia_pendientes` fetches up to the cap
in the given newest-first order; a fetch error on one day leaves the others fetched and the run
successful; the hosted token path persists a refreshed token; the local path never touches
`garmin_cuenta`; the local default pull and `pull_hosted`'s implicit sweep both call it with no
active experiment costing zero Garmin calls, and an explicit `--date`/`fecha` never triggers it.

**Gate**, once, foreground, from the repository root:
`.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .` -> first run caught two bugs in this

day, twice, and a token-decryption assertion placed outside the `BODY_TOKEN_KEY` env patch); fixed,

`d53febfedb3913834570da179c20defa093d43b6`, `git merge --no-ff
feat/body-experimentos-intradia-dias-faltantes-1` -> `a0b2b0011d023dc97a2987e811facc51c44ff2a1`.

## BODY-MEDIDA-PESO-1-M2 -- precision, the zero-arrow and the chart/hint pairing on Tendencias (2026-11-09)

Three corrections from the orchestrator's 375 px measurement of BODY-MEDIDA-PESO-1(-M), inside the
screens that slice already changed (ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1).

**Precision as data.** `db.DECIMALES_MEDIDA` (next to `db.RANGOS_MEDIDA_PERSONAL`, same file, same
shape): a metric key's own decimal count, `1` for `body_weight_kg` and `waist_cm`, every other key
absent and defaulting to `0` -- today's behaviour, unchanged. `body/rutas/comun.py`'s new
`_decimales(key)` reads it; `comun._value` (the one place that formats a metric's own figure,
reached by `_fig_unit`, a card's `last30`/`low`/`high` and the normal-range legend) calls
`t.num(v, _decimales(key))` instead of the old bare `t.num(v)`. `body/rutas/tendencias.py`'s
`_compare` (the "vs. tu historia"/"vs. anterior" difference) reads the same `_decimales(k)` for its
own `t.num` call. Numbers localise through `i18n.T.num`'s existing `decimals` parameter -- no new
formatting helper needed, es "70,9" / "81,1", en "70.9" / "81.1"; `resting_hr` and every other key
still read "57", a whole number, unchanged.

**No arrow at zero.** `_compare` already returned `t("delta.same")` ("= como siempre" / "= as
usual") when a difference was small relative to the metric's own spread (the 15% check). It now
also returns that same text, cls "flat", whenever the difference rounds to "0" at the metric's own
precision -- whole minutes for a minutes key, `_decimales(k)` decimals otherwise -- even when that
difference cleared the spread check (a tight spread let a sub-threshold diff still read as a
"real" change before this fix). Reuses the existing wording rather than adding a new i18n key, per
the spec's "or the existing wording for no change if one exists -- reuse it."

**Chart hint only with a chart.** `body/templates/trends.html`'s `trends.chart_hint` paragraph is
now `{% if c.svg %}`-gated, next to the `{{ c.svg|safe }}` line that was already there -- the hint
no longer renders for an empty chart. Measured (not as the spec described it): at the literal
`r=30`/`r=90` window view, a weekly self-measured key already drew a chart under the existing
`len(pts) < 2` rule in `body/profile.py`'s `window_svg` -- 4-5 points clears 2 easily. The actual
empty chart was the **default view** (`r` unset, labelled "últimos 30 días"/"last 30 days" via
`trends.last30`, which is really `body/profile.py`'s monthly `month_svg`): `metric_profile`'s
`by_month` filter required 7+ raw points in a month before that month joined the line, a near-daily
Garmin cadence's own floor, which a once-a-week self reading (4-5/month) never reaches. `
metric_profile` gained a `min_month_points: int = 7` parameter (default unchanged, so every other
caller -- `WEEK_KEYS`, the assistant's own profile read -- is untouched); `tendencias.py`'s
`_trend_card` passes `SELF_MIN_MONTH_POINTS = 2` for a self-measured key and
`GARMIN_MIN_MONTH_POINTS = 7` otherwise, per origin as the spec asked, not per key. `flex_alcance_cm`,
already on `main` with the same defect, is fixed by the same origin-keyed change -- no separate
fix needed. A single self-measured point (one month, one point) still draws no chart and now shows
no hint either, on any view.

**Tests** (`tests/test_medida_peso.py`, extended; 1858 -> 1868 tests, +10): `PrecisionAsDataTest`
(weight at one decimal in es "70,9" and en "70.9"; `resting_hr` still a bare whole number);
`CompareZeroArrowTest` (a diff rounding to "0" at 1 decimal returns "delta.same" in es and en, the
same at 0 decimals for `resting_hr`, and a real difference still gets its arrow -- calls
`tendencias._compare` directly); `SelfKeyMonthlyChartTest` (a weekly series over two months draws a
chart with the hint on both the default view and `r=30`, for `body_weight_kg` and `flex_alcance_cm`);
`SelfKeySinglePointNoChartTest` (one point -> no chart, no hint). `tests/test_tendencias_todas.py`,
`test_ejes_fechas.py`, `test_history.py`, `test_i18n_paridad.py`, `test_rendimiento.py` run
unmodified and green -- no new i18n key, route, or SQL statement, so none needed extending.

## BODY-DESPERTAR-1-M -- the wake check, finished and merged (2026-11-09)

BODY-DESPERTAR-1 (1c478fb on `feat/body-despertar-1`) never wrote its own ledger entry, so this
entry carries both: what that slice built, and the test-isolation fix this one made to finish it.

**What BODY-DESPERTAR-1 built.** `garmin_adapter.fetch_sleep(day, token_str=None)` pulls ONLY the
sleep endpoint (`get_sleep_data`) for one day, sharing a new `_parse_sleep_end` helper with
`parse_day` so the two never drift apart. `body/despertar.py` (`python -m body.despertar [--day
YYYY-MM-DD]`), local person only: zero Garmin calls once `BODY_HOME/vida/despertar-<day>.json`
already exists or `sleep_session` already holds that day's `end_local` -- otherwise exactly ONE
`fetch_sleep` call per check. It respects `pull.py`'s lock: if a pull already holds it, despertar
skips that check entirely (no wait, no retry) rather than contending for it. The file it writes is
exactly `{"woke_at": "<local ISO with offset>", "source": "garmin", "written_at": "<local ISO with
offset>"}` -- no other key -- written atomically (temp file + `os.replace`, the same pattern as
`body/traer_semana.py`) so Personal's watcher never reads a half-written file. Every path always
returns exit 0: a missing token, an empty result, or a fetch error each print a kind
(`type(e).__name__`), never a payload or a traceback, so the scheduled task stays calm.
`body/vivo.py` learned the `despertar` task. `scripts/install-daily-sync.ps1` registers a fifth
scheduled task, "Body app wake check": daily at 04:00, repeating every 20 minutes for 9 hours
(through ~13:00), running `python -m body.vivo despertar` from the live worktree, same as the
installer's other tasks -- the installer itself was not re-run by either slice. The exact line
Carlos re-runs, from `scripts/`, is `.\install-daily-sync.ps1` (plus whatever `-ShiftsDir`/`-Lan`/
`-Hosted` flags he already runs it with); it is idempotent (`-Force` on every `Register-
ScheduledTask`) and safe to re-run to pick up this fifth task.

**What this slice fixed (BODY-DESPERTAR-1-M).** `tests/_isolate.py` sets one `BODY_HOME` for the
whole test process; `tests/test_despertar.py` sorts before `tests/test_dispositivo.py`, and its
tests wrote into that shared `BODY_HOME/vida/`, which `test_dispositivo.py`'s
`VidaExportHostedRefusalTest.test_main_refuses_and_writes_nothing` asserts is absent -- GATE_RED at
1888/1890 on the first run. Rather than keep the cleanup-by-deletion 1c478fb had committed (unlink
the file, `rmdir` the shared dir if now empty -- fragile, and liable to race any other module that
legitimately uses that directory), this slice gave `test_despertar.py` its own isolation:
`despertar.py` already reads `config.BODY_HOME` fresh on every call (`_path_for`, `_write`), so a
new `_AisladoTestCase` base class patches `config.BODY_HOME` to a fresh `tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=TMP)`
per test in `setUp`, and every test class that touches the wake-check file now inherits it. No
change to `body/despertar.py` was needed, and `tests/test_dispositivo.py` was not touched, keeping
its guard test's subject intact.

**Commits** (`git rev-parse`): fix `547c0e5a1991bf3208ab1352a75a9438478257bb` on
`feat/body-despertar-1`; merge into `main`, `--no-ff`,
`cc624dcb6549261328a5b637fbea7c0c4359aa0b` (tree `1b23009721ca881a8c7cae95ad1a19fb4f04954e`,
identical to the branch tree -- no conflict, nothing else changed by the merge).

## BODY-PROTEINA-1 -- a protein intake tracker, logged by talking

Carlos asked for "constant interaction with my assistant" and a protein tracker ("that's important
for me"). An INV had already found that `daily_metric` holds one value per (person, day, key) via
INSERT OR REPLACE, so a bare `protein_g` self-metric cannot hold several meals a day. The
orchestrator's binding rulings (ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1) that bound this build: a GENERIC
intake entry table, one row per thing eaten or drunk, keyed by a metric_def key, with the day total
DERIVED into `daily_metric` by one writer -- future metrics like calories or water are rows, never
new tables (Q1); several entries a day, the model estimates grams from the person's words and says
so, the person confirms with one tap through the existing propose/apply/undo pattern, corrections
and deletions go through the same path, the person's own words stay on the entry -- their data, on
their PC, never in a log or print (Q2); per-kg goals and screens are explicitly later slices (Q3/Q4);
the external interface is Carlos's own choice, not touched here (Q5). Customer-facing bytes (the
assistant card text and the new metric's words) stop this slice AWAITING_APPROVAL for the
orchestrator's 375px check -- not merged by this slice.

**Schema.** `ingesta` (id, person_id, day, ts_local nullable, metric_key FK -> metric_def, amount
REAL CHECK > 0, estimado INTEGER 0/1, descripcion TEXT nullable, created_at, updated_at), indexed by
(person_id, day); created by `db.init` on an existing DB too. `metric_def.agregado` (new column,
ALTER-added like `kind`/`origen` before it): `'suma_ingesta'` marks a key whose day total is derived
from `ingesta` rows, NULL for every other key. The first intake row: `protein_g` ("Proteína"/
"Protein", unit g, origen 'self', better 'neutral' like weight). `propuesta_agente.accion`'s CHECK
widened for `registrar_ingesta`, `corregir_ingesta`, `borrar_ingesta` (SQLite can't ALTER a CHECK,
so the guarded rebuild pattern already used for the `experimento` actions rebuilds the whole table
again).

**One writer of the day total.** `db.registrar_ingesta`/`corregir_ingesta`/`borrar_ingesta` each
recompute `SUM(amount)` for that (person, day, metric_key) and write it via `set_metric(...,
source='self', ...)`, which removes the `daily_metric` row once no entries remain (via `set_metric`'s
existing NULL-deletes-the-row behavior). All three are person-scoped: another person's entry id
raises `ValueError`, never revealing whose it is. `registrar_medida` now REFUSES an intake key (a
live `metric_def.agregado` check, defense-in-depth past its own JSON-schema enum), pointing the
caller at `registrar_ingesta`.

**Assistant tools**, the same propose/apply/undo shape every other write tool here uses:
`registrar_ingesta(metric_key, amount, estimado, descripcion?, day?, hora?)` -- insert-shaped, no
"before"; `corregir_ingesta(ingesta_id, amount)` and `borrar_ingesta(ingesta_id)` -- both carry
`antes` so undo restores exactly (borrar's undo re-inserts a new row with the same values, the same
"functionally equivalent" restoration `proponer_experimento`'s own undo already uses, never an
id-preserving trick). Each tool's description tells the model to estimate grams from the person's
words, say it is an estimate and what was assumed, one entry per meal, and ask only when the food is
too vague. `leer_dia` (via `db.load_day`) now carries that day's `ingesta` list and its derived total
in `metrics`, so the model can see what is already logged before proposing another entry. The meal
label on the card (desayuno/almuerzo/merienda/cena) is read off `ts_local`'s hour through four fixed
time bands, never its own stored column, and omitted when `ts_local` is null -- four literal `t()`
calls, not a concatenated key, so `test_i18n_paridad.py`'s dynamic-prefix guard needs no new entry.

**Privacy.** `ingesta` joined `FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES`; `export_person` includes every entry;
`delete_person` removes them. `descripcion` never appears in a ToolError or ValueError message on
any refusal path (tested directly with a planted marker).

**Demo.** `body/demo.py` seeds 3-4 invented protein entries on ~90% of days (invented grams, no
descripcion) via `db.registrar_ingesta` directly, so Tendencias' self-measured group shows protein
for the demo person; `tests/test_demo.py`'s determinism checksum now covers `ingesta`.

**The demo assistant provider never calls the new tool.** `body/agente/cliente.py`'s `Demo` provider
(Tier 1, read-only, not touched) is a fixed two-round script: round one calls `proponer_idioma` only
when the question contains "idioma", else `leer_ajustes`; round two always answers with the same
canned Spanish text. It has no branch for food or protein, so typing into the demo panel's chat can
never produce a `registrar_ingesta` card. To see the card for the 375px check, open the panel once
(any message creates a conversation), then run, against that same demo BODY_HOME:

    conn.commit()

live demo instance from this session; it is instructions for the orchestrator to run.

**A bug this slice found in its own first draft.** `METRIC_DEFS`'s 7th-field (`agregado`) padding
line ran BEFORE the self-measured rows (`flex_alcance_cm`, `snoring_min`, `body_weight_kg`,

## BODY-GARMIN-IMPORT-1 -- merged

Builds the importer for Carlos's full Garmin account export (BODY-GARMIN-EXPORT-INV step 2):
874 days of minute heart-rate/stress history Garmin's own API no longer serves, needed for the
heart-rate-recovery, shift and commute studies. Tested on invented FIT fixtures only, per
ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1 -- nothing in this slice reads a real file; running it on Carlos's
real export stays with him (his yes, a backup first, run by the orchestrator).

**The reader** (`body/fit.py`, no dependency): header (12/14 bytes, `.FIT` signature checked),
normal and compressed-timestamp record headers, definition messages in both byte orders,
developer-field definitions read and their data skipped (never decoded). Decodes only the five
fields this slice needs -- file_id.type (msg 0 field 0), monitoring's heart_rate/timestamp_16/
timestamp (msg 55 fields 27/26/253) and stress_level's value/time (msg 227 fields 0/1) -- as
uint8/16/32, plus sint8/16/32 (sint16 needed for stress_level_value's negative "no reading"
sentinels; the spec's "uint8/16/32" was read as the three widths, not as excluding their signed
counterparts). Every other field is skipped by its declared byte length from the definition
message, never decoded, so no other base type is needed at all. CRC is explicitly NOT checked --
neither the file's own trailing 2 bytes nor an optional 14-byte header's CRC are read; a
structurally broken stream (bad header, truncated record, a data message for an undefined local
type) still raises FitError per file, caught by the importer so one bad file never stops the run.
Timestamps are reconstructed inside the reader: a full field 253 sets the running base; monitoring's
16-bit field 26 and a compressed header's 5-bit offset each roll forward from it (with rollover),
and the running timestamp is carried to any later message lacking its own (msg 227's
stress_level_time, when absent, falls back to it).

**The importer** (`body/importar_garmin.py`, `python -m body.importar_garmin <export.zip>
[--desde YYYY-MM-DD] [--hasta YYYY-MM-DD] [--seco]`): opens the outer zip and reads ONLY entries
under `DI_CONNECT/DI-Connect-Uploaded-Files/` ending `.zip`, and inside those only `.fit` entries
-- the export's profile/consent/customer entries are never opened (`tests/test_importar_garmin.py`
spies on `zipfile.ZipFile.open` to confirm it). Keeps file_id.type 32 (monitoring_b); from msg 55
keeps (timestamp, heart_rate) where heart_rate > 0 (0 bpm is not a reading either); from msg 227
keeps (stress_level_time or the record's own running timestamp, stress_level_value) where
value >= 0, matching `garmin_adapter.parse_stress_series`'s own "negative = no reading" rule.
Samples are de-duplicated by exact UTC-ms timestamp across every file (a day spans several
monitoring files) before being grouped into local calendar days in the person's own timezone.
Leaves file_id.type 4 (activity) files alone, as the spec asked -- an activity-record import would
add per-activity detail (laps, HR-in-activity) Body does not have today; left for a later slice.

**Storage and precedence, same reader.** Each day's samples are stored in Garmin's own intraday
payload shape (`{"heartRateValues": [[ts_ms_utc, value], ...]}` / `stressValuesArray`) under
`raw_payload` with `source='garmin_export'` (`garmin_adapter.SOURCE_EXPORT`, new) --
`db.guardar_intradia` now takes an optional `source` (default `garmin_adapter.SOURCE`, the live
API's own tag) instead of hard-coding it, so the importer never overwrites or deletes an API row:
raw_payload's existing `(person_id, day, kind, source)` key makes them different rows, no schema
change. `db.intradia` now orders its read by `source != garmin_adapter.SOURCE` so an API row for
the same day and kind always wins when both exist -- the SAME parser
(`parse_heart_rate_series`/`parse_stress_series`) reads either source's payload unchanged, since
the export's payload is shaped exactly like the API's own, so `db.intradia` returns identical
pairs for an export day and an API day built from the same samples (tested). `db.intradia_
almacenado` is now filtered to `source=garmin_adapter.SOURCE` explicitly -- an export-only day
must keep reading as "not yet pulled through the API" so the missing-days job
(`pull._pull_intradia_pendientes`, via `experimentos.dias_intradia_necesarios`) still fetches a
day inside Garmin's API reach and never skips one the API never actually covered (tested in both
`tests/test_importar_garmin.py` and a new case added to `tests/test_pull_intradia_experimentos.py`).
The importer itself skips writing (counted as "already covered") any day `db.intradia_almacenado`
already reports complete, so a backfill run never bothers storing a day the live API already
owns -- the precedence rule above is what makes that read-side-safe either way. Idempotent (a
second run writes the same rows again via `INSERT OR REPLACE`, verified by comparing `db.intradia`
output and the `raw_payload` row count before/after); `--seco` counts without writing.

Registered in `body/vivo.py`'s `TAREAS` as `importar_garmin` (no argv prefix needed, unlike
`intradia`), so the orchestrator runs it from the live tree: `python -m body.vivo importar_garmin
<export.zip> --seco` first, then without `--seco` once the orchestrator has Carlos's go-ahead and
a backup.

## BODY-DESPERTAR-INSTALADOR-1 -- fix the wake check trigger's parameter set (2026-11-09)

BODY-DESPERTAR-1 (merged `cc624dc`) added the wake check to `scripts/install-daily-sync.ps1` as a
single `New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At "04:00" -RepetitionInterval (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 20)
-RepetitionDuration (New-TimeSpan -Hours 9)` call. On this machine's Windows PowerShell 5.1 that
call fails: "Parameter set cannot be resolved using the specified named parameters" --
`-RepetitionInterval`/`-RepetitionDuration` belong to the `-Once` parameter set, not `-Daily`, so a
re-run of the installer would silently stop registering the wake check (`Register-ScheduledTask`
then gets a null trigger). The orchestrator had already registered the task by hand in the form
proven to work and verified it (StartBoundary 04:00, Interval PT20M, Duration PT9H, next run
2026-11-10 04:00); this slice puts that same form into the installer script: `$wakeTrigger =
New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Daily -At "04:00"` followed by `$wakeTrigger.Repetition = (New-
ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At "04:00" -RepetitionInterval (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 20)
-RepetitionDuration (New-TimeSpan -Hours 9)).Repetition` -- the `-Daily` trigger's `Repetition`
property is copied from a `-Once` trigger carrying the 20-minute/9-hour repetition, rather than
built in one combined call. Nothing else in the script changed.

`tests/test_installer.py`'s `InstallerWakeCheckTaskTest` now pins the split form (`$wakeTrigger`
is `-Daily -At "04:00"` with neither repetition flag; `$wakeTrigger.Repetition` is assigned from a
`-Once` trigger carrying both) and adds a guard,
`test_no_recurring_trigger_combines_repetition_params_in_the_same_call`, that scans every
`New-ScheduledTaskTrigger` call in the script and fails if any one call combines `-Daily` or
`-Weekly` with `-RepetitionInterval`/`-RepetitionDuration` -- the exact parameter-set rule that
broke BODY-DESPERTAR-1 -- so it cannot come back in this or any other trigger the script builds
later. No existing assertion was loosened.

## BODY-PERIODO-1 -- mark unwell/travel/injury days, excluded from baselines and experiments (2026-11-09)

A `period_kind` catalog (`malestar`, `viaje`, `lesion` -- rows, seeded by `db.PERIOD_KINDS`, never
code: a fourth kind is a row and an i18n entry, not a release) and a `period` table (`person_id`,
`kind`, `start_day`, `end_day` NULL = open, `note`, CHECK `end_day >= start_day`), plus four
propose/apply/undo assistant tools -- `marcar_periodo`, `cerrar_periodo` ("I'm better since
Thursday"), `corregir_periodo`, `borrar_periodo` -- that OFFER a period when the person says
they're ill, travelling or injured, never create one silently. The five ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-
TIER-1-1 rulings, followed exactly: (1) kinds are data; (2) the note is kept like `moment.note`/
`ingesta.descripcion`, never printed, logged or exported off the PC; (3) a marked day is left OUT
of a baseline's usual range and of an experiment's counted days, before and test alike,
unconditionally, never re-weighted -- no fourth `filtro_dias` key, since every caller of
`baselines.baseline`/`experimentos.dias_que_cuentan` gets this for free from the one place each
calls `db.dias_marcados`; a verdict with too few clean days reads through the EXISTING
`pocos_dias` path, nothing new; (4) readiness's own score is untouched -- the screens that state a
period in words are BODY-PERIODO-PANTALLAS-1, a separate, later slice; (5) periods do not enter
the vida-v1 weekly export this slice (reversible later, Carlos's call). `db.load_day`'s own
`leer_dia` tool now carries a day's covering periods too, so the assistant can discover a
period's id without a fifth, newly-counted read tool. `body/privacidad.py`'s export and delete-all
now cover `period` (the note in the person's own export only); `body/demo.py` seeds one invented
closed `malestar` period.

**Performance (BODY-RENDIMIENTO-1/2 invariant, found by this slice's own gate run, fixed before
the gate counted as passing):** the first gate run was RED -- `/goals/new`, `/shifts`, `/`,
`/how/{day}` and `/day/{day}` all went over `tests/test_rendimiento.py`'s own statement ceiling,
because `readiness.compute` calls `baselines.baseline` up to five times per day and `/shifts`
calls it across its own 56-strip-day loop through ONE `Lector`-backed connection (BODY-RENDIMIENTO-
2) -- a fresh `db.dias_marcados` query per `baseline()` call reintroduced exactly the per-day query
cost that `Lector` exists to avoid (286 extra statements on `/shifts` alone). Fixed inside
`body/db.py` only (no change to `body/lector.py`, `body/readiness.py` or any route, so this stayed
inside `touches:`): `periodos()`/`dias_marcados()` now read from `_periodos_de_persona`, a
per-connection cache of a person's own period rows (periods are rare, so one real query per
connection beats one per call), invalidated on every write (`crear_periodo`/`actualizar_periodo`/
`borrar_periodo`, and `privacidad.delete_person` via the new public `db.invalidar_periodos_cache`).
Keyed by `id(conn)`, never the Connection object itself (not weak-referenceable, accepts no extra
attribute -- checked directly against this interpreter); `db.connect()` purges any cache entry
left under a reused id before a new connection could ever read through it, the same "a stale key
must never survive past the file/connection it named" discipline `ensure_ready`'s own
`_READY_FILES` already uses, so a cache hit can only ever be this same live connection's own
earlier read. `dias_marcados` also defers its `person()` timezone lookup until an OPEN period
actually overlaps the range, so the common case (no periods, or only closed ones) costs zero extra
queries beyond the one cached periods read. Re-measured after the fix: the same five routes back
at or under their existing ceiling, no ceiling number changed.

**Deviation -- four files outside `touches:`, the same shape BODY-PROTEINA-1 recorded, not
reworked:** adding four new `tipo='propuesta'` tools forces mechanical widenings wherever an
existing guard hardcodes the tool-name set or its count, and this slice's own gate run surfaced a
fifth such guard (`tests/test_persona_fuga.py`'s table census) that BODY-PROTEINA-1's own ledger
entry did not have to touch for a different reason (ingesta already needed it there too, for the
same census, and did touch it -- this slice is the second table to need it, not the first).
Touched, each a mechanical widening with no logic change: `tests/test_agente_bucle.py` (the
`nivel='ninguno'` tool-name set gains the four names), `tests/test_agente_propuestas.py` (the
`tipo='propuesta'` name set, same four), `tests/test_agente_registro.py` (`PROPUESTA_NOMBRES` gains
the four, the tool count 26 -> 30, and the test's own name corrected from "thirteen" to
"seventeen" since it would otherwise assert a number contradicted by its own docstring),
`tests/test_persona_fuga.py` (`_seed_person` seeds one `malestar` period per person with a
`ZZ<tag>-PERIODO` marker, `_sweep_tools_as` checks `leer_dia`'s new `periodos` list the same direct
way BODY-PROTEINA-1 checked `ingesta` -- own marker renders, the other person's never does; the
marker stays OUT of the route-sweep active list, same reasoning as `moment`: no screen reads it
yet, that is BODY-PERIODO-PANTALLAS-1's own job). `tests/test_experimentos_esquema.py` stayed in
`touches:` but needed no edit -- `experimento`'s own CHECK did not change, only
`propuesta_agente.accion`'s did.

**Customer-facing bytes -- STOPS here, this worker does not merge:** the four tools' card text
(`asistente.propuesta.titulo.marcar_periodo` etc., `periodo.kind.malestar/viaje/lesion`,
`asistente.propuesta.periodo_resumen/periodo_abierto/periodo_un_dia/periodo_rango/periodo_excluido/

## BODY-AGUJETAS-1 -- next-day muscle soreness as self-measured metric_def rows (2026-11-09)

Carlos (relayed by his Personal desk) uses next-day muscle soreness as his own check that a session
gave a muscle enough work. Seven new `metric_def` rows, `origen = 'self'`, `direction = 'neutral'`
(ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1 ruling 1-2): `soreness_legs`, `soreness_glutes`, `soreness_back`,
`soreness_chest`, `soreness_shoulders`, `soreness_arms`, `soreness_core` -- one key per muscle
GROUP, never a finer list -- unit `pts`, on the same propose/apply/undo path `registrar_medida`
already gives `flex_alcance_cm`/`body_weight_kg` (BODY-ENTRENO-MEDIDA-1, BODY-MEDIDA-PESO-1).
`SELF_METRIC_KEYS` and Tendencias' "self" group pick up all seven with no second list, both derived
from `db.METRIC_DEFS`.

## BODY-AGUJETAS-1-B -- the per-key reads batched

Continues BODY-AGUJETAS-1 (commits `6c6fbea`, `3e625da`, GATE_RED), on `feat/body-agujetas-1`.
ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1 ruled against raising `/goals/new`'s and `/trends`' ceilings
(ORCH-A-SUITE-NO-GATE-RUNS-ROTS-TOWARD-YOUR-RULINGS-1: fix a red by restoring the case's subject,
which is that a page's statement count must not grow with the metric catalogue) -- the fix batches
the per-metric-key reads instead.

**`body/baselines.py`**: new `baselines(conn, keys, day, window=WINDOW_DAYS, *, person_id)` reads
every key's 30-day window in one `SELECT ... WHERE metric_key IN (...)`, reads the marked-days
exclusion (BODY-PERIODO-1 ruling 3) once, and returns `{key: Baseline | None}` -- the same per-key
answer `baseline()` already gave. `baseline()`'s own conn-backed path now delegates to it for a
single key; its `lector=`-backed path (`readiness.compute`, `turnos_costo`, from BODY-RENDIMIENTO-2)
is untouched.

**`body/profile.py`**: the row-to-`MetricProfile` math pulled out of `metric_profile()` into
`_build_profile(key, rows, today, min_days, min_month_points)`; new `metric_profiles(conn, keys,
today=None, *, person_id, min_days_por_clave=None, min_month_points_por_clave=None)` reads every
key's `daily_metric` rows in one query and builds each key's profile from it, a key missing from
either `_por_clave` dict falling back to `metric_profile()`'s own defaults (14, 7). Likewise `window()`
now delegates to new `windows(conn, keys, start, end, *, person_id)`, one query spanning every key's
current AND previous period instead of two per key.

**`body/rutas/metas.py`**: `goal_new_form` calls `baselines(conn, list(defs), today,
person_id=person_id)` once instead of `baseline()` once per `metric_def` row.

**`body/rutas/tendencias.py`**: `trends()` now prefetches `profile.metric_profiles()` once for
`catalogo_tendencias.TODAS` (every key the screen can show, the default nine plus every "Ver todas
las medidas" group) with each key's own `min_days`/`min_month_points` (self vs Garmin, same
reasoning `_trend_card` used per key before), and `profile.windows()` once when a date range is
open. `_trend_card` no longer takes `conn`/`person_id` -- it reads its key's profile and window from
the two prefetched dicts and issues no SQL itself. `WEEK_KEYS`' own table (a subset of `TODAS`, read
with the same default thresholds) now reuses the same prefetched profiles instead of a second query
per key -- one redundant query per `WEEK_KEYS` entry removed as a side effect of the same batch.

## BODY-AYUNO-1 -- an eating-window card on Hoy and Día

Carlos asked (via Personal, 2026-11-09): "we can keep track of fasting windows also", and this
week he aims to go to sleep "at least 3-4 hours after eating". BODY-INFERENCIA-FC-1-INV found the
eating window is a pure read of `ingesta.ts_local` (BODY-PROTEINA-1): no inference, no schema
change.

**`body/ventana_comida.py`**, pure reads, no write, no new table:
- `ventana(conn, person_id, day)` -- the day's first and last TIMED `ingesta.ts_local`, its
  length, the total entry count and how many carried no time. `None` with no `ingesta` row that
  day; a day with only untimed rows still returns a `Ventana` (so the caller can say "you logged
  food, but no time"), just with `primera`/`ultima`/`duracion_min` all `None`. One timed entry is
  a window of one meal (`duracion_min = 0.0`), never a missing value -- a gap is never invented
  from nothing, and never collapsed into one either.
- `ayuno_previo(conn, person_id, day)` -- the overnight gap from the PREVIOUS day's last timed
  meal to THIS day's first, only when both exist.
- `comida_a_sueno(conn, person_id, day)` -- the gap from `day`'s last timed meal to the START of
  that night's sleep, the "3-4h after eating" check, a read never a verdict. `sleep_session`
  files a night under its WAKE day (`body/db.py`'s `save_day`, same reading `body/despertar.py`
  already relies on), so this reads `sleep_session` at `day + 1`, only when both exist.
- `ayuno_ahora(conn, person_id, now_local)` -- hours since the person's own last timed meal,
  whichever day it fell on, for Hoy's "fasting now"; `None` with no timed meal at or before
  `now_local`.

**Hoy** (`body/rutas/hoy.py` `_ventana_ctx`, `today.html`): a card under the day's metric cards,
always present. With at least one timed entry: the window's length, first/last meal times,
"fasting now" (from `ayuno_ahora`, independent of today's own data) and, when known, yesterday's
last meal to sleep (`comida_a_sueno` on yesterday -- last night's sleep has already happened, so
this is the one concrete 3-4h reading Hoy can show). With entries but none timed: one line saying
so. With no entry at all: one plain line inviting the person to tell Body when they eat -- no
empty chart, no target, no "good"/"bad" word (DESIGN rule 6, rule 12).

**Día** (`_ventana_dia_ctx`, `day.html`): the same window figures for that specific day, plus the
overnight fast before it (`ayuno_previo`), in a new "Ventana de comida" section between Turno and
"Todas las medidas".

Both screens share `_ventana_base` (the state -- `sin_registro` / `sin_hora` / `una_comida` /
`con_ventana` -- and the figures each needs); Hoy adds `ayuno_ahora`/`comida_sueno`, Día adds
`ayuno_previo`. Every hour/minute figure is formatted through the existing `T.minutes()`, the
same convention sleep and shift durations already use, rather than a new formatter.

**Strings**, new keys only, es/en (es default, Cuenta register, tú; both verified by
`tests/test_i18n_paridad.py`):
- `today.ventana.titulo` "Ventana de comida" / "Eating window"
- `today.ventana.sin_registro` "Cuéntale a Body cuándo comes para ver tu ventana de comida." /
  "Tell Body when you eat to see your eating window."
- `today.ventana.sin_hora` "Hoy registraste comida, pero sin hora — agrégala para ver tu
  ventana." / "You logged food today, but with no time — add it to see your window."
- `today.ventana.una_comida` "Una comida registrada hoy, a las {hora}." / "One meal logged today,
  at {hora}."
- `today.ventana.rango` "primera comida {primera} · última {ultima}" / "first meal {primera} ·
  last {ultima}"
- `today.ventana.ayuno_ahora` "En ayuno hace {horas}" / "Fasting for {horas}"
- `today.ventana.comida_sueno` "Ayer dormiste {horas} después de tu última comida" / "Yesterday
  you slept {horas} after your last meal"
- `day.ventana.titulo` "Ventana de comida" / "Eating window"
- `day.ventana.sin_registro` "Sin comidas registradas este día." / "No meals logged this day."
- `day.ventana.sin_hora` "Comida registrada este día, pero sin hora." / "Food logged this day,
  but with no time."
- `day.ventana.una_comida` "Una comida registrada, a las {hora}." / "One meal logged, at {hora}."
- `day.ventana.rango` same shape as Hoy's.
- `day.ventana.ayuno_previo` "Ayuno nocturno antes de este día: {horas}" / "Overnight fast before
  this day: {horas}"

**Demo**: `body/demo.py`'s `_seed_ingesta` now gives each invented meal a time -- one per slot in
a fixed `_COMIDA_MINUTOS` list (breakfast/lunch/snack/dinner windows), always in order -- so the
demo server's card has a real window to show, never an invented one. No CSS change was needed:
the card reuses `.card`/`.q`/`.fig`/`.note` and the existing `.mt-6`/`.mb-0`/`.m-0` utilities.

**What the spec got slightly wrong**: it describes the card as sitting "under the protein card",
but Hoy has no protein card today -- BODY-PROTEINA-1 only ever logs protein through the
assistant's chat tools and `ingesta`'s own total shows up in Tendencias and in Día's "Todas las
medidas" grid, never as a Hoy card of its own. This card is placed as its own last card in Hoy's
metrics column instead. It also does not reach `soon.html` (no Garmin data at all): that template
is outside this slice's `touches:`, so a person with zero Garmin history never sees the eating
window on Hoy, only on Día, until a later slice touches `soon.html`.

**Tests**: `tests/test_ventana_comida.py` (20 tests) -- the window across several timed entries,
across a NULL `ts_local`, with only NULL entries, with exactly one timed entry, with none at all;
cross-person isolation; the overnight fast across midnight (including under a non-UTC person
timezone, to show the module's own math never depends on it); the meal-to-sleep gap with and
without a sleep session, and reading the WAKE day correctly; `ayuno_ahora` across days and
ignoring untimed entries; a redirect-stdout check that none of the four functions prints
anything. `tests/test_hoy_ventana_comida.py` (10 tests) -- Hoy's and Día's card in each of the
four states, in es and en, plus the same stdout check across both routes.

`body/templates/today.html`, `body/templates/day.html`, `body/i18n/es.json`, `body/i18n/en.json`,
`body/demo.py`, `tests/test_ventana_comida.py`, `tests/test_hoy_ventana_comida.py`).

## BODY-PERIODO-PANTALLAS-1 -- GATE_RED

Made BODY-PERIODO-1's marked periods (illness, travel, injury) visible on the four screens that
already read `db.dias_marcados`/`db.periodos` without saying so (BODY-PERIODO-1-INV's own census):

* **Hoy** (`body/rutas/hoy.py` `_periodo_hoy_ctx`, `templates/today.html`): while a period covers
  today (open, or closed after today), a plain `.aviso` line naming the kind and start date
  ("Lesión desde el 10 nov · Body deja esos días fuera de tu rango habitual"), with a link whose
  `href="#asis-btn"` focuses the page's own assistant button -- `body/static/assistant.js` and
  `templates/base.html` are both outside this slice's `touches:`, and BODY-SEGURIDAD-2 forbids an
  inline `onclick`, so there is no way to also pre-fill the assistant's input without touching one
  of them; the link's own text carries the call to action instead. Nothing when no period covers
  today. Never the person's own note text (stays inside the assistant panel's own card, per the
  orchestrator's ruling).
* **Día** (`hoy.py` `_periodo_dia_ctx`, `templates/day.html`): a marked day says so at the top, in
  words, with every kind that covers it.
* **Tendencias** (`body/profile.py` `window_svg`'s new `marcas` param, `rutas/tendencias.py`
  `_marcas`, `templates/trends.html`): marked days shaded on every daily chart (`c-amber op-35`,
  distinct from night's `c-night op-18`; both can draw on the same day), with a legend entry only
  when the window has one. No figure changes -- same as `nights`, a marked day is shaded, not
  excluded, from this chart's own mean/band; a month-level "counted days reduced" caveat for the
  long-run monthly line (month_svg) was **dropped**: that line never excludes a marked day either
  (nothing in `profile.py`'s own aggregates does, matching the orchestrator's ruling that this
  slice changes no figure but readiness, generalised to every figure Tendencias shows), so a
  caveat claiming a reduction would have been dishonest. Read once per page, like `nights`, costing
  no extra statement when `r=all` (the ceiling-tested default has no window at all).
* **Tu historia** (`body/history.py` `patterns`/`by_shift`, `rutas/historial.py`
  `_periodo_excluido_ctx`, `templates/history.html`): a marked day is now left out of both
  functions' own buckets and counts, the same rule `baselines.baseline()` already applies -- and
  the page says how many days and which kinds, in one line.

**A real finding, not a style choice**: `db.dias_marcados()` re-reads `person()` for "today" on
*every call* while an open period overlaps the queried range (the `hoy: str | None = None` guard
is local to the function, not cached across calls) -- latent since BODY-PERIODO-1 because the demo
never had an open period before. Seeding one (below) surfaced it as a real N+1: `/day/{day}`'s own
`_delta` calls `baseline()` once per metric key (17 of them), so one open period inside that day's
30-day lookback turned 38 statements into 55 against a ceiling of 45. Fixed within this slice's own
`touches:`, not in `db.py` (outside it): `history.patterns()`/`by_shift()` now take an optional
precomputed `marcados` set (`historial.py` reads it once and passes it to both, the same way
`tendencias.py` already reads `nights` once for every card) instead of each re-deriving it per
`PATTERN_KEYS` entry; and the demo's own new open period (below) starts exactly on "today", which
keeps it outside every baseline window (always ending the day *before* the day it is computed for),
so `/`, `/day/{day}` and `/how/{day}` see no extra statement at all. `/history` still costs +2 (one
for `SELECT * FROM period`, one for the single remaining `person()` re-read), `/trends` costs +1
only on a range that actually has a window (never on the ceiling-tested `r=all` default). Measured
before/after on `demo._seed(dias=30)`: `/` 61→61, `/day/{day}` 38→38 (ceiling 45), `/trends` 14→14
(ceiling 19), `/history` 22→24 (ceiling 29) -- no ceiling raised, none of them needed to be.

**Demo** (`body/demo.py` `_seed_periodo`): the existing closed `malestar` period (BODY-PERIODO-1)
is unchanged and still shows on Tendencias and Día; added an open `lesion` period starting on the
demo's own today (not NULL-ended two days earlier, as first tried -- see the N+1 finding above) so
Hoy's own line shows on the demo server too. `periodos` count in `_seed`'s own return dict: 1 → 2.

**Strings**, es / en (both complete, `tests/test_i18n_paridad.py`'s shape/placeholder checks pass):
`today.periodo` "{kind} desde el {fecha} · Body deja esos días fuera de tu rango habitual." /
"{kind} since {fecha} · Body leaves those days out of your usual range."; `today.periodo_enlace`
"Cuéntale al asistente si ya terminó" / "Tell the assistant if it's over"; `day.periodo` "Día
marcado: {kind}" / "Marked day: {kind}"; `trends.periodos` "Día marcado" / "Marked day";
`history.periodo_excluido` "{n} días quedaron fuera de estos patrones por estar marcados
({kinds})." / "{n} days were left out of these patterns because they were marked ({kinds})."

## BODY-PERIODO-PANTALLAS-1-B -- fixes the two red tests, removes the per-call zone read (2026-11-10)

Continuation of BODY-PERIODO-PANTALLAS-1 (6af5bad, d1d427d, c3741bf), which stopped GATE_RED with two
pre-existing tests broken by its own new behaviour (not a defect) and a latent per-call read measured by
BODY-PERIODO-1-INV (see that observed-report, and this slice's own `logs/worker-...json` reference in its spec).
Dispatched as BODY-PERIODO-PANTALLAS-1-B, Tier 1 (`body/db.py` touched only in a READ helper -- no schema, no
migration, no person's value written; ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1), `approved: yes` authorising the build only.

**Fix 1 -- `test_demo_person_unchanged` (`tests/test_estados_vacios_2.py`).** Its subject, "a fully populated
person sees no warning they should not", is preserved rather than weakened or deleted: the assertion now requires
the demo Hoy page carry EXACTLY ONE `class="aviso"` element, and that it is the period line (checked via its own
`today.periodo_enlace` i18n text inside it) -- any other aviso still fails the test.

**Fix 2 -- `tests/test_i18n_paridad.py`.** Added `"periodo.kind.+": [k for k, _ in db.PERIOD_KINDS]` to
`_FIXED_DYNAMIC`, naming the dynamic call sites (`body/rutas/historial.py`, `body/rutas/hoy.py`), same shape as
its neighbours.

**Fix 3 -- the per-call timezone read (`body/db.py`).** `dias_marcados` called `person(conn, person_id)
["timezone"]` fresh on every call whenever an open period overlapped the range -- a real per-call SELECT, the
cost BODY-PERIODO-1-INV measured turning `/day/{d}`'s 38 statements into 55 against a ceiling of 45. Fixed by
reading the zone in the SAME statement as the period rows: `_periodos_de_persona` now runs one JOIN against
`person` and caches `(rows, zona)` together under the existing `_PERIODOS_CACHE`, purged on `connect()` (for a
reused `id(conn)`) and on every period write (`crear_periodo`/`actualizar_periodo`/`borrar_periodo`'s own
`invalidar_periodos_cache`), unchanged. A person with no periods still pays no timezone lookup (`zona` stays
`None`, read from the JOIN's own first row only when one exists). "today" is still computed fresh from the cached
zone at call time (`datetime.now(ZoneInfo(zona))`), so a midnight crossing still moves it -- only the ZONE is
cached, never the date. No write path exists today that changes a person's timezone after creation (grepped
`body/` for `UPDATE person SET timezone`: only the one-time Europe/Madrid migration and demo/test setup), so
there is nothing to purge a cached zone against directly; the mechanism that would have to see such a change
already exists regardless (any period write invalidates the same cache entry the zone now lives in), and
`tests/test_periodo.py::DiasMarcadosNoPerCallReadTest` exercises it.

**Fix 4 -- demo's open period (`body/demo.py`).** The invented open "lesion" period now starts the demo's today
minus 3 days, as a person would actually mark one ("unwell since the 5th"), instead of starting exactly on today
to hide the per-call cost that no longer exists.

**New tests.** `tests/test_periodo.py::DiasMarcadosNoPerCallReadTest` -- 5 calls to `dias_marcados` on one
connection, with an open period inside the range, issue at most 1 SQL statement total (measured with
`conn.set_trace_callback`); a midnight crossing in a non-UTC zone (America/Bogota, UTC-5) still moves "today"
even once the zone is cached; a timezone change is seen once the cache holding it is invalidated by a period
write. `tests/test_periodo_pantallas.py::CeilingConSinPeriodoAbiertoDiasAntesTest` -- with demo's own fixture
(open period now 3 days before today, inside every 30-day lookback), `/`, `/trends`, `/day/{d}` and `/history`
stay at or under `tests/test_rendimiento.py`'s own `_CEILINGS` (that file, not in `touches:`, is never edited).

**Statement counts**, measured with `demo._seed(dias=30)` (its own fixture, open period now 3 days before today,
inside the 30-day lookback) via `tests/_rutas.contar_sql`, same figures `CeilingConSinPeriodoAbiertoDiasAntesTest`
asserts:

| route | statements, with the fix | ceiling (`tests/test_rendimiento.py`) |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | 61 | 75 |
| `/trends` | 14 | 19 |
| `/day/{d}` | 38 | 45 |
| `/history` | 23 | 29 |

`/day/{d}`'s 38 matches BODY-PERIODO-1-INV's own pre-regression figure exactly -- the fix removes the per-call
cost rather than avoiding the one scenario that exposed it. The "55" figure (the per-call cost, open period
inside the lookback, before this fix) is BODY-PERIODO-1-INV's own measurement, a ledger_claim here, not
re-measured by this slice -- re-measuring it would mean reverting the fix first.

**Gate**, once, foreground, on commit `97e2a938bb618131d9f564d9db94ec7ec94c317d`:
`.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .` -> `Ran 2110 tests in 313.232s ... OK (skipped=1)`.
