## BODY-ENTRENO-VINCULO-1 -- a late-syncing watch session joins its manual twin instead of doubling it

A strength session logged by hand right after training, then the watch's own sync of the same
session arriving hours later, used to read as two activities. ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1
approved this Tier 1 build in words: "One additive nullable column on activity, a link set at sync
and read everywhere, undoable through a proposal; no row deleted or rewritten; asked for through
the desk in the person's own use." Eight rulings.

**Ruling 1 -- additive columns.** `activity.vinculo_manual TEXT NULL` (the other half's own
`source_id`, or NULL) and `activity.vinculo_separado INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (...IN (0,
1))` (the person said no to a link db.save_day offered, or undid one -- never offered again for
that pair), both in `SCHEMA` for a fresh database and behind the usual `PRAGMA table_info` guard in
`_migrate` for an existing one.

**Ruling 2 -- save_day links exactly one pair.** `db._enlazar_sesion_manual_unica` runs once per
newly-synced `strength_training` row with `vinculo_manual IS NULL` and `vinculo_separado = 0`: it
links only when the day has exactly one unlinked manual session that day, never on zero (nothing to
join) or two-or-more (ambiguous -- `unir_sesiones`, ruling 5, is the person's own batch fix for
that). `save_day`'s `INSERT OR REPLACE` reads the row's own prior `vinculo_manual`/`vinculo_separado`
before replacing it, so a re-sync of the same watch activity never drops an existing link or a
separated flag.

**Ruling 3 -- a linked pair reads as one session everywhere.** `db.merge_linked_training(rows)` is
the one fold: the manual half's `name` (title) and its `exercise_set` rows win; the watch half's
`start_local`, `duration_s`, `avg_hr`/`max_hr`, `calories` win; the merged row keeps the WATCH row's
own `source`/`source_id` (every existing keyed lookup -- recovery, lesion zonas -- stays correct
unchanged) plus new `sets_source`/`sets_source_id` fields pointing at whichever half's sets are the
real ones, and a `vinculado` flag. `db.load_day`, `herramientas._leer_entreno`, and
`hoy._actividades_hoy` all wrap their activities query in it; each exercise-set lookup downstream
reads `sets_source`/`sets_source_id`, never the merged row's own `source`/`source_id`.
`history.coverage`'s `activity_count` and `history.training`'s rows both exclude the manual half of
a linked pair with a `NOT (source = 'manual' AND source_id IN (SELECT vinculo_manual ...))` filter,
so a linked pair counts once without needing the full dict-merge. Día's card for a linked activity
shows `day.entreno.unida` ("Unida con la sesión de tu reloj" / "Joined with your watch's session")
with a "Separar" control.

**Ruling 4 -- `separar_sesion` undoes a link.** A new `tipo: "propuesta"` tool,
`herramientas._separar_sesion(conn, person_id, conversacion_id, day, source_id)` (either half's
`source_id` names the pair), resolves the pair via `_resolver_par_vinculado`, and raises a proposal
through `agente_propuestas.crear` the ordinary way; applying it calls `db.set_vinculo_manual(...,
separado=True)` so the pair is never auto-relinked by a later sync. Día's own "Separar" form posts to
`/day/{day}/entreno/{source_id}/separar` (`hoy.entreno_separar`), which raises and immediately
applies the SAME proposal through `herramientas._separar_sesion` and `agente_propuestas.aplicar` a
chat/MCP call would use -- no second apply path. Listed in `herramientas.HERRAMIENTAS` at
`nivel: "ninguno"` (a proposal tool never reads health data), so `body/mcp.py`'s dynamic tool list
carries it with no change there.

**Ruling 5 -- `unir_sesiones` is the batch fix for an already-doubled day.** A second new
`tipo: "propuesta"` tool, `herramientas._unir_sesiones(conn, person_id, conversacion_id, day)`, calls
`db.candidatos_union_entreno(conn, person_id, day)` -- which returns the day's one unlinked manual
and one unlinked watch `strength_training` row only when there is exactly one of each, else `None`
-- and refuses (`agente.error.entreno_unir_ambiguo`) otherwise. Applying it is the same
`db.set_vinculo_manual` write ruling 2's auto-link makes. Día's own "Unir" card (shown only when
`db.candidatos_union_entreno` finds a pair) posts to `/day/{day}/entreno/unir`
(`hoy.entreno_unir`), through the same tool and `agente_propuestas` functions.

**Ruling 6 -- the watch-first path is unchanged.** `_registrar_entreno`'s own path (the watch's own
activity already exists; the person corrects or adds sets onto its own active slots) never touches
`vinculo_manual`/`vinculo_separado` and was not edited.

**Ruling 7 -- mudanza/privacidad.** `body/mudanza.py` and `body/privacidad.py` both read/write
`activity` through `SELECT *` and dict construction, never an explicit column list, so neither
needed a change for the two new columns to travel with every other one -- read, not edited.

**Ruling 8 -- demo.** `body/demo.py`'s `_seed_entreno_vinculado` links the demo person's EARLIEST
`strength_training` activity to a new manual session on the same day (`_ENTRENO_VINCULADO_TITULO`,
"Fuerza (registrada a mano)" / "Strength (logged by hand)"), so Día shows ruling 3's "Unida" line
without the orchestrator needing a real two-sync day. Inserted directly by SQL with a deterministic
id (`f"demo-manual-{day}"`) rather than through `db.create_manual_session`, which stamps a random
`uuid.uuid4()` into `source_id` -- `tests/test_demo.py::DeterminismTest` hashes every seeded row, and
a random id broke it on the first attempt (two seed runs, two different checksums); fixed by writing
the row with a fixed id instead of changing the determinism test.

**Deviation 1 -- no cross-import for a text helper.** `body/rutas/asistente.py` carries its own rule
("Duplicated in body/rutas/hoy.py ... since neither module may import the other for one helper"), so
Día's own `_sesion_con_hora_txt`/`_entreno_vinculo_txt` are duplicated in `hoy.py` rather than
imported, matching the existing `_momento_checkin_txt` precedent -- `hoy.py` keeps its
`from . import comun, experimentos` import line unchanged.

**Deviation 2 -- four stale censuses, outside this slice's own touches, needed to turn the gate
green**, the same "needed to turn the gate green" reason BODY-PROPUESTA-VIGENCIA-1 and
BODY-TUTORIALES-EN-1 above record for the same kind of fix: adding `separar_sesion`/`unir_sesiones`
to `herramientas.HERRAMIENTAS` is exactly the sort of change these four tests exist to catch.
`tests/test_agente_bucle.py::NivelDatosEnforcementTest` and
`tests/test_agente_registro.py::RegistryShapeTest` (two assertions: a 33-tool count, now 35; a
hardcoded `PROPUESTA_NOMBRES` set -- that test method renamed from `test_nineteen_...` to
`test_twentyone_propuesta_tools_at_nivel_ninguno` to keep its own name honest) each keep an
independent hardcoded census of every `tipo: "propuesta"` tool name, both now including the two new
ones. `tests/test_registro_tu.py`'s third-person-register guard flagged
`agente.error.entreno_no_unida`/`agente.error.entreno_unir_ambiguo` ("tiene" -- its subject is "ese
día", not the reader) and needed two new allow-list lines. `tests/test_web_entry.py::RouteSetTest`
pins the FastAPI route set as of the `/ayuda` move; the five new routes (`entreno_separar`,
`entreno_unir`, and the three `entreno_propuesta_*` resolver routes) are added to its `BEFORE` set.

**Not this slice's to fix -- a pre-existing, unrelated gate failure.**
`tests/test_pipeline.py::PipelineTest::test_end_to_end_page` expects "No hay turno registrado" /
"No shift recorded" on a fresh person's `/day/{day}` page, but `db.trabaja_turnos_si` returns False
(hiding the whole Turnos section, the no-shift line included) for a brand-new `person` row -- its
`trabaja_turnos` column has no default, only a CHECK, and a fresh person has no `shift`/`shift_batch`
row either, so the read-time NULL-with-no-data inference (`BODY-TURNOS-INFERIR-1`) resolves to
False. Confirmed unrelated to this slice before leaving it alone: `git diff body/db.py` touches

once, report honestly, do not re-run it into green") for a failure whose fix sits outside this
slice's own files and substance, this is reported, not patched. Open follow-up:
`BODY-ENTRENO-VINCULO-1-FOLLOWUP-GATE-RED` -- either give `person.trabaja_turnos` a real default (and

`test_pipeline.py` to set `trabaja_turnos` explicitly before asserting on the shift section; either

**Tests**: `tests/test_entreno_vinculo.py` (new, 26): schema/migration (2), `propuesta_agente` CHECK
widening (1), `save_day` auto-link on exactly-one-candidate and never on zero/many (plus

untouched (1), merged reads from `load_day`/`leer_entreno`/`history.coverage`/`history.training` (6),
`separar_sesion` propose/apply/undo and ownership (5), `unir_sesiones` propose/apply and its

## BODY-HOST-BACKUP-ESTADO-1 -- status tells the backup/pull/backfill outcome, upload failure names R2's reason (2026-11-11)

Main relayed that the R2 bucket `duna-respaldo` held 0 objects on 11 Nov while `duna-deploy-body
status` showed `body-backup.timer: active` and a last run at the timer's own schedule
(03:30 Bogota). `body-backup.sh` fails loudly on its own (`set -Eeuo pipefail`, exits 1 on a
missing `BODY_BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT`/`BODY_R2_*`, `curl -sS --fail` on an HTTP error), so
`body-backup.service` does end `failed`. The blind spot was `status` itself
(`deploy/host/duna-deploy-body`): it printed `systemctl is-active` for the TIMERS, which stay
active whatever the service did, and `ExecMainExitTimestamp`, which is WHEN the last run ended,
never WHETHER it worked -- a failing backup read exactly like a healthy one.

**Ruling 1/2 -- `duna-deploy-body status` tells the outcome.** For `body-backup.service`,
`body-pull.service` and `body-backfill.service`, `status` now reads
`systemctl show -p Result,ExecMainStatus --value <unit>` and prints `<unit> last result: success`
or `<unit> last result: FAILED (<Result>, exit <N>)`, right after the existing `<unit> last run:
<timestamp or never>` line; a job that has never run still prints only the `last run: never` line,
unchanged. `status` itself now exits 3 when the last *backup* run failed (scoped to
`body-backup.service` only, per the ruling's own words), so a failing backup cannot read as
healthy; every other status line still prints before that exit. `usage` and the README document
the new exit code.

**Ruling 5 -- the upload failure names R2's reason.** Main ran `duna-deploy-body backup` on the
host and the upload ended `curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 400`, with R2's error XML
swallowed by `--fail`. `body-backup.sh`'s upload `curl -sS --fail` becomes `curl -sS
--fail-with-body` in both the real call and the dry-run echo, so R2's `<Code>`/`<Message>` reaches
the journal. curl's exit status is captured with `|| upload_rc=$?` (never breaking `set -e`); on
failure the script prints one line to stderr, `body-backup.sh: upload failed (curl exit <N>); R2's
reply is above`, plus `curl --version`'s first line, then exits with curl's own status. The secret
still never becomes argv (`-K -` fed by `printf`); R2's reply body is never the secret.

**Ruling 3 -- where to look.** README's backup section gains `journalctl -u body-backup.service -n
50 --no-pager`, names the success log line's shape (`body/body-<stamp>.sqlite.age size=<bytes>` --
a run with no such line did not upload), documents `--fail-with-body`, and explains the common R2
error codes (`InvalidArgument`, `SignatureDoesNotMatch`, `AccessDenied`, `NoSuchBucket`) against the
`BODY_R2_*`/`BODY_BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT` env values -- `InvalidArgument` on the credential usually
means an API token was pasted where the R2 access key ID belongs. No secret value is ever printed
(unchanged).

**No other change** to `body-backup.sh`'s env reading, its units or its timer.

**Tests.** `deploy/host/duna-deploy-body`, `body-deploy.sh`'s systemd units and the real
`body-backup.sh`/`duna-deploy-body status` logic cannot run `systemctl`/`runuser`/as root on this
Windows worker (the existing `tests/test_host_deploy.py`/`tests/test_host_backup.py` files are
text-level checks for the same reason, not execution tests) -- this slice follows that pattern
rather than the spec's literal "stubbed systemctl" phrasing: new text-level tests in
`tests/test_host_backup.py` assert the exact loop over the three job units, the exact
`last run`/`last result: success`/`last result: FAILED (...)` strings, that `status_exit=3` is
scoped inside the `body-backup.service` branch only, that a never-run job prints no `last result`
line, and that the data-dir line still prints before the final `exit "$status_exit"`; for the
upload, that both curl invocations carry `--fail-with-body`, that the exit status is captured with
`|| upload_rc=$?`, that the failure line and `curl --version` both go to `>&2`, that the script
exits with `$upload_rc`, that the secret never reaches curl's argv, and that this handling exists
only in the real (non-dry-run) branch. One new test in `tests/test_host_deploy.py` cross-checks the
three unit names status reports against the real `body-pull.service`/`body-backfill.service` unit
files. README gets four new assertions for the journalctl command, the `size=` log shape, the R2
error codes, and the documented exit code. This is a deviation from the spec's test description,
recorded here rather than guessed past.

**Merge policy.** The diff has no schema or migration change and no cross-repo contract/DTO change,
but it does change bytes Carlos reads as the deploy's own operator (`status`'s new output lines,
`usage`, and README's backup section), the same customer-bytes condition that stopped
BODY-HOST-BACKUP-1 `AWAITING_APPROVAL`. Unlike that slice, this spec's body says in words that this
merges on a green gate ("Green -> ... APPROVED to merge on a green gate"), under
`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`: a read-only status verb gaining truthful lines plus the upload's
`--fail-with-body`, no secret handling, env reading, units or timer change. So this merges rather
than stopping `AWAITING_APPROVAL`.

Gate: `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .` -- 2756 tests, `OK (skipped=1)`,
run once on the final committed tree (commit `19d66cc7b0349d27633784592c52cde5bbc36375`).

No password, token, session secret or health figure was read, printed, or written anywhere in this
slice's own work.

(`19d66cc7b0349d27633784592c52cde5bbc36375`).

## BODY-NUTRIENTE-OBJETIVO-1 -- a daily target for one of the eight intake keys, surfaced on Today, Día and Ajustes (2026-11-11)

**Schema** (`body/db.py`, additive): `nutrient_target(person_id, metric_key, start_day, kind, amount,
sentido, created_at)`, primary key `(person_id, metric_key, start_day)`. `kind` is `absolute`,
`per_kg` or `off` (`db.NUTRIENT_TARGET_KINDS`); `sentido` is `al_menos` or `como_maximo`
(`db.NUTRIENT_TARGET_SENTIDOS`); `amount` is `NULL` iff `kind = 'off'`, else `> 0` (CHECK). Ruling
1: a changed target is a NEW row, never an overwrite of an existing one -- history stays, the
target for a day is the row with the latest `start_day <= day`. The `propuesta_agente` CHECK
widened by the existing rebuild dance (`_propuesta_agente_needs_nutriente_rebuild`, a ninth
widening on top of BODY-ENTRENO-VINCULO-1's eighth) to accept `proponer_objetivo_nutriente`. One
writer pair, `db.set_nutrient_target`/`db.borrar_nutrient_target`, called only from
`body/agente/propuestas.py`'s apply/undo -- the person sets every value, Body never invents one
(`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`).

**Reader** (`body/nutriente_objetivo.py`, new, the only module reading this table): `sentido_por_
defecto` (ruling 6 -- caffeine_mg/alcohol_g default to `como_maximo`, every other intake key to
`al_menos`); `texto_objetivo` (the target in words, shared by the proposal card, Ajustes' listing
and Today/Día); `ultimo_valor` (generic latest-value-within-N-days lookup, not hardcoded to
body_weight_kg, so a future per-something-else target can reuse it); `objetivo_del_dia` (one
metric, one day); `objetivos_vigentes` (every metric's live target as of a day, for Ajustes);
`estado_del_dia` (every metric with a live target on a day -- total told, count, resolved target,
`restante` -- shared by Today, Día and `leer_hoy`/`leer_dia`). Ruling 2: `kind = 'per_kg'` resolves
against the person's own latest `body_weight_kg` within 30 days; with none, `objetivo` is `None`
and `falta_peso` is `True` -- an honest gap, never a guessed weight. Every read batches its queries
(one IN-clause per read, never one per metric_key) to stay inside BODY-RENDIMIENTO-1's per-route
query ceiling.

**Tool** (`body/agente/herramientas.py`): `proponer_objetivo_nutriente` (tipo `propuesta`, nivel
`ninguno`) -- params `metric_key` (enum, the eight `INGESTA_METRIC_KEYS`), `kind` (enum
`NUTRIENT_TARGET_KINDS`), `sentido` (enum `NUTRIENT_TARGET_SENTIDOS`), `amount` (number or null,
required only when `kind != 'off'`), `start_day` (ISO date, defaults to today); refuses a
non-accumulable metric_key, `per_kg` on a metric not measured in grams, a non-positive amount, an
invalid `kind`/`sentido`, or a malformed `start_day`. `propuestas.py`'s matching `_Accion`
(`_drift_aplicar_objetivo_nutriente`, `_drift_deshacer_objetivo_nutriente`,
`_aplicar_objetivo_nutriente`, `_deshacer_objetivo_nutriente`) is update-shaped like
`registrar_medida` on `daily_metric`: `antes` carries that exact day's existing row (or `None`) so
undo restores it exactly; drift is checked against `(kind, amount, sentido)` on that same
`(person_id, metric_key, start_day)` slot. `leer_hoy`/`leer_dia` both gained an `objetivos_
nutriente` key (`nutriente_objetivo.estado_del_dia`). The MCP server lists and can call the tool
like any other propuesta-kind one (`tests/test_mcp.py`).

**UI.** Today and Día share one context builder (`body/rutas/hoy.py::_objetivos_nutriente_ctx`): a
"Metas de nutrientes" card, one line per intake key with a live target on that day (never today's
-- `estado_del_dia` is already history-aware), a CSP-safe inline-SVG progress bar
(`<rect width="{{ o.pct }}">` against the fixed `.c-inset`/`.c-body` palette classes, never an
inline `style=`) when a number can be shown, and `falta_peso`'s own line with no number guessed.
Ajustes gained a "Metas diarias" card (`body/rutas/ajustes.py`): a listing of every live target
(`nutriente_objetivo.objetivos_vigentes`), any still-pending proposal with its own Aplicar/
Descartar, and a form (behind a `<details>`) that raises the SAME `proponer_objetivo_nutriente`
proposal the chat and MCP use (`POST /settings/nutriente/proponer`) -- never a direct write, apply/
discard go through the generic `agente_propuestas.aplicar`/`descartar` via two more routes
(`/settings/nutriente/propuestas/{id}/aplicar`, `/.../descartar`), the same template
`entreno_separar`/`_entreno_propuesta_resolver` in `hoy.py` already uses.

## BODY-DESPLAZAMIENTO-2 -- the commute data path: a fourth `metric_def.origen`, a generic import-status table, one importer, and the two ways in (2026-11-12)

Carlos said yes to Body showing his commute time and whatever else it needs. The Personal desk
writes a daily commute summary CSV (`day,vehicle_minutes,vehicle_trips,walking_minutes,
cycling_minutes,computed_at`, no coordinates or place names) computed from his Timeline export.
This slice builds the data path end to end -- not the screens: Tendencias grouping, freshness
wording and per-source delete are BODY-DESPLAZAMIENTO-3's job.

**Ruling 1 -- `origen` widened.** `metric_def.origen`'s CHECK constraint gains `'vida'` alongside
`'garmin'` and `'self'`, via the repo's existing rebuild-without-ALTER pattern (new
`_metric_def_needs_vida_rebuild`/`_rebuild_metric_def_table` in `body/db.py`, guarded by
`_rebuild_with_fk_off`, old-row count verified before the swap). Every place the code branches on
`origen` compares explicitly to `== "self"` (`body/rutas/tendencias.py`,
`body/catalogo_tendencias.py`, `body/agente/herramientas.py`), so `'vida'` inherits the same
measured/garmin treatment with no code change in any of the three -- pinned by
`OrigenBranchTreatsVidaAsMeasuredTest` in `tests/test_desplazamiento_import.py`.

**Ruling 2 -- four metric rows.** `vehicle_minutes` (min), `vehicle_trips` (unit `trips`, an
unmapped literal like the repo's existing `kg`/`cm`/`g`/`ml`/`mg`, since `body/rutas/comun.py`'s
`UNITS` map is outside this slice's `touches`), `walking_minutes` (min), `cycling_minutes` (min) --
all `better="neutral"`, `kind="measured"`, `origen="vida"`, `agregado=NULL`. i18n labels
`metric.vehicle_minutes`/`metric.vehicle_trips`/`metric.walking_minutes`/`metric.cycling_minutes` in
both languages. `body/desplazamiento_import.py`'s `VIDA_KEYS` maps each Body key to its vida-v1
shared key (`vida.vehicle_minutes`, `vida.vehicle_trips`, `vida.walking_minutes`,
`vida.cycling_minutes`).

**Ruling 3 -- `fuente_importacion`.** A new generic table (`person_id`, `fuente`, `primer_dia`,
`ultimo_dia`, `computed_at`, `dias`, `importado_at`, `ultimo_error`, `ultimo_error_at`, PK
`(person_id, fuente)`) tracks any file-based import's status, no figure stored. `fuente` for this
file is `personal:commute-diario.csv`.

**Ruling 4 -- the importer.** `body/desplazamiento_import.py`: `validar(texto)` refuses the whole
file on any defect (wrong header, bad date, duplicate day, non-integer/negative count, mixed
`computed_at`, future day, over 1 MB) -- all-or-nothing, same rule as `shift_import._validate`.
`importar(conn, person_id, texto)` writes via the existing `db.set_metric` writer on success and
updates `fuente_importacion`; on refusal it records only `ultimo_error`/`ultimo_error_at`, changing
nothing else; the same `computed_at` twice is a no-op; a day absent from a later file is never
deleted or zeroed. Prints counts and a date range only, never a value.

**Ruling 5 -- two ways in, one function.** (a) the local vivo task
`importar_desplazamiento --file <path>`; (b) a new device-key scope `desplazamiento:subir`, route
`POST /api/desplazamiento` mirroring `/api/turnos`'s auth/size-cap/JSON-answer shape (1 MB cap,
422 on refusal, `{dias, primer_dia, ultimo_dia, sin_cambios}` on success), and the PC uploader
`body/subir_desplazamiento.py` as vivo task `subir_desplazamiento --file <path>`. The file path
comes from `--file`, else `BODY_COMMUTE_FILE` read through the new `body/config.py::commute_file()`,
else a clear "no file configured" exit -- no default path names any person's folder. Ajustes'
Dispositivos page offers `desplazamiento:subir` as a checkbox like `turnos:subir`; since scopes are
fixed at key creation (no update function exists), the page also says in plain words
(`dispositivos.scope_fixed_note`) that a new key is needed to add a scope to an already-connected PC.

**Ruling 6 -- the installer.** `scripts/install-daily-sync.ps1` gains an optional `-CommuteFile
<path>`: when given, it registers one more daily scheduled task right after the shift upload
(`-m body.vivo subir_desplazamiento --file "<path>"`); when absent, no task is registered and the
installer says so in one line. Person-run command (placeholder paths):
`.\install-daily-sync.ps1 -Hosted -ShiftsDir "C:\path\to\your\shifts\folder" -CommuteFile
"C:\path\to\commute-diario.csv"`.

**New/changed strings** (es / en): `dispositivos.scope.desplazamiento` "Subir desplazamiento" /
"Upload commute"; `dispositivos.scope_fixed_note` "Un PC que ya conectaste solo tiene los permisos
que marcaste en ese momento. Para añadir uno nuevo, conéctalo otra vez con una clave nueva." / "A PC
you already connected only has the permissions you checked at the time. To add a new one, connect it
again with a new key."; `metric.vehicle_minutes` "Tiempo en vehículo" / "Time in a vehicle";
`metric.vehicle_trips` "Viajes en vehículo" / "Vehicle trips"; `metric.walking_minutes` "Minutos
caminando" / "Walking minutes"; `metric.cycling_minutes` "Minutos en bicicleta" / "Cycling minutes".

**Census tests outside `touches` extended to the new truth** (never loosened), per the slice's own
carve-out, each a structural census firing on any new table/route/scope added anywhere -- see
commit `08422f9` for the full file-by-file rationale: `body/privacidad.py` (`fuente_importacion`
joins `FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES`, exported by date/count/reason-class only, deleted with the person),
`body/mudanza.py` (`fuente_importacion` registered in `REGISTRY`, matched on `(person_id, fuente)`),
`tests/test_persona_fuga.py` (seeds one `fuente_importacion` row per test person),
`tests/test_web_entry.py` (`POST /api/desplazamiento` added to the pinned route set),
`tests/test_registro_tu.py` (`dispositivos.scope_fixed_note`'s "tiene" allow-listed: third person,
subject is "un PC"), `tests/test_demo.py` (the four commute keys excluded from the demo-seeded
census with a dated comment -- they arrive from Personal's importer, not `body/demo.py`'s own
curated lists, consistent with ruling 7: no screen work this slice).

### BODY-DESPLAZAMIENTO-3-M -- three defects from the 375 px review, one of them pre-existing (2026-11-12)

The orchestrator's AWAITING_APPROVAL review at 375 px found the round working as specced, and three
defects, named in ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1's own approval reason: two presentation defects in
this round, plus one unit bug that decided a metric's formatting from its KEY's spelling instead of
its declared unit -- pre-existing in both `body/rutas/comun.py` and `body/history.py` before this
round touched either, but exposed by the three new commute minute keys.

**Fix 3 -- minutes by declared unit.** `_is_minutes(key)` in both files decided "this is minutes"
from `key.endswith("_min") or key == "sleep_minutes"` -- a false positive for `sleep_hr_min` (unit
`bpm`, `db.py:851`: rendered on Trends as "≈ 55 min" with no unit) and a false negative for the new
`vehicle_minutes`/`walking_minutes`/`cycling_minutes` (unit `min`, but the KEY ends `_minutes`, not
`_min`: rendered with no minute formatting and no unit at all). `body/history.py` now holds the one
real decision, `es_minutos(key)`, reading `_UNIT_BY_KEY` -- `{d[0]: d[2] for d in db.METRIC_DEFS}`,
built once at import time -- never the key's spelling; `sleep_minutes` needed no special case, its
own declared unit already being `"min"`. `body/rutas/comun.py::_is_minutes` reads the SAME dict
directly (`history._UNIT_BY_KEY.get(key) == "min"`) rather than calling `history.es_minutos(key)`:
`tests/test_guardia_parches.py::NoShimFunctionGuardTest` refuses a route-module top-level function
whose body is only `return other_module.fn(same_args)` (caught live on the first gate run, below),
and `comun._is_minutes` could not simply be deleted -- `body/rutas/turnos.py`, outside this slice's
`touches`, still calls it by name. Grepped for every other `key.endswith("_min")` heuristic in
`body/`: none found outside these two now-fixed definitions. Census test (`tests/test_history.py`):
every `db.METRIC_DEFS` key is minutes iff its own unit is `"min"`, no other key is; `sleep_hr_min`
renders in bpm on Trends (not minutes) and keeps `NOISE_FLOOR_DEFAULT`; `vehicle_minutes` renders its
delta and normal range exactly as `sleep_awake_min` does.

**Fix 1 -- Día without commute data.** `day_view()`'s generic card grid listed all four commute keys
on every day, each reading a bare "—" past `ultimo_dia` or for a person who never imported the source
at all -- ruling 3's own "no row, no code needed for that half" turned out wrong for the generic grid
(only `_desplazamiento_dia_ctx`'s one-line provenance note already read it correctly). Fixed with one
check before the grid loop: a key whose own registered source (`fuentes.fuente_de_metrica`) has no
value at all for this day, across every key that source owns, is skipped entirely; a day with at
least one of a source's keys present still shows all of that source's cards, a missing one still
reading "—", unchanged. Self-typed and Garmin-origin rows are untouched (`fuente_de_metrica` returns
`None` for them). Tests (`tests/test_desplazamiento_vista.py`): no commute card the day after
`ultimo_dia`; none at all for a never-imported person, on any day; a day with data still shows all
four plus the source line.

**Fix 2 -- confirmation wording.** Both the confirmation and the done string used a possessive on
the source's own label ("Delete {fuente}'s data?" / "¿Borrar los datos de {fuente}?"), awkward in
both languages. Both now quote the label instead, the same «»/“” convention this app already uses
for a quoted value elsewhere (e.g. `today.noche_inusual.nota_guardada`), with a singular "it" in
place of the now-dropped plural "los/the data of":

    es confirm: ¿Borrar «{fuente}»? Una nueva subida lo vuelve a traer.
    en confirm: Delete "{fuente}"? A new upload brings it back.
    es done:    Se borró «{fuente}». Una nueva subida lo vuelve a traer.
    en done:    "{fuente}" deleted. A new upload brings it back.

(replacing `privacidad.fuente.confirmar` "¿Borrar los datos de {fuente}? Una nueva subida los vuelve
a traer." / "Delete {fuente}'s data? A new upload brings it back." and `privacidad.fuente.borrada`
"Se borraron los datos de {fuente}. Una nueva subida los vuelve a traer." / "{fuente} data deleted. A
new upload brings it back.") Tests: both strings, both languages, with the real label substituted
in; `tests/test_i18n_paridad.py` (placeholder and key-set parity) stays green with no change needed.
A pre-existing golden assertion in `tests/test_desplazamiento_vista.py` that pinned the old done
string (`"Se borraron los datos de"`) was updated to the new, correct text, never loosened.

## BODY-DESPLAZAMIENTO-LOCAL-1 -- the local daily sync imports the commute file too (2026-11-12)

BODY-DESPLAZAMIENTO-2 (merged `0ed81c4`) gave `scripts/install-daily-sync.ps1` an optional
`-CommuteFile`, but only its `-Hosted` branch read it; the local branch (built when `-Hosted` is not
given) never mentioned it, so on a PC still running in LOCAL mode -- which is where Carlos's PC is
today, since the move to the host has not happened -- the commute file would never reach the
database. This slice wires it into the local branch, reusing the `importar_desplazamiento` vivo task
`-Hosted` already has as `subir_desplazamiento`'s local-path twin (from BODY-DESPLAZAMIENTO-2).

**The change.** When `-CommuteFile` is given, `"Body app daily sync"`'s `$dailyActions` gains one
more action right after `shift_import` (same `-WorkingDirectory $LiveDir`):

    -m body.vivo importar_desplazamiento --file "<path>"

so the task now pulls, imports shifts (if `-ShiftsDir`), then imports the commute file (if
`-CommuteFile`) -- each guarded independently, in that order. The local summary line's new
`$commuteMsg` matches how it already reports shifts: `"on, from $CommuteFile"` when given, `"off
(pass -CommuteFile to turn it on)"` when not, folded into the one `Write-Host "Registered: ..."` line
next to the existing `shift import:` phrase. The header usage comment gains a local example
(`Example with commute import on: .\install-daily-sync.ps1 -CommuteFile
"C:\path\to\your\commute-diario.csv"`), placed next to the existing `-ShiftsDir` example and before
the `-Hosted:` section. The `-Hosted` branch (commute upload task, `subir_desplazamiento`) is
unchanged.

`tests/test_installer.py` gained `InstallerLocalCommuteImportTest` (6 cases): the commute action is
present in `$dailyActions` and reads `-m body.vivo importar_desplazamiento` with `--file
"$CommuteFile"` and `-WorkingDirectory $LiveDir`; it comes after the `shift_import` guard; it exists
only inside its own `if ($CommuteFile)` guard (absent outside it); the local `$commuteMsg` assignment
(the second of two in the file, the hosted one being the first) reads `"on, from $CommuteFile"` and
`"pass -CommuteFile to turn it on"`; the `Write-Host "Registered: ..."` line references `$commuteMsg`;
the header carries the new local example before the `-Hosted:` marker. All prior hosted-commute and
local-shift-import cases are unchanged and still pass.

## BODY-TURNOS-PERFIL-DIA-1 -- the hero's day-offset chart, and the reader it is built on (2026-11-12)

BODY-MOCK-R2-CENSO-1-INV named two followups from mock round 2's `PhoneShiftsLight` board: this
slice (a reusable day-offset profile around a night block, reused as its own first consumer so it
never sits unused) and BODY-TURNOS-MINIGRAFICO-1 (the mini chart on Shifts' hero) -- the second is
resolved here too, by the same chart.

**Ruling 1, the reader.** `turnos_costo.perfil_por_dia(conn, person_id, metric, hoy=None)`: for each
fixed `OFFSETS` entry (`antes`, `noche_1`, `noche_ultima`, `post_1`..`post_4`, relative to a night
block's own first/last night), the mean of that day's value minus the person's own day-week
reference centre, averaged over every night block in `resumen()`'s own RESUMEN_DIAS window. The
centre and band are `referencia()`'s own mean and 25th-75th percentile -- the same one the hero's
cost rows already use -- re-expressed around a centre of 0 (`banda.bajo`/`banda.alto` = `r.bajo -
r.media` / `r.alto - r.media`). A day with no value is skipped, never zeroed; an offset no block
actually reaches (`noche_ultima` on an all-one-night history) is left out of `offsets` rather than
reported as a zero. The function never returns a bare `None` -- `resumen()`'s and
`_ultima_semana`'s own convention -- it always returns a dict: `{"metric", "motivo":
"pocos_bloques_previos"}` and nothing else when there are fewer than MIN_BLOQUES_PREVIOS night
blocks in the window or the metric has no reference at all (both conditions reuse that one existing
REASON_CODES entry, no new code added); otherwise `motivo` is `None` and the dict carries `offsets`
(`[{"offset", "media", "n"}, ...]`), `centro`, `banda`, `mas_bajo` **or** `mas_alto` (whichever
`db.METRIC_DEFS`' own direction calls worse for this metric -- the key name itself switches) naming
the offset furthest from usual, `vuelta` (the first `post_*` offset back inside the band, or `None`
if none ever is), `noches_tipicas` (the median block length) and `n_bloques`.

**Ruling 2, one version.** `turnos_costo.VERSION` stays `"turnos-v1"`: `perfil_hrv` is additive on
`resumen()`'s own return dict, and no existing figure `resumen()` already reported changed -- the
full pre-existing `tests/test_turnos_costo.py` suite (41 tests) stayed green unmodified, which is
this slice's own proof.

**Ruling 3, the chart.** Under "What a night week costs you" (the hero), for `hrv_last_night`, an
inline server-rendered SVG (Body's CSP forbids inline `style`/`<style>`/script; the chart's one new
rule, `.tick`, lives in `body/static/body.css`): the usual-range band as a light rect, the night
offsets (`noche_1`, `noche_ultima`) shaded, a line with a point through each offset's own mean, and
three y ticks read off the data's own range (top, zero, bottom) -- never a population figure. x-axis
labels: es "día antes" / en "day before"; "noche 1" / "night 1"; "noche {n}" / "night {n}" (n =
`noches_tipicas`, present only when some block actually reached `noche_ultima`); "+1".."+4" for the
`post_*` offsets, identical in both languages, never translated. An `aria-label` carries the
caption, built from the data every time: es «Variabilidad de la frecuencia cardiaca, en ms frente a
lo usual, alrededor de {n} noches. El punto {punto} es {offset}; {vuelta}.» / en "Heart-rate
variability, in ms against your usual, around {n} nights. The {punto} point is {offset}; {vuelta}.",
with a singular `_one` variant for one night, `punto` = "más bajo"/"lowest" or "más alto"/"highest"
(whichever `mas_bajo`/`mas_alto` the reader returned), `offset` from a per-offset wording key
(`shifts.perfil.offset.*`, e.g. «la última noche» / "the last night"), and `vuelta` either «el
{offset} vuelves a tu rango» / "by {offset} you are back in your range" or the fixed «en 4 días aún
no vuelves a tu rango» / "4 days after, you are not back in your range yet". A small line under the
chart: «de {k} bloques de turno nocturno» / "from {k} night blocks". With no profile (`perfil_hrv`'s
own `motivo` set), no chart and no empty frame -- the hero's existing honest-gap text stands
unchanged.

**Ruling 4, the assistant.** `_leer_costo_turnos` already just returns `turnos_costo.resumen(...)`,
so `perfil_hrv` reaches the `leer_costo_turnos` tool output for free; its catalogue description now
names what the field answers ("cuándo está más bajo y cuándo vuelve a su rango").

**Ruling 5, the demo.** No `demo.py` change was needed: `NIGHT_EFFECT["hrv_last_night"]` (-12) and
`_recovery_factor`'s own taper (1.0/0.7/0.4/0.15/0 over the nights and the four days after) already
give a real dip and, on 24 of the 28 possible shift-cycle anchor days, an actual return into band --
confirmed by a new regression test (`PerfilHrvReachableTest`) across the full cycle, rather than
assumed.

**A cost finding, caught by the gate itself.** Computing `perfil_hrv` unconditionally inside
`resumen()` first pushed `/shifts/como` one statement over `tests/test_rendimiento.py`'s pinned
ceiling (26 vs 25) -- `perfil_por_dia` was opening its own second `Lector` (one SELECT per metric)
and recomputing `referencia()` (which recomputes `bloques_noche()` again for its own exclusion
window) on top of what `resumen()` had already read, even on a route that never reads `perfil_hrv`
at all. Fixed by giving `perfil_por_dia` optional `lector`/`bloques`/`ref` parameters -- the same
shared-reader pattern `referencia`/`_costo_bloque`/`_medias_bloque`/`_recuperacion_bloque` already
use -- and widening `resumen()`'s own single Lector to `[hoy - RESUMEN_DIAS - 1, hoy +
ventana_post]` (a wider date range costs no extra statement, only more rows per statement already
read). `tests/test_rendimiento.py` needed no change at all; its existing ceilings stood.

**New strings**, es / en:

    shifts.perfil.banda: "tu rango habitual" / "your usual range"
    shifts.perfil.n_bloques: "de {k} bloques de turno nocturno" / "from {k} night blocks"
    shifts.perfil.eje.antes: "día antes" / "day before"
    shifts.perfil.eje.noche_1: "noche 1" / "night 1"
    shifts.perfil.eje.noche_ultima: "noche {n}" / "night {n}"
    shifts.perfil.offset.antes: "el día antes" / "the day before"
    shifts.perfil.offset.noche_1: "la noche 1" / "night 1"
    shifts.perfil.offset.noche_ultima: "la última noche" / "the last night"
    shifts.perfil.offset.post_1: "el día +1 después" / "day +1 after"
    shifts.perfil.offset.post_2: "el día +2 después" / "day +2 after"
    shifts.perfil.offset.post_3: "el día +3 después" / "day +3 after"
    shifts.perfil.offset.post_4: "el día +4 después" / "day +4 after"
    shifts.perfil.punto.bajo: "más bajo" / "lowest"
    shifts.perfil.punto.alto: "más alto" / "highest"
    shifts.perfil.vuelta: "el {offset} vuelves a tu rango" / "by {offset} you are back in your range"
    shifts.perfil.vuelta_ausente: "en 4 días aún no vuelves a tu rango" / "4 days after, you are not back in your range yet"
    shifts.perfil.caption: "Variabilidad de la frecuencia cardiaca, en ms frente a lo usual, alrededor de {n} noches. El punto {punto} es {offset}; {vuelta}." / "Heart-rate variability, in ms against your usual, around {n} nights. The {punto} point is {offset}; {vuelta}."
    shifts.perfil.caption_one: "Variabilidad de la frecuencia cardiaca, en ms frente a lo usual, alrededor de una noche. El punto {punto} es {offset}; {vuelta}." / "Heart-rate variability, in ms against your usual, around one night. The {punto} point is {offset}; {vuelta}."

### BODY-TURNOS-PERFIL-DIA-1-M -- five defects the orchestrator measured on the live chart at 375 px (2026-11-12)

The orchestrator opened `/shifts` at 375 px on the demo and measured the SVG in the DOM (viewBox
"0 0 320 116", rendered 314 px wide from x=30.6). Five defects, all against ruling 3 above:

1. **No visible caption.** The data-built sentence lived only in the `aria-label`; ruling 3 and the
   mock (`PhoneShiftsLight.dc.html`) show it as text under the chart. Fixed: `_perfil_caption(t,
   perfil)` is now the ONLY builder -- `_perfil_hrv_ctx` calls it once, hands the result to
   `_perfil_svg` for the `aria-label` and to the context as `caption`, and `shifts.html` renders
   `<p class="read mt-6">{{ perfil_hrv.caption }}</p>` under the chart, above "from k night blocks".
   Tests (`PerfilChartGeometryTest.test_visible_caption_equals_the_aria_label_in_both_languages`,
   `WebAndToolTest.test_shifts_page_shows_a_visible_caption_matching_the_aria_label`): the paragraph
   equals the aria-label byte for byte (`html.escape`d), in both languages; the existing
   `test_no_chart_without_a_profile` already covers the no-profile case (no chart, so no caption
   either -- the `{% if perfil_hrv %}` guard covers both).
2. **Y-tick labels sat inside the plot** (x=33, "+10.8" over the first point's own circle at
   x=28), carried no unit, and showed a decimal. Fixed: a left gutter, sized from the actual tick
   text width (`_label_px`), that the plotted line and its points never enter; at most three ticks
   (top/zero/bottom), each a whole number on one shared **nice-number step** -- `_nice_step(raw)`
   picks the smallest of {1, 2, 5, 10} x a power of ten at least as large as `raw`, applied to
   `(rango_alto - rango_bajo) / 4` (`_PERFIL_TICK_DIVISIONS`), then both the top and bottom raw
   values round to the nearest multiple of that one step (`_perfil_ticks`) -- "+10.8"/"-20.0"
   become "+10"/"-20". The unit (from the metric's own declared unit, `comun._unit(t,
   defs[perfil["metric"]])` -- "ms" for hrv, never hardcoded) rides whichever of the two non-zero
   ticks is drawn (alto preferred; bajo if alto rounds to 0; the "0" tick itself only as a last
   resort if both round to 0). A tick whose value rounds to 0 is not drawn at all (it would
   duplicate "0"), so "at most three" is sometimes fewer.
3. **The first point (x=28) was left of the svg's own rendered left edge**, clipped. Fixed: the
   same gutter/inset arithmetic that places the y ticks also places the plot's own left/right
   edges (`plot_left`/`plot_right`) far enough in that the first and last point AND their x-axis
   labels (half their approximate width, `_label_px(label) / 2`) sit fully inside `[0, width]`,
   with a 2 px margin (`_PERFIL_EDGE_PAD`) kept at each edge.
4. **The x labels were an independent HTML flex row**, laid out at a fixed 52 px pitch from a
   fixed-width svg, never aligned to the points' own (now variable) pitch. Fixed: the row is
   deleted; each label is a `<text text-anchor="middle">` drawn inside the svg at the same `cx` its
   point uses, so `label.x == point.cx` by construction, never by two separate layouts agreeing.
   The chart's own width (`_PERFIL_WIDTH` = 320, never shrunk) grows exactly as far as the widest
   ADJACENT label pair needs -- `pitch = max(label[i]/2 + label[i+1]/2 + gap)` over every
   consecutive pair, width grows to fit `pitch * (n-1)` when the default 320 would make labels
   touch. Label width is an approximation from character count (`_PERFIL_CHAR_W = 6` px/char, at
   the chart's existing 10 px axis font-size, CSS class `.tick` -- reused for the x-axis labels
   too, rather than adding a second font-size rule) -- generous on purpose, since real glyph
   metrics are not available server-side. Verified on the full seven-offset case (`antes`,
   `noche_1`, `noche_ultima`, `post_1..4`) in both languages: es grows the viewBox to 393 (pitch 52,
   "día antes" against "noche 1"), en to 414 (pitch 55, "day before" against "night 1") --
   `PerfilChartGeometryTest.test_adjacent_x_axis_labels_never_overlap_in_either_language`,
   `.test_each_x_axis_label_x_equals_its_points_cx`,
   `.test_every_circle_and_label_sits_inside_the_viewbox`,
   `.test_y_ticks_are_whole_numbers_include_zero_and_sit_left_of_the_plot`.
5. **Minor, same pass.** The night legend swatch reused `shift.kind.night` ("Noche"/"Night"); the
   mock calls it "night shift". Given its own key, `shifts.perfil.noche`: es «turno de noche» / en
   "night shift". `shifts.kept_note` read "1 days where..." for exactly one kept day -- it now

   two-count shape); `shifts.como_bloques` is on `/shifts/como`, outside this fix's stated scope
   ("/shifts and its confirm step").

**New strings**, es / en:

## BODY-TURNOS-PERFIL-LEGIBLE-1 -- the hero's HRV profile chart, fixed width and a real axis font (2026-11-12)

The orchestrator opened `/shifts` at 375 px on the demo after BODY-TURNOS-PERFIL-DIA-1-M's own
merge (main `9ead43d`, gate green). Everything that round fixed held; one new defect, caused by
that fix: so seven x-axis labels would not overlap, the chart's viewBox width grew with label
length (measured `0 0 414.0 128`), but the `<svg>` is drawn at the card's own width (measured
313 px). Everything inside scaled down by 313/414, so the 10-unit `.tick` text rendered at about
7.6 px -- below the size the app uses for any small text.

**Ruling 1, the fixed width and the font floor.** `_PERFIL_WIDTH` is now a FIXED constant, 313,
read from body.css rather than grown to fit a label: on a 375 px phone, `main`'s own page gutter
(`padding:16px 16px`) and `.card`'s own padding (`padding:12px 14px`) and border
(`border:1px solid`) leave `375 - 2*16 - 2*14 - 2*1 = 313` px of content width, and the `<svg
width="100%">` is drawn at exactly that -- so one viewBox unit is now about one real CSS pixel
there, matching the orchestrator's own measurement. The width never grows with a label's length
again, in either language or offset count
(`PerfilChartGeometryTest.test_viewbox_width_is_the_fixed_constant_for_every_label_set`). The axis
text (CSS class `.tick`) moves from 10px to 12px -- `.fs-12` is the smallest of body.css's general
small-text classes (`.k` is 13px), and 12 is also above the ruling's own 11px floor
(`.test_axis_font_size_meets_the_small_text_floor`). `_PERFIL_CHAR_W`, the character-count
approximation BODY-TURNOS-PERFIL-DIA-1-M used for label-width, is restated against the new font
size (`0.6em` at 12px = 7.2 px/char, was 6.0 px/char at 10px) rather than redefined from scratch.

**Ruling 2, wrap instead of widen.** The point pitch is fixed too, now that the width is; a label
wider than its own slot (the pitch minus `_PERFIL_LABEL_GAP`, the same character-count
approximation) breaks at its one space into two `<tspan>` lines centred on the point
(`_perfil_wrap`): es «día / antes», «noche / 1»; en "day / before", "night / 1". A label that
fits -- "+1".."+4", and any label with no space to break at -- stays one line. The chart's own
height grows by `_PERFIL_WRAP_LINE_HEIGHT` (13 px) only when at least one label actually wrapped;
a short two-offset chart never grows
(`.test_chart_height_grows_by_one_line_only_when_a_label_wraps`). No string changed -- the same
`shifts.perfil.eje.*` values BODY-TURNOS-PERFIL-DIA-1 wrote, now wrapped by markup rather than
widened by layout.
`PerfilChartGeometryTest.test_adjacent_x_axis_labels_never_overlap_in_either_language` is rewritten
for the wrapped markup (the box checked is the wider of a wrapped label's two lines, read from its
`<tspan>`s, never its full unwrapped width) -- the promise itself (no two label boxes overlap) is
unchanged, never loosened; `.test_every_label_lines_anchor_x_equals_its_points_cx` is new, checking
every `<tspan>`'s own `x` equals its `<text>`'s (which already equals its point's `cx`).

**Ruling 3, the two-count sentences say one correctly.** `shifts.confirm_summary`,
`shifts.confirm_summary_patron`, `shifts.confirm_summary_many`,
`shifts.confirm_summary_many_mixed`, `shifts.confirm_all_result` and `shifts.como_bloques` (on
`/shifts/como`) each carried a bare `{days}`/`{nights}`/`{n}`/`{con}`/`{batches}`/`{applied}` of

has the count and passed into the outer sentence key, which now takes the fragments instead of
the raw numbers. The outer key itself never needs its own `_one` variant -- it joins pre-rendered

### -M -- the right edge had no inset (2026-11-12)

Dispatched after the orchestrator looked at `/shifts` on the demo at 375 px (gate `Ran 2944 OK`,
worker report `logs/worker-body-turnos-perfil-legible-1-body-app-20261112T062418.json`); the -1
deviation (width 313 from the arithmetic, not 320) was accepted, and this was the only open
defect: the plot's right side had no inset of its own. The `<svg>` spans x 30.6-344.9 on screen
with `overflow` hidden; the last point was drawn at 340-346 and its "+4" label at 335-350, so both
were cut at the right edge (the label read as "+" and a fragment). The left side already had the
y-tick gutter; the right side had none.

**The inset rule.** Unlike an interior point, the first and last point have no neighbour on their
outer side for the slot/gap rule (ruling 2, above) to keep off the viewBox's own edge, so each now
gets its own margin: half its widest wrapped line (the same `_label_px` character-count
approximation) or the point's own radius (`_PERFIL_POINT_R`, 3.0 -- also now the `<circle>`'s own
`r`, read from one constant instead of a bare `"3"`), whichever is larger, plus `_PERFIL_EDGE_PAD`
(the same small clearance the left gutter already adds). The point pitch (`step`) is computed
twice: once at the old (wider) bounds to size each label's wrap, then again at the new, narrower
`plot_left`/`plot_right` -- re-wrapping against the smaller pitch, since a label can only need
*more* wrapping as the pitch shrinks, never less, so the first pass is always a safe upper bound
for sizing the inset. The left bound is raised past the existing gutter only if the first label's
own half-width needs more room than the gutter already gives it; in every case measured here the
gutter already covered it.

**Resulting pitch**, the seven-offset case (`PerfilChartGeometryTest._perfil()`, es, floats from
the rendered SVG): `cx` = 53.2, 95.0, 136.7, 178.5, 220.3, 262.0, 303.8 -- pitch 41.8, down from
42.97 before this fix. `plot_left` (53.2) is unchanged -- the gutter already covers the first
label's own half-width; `plot_right` moves from 311.0 to 303.8, a new 9.2 px right margin: the
last point's own label, "+4" at 2 characters, `_label_px` 14.4, half 7.2, against the point's own
radius 3.0 (whichever is larger), plus the 2.0 px edge pad already used on the left. New constant
`_PERFIL_POINT_R = 3.0`, the point radius, also now the `<circle>`'s own `r` instead of a bare
`"3"`.

New test `PerfilChartGeometryTest.test_right_inset_keeps_the_last_point_and_label_inside_the_viewbox`:
for es/en and both the 1-night (no `noche_ultima`) and 5-night (`noche_ultima` present) label sets,
every circle's `cx +/- r` and every label LINE's own anchor `x +/- half its approximate width`
(read from its `<tspan>`s when wrapped) lie within `[0, viewBox width]`, and no two label boxes
overlap. Every existing geometry test in this file still passes unchanged.

## BODY-TENDENCIAS-LEYENDA-PATRON-1 -- one plain sentence under every Trends card the shift-cost model has a reference for (2026-11-12)

Mock round 2's `PhoneTrendsLight` board (Carlos's approved mock), deferred by BODY-MOCK-R2-CENSO-1-INV
until BODY-TURNOS-PERFIL-DIA-1 made the day-offset claims truthful (it has, on main since `9ead43d`).

**Ruling 1, one phrase builder, data-driven.** `turnos_costo.frase_patron(perfil, metric) -> dict |
None` turns a successful `perfil_por_dia` result into a sentence SPEC -- a kind plus its own
parameters, never prose -- so the screen and the assistant can share it. `perfil["motivo"]` set ->
`None`. Otherwise, in precedence order: the worst offset's mean inside the band -> `{"kind":
"estable"}`; outside the band with `vuelta` set -> `{"kind": "vuelve", "peor", "vuelta",
"direccion"}`; outside the band with no `vuelta` -> `{"kind": "no_vuelve", "peor", "direccion"}`.
`direccion` ("baja"/"sube") is the side the worst offset's mean sits on relative to centre (0, once
`perfil_por_dia` re-expresses it that way) -- never the metric's own better/worse word, so a
lower-is-better metric whose nights run high still reads "sube". `peor`/`vuelta` are OFFSET NAMES
and `direccion` is a word: no mean, no ms, nothing from the person's own data that a log could read
as a health figure.

Reusing `perfil_por_dia` for all five of `MODELO['metricas']` (sleep_minutes, resting_hr,
hrv_last_night, stress_avg, body_battery_wake) every time Trends renders would cost one `Lector`
(one SELECT per metric) plus `referencia()`'s own exclusion-window `bloques_noche` plus a second
`bloques_noche` for the profile itself -- 7 statements, previously paid only once for `hrv_last_night`
inside `/shifts`' own `resumen()`. Measured against `/trends`' own ceiling (19, headroom only 4 over
the pre-slice baseline of 15), that would have blown it. `turnos_costo.perfiles_patron(conn,
person_id, hoy)` shares one `_LectorVarias` (private, loads every metric in `MODELO['metricas']` with
ONE combined `metric_key IN (...)` SELECT instead of `Lector`'s one-per-metric loop), one
`bloques_noche` and one `referencia()` call across all five -- 3 statements total, regardless of how
many of the five succeed. Measured `/trends` statement count: 15 before this slice, 18 after
(`PerfilesPatronTest.test_one_statement_per_metric_never_happens` pins the 3, plus `db.connect()`'s
own 2 PRAGMAs on a freshly opened connection = 5 traced there). No ceiling in
`tests/test_rendimiento.py` changed.

**Ruling 2, the caption on Trends.** Every Trends card for a metric in `MODELO['metricas']` with a
successful profile shows one sentence in the card's existing `.read` reading style, under the chart
and above the legend: es «Estable alrededor de tus noches.» / en "Steady around your night shifts."
(estable); «Baja/Sube más {peor}; vuelve a tu rango {vuelta}.» / "Lowest/Highest {peor}; back in your
range {vuelta}." (vuelve); «Baja/Sube más {peor}; 4 días después aún no vuelve a tu rango.» /
"Lowest/Highest {peor}; 4 days after, not back in your range yet." (no_vuelve, with the post-offset
count read off `turnos_costo.OFFSETS`, never typed as a literal "4"). `{peor}`/`{vuelta}` are
per-offset time-phrase i18n keys. `body/rutas/tendencias.py`'s `_frase_patron_texto(t, frase)` is the
one place these words are built; it returns `None` for `frase is None` (no profile, or a metric
outside the model), and the template's `{% if c.patron %}` then renders no caption and no empty line.

**Ruling 3, the assistant.** `leer_tendencias` (`body/agente/herramientas.py`) carries
`patron_turnos` -- the same `frase_patron` spec, additive -- for every metric in its result that is
also in `MODELO['metricas']`, sharing one `perfiles_patron` call across however many of them the
request asks for, never a read per metric.

**Ruling 4, the window.** The profile reads over `turnos_costo.RESUMEN_DIAS`, the shift-cost model's
own window, regardless of the range (`r`) Trends shows -- no new note was added, since no existing
card carries one for this reason (the ruling's own fallback).

**New i18n keys**, es / en (16 keys, both languages; placeholders match on both sides):

    trends.patron.estable: "Estable alrededor de tus noches." / "Steady around your night shifts."
    trends.patron.vuelve.baja: "Baja más {peor}; vuelve a tu rango {vuelta}." / "Lowest {peor}; back in your range {vuelta}."
    trends.patron.vuelve.sube: "Sube más {peor}; vuelve a tu rango {vuelta}." / "Highest {peor}; back in your range {vuelta}."
    trends.patron.no_vuelve.baja: "Baja más {peor}; {n} días después aún no vuelve a tu rango." / "Lowest {peor}; {n} days after, not back in your range yet."
    trends.patron.no_vuelve.sube: "Sube más {peor}; {n} días después aún no vuelve a tu rango." / "Highest {peor}; {n} days after, not back in your range yet."
    trends.patron.cuando.antes: "el día antes" / "the day before"
    trends.patron.cuando.noche_1: "la primera noche" / "on the first night"
    trends.patron.cuando.noche_ultima: "la última noche" / "on the last night"
    trends.patron.cuando.post_1..post_4: "el día +1 después".."el día +4 después" / "on day +1 after".."on day +4 after"
    trends.patron.vuelta.post_1..post_4: "el día +1 después".."el día +4 después" / "by day +1 after".."by day +4 after"

**Which metrics carry a caption, and why.** All five of `MODELO['metricas']` have a Trends card
(sleep_minutes, hrv_last_night, resting_hr, body_battery_wake are default cards via `TREND_KEYS`;
stress_avg is an extra card via `TREND_GROUPS`' "stress" group) -- every one of them can carry a
caption once its own profile succeeds. No other metric can: `frase_patron` is only ever called for a
key in `MODELO['metricas']`, so a self-measured, commute or any other catalogue key never carries one,
by construction rather than a per-screen exclusion list. Gated on `turnos_on`
(`db.trabaja_turnos_si`) at the route level too: a person who does not track night shifts gets no
`perfiles_patron` call at all, not just no caption.

**`frase_patron`'s return shape, as built**: `{"kind": "estable"}` |
`{"kind": "vuelve", "peor": <offset>, "vuelta": <offset>, "direccion": "baja"|"sube"}` |
`{"kind": "no_vuelve", "peor": <offset>, "direccion": "baja"|"sube"}` | `None`.

New tests: `tests/test_tendencias_patron.py` (new file, 16 tests -- `FrasePatronTest` on invented

### -M -- two defects from the orchestrator's own review: a vuelta that did not hold, and a second reader (2026-11-12)

Dispatched after the orchestrator looked at `/trends` on the demo at 375 px (gate `Ran 2965 OK,
skipped=1`, worker report `logs/worker-body-tendencias-leyenda-patron-1-body-app-*.json`, newest):
captions rendered under four cards with no horizontal scroll, but sleep's own read -- "Lowest on
day +3 after; back in your range by day +2 after." -- had the return land BEFORE the low point.

**Defect 1, a logic bug in `vuelta` itself.** `perfil_por_dia`'s `vuelta` used to be "the first
post_* offset back inside the band", picked without regard to where the worst offset fell -- a dip
that returns, leaves again and bottoms out later reported the earlier, non-holding return. The
Shifts hero caption (`body/rutas/turnos.py`'s `_perfil_caption`, BODY-TURNOS-PERFIL-DIA-1) reads the
same `vuelta` field and could say the same false thing; fixing the reader fixed both captions with
no change to `turnos.py` itself.

**`vuelta`, as built.** The first post_* offset after the LAST offset anywhere in `OFFSETS` that
lies outside the band in the metric's own worse direction, itself inside the band; `None` when no
offset lies outside the band at all (nothing to return from -- `frase_patron`'s kind stays
`estable`), when no post_* offset is measured after that last excursion, or when what is measured
there is still outside the band. The global extreme (`mas_bajo`/`mas_alto`) is always itself one of
the offsets outside the band whenever any are (it cannot be less extreme than a value already past
the band threshold), so the anchor -- the LAST such offset -- is always at or after it, and `vuelta`,
one step further still, is always strictly later. `frase_patron` asserts exactly that
(`OFFSETS.index(vuelta) > OFFSETS.index(peor_offset)`) at the one place both offsets are read
together, since a spec never says "back by" an offset earlier than or equal to the worst.

**Defect 2, two readers of the same rows.** `turnos_costo.py` carried a private `_LectorVarias`
beside `body/lector.py`'s `Lector`, differing only in spending one combined `metric_key IN (...)`
statement instead of one statement per metric -- added so `/trends`' own statement ceiling would
not have to pay once per metric for `perfiles_patron`. `Lector` itself now loads every metric that
way; `_LectorVarias` is deleted and `perfiles_patron` builds a `Lector` like every other caller.

**Statement counts, this module's own fixture** (`demo._seed(dias=30)` + one assistant
conversation, the same fixture `tests/test_rendimiento.py` already uses): `/trends` unchanged at 18
(it already used the combined reader via `_LectorVarias`); `/shifts` 41 -> 32 (`resumen()`'s own
5-metric `Lector` and `_turnos_strip`'s own 6-metric `Lector`, each now 1 statement instead of 5/6);
`/shifts/como` 19 -> 15 (`resumen()`'s same `Lector`). `tests/test_rendimiento.py`'s `_CEILINGS`
drop from 50/25 to 42/20 (`ceil(measured * 1.3)`, the same ~30% margin rule the table already uses);
no ceiling raised.

New tests: `tests/test_turnos_perfil.py` gained 3 -- the sleep-shaped case (out at post_1, in at
post_2, out and worst at post_3, in at post_4) giving `vuelta` `post_4`, not `post_2`; out at
post_4 alone giving `vuelta` `None` and `frase_patron`'s kind `no_vuelve`; and the Shifts hero
caption (`turnos._perfil_caption`) on the same sleep-shaped data reading "day +4 after" in both

`tests/test_turnos_perfil.py` and `tests/test_tendencias_patron.py` already placed its worst offset

definition -- checked by running them, not assumed. 3 new tests total (2965 -> 2968).

## BODY-COMIDA-COMPARTIDA-1 -- one cooks, several eat, each eater's own log gets their own portion (2026-11-12)

One person logs a meal they cooked for the household; each other eater gets a card in their own
Body and taps Apply or Discard before a single gram reaches their log. Three rulings came with
this spec: (a) **consent** -- a household member opts in once, revocably, before any shared meal
can reach them, the same shape `body/compartir.py`'s `figura_compartida` already uses for sharing a
figure; (b) **editing** -- once applied, each eater's row is their own `comida`/`ingesta`, their own
words, their own correction, their own delete; the shared parent only links; (c) **pantry home** --
a future Duna product ("Hogar") will one day write a cooked meal once per eater through this same
split, so the split had to be a CALLER-AGNOSTIC entry point, not a screen's own code. The cross-
product wire itself is not built here.

**Schema**, additive, three new tables (`body/db.py`): `comida_compartida` (the parent link --
`id`, `hogar_id`, `autor_person_id`, `day`, `ts_local`, `origen`, `origen_ref`, `created_at`, with a
unique index on `(origen, origen_ref)` so a caller's own idempotency key is enough to never double-
write); `comida_compartida_porcion` (one row per eater -- `id`, `comida_compartida_id` (nullable),
`person_id`, `descripcion`, `porcion_texto`, `nutrientes` (JSON, metric_key -> amount), `estado`
(`pendiente`/`aplicada`/`descartada`), `comida_id`, `decided_at`, unique on
`(comida_compartida_id, person_id)`); `consentimiento_comida_compartida` (`body/compartir.py`'s own
second table -- `id`, `person_id`, `hogar_id`, `granted_at`, `withdrawn_at`, unique on
`(person_id, hogar_id)` while active). **Deviation**: the spec's column list said `household_id`;
built as `hogar_id` to match every sibling table's own column name (`figura_compartida.hogar_id`,
`hogar_miembro.hogar_id`) -- the measured convention won over the spec's literal word.
`consentimiento_comida_compartida` is its own table, not a reuse of `figura_compartida`: that
table's `metric_key` is a FK into `metric_def`, and "may a shared meal reach me" is a feature flag,
not a metric.

**The service**, `body/comida_compartida.py`, new, the one module that reads or writes these three
tables: `compartir_comida(conn, autor_person_id, *, day, ts_local=None, descripcion=None,
comensales, origen, origen_ref=None)` writes the parent, the author's own `comida`/`ingesta` (via a
new transaction-less `db._crear_comida_tx`, so the whole write is one atomic transaction) and every
other eater's `pendiente` portion, in one call keyed by `(origen, origen_ref)` for idempotency --
`origen` is the caller's own name ("body" today; "hogar" tomorrow, unbuilt). Refuses
(`ComensalFueraDeHogar`, `ComensalSinConsentimiento`, `ValueError`) before writing anything on an
eater outside the household, one without consent, a repeated person, invalid nutrient amounts, or a
`comensales` list missing the author's own portion -- **deviation**: the spec's "the author appears
at most once" could be read as allowing the author to be left out of the list entirely; built as
REQUIRED instead, since nothing else in the call carries the author's own amounts and ruling (b)
calls the author's own portion applied "at once," unconditionally. `aplicar_porcion`/
`descartar_porcion(conn, person_id, porcion_id)` are owner-only, idempotent, and never delete a row
-- discarding just marks `estado`. `pendientes(conn, person_id)` lists every portion still waiting
for this person, author's name attached. `deshacer_autor` undoes the author's own meal and discards
every still-pending portion, leaving an already-applied portion of another eater's untouched (their
own `comida` row is now theirs, same as ruling (b) says).

**The tool**, `body/agente/herramientas.py`'s `registrar_comida` gains an optional `compartida_con`
(name, nutrientes, optional porcion_texto): every name is resolved to a household member WITH
consent on before any proposal is created (`ToolError`, nothing written, otherwise), and applying
calls `compartir_comida`; undoing calls `deshacer_autor`. `body/agente/propuestas.py` gained a new
pre-apply drift check (`_drift_aplicar_registrar_comida`) specifically for this path, since the
plain TABLA entry used `_sin_drift` -- consent withdrawn or membership lost between propose and
apply now drifts cleanly instead of writing into a household that said no in the meantime.

**The Hoy card**, `body/rutas/hoy.py`: every pending portion addressed to the signed-in person, who
cooked it, their own description and nutrients, with two plain-POST forms (`/comida-compartida/
{porcion_id}/aplicar`, `/comida-compartida/{porcion_id}/descartar`) -- no JS, same shape every other
propose/apply card in this app already uses. `body/rutas/ajustes.py` gained the consent toggle,
OFF by default, beside the existing per-figure sharing card; turning it off also discards this
person's own still-pending portions (`compartir.desactivar_recibir_comidas` +
`comida_compartida.descartar_pendientes_de`).

**i18n**, six new keys, es/en, verbatim from the spec: `agente.error.comensal_no_encontrado`
("No encuentro a {nombre} en tu hogar." / "I can't find {nombre} in your household."),
`agente.error.comida_sin_consentimiento` ("{nombre} no tiene activado recibir comidas compartidas."
/ "{nombre} has not turned on receiving shared meals."), `today.comida_compartida.titulo`
("Comidas compartidas" / "Shared meals"), `today.comida_compartida.aviso` ("{autor} registró una
comida compartida" / "{autor} logged a shared meal"), `settings.comidas_compartidas.pregunta`
("Recibir comidas compartidas de mi hogar" / "Receive shared meals from my household"),
`settings.comidas_compartidas.desc` ("Cuando alguien de tu hogar registra una comida que comieron
juntos, te llega tu porción para que la apliques o la descartes. Nada entra a tu registro sin que
toques Aplicar." / "When someone in your household logs a meal you ate together, your portion
reaches you to apply or discard. Nothing enters your log until you tap Apply."). The Hoy card's two
buttons reuse the existing `asistente.propuesta.aplicar`/`descartar` keys -- no new button text.

**Privacy** (`body/privacidad.py`, ruling 6): export carries this person's own authored parent
links and their own portion rows, never another eater's (`comida_compartida_porcion`'s own
`person_id` already scopes it); delete-all removes this person's own portion rows and, when they
were the cook, their authored parents -- an already-applied OTHER eater's portion keeps its own
`comida`/`ingesta` and only loses the link back to the deleted parent (`comida_compartida_id` set
NULL), never the nutrition itself; a still-pending other eater's portion is discarded outright, same
as withdrawing consent does.

**Demo** (`body/demo.py`, ruling 7): both the demo person's and Ana's consent are turned on, and one
pending shared meal sits in each direction (the demo person cooked one for Ana, Ana cooked one for
the demo person) -- invented demo text only (`_COMIDA_DEMO_PERSON`/`_COMIDA_DEMO_ANA`), no real
figure. `tests/test_demo.py`'s row checksum (`_row_checksum`, the two-runs-identical guard) now also
covers the three new tables; `granted_at` joins its excluded wall-clock columns, the same reasoning
already there for `created_at`/`decided_at`.

**Deviations found running the full suite, outside this slice's own touches, each a census or guard
that failed on the new tables/routes/strings rather than on anything this slice got wrong on its own
terms:**

- `tests/test_persona_fuga.py`'s `_HOUSEHOLD_ONLY_TABLES` gained `consentimiento_comida_compartida`
  and `comida_compartida_porcion` (its own seeding-completeness census, extended, never loosened).
- `body/mudanza.py` (BODY-MUDANZA-HERRAMIENTA-1, the PC-to-host move tool) keeps its own table
  registry, checked by `tests/test_mudanza.py`'s `RegistryTest`. All three new tables joined
  `SKIPPED_TABLES`, never hand-copied on a move -- the same choice already made for
  `figura_compartida` and `hogar_miembro`: a shared-meal link and its consent name another
  household member, who a single-person source install never has a row for, and no nutrition is
  lost by skipping them (an already-applied portion's own `comida`/`ingesta` rows migrate normally
  through the existing `comida` table regardless).
- `tests/test_registro_tu.py`'s register guard flagged `agente.error.comida_sin_consentimiento`'s
  "tiene" as an usted address; allow-listed with its reason ('tiene' subject is the named household
  member, not the reader), the same pattern every other third-person entry there already uses.
- `/settings`' statement ceiling (`tests/test_rendimiento.py`) went from 24 to 25: the new consent
  lookup re-resolved `household.household_of`, which `settings()` already had. `compartir.
  recibe_comidas` now takes that already-resolved household as an optional argument; ceiling left
  at 24, per that file's own rule ("the fix ... was to batch ... not to widen the ceiling").
- `tests/test_web_entry.py`'s frozen route-set snapshot gained the three new routes, each tagged
  with this slice's id, the same way every earlier slice's own addition is tagged there.

No password, token, session secret, device key or health figure of a real person was read, printed,
or written anywhere in this slice's own work; every number in the demo and in every test is
invented.

**Gate**, on this branch's final tree (`git status --porcelain` clean before this entry), the exact

## BODY-COMIDA-CORREGIR-1 -- correct a whole meal as one proposal, one apply (2026-11-12)

The Personal desk's friction report: correcting one logged meal's time and half of one food took 6
`borrar_ingesta` (one per nutrient row) + 1 `registrar_comida` = 7 applies, hitting body.mcp's
per-15-minute apply cap. The orchestrator's ruling, ahead of this slice: one correction the person
means as one change is ONE proposal, and the cap (`body/mcp.py` LIMITES, untouched) is not loosened
-- a meal's rows are not specially counted.

**Ruling 1 -- one writer for a meal as a unit.** `db.py` gains `corregir_comida(conn, person_id,
comida_id, *, ts_local=None, day=None, descripcion=None, cantidades=None)`: owner-scoped (refuses a
comida_id that is not this person's own, `ValueError`), unconditionally sets the `comida` row's
day/ts_local/descripcion to whatever is passed, and when `cantidades` is given REPLACES the meal's
whole set of `ingesta` children wholesale -- never merged with what was there, the same all-or-
nothing shape `crear_comida` itself writes with. Left out, the existing rows just follow the meal's
own new day/ts_local (needed so `comidas_del_dia`'s own day filter, which reads each `ingesta` row's
OWN `day` column, keeps finding the meal under its new day). One transaction; every touched
metric_key's daily total is re-derived for both the old day and the new one when the day moves.
Unlike `actualizar_periodo`'s `_SIN_DAR` sentinel, plain `None` defaults are enough here: the one
caller (`body/agente/propuestas.py`) always carries the meal's FULL resolved state in `antes`/
`despues`, so there is no "clear this field" case distinct from "not given" to support.

**Ruling 2 -- one proposal.** The assistant tool `corregir_comida` (`body/agente/herramientas.py`)
takes `comida_id` and any of `hora`/`day`/`descripcion`/`cantidades`; a field left out keeps its
current value (the same convention `corregir_periodo` already uses), refusing when none is given.
`cantidades`, when given, is door-validated exactly like `registrar_comida`'s own (one amount per
metric key, `_numero_cantidad_comida`, no partial result on a bad one) and REPLACES the whole set.
`antes`/`despues` each carry the meal's full state (day, ts_local, descripcion, every amount), so
`propuestas.deshacer` restores it exactly through the same writer. Apply/undo/drift
(`_aplicar_corregir_comida`, `_deshacer_corregir_comida`, `_drift_aplicar_corregir_comida`,
`_drift_deshacer_corregir_comida`) compare the meal's day/ts_local/descripcion and its ingesta
amounts against the recorded state; a changed or deleted meal since the proposal refuses apply/undo
as `propuesta_desactualizada`, the same as every other drift-checked proposal. Not added to
`ACCIONES_REEMPLAZABLES`: two corrections of two different meals on the same day are both real,
never a same-day replacement. The catalogue description says this is the way to change a meal's
time, wording or amounts, and that per-row `corregir_ingesta`/`borrar_ingesta` stay for a single
standalone intake row that is not part of a meal.

The card (`body/rutas/asistente.py`) is one summary line naming the meal by its OLD time (its prior
ts_local's HH:MM, or its short date when it had none) and listing only what differs -- new time, new
description, each amount changed/added/removed, one i18n key per kind, in catalogue order
(`herramientas.INGESTA_METRIC_KEYS`): es «Corregir la comida de las {hora_antes}: {cambios}», en
"Correct the {hora_antes} meal: {cambios}". New i18n keys, es/en:
`asistente.propuesta.corregir_comida_resumen` ("Corregir la comida de las {hora_antes}: {cambios}" /
"Correct the {hora_antes} meal: {cambios}"), `asistente.propuesta.comida_cambio_hora` ("nueva hora
{hora}" / "new time {hora}"), `asistente.propuesta.comida_cambio_descripcion` ("nueva descripción
«{descripcion}»" / new description, curly-quoted, in en.json), `asistente.propuesta.comida_cambio_
cantidad_nueva` ("+ {metric}: {valor}" / "+ {metric}: {valor}"), `asistente.propuesta.comida_cambio_
cantidad_quitada` ("- {metric}" / "- {metric}"), `asistente.propuesta.comida_cambio_cantidad_valor`

## BODY-ENTRENO-ULTIMA-VEZ-1

Open follow-up from `BODY-MOCK-R2-CENSO-1-INV`: no reader answered "the previous session's same
exercise's reps/weight", needed before the Session screen's "last time -> today" comparisons
(`BODY-METAS-SESION-PANTALLA-1`). This slice adds the one reader module and wires its answer,
additively, into the assistant's existing `leer_entreno` tool. No schema change -- `body/db.py` was
not touched; the new module reads `workout_set`/`activity` with plain SELECTs plus `db.exercise_sets`
for display values, never a second copy of the correction/kg-conversion logic.

**Ruling 1, the exercise identity.** The effective exercise of a set is `person_exercise` when the
person corrected the slot, else `garmin_exercise` -- exactly the `exercise` field `db.exercise_sets`
(`db.py:2210`) already computes, so `body/entreno_historial.py` reads that field rather than
re-deriving the corrected-or-watch rule a second time; `_cuenta(s)` (`entreno_historial.py`) is the
one place "only 'active', non-excluded sets count" is checked. Matching is on the stored string,
case and watch's own code untouched, never translated.

**Ruling 2, `body/entreno_historial.py` (new, reads only).**

    ultima_vez(conn, person_id, ejercicio, *, antes_de=None) -> dict | None
    ultimas_veces(conn, person_id, source, source_id) -> dict[str, dict | None]

`ultima_vez` finds the most recent session, by `COALESCE(activity.start_local, activity.day)`,
strictly before `antes_de` (a local ISO datetime or date string) when given, with at least one
counting set whose effective exercise equals `ejercicio` -- found with one SQL query whose own
`CASE WHEN corrected_by_person THEN person_exercise ELSE garmin_exercise END` mirrors
`db.exercise_sets`'s rule, so the search and the display value can never disagree; then one
`db.exercise_sets` call on the session it finds. Two statements. Returns
`{source, source_id, day, sets: [{reps, weight_kg, corrected}, ...], mejor}` in set order, or `None`
when the exercise was never done. `mejor` is the heaviest set, ties broken by more reps; a
bodyweight exercise (every `weight_kg` is `None`) falls through to the same sort key (`(weight_kg is
not None, weight_kg or 0, reps or 0)`), which compares by reps alone once every candidate's first key
component ties at `False` -- no separate bodyweight branch.

`ultimas_veces` answers it for every exercise one session has, bounded independent of the number of
exercises: one statement for that session's own sets (`db.exercise_sets`), one for its own
`day`/`start_local`, one for the candidate earlier sessions (each already known, by the join, to hold
at least one counting set, ordered newest-first) -- then `db.exercise_sets` only for the earlier
sessions actually opened, stopping the moment every exercise is resolved. **Measured**: 5 exercises
in the current session, all answered by one earlier session that has all 5 -> **4 statements**,
regardless of whether the current session names 2, 3 or 5 of them
(`tests/test_entreno_historial.py::UltimasVecesTest::test_statement_count_does_not_grow_with_the_
number_of_exercises`, a connection-wrapping counter asserting the count is identical across 2/3/5).

Person-scoped throughout by the SQL `WHERE`/`JOIN` on `person_id` -- another person's sets, even for
the same exercise name, are never candidates.

**Ruling 3, the assistant.** `_leer_entreno` (`body/agente/herramientas.py`) now adds one additive
key per session it returns: `"ultima_vez": entreno_historial.ultimas_veces(conn, person_id,
a["sets_source"], a["sets_source_id"])` -- the same `sets_source`/`sets_source_id` pair the session's
own `series` already reads through, so a linked watch/manual pair's "last time" reads the person's
own sets too, never the watch's unlisted slots. Nothing else in `leer_entreno`'s output changed:
`tests/test_agente_entreno.py::LeerEntrenoUltimaVezTest::test_nothing_else_in_the_output_changes`
pins the session dict's full key set to `{dia, titulo, fuente, hora_inicio, series, ultima_vez}`. No
new tool, no screen (the Session screen is `BODY-METAS-SESION-PANTALLA-1`, separate).

No census test outside `touches` pinning `leer_entreno`'s own output key list was found to extend;
the key-set assertion above is new, inside `touches`.

No password, token, session secret or health figure of a real person was read, printed or written
anywhere in this slice; every fixture in both new/changed test modules is invented demo data.

the harness moved it to the background past its own 600 s cap, and this session blocked on the
output file until its `Ran ` line appeared rather than polling turn-by-turn:

    OK (skipped=1)

3074 - 3060 (`BODY-I18N-TITULO-PROPUESTA-CENSO-1`'s own count, entry above) = 14 new tests: 11 in
`tests/test_entreno_historial.py` (new module) and 3 in `tests/test_agente_entreno.py`'s new
`LeerEntrenoUltimaVezTest`.
