## BODY-ENTRENO-RACHA-SEMANAL-1

Open follow-up from `BODY-MOCK-R2-CENSO-1-INV`: a pure read of the weekly strength-session count
across the whole watch history against the plan's floor, tagged by night-shift week -- what feeds
`BODY-TENDENCIAS-RACHA-GRAFICO-1`'s Trends chart (mock round 2's "Since June 2024 -- closing the
gap" study). New module only, nothing calls it yet; no schema change (`body/db.py` untouched).

**Ruling 1, what counts as a strength session.** An `activity` row of the person whose own `type`
is in a module constant `TIPOS_FUERZA` (`{'strength_training'}` to start), OR one that has at least
one active, non-excluded `workout_set` row -- checked on EITHER half of a linked watch/manual pair
(`activity.vinculo_manual`), since the pair is one session and either half may carry the type or the
sets. A linked pair counts once, keyed to the watch row's own day. Week = the ISO week starting
Monday (`fechas.lunes_de` of the session's day).

**Ruling 2, the floor is data.** `racha_semanal`'s `piso: int | None` is never defaulted to 3 or any
other number inside this module. With `piso=None` the reader still returns every week's own session
count and night flag, just no run analysis. Which plan or habit should supply the floor is left to
`BODY-TENDENCIAS-RACHA-GRAFICO-1` to decide -- the `habit` table (`goal_id, title, cadence, assignee_
person_id, active`) has no link to an activity type, so this slice does not guess one (open
follow-up below).

**Ruling 3, `body/entreno_racha.py` (new, reads only).**

    racha_semanal(conn, person_id, *, piso=None, hoy=None) -> dict | None

`None` when the person has no strength session at all (including no activity at all). Otherwise:

- `semanas`: every week from the Monday of the person's FIRST activity of any kind (the start of
  the watch history, not the first strength session) to the Monday of `hoy`, in order, each
  `{lunes, sesiones, noche, alcanza}` -- `noche` true when the week contains at least one night
  from `turnos_costo.bloques_noche`; `alcanza` is `sesiones >= piso`, or `None` when `piso` is
  `None`. Weeks with zero sessions are present with `sesiones: 0` -- an honest gap, never a missing
  week.
- `desde`: the first Monday (ISO). `dias_historia`: days from the first activity's own day to `hoy`.
- With `piso` given, four more keys: `rachas`, every maximal run of consecutive weeks with `alcanza`
  true, each `{inicio, fin, semanas, termina_en_noche}` (`termina_en_noche` is the FIRST week after
  the run's own end being a night week; always `False` for a run with no week after it, i.e. the
  current run); `mas_larga`, the longest run (ties broken toward the more recent one, by scanning
  `rachas` in reverse and taking the first match); `actual`, the run that includes the current week
  OR the week right before it -- so a current week still in progress, with too few sessions so far
  to show `alcanza`, never breaks a run that was still intact through last week; `None` when neither
  the current nor the previous week belongs to any run. `terminadas_en_noche`: `{n, de}` over every
  run that is NOT `actual` (identity check, since a run dict is never duplicated) -- a run still in
  progress has no "week after" yet and is never counted toward this.

**Statement count.** Four statements total, independent of the number of weeks: one `MIN(day)` over
`activity`, one flat `SELECT` of every `activity` row, one `SELECT DISTINCT` of counting
`workout_set` identities, and `bloques_noche`'s own one query. Pinned by
`tests/test_entreno_racha.py::RachaSemanalTest::test_statement_count_is_bounded_independent_of_
history_length` (a connection-wrapping counter, identical count across 2/6/12 weeks of history).

Person-scoped throughout by `WHERE person_id = ?` on every statement -- another person's activities
are never candidates (`test_another_persons_activities_are_invisible`).

21 new tests in `tests/test_entreno_racha.py`, covering: type-based and set-based sessions; rest and
excluded sets never making a session; a linked watch/manual pair counted once; weeks starting at the
first activity of any kind, not the first strength session; zero-session weeks present; `dias_
historia`; the `noche` flag with and without a night block; `piso=None` carrying no `rachas`/`mas_
larga`/`actual`/`terminadas_en_noche` keys at all; `alcanza` against the floor; the longest run with
its tie-break to the more recent one; the current run tolerating an in-progress current week;
`actual` being `None` when neither the current nor the previous week reaches; `termina_en_noche` and
the `{n, de}` count, excluding the run still in progress; another person's activities invisible;
`None` with no strength session and with no activity at all; the bounded statement count.

No password, token, session secret or health figure of a real person was read, printed or written
anywhere in this slice; every fixture in the new test module is invented demo data (dates in
2026-10/11, 3-4 sets per session, invented night shifts).

**Gate**, on this branch's final tree (`git status --porcelain` clean before this entry), the exact
command is `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`, run ONCE in the foreground;
the harness moved it to the background past its own 600 s cap, and this session blocked on the
output file until its `Ran ` line appeared rather than polling turn-by-turn:

    Ran 3095 tests in 762.012s

    OK (skipped=1)

3095 - 3074 (`BODY-ENTRENO-ULTIMA-VEZ-1`'s own count, entry above) = 21 new tests, all in
`tests/test_entreno_racha.py`.

## BODY-TENDENCIAS-RACHA-GRAFICO-1 -- the strength-session study card on /trends, built in three
slices (this entry, never written by the first two, covers all of it)

**Ruling 1 -- `racha_piso`, the person's own floor pick** (`0242bb6`). An additive table, `person_id
INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES person(id)`, `habit_id INTEGER REFERENCES habit(id)` (nullable), `
updated_at TEXT NOT NULL`, with `db.set_racha_piso`/`db.racha_piso_habit_id`. `habit_id = NULL`
records an explicit "no floor" pick, never the absence of a row. The floor names one of the
person's own habits rather than a fixed habit-type taxonomy, the same shape `BODY-ENTRENO-HABITO-
AUTO-1`'s `marcar_habito` already settled for matching an activity to a habit -- that tool "never
carries a hardcoded activity-type list", letting the model decide which activity fulfils which of
the person's active habits instead of enumerating types in code; `racha_piso` follows the same
rule, so any weekly, active habit the person creates is automatically comparable with no code
change. Exported under "vida" and deleted by `privacidad.export_person`/`delete_person`: a
household member's own `racha_piso` naming one of THIS person's habits is nulled (not failed)
before that person's habits go, and the person's own row is deleted outright. `mudanza.py`'s
`SKIPPED_TABLES` and `tests/test_persona_fuga.py`'s `_seed_person` gained the narrow, explicit
census exception every new person-scoped table needs.

**Rulings 2-3 -- the card, its chart and the picker** (`ea3235d`). A card on `/trends`, built from
`entreno_racha.racha_semanal`: a bar chart of weekly strength-session counts against the chosen
floor (green bars at or above it, blue ticks under night-shift weeks, a dashed floor line), up to
three figures -- longest run, night-ending-run ratio, current run, each *absent* rather than zero
when there is none -- and a plain POST form picker, `/trends/racha-piso`, of the person's own
active weekly habits plus "No floor". The picker 404s an inactive, non-weekly, unread or another
person's habit, and keeps the range query on redirect. The card appears only when `racha_semanal`
returns a result. No inline `<script>`, `style` attribute or `<style>` tag -- bar geometry is plain
SVG attributes throughout, unchanged by every later slice.

**Ruling 4 -- the demo person's own pick** (`0936dbc`). A new "Entrenar fuerza"/"Strength
training" habit under the resting-heart-rate goal (weekly, 3x), set as the demo person's own
`racha_piso`, with three clean weeks of three invented strength sessions each, ending two weeks
before the current one -- a real longest run, with no still-open current run. `test_demo.py`'s
habit count moved from 3 to 4 and its determinism checksum now covers `racha_piso`.

**Strings, es/en, exact key and placeholder parity** (as they stand after `-M2`'s one wording
fix below): `trends.racha.titulo` ("Desde {mes} · cerrando la brecha" / "Since {mes} · closing the
gap"), `.sub` ("{dias} días de todo el historial de tu reloj..." / "{dias} days from your watch's
full history..."), `.piso_nota` ("Verde cuando llegó a {piso}..." / "Green when it reached

## BODY-AGENTE-LEER-SERIE-1 -- leer_serie, one bounded range read of day-by-day figures

Report from the Personal desk, 2026-11-12: a desk helper building the person's body history across
the whole watch history called body.mcp's `leer_dia` once per day from a script, hit the
5-reads-per-15-minutes cap (`body/mcp.py`'s `LIMITES["lecturas"] = bucle.MAX_LECTURAS`) and logged
~870 refused calls, then fell back to reading the database file directly. The cap stays; this
slice adds the tool that should have existed instead: `leer_serie`, a new `tipo: lectura` entry in
`body/agente/herramientas.py`'s `HERRAMIENTAS`.

**Rulings, as built.**

1. Input `{metricas: [metric_key, ...] (1..12, each a key `catalogo_tendencias.TODAS` already
   lists for leer_tendencias), desde: YYYY-MM-DD, hasta: YYYY-MM-DD, paso: 'dia'|'semana'|'mes'}`.
   Output `{paso, desde, hasta, metricas: {key: {unidad, puntos: [{fecha, valor, n_dias}]}}}`.
   `fecha` is the day itself at paso 'dia', the week's Monday (`fechas.lunes_de`) at 'semana', the
   month's first day at 'mes'. A period with no data is ABSENT from `puntos` (never 0); a metric
   with no data at all in the range is present with an empty list. 'semana'/'mes' average with
   `statistics.fmean` -- the exact function `body/profile.py`'s own `_build_profile` uses for
   Trends' monthly line -- grouped the same way, never a second averaging rule; `n_dias` carries
   the point's own count.
2. Bounds: paso 'dia' <= 366 days, 'semana' <= 260 weeks (`(lunes_de(hasta) - lunes_de(desde)).days
   // 7 + 1`), 'mes' unbounded. Crossing one, `desde` after `hasta`, `hasta` after the person's
   local today (`fechas.hoy_local`), or an unknown metric key, all refuse with a `ToolError` before
   any SQL runs (proven in tests by a `set_trace_callback` count of 0). The one query over
   `daily_metric` is ONE statement regardless of range length or metric count: `SELECT metric_key,
   day, value ... WHERE person_id = ? AND metric_key IN (...) AND day BETWEEN ? AND ?`.
3. Data level follows leer_tendencias' own: the registry entry's `nivel` is `"resumen"` (so
   `disponibles()` offers it at resumen/completo, hides it at ninguno, exactly where
   `ajustes.py`'s own docstring says "resumen = only aggregates ... never one day's value" already
   draws the line) -- and `paso='dia'` is refused ADDITIONALLY inside `_leer_serie` itself when
   `nivel == 'resumen'`, since that paso IS one day's value. `ejecutar()` gained one small, generic
   hook for this: a registry entry may carry `"necesita_nivel": True`, and only then does
   `ejecutar()` pass `nivel` as `_leer_serie`'s third positional argument -- every other tool's own
   call shape (`funcion(conn, person_id, **params)`) is unchanged.
4. Through `body.mcp` it is listed and callable with NO new code in `body/mcp.py`: `tools/list`
   reads `bucle._tool_specs(nivel)` -> `herramientas.disponibles(nivel)` generically, and
   `tools/call`'s `_llamar_herramienta` already counts any `tipo == "lectura"` call once against
   `sesion.tope_lecturas` regardless of which tool or how big its result is. Proven directly: one
   `leer_serie` call over a 28-day range, through `body.mcp`, costs exactly one of the 5-read
   window (`tests/test_mcp.py::ToolsCallTest::test_one_leer_serie_call_counts_as_one_lectura_not_
   one_per_day`), and the same through the in-app loop
   (`tests/test_agente_bucle.py::LecturasCapTest::test_one_leer_serie_call_over_many_days_still_
   counts_as_one_lectura`). `body/agente/bucle.py` needed no change at all -- left untouched, as
   the spec allowed.

`tests/test_agente_registro.py`'s two census tests that pin the registry's exact shape were
extended to the new truth, never loosened: the lectura count 13 -> 14 (renamed
`test_fourteen_lectura_tools_with_expected_levels`, `leer_serie: "resumen"` added to
`expected_levels`), and `HERRAMIENTAS`'s own length 37 -> 38. `_all_tool_calls()` gained a
`leer_serie` case so the existing no-writer static guard, the "running every lectura tool changes
nothing" behavioural guard, and the "every lectura tool's output survives json.dumps" test all
cover it automatically, with no new test logic of their own.

`tests/test_agente_leer_serie.py` (new, 20 tests): day/week/month shapes; a gap absent, never 0; an
empty-data metric present with `[]`; the 'mes' figure checked equal, value and `n_dias` both, to
`profile.metric_profile(...).months` for the same key and month; the 'dia'/'semana' bounds refused
with a traced statement count of 0; a future `hasta` refused; an unknown metric refused; 'dia'
refused at nivel 'resumen' while 'semana'/'mes' are allowed there; the tool absent from
`disponibles('ninguno')` and refused by `ejecutar()` there; another person's `daily_metric` rows
(person_id=2) never appearing in person 1's own result; and the statement count held at exactly 1
across a 10-day vs. a 366-day range, and across 1 vs. 3 metrics.

## BODY-TENDENCIAS-KPI-MINI-1 -- a compact KPI strip above /trends' cards

Mock round 2, approved by the person as drawn (research/mock-r2/TEXTOS.md's "## PhoneTrendsLight.dc.html"):
four tiles "Heart-rate variability 58 ms · in your range", "Resting pulse 53 bpm · in your range",
"Sleep 7 h 05 · in your range", "Stress 24 · in your range", then "Strength this week 2 of 4 · on
track" -- a strip above Trends' full cards, reusing data the route already computed.

**Rulings, as built.**

1. The strip sits at the top of /trends' content, right above the metric cards (after the range
   picker and the body-silhouette graphic). One row of `.grid2` tiles (two columns at 375 px),
   each an `<a class="card" href="#<key>">` linking to its card's own anchor -- every card already
   carries `id="{{ c.key }}"` (`render_card`'s own macro); only the strength study card needed a
   new `id="racha"`, added to `trends.html`. Tiles, in this fixed order, each only when its
   metric's card exists on the page (built once into `card_by_key`, read by both the primary-9 and
   the "Ver todas las medidas" loop, so no card is computed twice): `hrv_last_night`, `resting_hr`,
   `sleep_minutes`, `stress_avg` (the last lives only behind "Ver todas las medidas", in the
   `stress` group -- still rendered into the DOM even collapsed, so its tile and its card always
   agree). Each tile shows the metric's own short label (new keys, since the mock wants the full
   word, not the week table's abbreviation already in `trends.short.*`), the SAME figure and unit
   its card shows (`card["last30"]`/`card["unit"]`, never recomputed), and a status word against
   the card's own band (`p.low`/`p.high`, the same quantiles `_trend_card` already read for the
   normal-range legend) -- `_kpi_banda(fig, low, high)` returns `"abajo"`/`"arriba"`/`"dentro"`/
   `None` (no figure in the picked range). `_kpi_estado` turns that into text: "dentro" may use the
   app's own positive token (`good`, i.e. `var(--ok)`); "arriba"/"abajo" stay neutral text
   (`flat`, `var(--muted)`) -- never an alarm colour. A card with no band (`pocas`) gets no status
   word; none of the four KPI keys is ever self-measured, so this branch is defensive rather than
   reachable today.
2. The strength tile (fifth), built from the already-loaded `racha_semanal` result and the
   person's own floor (`_racha_ctx` now also returns `piso` and `semana_actual_sesiones` --
   `semanas[-1]`, the week containing `hoy`, already computed) -- absent with no floor. `_fuerza_mini`:
   `n >= piso` -> "cumplida"/"reached" (`good`); else if the days left in the week, today included
   (`8 - hoy.isoweekday()`, so Monday=7 down to Sunday=1) `>= piso - n` -> "vas bien"/"on track"
   (`good`, still achievable this week); else "faltan {k}"/"{k} to go" (`flat`), singular-aware
   ("falta 1" vs "faltan {k}", `_kpi_fuerza_faltan_txt`). The figure is "{n} de {piso}"/"{n} of
   {piso}". Because today always counts as at least one day left, a deficit of exactly 1 always
   resolves to "vas bien" through the real weekday clock -- the singular "falta 1"/"1 to go" wording
   is proven directly against `_kpi_fuerza_faltan_txt(t, 1)` rather than coaxed out of a live
   Monday-to-Sunday walk.
3. The assistant is unchanged: `leer_tendencias` already carries the same figures and bands this
   strip only re-displays; no tool touched.

**Every new string, es / en** (`body/i18n/es.json` / `en.json`):

    trends.kpi.hrv_last_night      "Variabilidad"                    "Heart-rate variability"
    trends.kpi.resting_hr          "Pulso en reposo"                 "Resting pulse"
    trends.kpi.sleep_minutes       "Sueño"                           "Sleep"
    trends.kpi.stress_avg          "Estrés"                          "Stress"
    trends.kpi.estado.dentro       "en tu rango"                     "in your range"
    trends.kpi.estado.arriba       "por encima de tu rango"          "above your range"
    trends.kpi.estado.abajo        "por debajo de tu rango"          "below your range"
    trends.kpi.fuerza.titulo       "Fuerza esta semana"              "Strength this week"
    trends.kpi.fuerza.figura       "{n} de {piso}"                   "{n} of {piso}"
    trends.kpi.fuerza.cumplida     "cumplida"                        "reached"
    trends.kpi.fuerza.vas_bien     "vas bien"                        "on track"
    trends.kpi.fuerza.faltan_one   "falta 1"                         "1 to go"
    trends.kpi.fuerza.faltan_other "faltan {k}"                      "{k} to go"

**ZERO new SQL statements**, as the spec required: `card_by_key`, the band/status computation and

## BODY-METAS-HABITO-SEMANA-TIRA-1 -- the M T W T F S S week strip under each weekly habit

Mock round 2, approved by the person as drawn (dev-protocol/research/mock-r2/TEXTOS.md's
"## PhonePlanLight.dc.html"): under "Strength · 4 a week / on track / 2 of 4 done", a row of seven
day letters "M T W T F S S". Open follow-up from BODY-MOCK-R2-CENSO-1-INV, no new data (habit_check
is per-day already) -- the shift-aware "moved to Saturday" annotation explicitly waits.

**Rulings, as built.**

1. For each of the person's own WEEKLY habits on goal detail (cadence per 'week'; day/month-cadence
   habits and another member's habit are untouched), a row of seven day cells, Monday first. The
   visible letter reuses the app's own `t('date.days')` initials (`name[:1].upper()`) rather than a
   second, hand-typed list: en "M T W T F S S" exactly; es "L M M J V S D" (martes and miércoles
   both start with 'm' -- the spec's own example, "L M X J V S D", was a hedge ("or whatever that
   formatter yields"), not a second list to hand-type). State: `hecho` (a habit_check done=1 that
   day -- wins over every other condition, even on today or a near-future tolerance day), `hoy`
   (today, not done), `futuro` (after today), `pasado` (before today, not done -- plain, the base
   `.habit-week-cell` style, never a `.pasado` rule of its own since it is identical to the
   default). Each cell's accessible text is `t("goals.week_strip.cell_aria", day=<full day name>,
   state=<state word>)` -- "lunes: sin marcar" / "Monday: not checked", "martes: hecho" /
   "Tuesday: done", "miércoles: hoy" / "Wednesday: today", "jueves: por venir" /
   "Thursday: coming up" -- never just the letter.
2. `metas._week_checks(conn, habit_ids, person_id, monday, sunday)`: one SELECT
   (`habit_id IN (...)`) over `habit_check` for every weekly own habit of the goal, built once
   before the habit loop and reused inside it for both the week strip and `checked_today` --

## BODY-PLAN-ESQUEMA-1 -- the plan's schema: four horizon tables, two additive columns, mudanza's self-ref pass (2026-11-12)

Ruling (ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1, taking BODY-PLAN-PERSONAL-1-INV's recommendation): the
plan's HORIZON is a milestone `goal` -- its deadline is the end date, its sharing is the
household's, its detail screen is goal detail -- never a second, parallel container that would
need its own sharing, deadline and screen. A person's plan is that person's own data and MOVES
WITH THEM: the four horizon tables join `body/mudanza.py`'s REGISTRY with real id remapping;
listing them in SKIPPED_TABLES ("nothing reads them yet") was rejected as a half-built shape that
would silently lose a plan the day the plan screens ship.

**Rulings, as built (both runs).**

1. **Schema** (`body/db.py`): `goal.horizonte_goal_id` and `experimento.goal_id` (additive,
   nullable, placed last in their column list so a fresh install's `PRAGMA table_info` order
   matches `_migrate()`'s `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` on an existing database) point a goal or
   experiment at the horizon goal. `horizonte_regla`, `horizonte_semana`, `horizonte_meta_semanal`
   and `horizonte_checkpoint` are the plan's own parts, each a child row under
   `horizonte_goal_id`. `horizonte_meta_semanal` is append-only (`vigente`/`reemplaza_id`), with a
   partial UNIQUE index refusing two vigente rows for one `(horizonte_goal_id, week_start,
   medida)`; `db.corregir_meta_semanal` is its one correction path -- never an UPDATE of `valor`.
   `db.validar_regla_horizonte` checks `contexto_valor` against `SHIFT_KINDS` or the `period_kind`
   table, since a CHECK cannot express either. Both the new columns and the new tables are created
   the guarded way: SCHEMA (idempotent `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`) covers every fresh install,
   `_migrate()` ALTERs the two existing tables for a database built before this slice. Plain
   writers only (`crear_regla_horizonte`, `crear_semana_horizonte`, `crear_meta_semanal`,
   `corregir_meta_semanal`, `crear_checkpoint_horizonte`) -- no route reads or writes them yet; the
   plan module, proposals, screen and Hoy hook are later slices.
2. **Privacy** (`body/privacidad.py`): all four horizon tables are in `FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES`.
   `export_person`'s own horizonte block reads this person's own rows, scoped by their own
   `person_id` column (a household member's own rows on a shared horizon goal stay theirs to
   export from their own account). `delete_person` removes them before the goal they reference,
   the same FK-order delete already follows for habit/habit_check/goal_check/plan, and clears the
   two new cross-goal references (`experimento.goal_id`, `goal.horizonte_goal_id`) before the
   referenced goal goes -- the only other place in the repository that deletes a goal.
3. **mudanza's self-ref pass** (`body/mudanza.py`): `TableSpec` gained `self_ref_cols` -- columns
   naming an id of the SAME table (`goal.horizonte_goal_id`, `horizonte_meta_semanal.reemplaza_id`).
   Such a column is excluded from the full-content match and from `_needs_update`'s comparison,
   inserted NULL, then resolved in a second pass, same transaction, from the table's own id map
   once every row of that table is migrated. A self-ref naming a row that was never migrated
   (another person's, or absent) stays NULL and is counted (`TableCounts.self_ref_unresolved`),
   printed in the dry-run/apply report, never silently. `goal` carries `self_ref_cols=
   ("horizonte_goal_id",)`; `experimento.fk_remap` adds `goal_id -> goal`; the four horizon tables
   each `fk_remap` `horizonte_goal_id -> goal` (so a horizon goal filtered out as another
   household member's leaves its children "missing", counted as `other_person`, same as any other
   `fk_remap`); `horizonte_semana` is matched on its own UNIQUE key `(horizonte_goal_id,
   week_start)`, remapped; `horizonte_meta_semanal` carries `self_ref_cols=("reemplaza_id",)` for
   its append-only correction chain. `_source_rows` now orders by id ascending when the table has
   an id column, so the second pass is exercised independent of source id order rather than
   relying on it.
4. **The census fixes** (outside the schema's own `touches`, widened into this slice -- see the
   `-R` paragraph below): `tests/test_experimentos_esquema.py`'s hardcoded `experimento` column set
   gained `goal_id`; `tests/test_mudanza.py`'s registry census tests needed no edit to their
   assertions once the four tables were registered, and gained `SelfRefRoundTripTest` /
   `SelfRefUnresolvedTest`, invented data, proving the round trip and the unresolved-count path;
   `tests/test_persona_fuga.py`'s `_seed_person` now plants one row in each horizon table, tagged,
   under `gid_proposed` (a milestone goal already in the fixture) as the horizon, satisfying the
   seeded-or-explained census -- their markers stay OUT of `_markers_of`'s active list, like
   `moment`'s own text, since no route, API or assistant tool reads `horizonte_*` yet. Not added to
   `_HOUSEHOLD_ONLY_TABLES`: they are personal rows.

No password, token, session secret or health figure of a real person was read, printed or written
anywhere in either run; every test fixture is invented demo data.

## BODY-PLAN-MODULO-1 -- the plan's own plan-vs-real module (2026-11-13)

Built on BODY-PLAN-ESQUEMA-1-R's schema and BODY-PLAN-PERSONAL-1's idea ("Carlos's own plan in
Body as plan vs real, just as we are doing with the money plan in Finanzas"). Three rulings,
read from the branch's own code and commits:

1. **The reachability rule and the strength classifier, shared out, not duplicated.**
   `goals.estado_cuota` is now THE "can this weekly count still be met" rule, taken out of
   `rutas/tendencias.py`'s `_fuerza_mini`, which calls it instead of carrying its own copy --
   same rendered tiles, `tests/test_tendencias_kpi.py` unedited and green.
   `entreno_racha.sesiones_fuerza` exposes the per-session strength classification (`_es_fuerza`
   plus the watch/manual pairing) as a public, range-filterable function that `body/horizonte.py`
   calls -- `racha_semanal` itself unchanged in output.
2. **`body/horizonte.py`, pure reads over a connection, never stores, never renders.** `semana`
   and `plan_vs_real` fetch every data source they need ONCE per call (daily_metric,
   sleep_session, the strength and cardio classifiers, the horizon's own rule/target/plan rows,
   shifts, periods and night blocks) and group it in Python per week, so the statement count
   stays BOUNDED -- independent of how many weeks, target lines, rules or checkpoints a horizon
   carries (proven flat at 10 statements across 1 vs 12 weeks and 1 vs 8 lines).
   `MEDIDAS` (the weekly-target vocabulary): `sueno_minutos`, `hora_acostarse`,
   `hora_levantarse`, `sesiones_fuerza`, `sesiones_cardio`, `minutos_intensidad` -- each with its
   unit, its `metodo` (media/mediana/cuenta/suma) and its allowed `sentidos`
   (al_menos/como_maximo or antes_de/despues_de). `TIPOS_CARDIO` is the 15 Garmin typeKeys from
   `body/history.py`'s own `KNOWN_ACTIVITY_TYPES` (18 keys) minus `strength_training` (its own
   measure, `entreno_racha.TIPOS_FUERZA`, never widened here), `yoga` and `other` (neither cardio
   nor strength). The orchestrator's spec named a few typeKeys this app has never actually seen
   (stair_climbing, rowing, soccer); left out until a pull actually produces one, rather than
   invented here (open follow-up, not this slice's to add). Contexts a rule can run under:
   `siempre`, `turno`, `tras_noche` (capped at `ventana_post` days past a night block), `periodo`,
   `descanso` (a no-shift day counts as `sin_dato`, never assumed rest). Chequeo shapes:
   `acostarse_antes`, `levantarse_antes`, `sueno_minimo`, `sin_sesion`, `sesion_antes_de`, plus
   `solo_texto`. Checkpoints resolve to `pendiente`/`cumple`/`no_cumple`/`sin_dato` over either
   `semana` or `desde_inicio` windows. `resumen` reads a household child goal only through
   `goals.goal_access`, never a raw query.
3. **`tests/test_horizonte.py`, invented data only**: 54 tests covering every `MEDIDAS` key's real
   figure (including a bedtime week crossing midnight), `sin_dato` vs a real zero, `en_curso` vs
   `no_cumple` through `estado_cuota` on a Thursday, a corrected weekly target line plus its
   `historial_meta` audit trail, planned sessions done/not done, every rule context (including
   `tras_noche` past the 10-day `ventana_post` cap, and a no-shift day as `sin_dato` for
   `descanso`), every chequeo shape plus `solo_texto`, checkpoints across both windows, `resumen`
   reading a household child goal, the three validators refusing bad input, `zona_medida`, and the
   statement-count test.

No route reads `body/horizonte.py` yet -- the proposal cards, goal-detail section and Hoy hook are
later slices. No password, token, session secret or health figure of a real person was read,
printed or written anywhere in any of the three runs below; every test fixture is invented demo
data.

### -R

The first run (logs/worker-body-plan-modulo-1-r-body-app-20261113T005850.json, superseding an
earlier report for the same family) fixed two independent, date-dependent defects in `body/demo.py`
found while proving the Hoy tile's stress band reads "usual" across a 21-date sweep:
`_seed()`'s anchor was always `date.today()`, so the partial "today" reading had no guarantee of
landing inside the person's own baseline band -- `_seed_today_stress` now overwrites it to the
midpoint of `baselines.baseline()`'s own low/high, reading the SAME baseline the live Hoy tile
reads, right after `_seed_periodo` seeds every day-excluding period. Second: `_seed_periodo`'s open
`lesion` period widened to the most recent `strength_training` day before "today" with no limit,
and on dates whose nearest such session was more than ~15 days back, the widen starved
`stress_avg`'s own 30-day baseline window below `baselines.MIN_DAYS`, turning "usual" into a false
"not enough data" -- `_LESION_MAX_DIAS_ATRAS = 15` now caps the widen, leaving 15 unmarked days
regardless. `_seed()` also takes an optional `today` parameter so a test can pin it without
monkeypatching the module's own `date` name. `tests/test_mock_r2_hoy.py` gained
`DemoStressBandAcrossDatesTest`, a 21-consecutive-date sweep (the Monday before a night week
through the week after it) asserting "usual" on every date. The orchestrator reviewed the
`demo.py` diff -- invented demo data only, `_seed_today_stress` reads the same baseline the tile
uses, `_LESION_MAX_DIAS_ATRAS = 15` -- and APPROVED it. This run also stopped **GATE_RED** on its
final chunk: `tests/test_vivo.py`'s `MainTest.test_el_archivo_de_estado_tiene_exactamente_los_
campos_esperados` and `TareaDesconocidaTest.test_tarea_desconocida_pero_el_arbol_refrescado_la_
conoce_lanza_un_hijo` failed whenever `test_vivo` shared a process with modules that imported
`body.*` submodules first (reproduced on `main` 0dc18d9 with `test_vo2max` + `test_web_entry`
alongside) -- measured as TEST ISOLATION, not a product defect: `body/vivo.py`'s stale-module
guard (`_MODULOS_AL_CARGAR`, captured at vivo's own import) is correct for a fresh process, where
vivo imports first; in a shared test process, another test module importing `body.*` afterward
makes the guard see a false "previous task leftover". Handed to BODY-PLAN-MODULO-1-R2.

### -R2

`test_vivo`'s order dependence (named above) was fixed by re-taking the guard's own baseline at
each affected test's own start rather than touching `body/vivo.py`: a new
`_refrescar_baseline_modulos` helper in `tests/test_vivo.py` patches `vivo._MODULOS_AL_CARGAR` to
`frozenset(vivo._modulos_body_actuales())`, with `addCleanup` restoring the prior value, called

(`MainTest.test_modulos_body_previos_se_registran_pero_la_tarea_igual_corre`) keeps its fake
`body.*` module and keeps asserting the guard fires, now against this same freshly-taken baseline.

plan lives in Body so he can say yes to it there, just as we are doing with the money plan in
Finanzas." Eight rulings, each read from the branch's own code:

1. **`proponer_plan`: one card, all-or-nothing.** Every part (metas finales, hábitos, reglas,
   semanas, metas semanales, checkpoints) is validated before the proposal is even stored; apply
   calls a new `db.crear_plan_horizonte`, ONE raw-SQL transaction (never a chain of the per-row
   helpers, whose own individual `with conn:` blocks would each commit on their own and break
   atomicity) -- an injected duplicate `(week_start, medida)` on the LAST insert that writer makes
   rolls the WHOLE transaction back, proven at the db layer
   (`AtomicWriteTest.test_crear_plan_horizonte_injected_failure_writes_nothing`: not even the
   horizon goal survives). Returns `{"goal_id": <horizon>}`. Undo follows `_deshacer_meta`'s own
   precedent (a soft drop: `status = 'dropped'` on the horizon and its child goals, `active = 0`
   on its habits, the horizonte_* rows deleted outright) and REFUSES on drift the instant anything
   was recorded against the plan since apply -- a habit check, a correction (`corregir_meta_plan`),
   an `ampliar_plan`, a linked experiment or training session, or a goal_check -- each its own
   count/existence check, tested individually.
2. **`proponer_meta` widened additively.** New optional `tipo` ('metric', the default, or
   'milestone'), `habitos`, `horizonte_goal_id`. A 'milestone' needs its (always-required)
   `deadline` and no metric fields; a 'metric' needs all three -- validated in Python, not the
   JSON Schema (`_validar_parametros` has no conditional-required). Apply still goes through
   `goals.propose`/`goals.add_habit`, never a hand-written INSERT. An old-shape stored row (no
   `tipo`/`habitos`/`horizonte_goal_id` keys at all) applies exactly as before
   (`ProponerMetaWideningTest.test_old_shape_row_applies_unchanged`).
3. **`corregir_meta_plan`: a correction is another append, never an UPDATE.** Apply calls
   `db.corregir_meta_semanal` (flips the old row's `vigente` to 0, inserts a new vigente row);
   undo calls it AGAIN with the original value -- a third row, never a rewrite. Proven as exactly
   three rows with exactly one vigente after apply-then-undo
   (`CorregirMetaPlanTest.test_apply_then_undo_leaves_three_rows_with_exactly_one_vigente`). The
   card shows before -> after with the measure's own unit (minutes, a clock time, or a session
   count).
4. **`ampliar_plan`: insert-only growth of an existing horizon.** A new `db.ampliar_plan_horizonte`
   (the same single-transaction shape as `crear_plan_horizonte`) returns every new row's own id, so
   undo deletes EXACTLY what that call inserted, never a row the original plan or a different
   `ampliar_plan` wrote. A duplicate `(week_start, medida)` against an existing vigente line is
   refused naming `corregir_meta_plan` instead of a bare "duplicate". Undo refuses once a later
   correction replaced one of its own inserted weekly-target rows.
5. **`proponer_experimento` and `planear_entreno` accept `horizonte_goal_id`.** Checked via a new
   shared `_plan_propio` (a milestone goal this same person created), stored as
   `experimento.goal_id` / `plan.goal_id`. Cards that omit it are unchanged.
6. **`leer_plan`/`leer_planes`, nivel `resumen`.** Both call `horizonte.resumen`/`plan_vs_real`,
   never recompute. A "horizon" is any milestone goal with no `horizonte_goal_id` of its own
   (`resumen` itself works correctly, returning empty lists, even for a plain milestone with no
   plan parts yet -- flagged as an open follow-up below, not a blocker). Access goes through
   `goals.goal_access` first, since `horizonte.resumen` does not check it for the horizon goal
   itself, only for its children -- another person's plan is untouchable through any of the five
   tools (`AnotherPersonsPlanTest`).
7. **The eleventh CHECK widening.** `propuesta_agente.accion`'s guarded detect+rebuild gained
   `proponer_plan`, `corregir_meta_plan`, `ampliar_plan`, following the same pattern the prior ten
   widenings used. While rebuilding the table, found and fixed a latent bug: the rebuild's own
   INSERT never carried `aplicada_via` across, silently nulling that marker on every existing row
   the next time ANY widening ran against a database that already had it populated -- fixed by
   adding the column to both the column list and the VALUES tuple, read defensively for a row from
   before the column existed.
8. **Cards: plain-word lines, never a JSON dump.** `proponer_plan`'s card lists only the parts
   that are non-empty (its title and date range always; "why", metas finales, hábitos, and a
   part-count line only when something is there). `ampliar_plan`'s card lists only what it adds,
   or says there is nothing to add. `corregir_meta_plan` shows before -> after. `proponer_meta`'s
   card branches on milestone vs metric and appends a hábitos line when there are any -- an
   old-shape stored row still renders. New helpers in `body/rutas/asistente.py`:
   `_cadencia_txt` (duplicated from `body/rutas/metas.py`'s own `_cadence_text`, outside this
   slice's touches), `_medida_label`, `_hora_desde_minutos` (the inverse of
   `horizonte._minutos_despues_mediodia`'s noon-relative convention), `_medida_valor_corto`,
   `_semana_targets_txt`. No `body/static/body.css` or `assistant.js` change was needed: the
   existing `.asis-propuesta-despues-linea` class and the JS's own `"\n"`-split rendering already
   support a multi-line card. ~30 new i18n keys in both `es.json`/`en.json` (3 `titulo.*`, the
   rest the card content and the weekly-target vocabulary's own words) --
   `tests/test_i18n_paridad.py` gained `asistente.propuesta.plan_medida.+`/`plan_sentido.+`/
   `plan_unidad.+` in `_FIXED_DYNAMIC` (`plan_medida` sourced from `horizonte.MEDIDAS`, never
   hand-typed).

## BODY-PLAN-HORA-ENTRADA-1 -- a clock measure's valor crosses the tool boundary as "HH:MM" (2026-11-14)

**The trap.** `body/horizonte.py:77-79 _minutos_despues_mediodia` stores every clock measure
(`hora_acostarse`, `hora_levantarse`) as minutes after 12:00 noon, wrapping across midnight (23:30 =
690, 00:45 = 765) -- the card already renders this correctly (`body/rutas/asistente.py`'s
`_hora_desde_minutos` is its inverse). But nothing in `body/agente/herramientas.py` ever told the
model that convention (`grep -n "mediod\|noon"` was empty there), so the in-app assistant and the
desk, through `body/mcp.py` (which lists `HERRAMIENTAS` automatically), had to guess a raw integer
for a clock time. The natural guess -- minutes since midnight -- is silently wrong by 12 hours: a
demo plan's `{"medida": "hora_acostarse", "sentido": "antes_de", "valor": 1380}` (meant as 23:00)
rendered as "acostarse antes de las 11:00". The same raw integers flowed OUT through `leer_plan` for
the model to put into words.

**Ruling 1 -- the tool boundary speaks "HH:MM", in both directions; storage is untouched.**
`body/horizonte.py` was not edited. New in `body/agente/herramientas.py`:
- `_MEDIDAS_HORA`, read off `horizonte.MEDIDAS` itself (`{k for k, v in horizonte.MEDIDAS.items()
  if v["unit"] == "hora"}`), never a hardcoded pair -- a future clock measure is covered for free.
- `_valor_reloj(campo, valor)`: a clock measure's `valor` must be a string matching
  `horizonte._parse_hhmm`'s own "HH:MM" regex, converted with `horizonte._minutos_despues_mediodia`
  (called directly, both private, per the dispatch's own instruction not to edit horizonte.py).
  Anything else -- a raw number, "24:00", "7pm", "" -- is refused: `ToolError(f'{campo}: una hora se
  escribe "HH:MM", p. ej. "23:00"')`.
- `_hora_desde_minutos(total)`: the inverse, duplicated from `asistente.py`'s own helper of the same
  name (the same duplication choice every other small helper in this module already makes, per its
  own module docstring).
- `_convertir_criterios_reloj(campo, criterios)`: converts a checkpoint criterio's clock `valor`
  to minutes BEFORE `horizonte.validar_criterios` sees it, since that validator requires a number
  for every medida and is outside this slice's touches.
- `_convertir_lineas_reloj`/`_convertir_plan_salida`: the out direction -- every clock-measure
  `valor`/`real` pair in a `horizonte.resumen`/`plan_vs_real` dict (the current week's `lineas`, the
  next checkpoint's `criterios`, and `leer_plan`'s own `plan_vs_real` weeks) converted to "HH:MM"
  before the tool returns it. `horizonte.resumen`/`plan_vs_real` themselves are unchanged.

Wired into `_validar_metas_semanales_plan` (`proponer_plan`/`ampliar_plan`'s `metas_semanales`),
`_validar_checkpoints_plan` (their `checkpoints[].criterios`), `_corregir_meta_plan` (its `valor`,
branching on the target line's own `medida`), and `_leer_planes`/`_leer_plan` (the out direction). A
non-clock medida keeps taking a plain number, exactly as before. The JSON-schema `valor` type for
`_PARAM_META_SEMANAL_PLAN` and `_PARAM_CORREGIR_META_PLAN` widened to `["number", "string"]`
(`_PARAM_CHECKPOINT_PLAN.criterios` was already a bare untyped array -- `_validar_parametros` never
recurses into an array item's own properties, confirmed at `herramientas.py`'s own line 138-140
comment, so no schema change was needed there, only the runtime conversion above).

**Ruling 2 -- the model is told.** One sentence appended to each of `proponer_plan`'s,
`ampliar_plan`'s and `corregir_meta_plan`'s `descripcion` in `HERRAMIENTAS`, naming the two clock
measures and the "HH:MM" (24h) convention, e.g. for `proponer_plan`: `"En metas_semanales y en los
criterios de un checkpoint, el valor de una medida de reloj (hora_acostarse, hora_levantarse) se
escribe \"HH:MM\" en formato 24 horas, por ejemplo \"23:00\"; el valor de cualquier otra medida es
un número."` `body/mcp.py:188-189` passes `descripcion` straight through as the MCP tool's
`description`, so the door picks this up automatically; `tests/test_mcp.py`'s new
`test_proponer_plan_description_tells_the_hhmm_convention` asserts `"HH:MM"` reaches
`tools/list`'s `proponer_plan` entry.

**Ruling 3 -- nothing already stored changes, no card string changes.** Confirmed by the full
existing `tests/test_plan_propuestas.py` suite passing unmodified (the fixture-rendering tests there
feed already-converted, stored numeric `valor`s straight to `asistente.TARJETAS`, bypassing the
tool layer entirely, so they were never touching this slice's change).

**New tests**, invented demo data only, never a real figure:
- `tests/test_plan_propuestas.py::HoraEntradaToolTest` (11 tests): "23:00" in a weekly line stores
  as 660, "00:45" stores as 765 (the midnight-wrap case); the `proponer_plan` card still renders
  "acostarse antes de las 23:00" (es) / "in bed before 23:00" (en) from that stored value; a number
  for a clock measure is refused naming the item in `metas_semanales`, `ampliar_plan`, a checkpoint
  criterio, and `corregir_meta_plan` (which also accepts and converts "HH:MM"); a number for a
  non-clock measure is still accepted unchanged; "24:00"/"7pm"/"" are refused; `leer_plan` returns
  "23:00" for that line's target via `plan_vs_real`.
- `tests/test_mcp.py::PlanToolsTest::test_proponer_plan_description_tells_the_hhmm_convention` (1
  test): the description reaching the MCP door for `proponer_plan` carries "HH:MM".

**`touches` held exactly**: `body/agente/herramientas.py`, `tests/test_plan_propuestas.py`,
`tests/test_mcp.py`, `DECISIONS.md`. `body/horizonte.py`, `body/rutas/asistente.py` and
`body/mcp.py` were read but not edited.

## BODY-PLAN-PANTALLA-1 -- the plan vs real screen (2026-11-14)

**Ruling 1 -- the plan lives in goal detail, not a new tab.** A milestone goal is a "horizon" once
it carries any plan row -- a child goal, a rule, a week, a weekly target line or a checkpoint,
`body/rutas/metas.py`'s `_es_horizonte` (one bounded `SELECT EXISTS(... UNION ...)`, gated on
`kind == "milestone"` first so a metric goal costs nothing extra). `goal_detail` builds the plan
section ONLY from `horizonte.semana`/`horizonte.checkpoints` (`_build_plan_ctx`), plus small direct
reads on `goal`/`experimento` for the end-targets and linked-experiments cards -- never a second
`horizonte_*` read and never `horizonte.resumen` (which would duplicate `semana`/`checkpoints`
internally). `body/horizonte.py` was not edited.

**Ruling 2 -- "this week of your plan".** A card with the week's own title/note, one row per
vigente weekly line (target in plain words reusing `asistente.propuesta.plan_*`'s own vocabulary,
real figure or the honest gap `goals.plan.sin_dato_reloj`, an estado chip `cumple`/`en_curso`/
`no_cumple`/`sin_dato` mapped onto the existing `ok`/`warn`/`low`/`off` chip classes -- never a new
chip colour), the cardio zone note (`goals.plan.zona_no_medida`) when a line's `zona_medida` is
`False`, this week's planned sessions grouped by day with done/not-done, this week's rules (a
measurable one gets "N of M days"; `solo_texto` ones render nothing judged), and week navigation
(`?semana=YYYY-MM-DD`, clamped to the horizon's own `start_day..deadline`, current week the
default). The head card gains "N days to end date" / "ended".

**Ruling 3 -- end targets, next checkpoint, experiments.** Child goals as links with a verdict
chip; the next checkpoint (date/title/criteria with estados), past checkpoints inside a closed
`<details>`; linked experiments as links to `/experiments/{id}`.

**Ruling 4 -- a child names its horizon; `/goals` nests them.** A child goal's detail shows "Part
of the plan: <title>", linking back only when `goals.goal_access` also allows this viewer to see
that horizon. `/goals` nests a horizon's own child goals under its card within the same status
section (`_nest_horizontes`, pure Python over rows already fetched -- no extra query); a child
whose horizon is not in this same accessible list (another person's private horizon, or a
different section) simply stays top-level, unmatched.

**Ruling 5 -- bounded regardless of plan size, proven.**
`tests/test_rendimiento.py::PlanPantallaCostIndependentOfSpanTest` builds a 1-week horizon with 1
weekly line against a 12-week horizon with 1 line per week (12 total), and a 1-line week against
an 8-line week (the six `horizonte.MEDIDAS` keys plus two plain `metric_def` keys) -- `GET
/goals/{goal_id}` costs the identical statement count in both pairs, proving `horizonte.semana`'s
own per-week scoping (confirmed by reading `plan_vs_real`: every data source is read once over the
padded range of the WEEK being viewed, never the horizon's whole span).

**Ruling 6 -- the demo seeds one invented, generic plan.** `body/demo.py`'s `_seed_plan_horizonte`:
a horizon from three weeks before the anchor day to five weeks after, two child metric goals, two
habits on the horizon, four rules (one per contexto kind the demo allows -- `siempre`, `turno`,
`tras_noche`, `periodo` -- the last one text-only), a weekly line set for every week (strength
sessions, cardio sessions, bedtime, sleep minutes) with one corrected via
`db.corregir_meta_semanal`, two checkpoints (one past, one ahead), this week's planned sessions
linked to the horizon, and one linked experiment -- all through `goals.propose`/`goals.activate`
and `db.py`'s own `horizonte_*` writers, except the two `plan` rows (that table has no `db.py`
writer, the same exception `_seed_plan_hoy` already takes). No real city, sport, employer, shift
code or figure. Consumes zero `rng` draws, so it does not shift the deterministic sequence any
later call depends on; placed right after `_seed_goals_and_habits` so sleep/rhr/steps/hogar ids are
unaffected. `tests/test_demo.py`'s `PlanHorizonteSeedTest` checks the horizon by title (in es and
en), its 2 active children, 2 habits, all 4 rule contextos, 1 week row, >0 vigente lines and exactly
1 corrected one, 2 checkpoints, 2 plan rows, 1 experimento row; `test_has_seven_active_goals_with_checks`
and `test_has_six_habits` updated for the +3 goals / +2 habits this adds.

**A real bug, found by this slice's own tests and fixed.** `_plan_sesiones_dias` grouped a day's
planned sessions into a dict keyed `"items"`; Jinja's attribute-then-item lookup on a dict resolves
`d.items` to the dict's own bound `.items` method before ever trying the key, so
`{% for it in d.items %}` raised `TypeError: 'builtin_function_or_method' object is not iterable`
for any horizon with a planned session that week. Renamed the key to `"sesiones"` in both

## BODY-MUDANZA-ORIGEN-ANTIGUO-1 -- the uploaded source can be at an older schema than the host's code (2026-11-14)

Measured live by the orchestrator (BODY-MUDANZA-PC-A-SERVIDOR-1) while running the first real dry run against a PC
snapshot: `duna-deploy-body importar-pc --cuenta-sub <sub> --archivo /srv/duna/data/body/mudanza-pc.sqlite` crashed
before writing anything -- `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: horizonte_regla` at `body/mudanza.py`'s
`_source_rows` (`SELECT * FROM "<table>"`), reached via `_process_table` -> `_run` -> `importar`. Cause: the PC
database was last opened by `body.backup snapshot` (which copies a database byte-for-byte, migrating nothing), and
nothing running today's code had opened it since BODY-PLAN-ESQUEMA-1 added the four `horizonte_*` tables --
`importar` opened the upload with `backup.open_readonly` and read it as if it already carried today's schema. Any
person's PC can be behind the host's code by design (BODY-MUDANZA-HERRAMIENTA-1's own module docstring already said
so), so the importer has to accept an older source, not assume the upload matches `body/db.py`'s current `SCHEMA`.

**Rulings, as built.**

1. **The importer reads a source brought to today's schema by the one migration path, never the upload itself.**
   `importar` no longer opens `origen` as the live source. A new generator, `_migrated_source(origen)`, opens it
   read-only (`backup.open_readonly`, the same way `body.backup snapshot` opens its own source) and copies it --
   sqlite's own backup API, never a plain file copy -- into a temporary file created with `tempfile.mkstemp` in
   `config.DB_PATH.parent` (the same directory the destination database lives in: same filesystem, same owner as the
   data user), `chmod`ed to 0600 best-effort. `db.init` -- the one function every fresh or existing database goes
   through to reach today's schema, never a hand-written `CREATE` that could drift from it -- runs on that COPY.
   Every source row `_run`/`_process_table`/`_source_rows` reads comes from the migrated copy, opened read-only in
   turn. `origen` is opened only for reading; nothing is ever written to it. The copy is deleted in
   `_migrated_source`'s own `finally`, on every exit path -- a dry run, an apply, or an exception raised while the
   caller is still reading the migrated rows (`importar`'s own `with _migrated_source(origen) as (source_conn,
   tablas_nuevas):` block covers the whole of `_run`, so a crash mid-way still unwinds through that `finally`).
2. **The report says it happened, with counts only.** `importar` inserts a synthetic `TableReport("origen",
   skipped_table=True, origen_tablas_nuevas=N)` as `reports[0]`, where N is the number of tables present in the copy
   after `db.init` that were absent before it ran (by name count only -- `_table_names` is a plain `SELECT name FROM
   sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table'`). `_print_report` recognises this entry before its normal per-table branch and
   prints `origen: esquema actualizado en la copia (N tablas nuevas)` as the first line, ahead of every per-table
   line. `skipped_table=True` on this entry also means code that already treats "skipped" as "not a real per-table
   count" (`ApplyTest.test_second_apply_is_a_no_op`'s blanket `for r in reports: if r.skipped_table: continue`) keeps
   working unchanged -- no existing test needed editing for this.
3. **Nothing else changed.** The matching, the remap, the self-ref pass, the person resolution and
   `deploy/host/body-import-pc.sh`'s own order (integrity check on the UPLOADED file, rollback snapshot, timers
   paused, file deleted after `--apply`) are exactly as BODY-MUDANZA-HERRAMIENTA-1 and BODY-MUDANZA-HOST-VERBO-1 left
   them; `deploy/` is outside this slice's `touches` and was not opened. `tests/test_host_import.py` asserts only on
   the shell script's text, never on `importar`'s own report lines, so it needed no edit.

**Tests** (`tests/test_mudanza.py`, invented data only, every fixture built in an isolated temp dir via
`MudanzaTestCase`): `OrigenAntiguoMudanzaTest` builds a source at the schema just before BODY-PLAN-ESQUEMA-1 -- its
own `_new_older_source` takes a fresh `db.init`-built database, drops the four `horizonte_*` tables, and rebuilds
`goal` and `experimento` without `horizonte_goal_id`/`goal_id` (a `CREATE ... AS SELECT` swap under `PRAGMA
foreign_keys = OFF`, the same technique `body/db.py`'s own column-drop migrations use) -- and proves: the dry run and
the apply both complete and import the rows (`test_dry_run_completes_and_reports_the_tables_the_copy_gained`,
`test_apply_imports_the_rows`); the report's first line is exactly `origen: esquema actualizado en la copia (4 tablas
nuevas)` (`test_report_line_names_the_tables_the_migration_added`); the uploaded file's bytes are byte-for-byte
unchanged after a dry run and after an apply (`test_uploaded_file_bytes_are_unchanged_after_a_dry_run`/`_after_apply`,
compared with `Path.read_bytes()` before and after -- never a value printed); no temp copy survives a normal dry run
or apply (`test_no_temp_copy_is_left_behind_after_a_dry_run`/`_after_an_apply`, scanning the temp `BODY_HOME` for
`.mudanza-origen-*` names); no temp copy survives an import that raises mid-way, injected by patching
`mudanza._run` to raise `RuntimeError` (`test_no_temp_copy_is_left_behind_when_the_import_raises_mid_way`).
`OrigenActualMudanzaTest` proves a source already at today's schema reports zero tables added

## BODY-MUDANZA-ORIGEN-ANTIGUO-1-R -- the migrated copy is read through db.connect, not a bare sqlite3.connect (2026-11-14)

Measured live by the orchestrator while running the real dry run against the host, after BODY-MUDANZA-ORIGEN-ANTIGUO-1
had already shipped (merged 7de9a3d, ledger ca14027, deployed ca14027 to body.duna.solutions under Carlos's "Go, you
run them"): `TypeError: tuple indices must be integers or slices, not str` at `body/db.py:1437`
(`_rebuild_propuesta_agente_table`'s `step`, reading `r["id"]`), raised before writing anything, via `db.init` ->
`_migrate_propuestas` -> `_rebuild_propuesta_agente_table`, reached from `body/mudanza.py`'s `_migrated_source`.
Cause: `_migrated_source` opened its temporary copy with a bare `sqlite3.connect(tmp_path)` -- no `row_factory =
sqlite3.Row`, no `PRAGMA foreign_keys`, no `busy_timeout` -- while every migration in `body/db.py` is written for a
connection made by `db.connect`, including the rebuilds that run `SELECT * FROM "<table>"` and then read each row
back by column name (`r["id"]`, `r["person_id"]`, ...), which raises a `TypeError` on a plain tuple row. The slice
that shipped this code never caught it because its own fixture (BODY-MUDANZA-ORIGEN-ANTIGUO-1's
`OrigenAntiguoMudanzaTest`) is a hand-trimmed copy of today's schema that never held a row in a table a current
migration REBUILDS -- only tables and columns were removed, no row was ever at risk of being read back as a tuple.

## BODY-DESHACER-DERIVADOS-1 -- an undo also removes what was derived from the row it deletes (2026-11-14)

Live on body.duna.solutions (a5a8cce), 2026-11-14 22:01:49 UTC, measured by the orchestrator in the host's own web
journal (route templates only): `POST /asistente/propuestas/{propuesta_id}/deshacer 500 IntegrityError`. The
person's desk tapped Deshacer on an applied `registrar_entreno` card (a manual workout logged twice); the card then
showed nothing and the session stayed applied.

**Cause.** `_deshacer_registrar_entreno` (`body/agente/propuestas.py`)'s manual case deleted the session's own
`workout_set` rows and then its `activity` row, but `recuperacion_actividad` (`body/db.py`'s
`_RECUPERACION_ACTIVIDAD_COLUMNS`) holds a FOREIGN KEY to `activity(person_id, source, source_id)`, and the hosted
pull computes a recovery row for a session right after it is logged (`body/pull.py`'s `_recalcular_recuperacion_
seguro` -> `body/recuperacion.py`'s `recalcular`). Connections run `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` (`db.connect`), so the
DELETE on `activity` was refused outright. `assistant.js`'s `llamarPropuesta` called `resp.json()` on the 500 and
swallowed the failure (`.catch(function () {})`), so the refused undo was invisible on the card. A `propuesta_
desactualizada` refusal (on either /aplicar or /deshacer) also read the same single sentence, not naming which path
or what actually changed.

**Census (BODY-DESHACER-DERIVADOS-1 ruling 1): every `escribir_deshacer` in `body/agente/propuestas.py` that
DELETEs a row**, the tables holding a FOREIGN KEY (or a plain id column used as a link) to it (read from
`body/db.py`'s own `REFERENCES`/`FOREIGN KEY` clauses), and what the undo does about each:

| action (TABLA key) | deleted table | dependent table(s) | what the undo now does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `registrar_entreno` (manual) | `activity` (+ `workout_set`) | `recuperacion_actividad` (FK to `activity`, DERIVED -- the hosted pull's own recompute); any other `activity` row's `vinculo_manual` TEXT link (not a FK, but a dangling reference) | **Fixed.** Deletes `recuperacion_actividad` first (recomputable, never a reason to refuse), unlinks any watch activity's `vinculo_manual` pointing at the deleted session (`UPDATE ... SET vinculo_manual = NULL`, never deleting that watch row), then deletes `workout_set` and `activity` as before -- all in the same `with conn:` transaction. |
| `registrar_entreno` (Garmin-matched, a watch slot that did not exist pre-correction) | one `workout_set` row | none found (nothing REFERENCES `workout_set`) | Unchanged -- no dependent row exists. |
| `planear_entreno` | `plan` | none found (nothing REFERENCES `plan`) | Unchanged. |
| `marcar_habito` (no prior row) | `habit_check` | none found | Unchanged. |
| `proponer_experimento` | `experimento` (via `db.borrar_experimento`) | `experimento_registro` (FK to `experimento`; PERSON-written, via `marcar_experimento`) | Already guarded: `db.borrar_experimento` itself refuses (`ValueError`) once any `experimento_registro` row exists, and `_drift_deshacer_proponer_experimento` checks the same condition first, so a dependent person row reads as the ordinary `propuesta_desactualizada` refusal, never a raised exception. No change needed. |
| `marcar_experimento` (no prior row) | `experimento_registro` | none found | Unchanged. |
| `registrar_ingesta` | `ingesta` (via `db.borrar_ingesta`) | none found (`ingesta` points outward to `comida`, nothing points inward to `ingesta`) | Unchanged. |
| `registrar_comida` | `comida` (via `db.borrar_comida` / `comida_compartida.deshacer_autor`) | `ingesta.comida_id`, `comida_compartida_porcion.comida_id` (both FK to `comida`; both DERIVED children of the same meal, never a separate person write) | Already correct: `db._borrar_comida_tx` deletes the meal's own `ingesta` children before `comida`; `comida_compartida.deshacer_autor` clears `comida_compartida_porcion.comida_id` to NULL before deleting `comida`. No change needed. |
| `registrar_checkin` | `checkin` (via `db.borrar_checkin`) | `checkin_nota` (same id as `checkin`, FK-shaped) | Already correct: `db.borrar_checkin` deletes `checkin_nota` before `checkin`, in one `with conn:`. No change needed. |
| `marcar_periodo` | `period` (via `db.borrar_periodo`) | none found | Unchanged. |
| `proponer_objetivo_nutriente` (no prior row) | `nutrient_target` (via `db.borrar_nutrient_target`) | none found | Unchanged. |
| `proponer_plan` | `horizonte_regla`/`horizonte_semana`/`horizonte_meta_semanal`/`horizonte_checkpoint` (by `horizonte_goal_id`) | `horizonte_meta_semanal.reemplaza_id` (self-referencing FK -- a later `corregir_meta_plan` correction row pointing at an earlier one; PERSON-written) | Already guarded: `_drift_deshacer_proponer_plan` refuses (drift) the instant any child table's row count no longer matches what was applied -- including a correction, which appends a row -- before the delete ever runs. No change needed. |
| `ampliar_plan` | same four tables, by the specific ids that call created | same self-referencing FK on `horizonte_meta_semanal` | Already guarded: `_drift_deshacer_ampliar_plan` checks each created id still exists and, for `horizonte_meta_semanal`, is still `vigente` (not replaced by a later correction) before deleting. No change needed. |

Only `registrar_entreno`'s manual case needed a fix: it is the one undo that deletes an `activity` row, and
`recuperacion_actividad` is the one derived table keyed to `activity`. Every other DELETE-shaped undo either has no
dependent table, or already refuses/clears the dependency correctly (the comida/checkin cases pre-date this slice;
the experimento/proponer_plan/ampliar_plan cases rely on their existing drift checks, which already implement this
same rule -- "a person's later record is never deleted by an undo, so this check runs before anything else does",
`_drift_deshacer_proponer_plan`'s own words).

**Ruling 2, as built.** `deshacer()` now wraps `entrada.escribir_deshacer(conn, row)` in `try`/`except Exception:
conn.rollback(); raise` -- the mark (`_marcar`'s UPDATE to `'deshecha'`) and the undo writer share one transaction
explicitly, rather than relying on whatever nesting of `with conn:` a given writer happens to use. Measured to be
necessary, not merely defensive: with the fix REVERTED and a writer that raises immediately (no nested `with conn:`
at all), the unfixed `deshacer()` left the proposal reading `'deshecha'` in the SAME connection's own next read --
the UPDATE had never been rolled back. `body/rutas/asistente.py`'s `_propuesta_respuesta` (shared by
/aplicar, /descartar, /deshacer) now catches any exception from the action, calls `conn.rollback()`, and returns
`JSONResponse({"estado": "error"}, status_code=500)` -- never FastAPI's default HTML error page.

**Ruling 3, as built.** `assistant.js`'s `llamarPropuesta` now disables the tapped button, and on a non-OK
response, a body that fails to parse as JSON, or a network failure, re-enables that button and shows
`asistente.propuesta.fallo` on the card ("No se pudo completar. Inténtalo de nuevo." / "That didn't go through. Try
again.") instead of failing silently. The four call sites (the card's initial Aplicar/Descartar buttons, and the
Deshacer button created either at card-build time or after a successful Aplicar) each now pass the button they
created.

**Ruling 4, as built.** `_propuesta_respuesta` takes the route's own name (`ruta="aplicar"|"descartar"|"deshacer"`);
when the action's result is `propuesta_desactualizada` AND `ruta == "deshacer"`, it relabels the response's `estado`
to `deshacer_desactualizado` before returning -- the route is the one place that already knows which path was
called, so the JS card never has to guess. The apply side is untouched (`_drift_aplicar_cambio_meta`, etc. still
read as `propuesta_desactualizada`). New i18n keys (both es.json and en.json):
`asistente.propuesta.deshacer_desactualizado` = "No lo deshice: algo registrado después depende de esto." / "Not
undone: something recorded later depends on this."; `asistente.propuesta.fallo` = "No se pudo completar. Inténtalo
de nuevo." / "That didn't go through. Try again." Both are read off `_ETIQUETA_KEYS` (a dict, never a literal
`t("...")` call), so `tests/test_i18n_paridad.py`'s own generic scan cannot see them; a new test names both keys
directly instead.

**Proof, red then green (`tests/test_deshacer_derivados.py`).** With the ruling-1 fix in `_deshacer_registrar_
entreno` and the ruling-2 `try`/`except` in `deshacer()` both reverted to `HEAD` (`git checkout HEAD --
body/agente/propuestas.py`) and the new test module run against that pre-fix code:

    test_deshacer_removes_the_session_and_its_derived_recovery_row ... ERROR: sqlite3.IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed
    test_deshacer_unlinks_a_watch_activity_that_pointed_at_the_deleted_session ... ERROR: sqlite3.IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed
    test_the_mark_stays_aplicada_when_escribir_deshacer_raises ... FAIL: AssertionError: 'deshecha' != 'aplicada'
    Ran 3 tests in 0.515s -- FAILED (failures=1, errors=2)

the first two ERRORs reproduce the exact live 500 (`sqlite3.IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`) byte for
byte; the FAIL independently proves ruling 2 was not already true (a writer that raises with no nested `with conn:`
left the mark committed to `'deshecha'` with the session still present). With the fix restored (the two edits
re-applied), the same module:

    Ran 3 tests in 0.519s -- OK

Each session used a manually-applied `registrar_entreno` proposal, with its own `recuperacion_actividad` row written
by `body/recuperacion.py`'s `recalcular` itself (never a hand INSERT) -- the same function the hosted pull calls, so
the fixture cannot drift from what that module actually writes. `tests/test_agente_propuestas.py` gains four route-
level tests: ruling 4's distinct `deshacer_desactualizado` estado via `/deshacer`, the apply side's unchanged
`propuesta_desactualizada` via `/aplicar`, and ruling 2's `{"estado": "error"}`/500 JSON body (never an HTML page)
on an unexpected exception, with the proposal confirmed still `'aplicada'` afterward.

No password, token, session secret or health figure of a real person was read, printed, or written anywhere in this
run; every fixture is invented demo data (a manual "Pierna en casa" session, sentadilla sets), and the live 500 is
described by route and exception class only, never by a row value.

## BODY-MCP-REMOTO-SERVIDOR-1 -- a hosted MCP door for the Personal desk, one core for both doors (2026-11-14)

Surface BODY-MUDANZA-PC-A-SERVIDOR-1: the Personal desk's MCP client needs to reach Carlos's health data on
`body.duna.solutions`, not the local PC database. This slice builds the hosted half of `body/mcp.py`'s existing
local stdio door -- two new HTTP routes, authenticated by a new device-key scope, sharing the exact same tool
dispatch the local door already runs, never a parallel copy of it.

**Ruling 1, as built.** `body/dispositivo.py`'s `ALCANCES` gains `"asistente:mcp"`, independent of the three
existing scopes, no schema change. `body/rutas/dispositivos.py`'s `_ALCANCE_LABELS` and `/ajustes/dispositivos`'s
create form gained one new, unchecked-by-default checkbox for it; `body/i18n/{es,en}.json` gained
`dispositivos.scope.asistente_mcp` ("Asistente personal (MCP): leer y proponer, como el asistente de Body" /
"Personal assistant (MCP): read and propose, like Body's assistant").

**Ruling 2, as built -- one core, two doors.** `body/mcp.py`'s dispatch functions -- `_lista_herramientas`
(mcp.py:344), `_llamar_herramienta` (mcp.py:458), `_aplicar_propuesta_mcp` (mcp.py:397),
`_descartar_propuesta_mcp` (mcp.py:431) -- now read a duck-typed session instead of the local-only `_Sesion`
they used before: `conn`, `person_id`, `caller`, `conversacion()`, `tope_lecturas`/`tope_propuestas`/
`tope_aplicaciones`, `contar_lectura`/`contar_propuesta`/`contar_aplicacion`. `_Sesion` (mcp.py:192, unchanged
shape, gained only `caller = CALLER` and the three `contar_*` methods) is the local stdio door's half; the new
`_SesionRemota` (mcp.py:286) is the hosted door's half -- same interface, DB-backed caps (`_TopeDB`, mcp.py:231)
instead of the in-memory `_Tope` (mcp.py:161), and no-op `contar_*`/`registrar()` since the audit row and the
running total it would feed are already written by the shared core itself. `body/rutas/mcp_remoto.py` (new) is
the only caller of `_SesionRemota`; `body/mcp.py`'s `_procesar_mensaje`/`ejecutar`/`main` (the local stdio loop)
are untouched and still only ever build a `_Sesion` -- `tests/test_mcp.py`'s full 39-test suite re-ran unchanged
and green, proving the refactor changed no local behaviour.

Refusals the shared core raises for its own named reasons (a cap, the `aplicar_mcp` setting, a proposal that
is not this caller's own) now raise `RehusoMCP` (mcp.py:144, `herramientas.ToolError` subclass) carrying a
machine `codigo` and raw `campos` alongside the same localized `mensaje` the local door already showed --
`except herramientas.ToolError` in the local loop needs no change (it is a subclass), while
`body/rutas/mcp_remoto.py` catches `RehusoMCP` first and reads `codigo`/`campos` directly, never
pre-localised text.

**GET /api/asistente/mcp/herramientas** (`body/rutas/mcp_remoto.py:44`), guarded only by
`identity.person_from_device("asistente:mcp")` (404 in local mode, before any person is resolved). Returns
`{"herramientas": [...], "nivel": "<nivel>"}`, byte-for-byte what `mcp._lista_herramientas`/`mcp._nivel` already
produce for the local door's own `_Sesion` on the same person -- proved directly in
`tests/test_mcp_remoto.py::HerramientasTest.test_list_matches_the_local_core_for_the_same_person` by comparing
the two outputs.

**POST /api/asistente/mcp/llamar** (`body/rutas/mcp_remoto.py:68`), same auth. Body `{"nombre", "argumentos"?,
"conversacion_id"?}`, capped at `MAX_BODY_BYTES = 64 * 1024` (`body/rutas/mcp_remoto.py:35`) -- `413` on an
oversized `Content-Length` header (checked before any body is read) or on the streamed body itself crossing
the cap; malformed/non-dict JSON is `422 {"error": "esquema"}`. On success: `200 {"tipo", "salida",
"aviso_reloj", "conversacion_id"}` (`conversacion_id` always present -- the one the client sent back, or the
one just created). On a refusal: always `200`, body `{"error": "<codigo>", ...campos}` --
- `"limite"` + `minutos` (int) -- a cap reached, any of the three windows below;
- `"aplicar_apagado"` / `"descartar_apagado"` -- the person's `aplicar_mcp` setting is off;
- `"aplicar_no_propia"` -- the proposal is not this person's, or its conversation's `origen` is not `'mcp'`;
- `"aplicar_no_vigente"` -- found, this caller's own, but no longer `'propuesta'` (already applied/discarded/drifted);
- `"aplicar_expirada"` + `expira_en` (the raw ISO timestamp `agente_propuestas.aplicar` returned, never
  pre-localised, so the PC client can render it in the person's own language locally);
- `"conversacion_ajena"` -- the `conversacion_id` sent back is not an int, not owned by this person, or its
  `origen` is not `'mcp'` (checked by `body/rutas/mcp_remoto.py:51`'s `_conversacion_valida` BEFORE a
  `_SesionRemota` is even built, so a foreign id is never looked at by the core at all);
- `"herramienta_rechazada"` -- the generic code for every other `herramientas.ToolError` the core raises
  (unknown tool name, a missing required parameter, a nivel-gated tool);
- `"error_interno"` -- any other exception: `conn.rollback()` runs, and the one line logged
  (`body/rutas/mcp_remoto.py`'s `logger.info`) carries the exception CLASS and the tool NAME only, never
  params, results, or the exception's own text. 401/403 (bad/missing/revoked key, key without the scope)
  are unchanged FastAPI/`identity.person_from_device` behaviour, never rewritten to this JSON shape.

**Ruling 3, as built.** The conversation id is entirely client-held: `_SesionRemota.conversacion()` creates one
(`origen='mcp'`) only on the first propuesta/aplicar/descartar call that sends none, and returns it in that same
response's `conversacion_id`; a later call that sends it back keeps using it -- proved in
`tests/test_mcp_remoto.py::LlamarPropuestaTest` (`test_sending_the_conversacion_id_back_keeps_using_it`), and
that a second call with NO id creates a genuinely separate conversation, never silently reusing session state
the remote door does not keep (`test_a_second_call_with_no_conversacion_id_creates_a_separate_one`).

**Ruling 4, as built -- caps, no schema change.** `_TopeDB` (mcp.py:231) runs ONE query per cap check:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(llamada_en) AS oldest FROM uso_herramienta_externa WHERE person_id = ? AND
llamada_en >= ? AND herramienta IN (...)`, cached so `permite()` followed by `minutos_para_reintentar()` costs
one query, not two. Which `herramienta` names count toward which cap is read off the EXISTING registry
(`herramientas.HERRAMIENTAS[*]["tipo"]`), never a new column: `_NOMBRES_LECTURA`/`_NOMBRES_PROPUESTA`
(mcp.py:137-138) are the frozensets of "lectura"/"propuesta" tool names; the apply cap counts only
`NOMBRE_APLICAR` by name. Reused window/counts, the SAME as the local door's `_Tope` (`LIMITES`, mcp.py:130):
`ventana_min=15` (`agente_propuestas.EXPIRA_MINUTOS`), `lecturas=5`, `aplicaciones=5` (both
`bucle.MAX_LECTURAS`), `propuestas=8` (`bucle.MAX_RONDAS`) -- ONE shared budget across both doors, by design
(ruling 4's own wording): `tests/test_mcp_remoto.py::CapsTest.test_local_calls_count_toward_the_same_remote_cap`
proves a local stdio call (`mcp._llamar_herramienta` against a plain `_Sesion` on the same connection) counts
toward the remote door's own cap. Because `_llamar_herramienta`'s first line already writes this call's own
audit row before any cap is consulted (ruling 5's "every call, refused or not, is audited" -- unchanged),
`permite()` compares `n <= cupo`, not `n < cupo`, so the row the current attempt just wrote is itself counted
correctly. `CapsTest` ages a window out by directly rewriting `uso_herramienta_externa.llamada_en`
(`_envejecer_ventana`) rather than injecting a fake clock, because the audit write itself always uses real
wall-clock time -- an injected `reloj` would only move the cap's OWN cutoff, not the rows it reads, and was
proved wrong by a failing test before this fix (`minutos: 457900`, logged in this slice's working notes, not
reproduced here since it carries no real figure).

**Ruling 5, as built.** Nothing new is logged or stored beyond the existing per-call audit row
(`db.registrar_uso_herramienta_externa`, template-only, `caller` now `"mcp-remoto"` for this door via
`_SesionRemota.caller`) and the one `logger.info` exception line described above (class + tool name only).
`tests/test_mcp.py`'s existing `AuditTest.test_every_call_writes_one_row_with_no_params_or_result` (exact
column set `{"id", "person_id", "herramienta", "llamada_en", "caller"}`) still passes unchanged, confirming no
column was added.

**Ruling 6, as built -- isolation.** `tests/test_mcp_remoto.py::AislamientoEntrePersonasTest` seeds two people
(A, B) with distinct device keys and proves, on every route: A's tool list never names B; A cannot apply or
discard B's proposal (`aplicar_no_propia` either way); A passing B's own `conversacion_id` back is refused
(`conversacion_ajena`) and creates no card in B's conversation; and a lectura tool run as A never contains a
raw figure seeded only for B (resting_hr=187) anywhere in the response text. `tests/test_persona_fuga.py`'s
existing cross-route sweep also now carries both new routes for its two invented people, swept with the same
device-key mechanics the existing `/api/vida/semana` case already used.
