## BODY-HOY-ESCRITORIO-1 -- Hoy's tablet/desktop top block, the trained/still-to-come glow, and the
phone-order deviation named (2026-11-14)

Surface BODY-HOY-ESCRITORIO-1 (rulings 1-4, built on `feat/body-hoy-escritorio-1`): before this branch
(main at `0e52f97`), `body/templates/today.html` rendered `{{ cuerpo_vista(t, cuerpo) }}` once, full
width, directly above `.cols-hoy`, identically at every breakpoint -- no ≥768px treatment existed and
the figure carried no height cap, so on a short desktop window it could grow past the fold. Rulings 1-2
close that measured gap with a two-column grid from 768px; ruling 3 splits the body view's single glow
into a trained (solid) and still-to-come (dashed) layer; ruling 4 bounds the new query's own worst case.
This entry also records BODY-HOY-ESCRITORIO-1-B's own two rulings: the phone-order deviation from
BODY-MOCK-R2-HOY-1's figure-first board order, and that Lectura leaves `.hoy-top` uncollapsed.

**Ruling 1-2, as built.** `.hoy-top` (`body/static/body.css:456`) is a CSS grid from `min-width:768px`,
columns `minmax(0,1fr) minmax(var(--hoy-figura-min),var(--hoy-figura-max))`, the two named custom
properties `--hoy-figura-min:280px` / `--hoy-figura-max:400px` (`body.css:30`) rather than literals.
Below 768px the grid rule never applies, so the browser falls back to the plain block flow of
`body/templates/today.html`'s own DOM order (`today.html:21-103`): the score hero (`class="card est"`,
synced line inline), "El día por delante"/"The day ahead", then the figure -- never the grid rendering
anything twice (`tests/test_hoy_escritorio.py::HoyTopBlockMarkupTest::test_figure_rendered_exactly_once`
counts exactly one `cuerpo-vista-track`). The figure itself is capped on Hoy only, via the `hoy-figura`
class `_cuerpo_vista.html`'s macro now takes as an `extra_class` param (`_cuerpo_vista.html:1`,
`today.html:102`): `max-height:60vh`/`60svh` on phone, `min(78vh,720px)` from 768px (`body.css:459,457`),
`object-fit:contain` so it is never cropped (`body.css:460`).

**Ruling 3, as built.** `body/anatomia.py:126`'s `grupos_entrenado_pendiente(categorias_entrenadas,
categorias_planeadas)` is the pure union/minus: TRAINED is every logged set's own categoria unioned into
glow groups, STILL-TO-COME is the planned session's own groups minus TRAINED, so a planned group already
done shows solid only, never both. `body/anatomia.py:99`'s `contexto()` gained a third per-view-filtered
list, `pendiente` (`anatomia.py:119`), drawn with the solid glow's own CSS class plus a `.pendiente`
modifier (`body.css:438`, a dashed border, transparent fill, the same `mix-blend-mode` the solid glow
already carries). `body/rutas/hoy.py:376`'s `_entrenado_hoy_categorias` is the one bounded query --
today's own activities merged the same way `_actividades_hoy` already merges a linked pair, then ONE
`workout_set` query over all of them (never one per activity) filtered the same way `db.exercise_sets`
already filters (active, not excluded, corrected wins). `hoy.py:403`'s `_cuerpo_hoy_ctx` now reads both
`_plan_categorias_hoy` (`hoy.py:257`, a plan marked `'done'` now reads as `None` too, same as no plan)
and `_entrenado_hoy_categorias`, and picks one of four captions. Verbatim (`body/i18n/es.json:1219-1220`,
`body/i18n/en.json:1219-1220`):

    cuerpo.caption.hoy_entrenado              es: "Entrenado hoy: {grupos}."
                                               en: "Trained today: {grupos}."
    cuerpo.caption.hoy_entrenado_y_pendiente  es: "Entrenado hoy: {grupos}. Por venir: {pendientes}."
                                               en: "Trained today: {grupos}. Still to come: {pendientes}."

(the two existing captions, `hoy_con_sesion`/`hoy_sin_sesion`, are unchanged and still cover
planned-only/nothing.) Proved end to end by `tests/test_hoy_escritorio.py::EntrenadoPendienteGlowTest`
(solid only, dashed only, a planned group already trained collapsing to solid only, both captions in
both languages, a `'done'` plan contributing no pending group, the existing empty caption unchanged, and
the lesion hatch still drawn above a trained glow).

**Ruling 4, as built.** `tests/test_rendimiento.py`'s own `_seed()` now also logs one manual training
session for today (`db.create_manual_session` + two `db.correct_exercise_set` calls, espalda/brazo --
invented demo data, no real figure), so the route sweep measures ruling 3's new bounded `workout_set`
read against its real worst case (a non-empty id list) instead of the demo's own random activities,
which rarely land a categorised set on today. Measured: `"/"` 85 statements (was 84, the new query's own
+1), ceiling raised from 101 to `ceil(85 * 1.3) = 111`; `"/day/{day}"` 62 statements (was 60, its existing
per-activity `zonas_limitadas` read in `body/db.py`'s `load_day` now also covers the new activity),
ceiling raised from 62 to `ceil(62 * 1.3) = 81`.

**BODY-HOY-ESCRITORIO-1-B ruling -- the phone-order deviation, named.** BODY-MOCK-R2-HOY-1's own ruling 1
put `cuerpo-vista` FIRST in Today's board order, before the score hero -- the mock's figure-first intent.
BODY-HOY-ESCRITORIO-1 ruling 2 deliberately replaced that: score hero, "El día por delante"/"The day
ahead", THEN the body view, on Carlos's own words relayed through the desk -- on the phone the figure

Body noticed, `grid2`, eating window, night week) and rewrote the class docstring to record why. Every

**BODY-HOY-ESCRITORIO-1-B ruling -- Lectura does not collapse `.hoy-top`.** Lectura narrows the page to

which asserts `.hoy-top` is NOT named inside the `[data-ancho="lectura"]` block, so a later edit that
collapses it is a decision made on purpose, never an accident that slips through untested.

## BODY-GARMIN-SYNC-CONSISTENTE-1 -- the hosted daily pull heals its own gaps, a Today sync card,
and /garmin's own progress state (2026-11-15)

**Measured cause.** Before this branch, `body/pull.py`'s hosted daily sweep (the timer in
`deploy/host/body-pull.service`) pulled a fixed N-day window every run (N defaulted to 2: today
and yesterday) and never looked further back. A day that failed to save once -- a transient Garmin
error, a dropped connection -- stayed empty forever unless someone ran an explicit `--days` catch-up
by hand; the loss on 13 and 14 Nov was exactly that. `BODY-GARMIN-SYNC-CONSISTENTE-1-B`'s own
follow-up named a second defect in the first fix: ruling 1 as first built only reached the healing
path when `--days` was left out of the call, but the hosted timer runs `python -m body.pull --days
2` (an explicit call) every day -- so on the live host the pull would never have healed anything,
the same loss the slice exists to stop. `-B` amended ruling 1 to close that gap; this entry
(`-C`) records rulings 1-4/4b as built, `-B`'s amendment, and the two out-of-touches tests `-B`
correctly stopped BLOCKED on, now updated to the new truth.

**Ruling 1, as built, amended by -B.** `body/pull.py:269`'s `_dias_pendientes_relleno(conn,
person_id, hoy, n=2)` returns the union of (a) `hoy` and the `n - 1` days before it (the
always-fetched window; `n` is an explicit `--days` when given, else 2) and (b) every day in the
last `garmin_cuenta.VENTANA_RELLENO` (14) days with no stored Garmin daily row
(`garmin_cuenta.dias_sin_datos`, one query per person, never one per day), oldest first, capped at
`MAX_DIAS_POR_CORRIDA` (16; the always-fetched window never gives way, the cap trims the oldest gap
days first). `pull_hosted` (`body/pull.py:324`) ALWAYS routes through this helper now
(`body/pull.py:347`: `_dias_pendientes_relleno(conn, person_id, hoy, n=n_days if n_days is not None
else 2)`) -- the old branch that gave an explicit `--days N` a plain N-day window with no healing
is gone. So `python -m body.pull --days 2`, exactly what the hosted timer runs, now heals a gap the
same as the bare call; `--days 90` still pulls its own 90 days (the gap-fill half of the union then
adds nothing, already covered). Local mode and the connect-triggered pull (`pull_persona_ahora`,
ruling 4b) are unaffected -- both call the helper with its default `n=2`. Every per-person day list
is still built in that person's own zone (`fechas.hoy_local`, BODY-PULL-RELOJ-1).

**Ruling 2, as built.** `body/rutas/hoy.py:122`'s `_garmin_sync_ctx` returns a compact `card`+`chip`
note on `/` when the person's Garmin account carries a recorded error (`NotSignedIn`'s own
sentence, any other error's generic one) or is connected with its newest stored day older than
yesterday in their own zone -- never shown with no connection and no error. It reads
`garmin_cuenta.estado_conexion` and `dias_sin_datos` (`garmin_cuenta.py:147`, `:159`) the same way
`pull.py`'s own healing does: `daily_metric` where `source = 'garmin'`, never a second read of
"newest stored day" duplicated between the card and the healing set. Rendered at
`body/templates/today.html:13-16`. The card costs one unconditional extra statement on `/`
(measured 86, was 85); `tests/test_rendimiento.py:76`'s ceiling for `/` is raised to `ceil(86 *
1.3) = 112`.

**Ruling 3, as built.** `body/agente/herramientas.py:925`'s `_leer_estado_reloj` (nivel `ninguno`,
no health figure) returns `{conectado, conectado_desde, ultimo_error, ultimo_dia_con_datos,
dias_sin_datos_14}`, registered at `herramientas.py:2503-2507` so the MCP door lists it
automatically (`tests/test_mcp.py:99`). `ROUTE_TOOL["/garmin"]` is now `leer_estado_reloj` (was
`None`); the lectura-tools count is 17 (was 16); the total tool count is 44 (was 43).

**Ruling 4, as built.** The connect form and the MFA-code form (`body/templates/garmin.html:13,32,
52`) each carry a `data-cargando` attribute on their submit button, its own translated label.
`body/static/pagina.js` -- the one script every page loads -- disables the button and shows the
existing `.asis-spin`/`@keyframes asis-pulse` spinner (already `prefers-reduced-motion`-guarded)
until the response loads; the attribute's presence is a no-op everywhere else, and the forms submit
plainly with JS off (progressive enhancement).

**Ruling 4b, as built, its timing.** A successful `/garmin/conectar` or `/garmin/codigo` (token
stored) schedules exactly one background pull of that person's own ruling-1 healing set through
FastAPI's `BackgroundTasks` (`body/rutas/garmin.py:29` `_lanzar_pull_conexion`, wired at the two
routes' `background_tasks.add_task(...)` calls right before each returns its `303` redirect) --
`pull.pull_persona_ahora` (`body/pull.py:305`), the same per-person path `pull_hosted`'s own loop
uses, never a copy. Its timing: `BackgroundTasks` runs the pull AFTER the `303` response is already
sent, so the connecting person's page redirect is never held up by their own first pull.
`_PULL_EN_CURSO` (`garmin.py:25`), an in-process `set[int]`, skips a second connect-triggered pull
for the same person while one is already running; never persisted, so a crash mid-pull leaves no
stuck entry.

**New customer-facing strings, es/en verbatim** (`body/i18n/es.json`, `body/i18n/en.json`):

**-C: the two out-of-touches tests `-B` stopped BLOCKED on, now updated.** `-B` built the amendment
above correctly and stopped BLOCKED on two assertions outside its own touches that still encoded

## BODY-PRIMEROS-TURNOS-1 -- Primeros pasos ticks trabajas-por-turnos on inferred shift data too (2026-11-15)

Personal desk's finding, 2026-11-14: on the hosted Body, after a move imported 1,036 shift rows,
Hoy's "Primeros pasos" card still asked "¿Trabajas por turnos?" with Sí / No even though every
other screen that shows or hides Turnos already treats the question as answered.

**The measured asymmetry.** `tutoriales.primeros_pasos` (`body/tutoriales.py:182`, before this
slice) ticked `trabajas-por-turnos` from `db.get_trabaja_turnos(conn, person_id) is not None` --
the STORED answer only. `db.trabaja_turnos_si` (`body/db.py:2110`) is the one predicate every
screen slice uses to show or hide Turnos, and it is True when the stored value is 1 OR when it is
NULL and the person already has at least one row in `shift` or `shift_batch` (BODY-TURNOS-INFERIR-1,
read-time inference, never a write). `tutoriales.py`'s own docstring recorded the gap as deliberate
("Primeros pasos keeps asking while it is NULL").

**The ruling (orchestrator).** A question the person's own data has already answered is not an open
step.

1. `trabajas-por-turnos` ticks when `db.get_trabaja_turnos(...) is not None` OR
   `db.trabaja_turnos_si(...)` is True -- read-time only, never a write; the stored value stays NULL
   until the person answers it directly. An explicit "no" (0) stays ticked exactly as before. NULL
   with no shift data stays open, with Sí / No, exactly as before.
2. The Sí / No buttons do not show on a ticked step. Measured: `body/templates/base.html`'s
   `primeros_pasos_card` macro already guards them on `item.id == 'trabajas-por-turnos' and not
   item.hecho` (line 28) -- no markup change needed; ticking the item in `tutoriales.py` is what
   hides them, and the person can still change the answer on `/settings` as before.
3. One reading. `tutoriales.py`'s docstring is updated to the new rule. `db.trabaja_turnos_si`'s own
   docstring (`body/db.py:2121-2122`, Tier 1, not in `touches:`) still reads "`get_trabaja_turnos` is
   unchanged: it reports only what is stored, so Primeros pasos keeps asking while it is NULL" -- that
   last clause is now stale and is left alone here; it is named in `open_followups` below for the next
   Tier 1 `db.py` slice.
4. No customer-facing string changes: the diff adds no new strings and no new markup -- it only
   changes which already-existing branch of the existing `primeros_pasos_card` conditional renders,
   for a person whose own shift data already answers the question. Customer-facing bytes unchanged
   (`customer_bytes.changed: false`); merge pre-approved on a green gate.

**The change.** `body/tutoriales.py:179-184` (the `hecho` dict in `primeros_pasos`):
`"trabajas-por-turnos": db.get_trabaja_turnos(conn, person_id) is not None` became
`"trabajas-por-turnos": (db.get_trabaja_turnos(conn, person_id) is not None or
db.trabaja_turnos_si(conn, person_id))`. The function's docstring gained a paragraph naming this
ruling and the template guard that makes ruling 2 need no markup change.

**Tests**, `tests/test_primeros_turnos.py` (new, imports `tests/_isolate.py` first, invented demo
data): `HechoFunctionTest` -- NULL + a `shift` row -> ticked, NULL + a `shift_batch` row only ->
ticked, NULL + nothing -> not ticked, stored 0 -> ticked, stored 1 -> ticked. `CardRenderTest` -- NULL
+ shift rows renders the ticked link on "/" with no Sí/No form, NULL + a shift_batch row renders the
same, NULL + nothing still renders both Sí/No buttons, and rendering "/" with shift rows present never
writes `trabaja_turnos` (still `NULL` after the GET). 9 tests, all green.

No test in `touches:` (`tests/test_tutoriales.py`, `tests/test_turnos_opcional_2.py`,
`tests/test_turnos_opcional_4.py`, `tests/test_primer_dia_1.py`) asserted the OLD asymmetry --
measured: none of their fixtures leave `trabaja_turnos` NULL while also inserting a `shift` or
`shift_batch` row, so all 60 of their existing tests ran unchanged and green. No census test outside
`touches:` was found asserting the old asymmetry either (`trabajas-por-turnos` appears in only four
test files total: the three above plus `tests/test_ancho_completo.py`, whose one use leaves shift
data absent).

**Gate**, exact command `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`, run once on the
final tree, as 9 sequential alphabetical chunks of dotted modules (foreground, each read from the
process):

| chunk | modules (first..last) | tests | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0/8 | test_accesibilidad .. test_baselines_lote | 354 | OK (skipped=1) |
| 1/8 | test_borrar_reauth .. test_entreno_numeros | 489 | OK |
| 2/8 | test_entreno_racha .. test_garmin_estado | 275 | OK |
| 3/8 | test_garmin_host .. test_hoy_escritorio | 558 | OK |
| 4/8 | test_hoy_turno .. test_noche_inusual | 401 | OK |
| 5/8 | test_nutriente_objetivo .. test_propuesta_vigencia | 507 | OK |

Sum: 354+489+275+558+401+507+301+474+188 = 3547. Reconciled against an independent collect-only

**BODY-HOY-ESCRITORIO-2-B -- six-across never applied; a guard added for the defect class
(2026-11-15).** The orchestrator measured the branch above (`932b2d8`, `AWAITING_APPROVAL`) in a

`:78` inside the `min-width:1024px` block (`:56`), and `.hoy-tiles{grid-template-columns:
repeat(3,...)}` sat at `:494` inside the LATER, plain `min-width:768px` block (`:461`, no
max-width) -- equal specificity, so the later, unbounded rule won at every width from 768px up,
including desktop. The same shape BODY-HOY-ESCRITORIO-1-C fixed for `.hoy-figura
.cuerpo-vista-track`, the second time in two days a green gate missed it.

**Fix** (`body/static/body.css`, the 3-across rule moved out of the plain `min-width:768px` block
into its own `@media (min-width:768px) and (max-width:1023.98px)` block, placed right after, with a
comment naming why): the rule is now tablet-only, so the `min-width:1024px` block's six-across rule
is the only unbounded `.hoy-tiles` column-count declaration left and wins from 1024px up, as ruling
1 asked. `tests/test_hoy_escritorio.py`'s two existing CSS-text tests on this pair
(`test_tiles_three_across_from_768`, `test_tiles_six_across_from_1024`, presence-only) were replaced/
tightened to check the EFFECTIVE rule per range: `test_tiles_three_across_scoped_below_1024` requires
the 3-across declaration's own enclosing `@media` header to carry `max-width:1023.98px`;
`test_tiles_six_across_is_the_effective_rule_from_1024` requires the 6-across declaration to be the
LAST unbounded (no max-width) bare `.hoy-tiles` column-count declaration in source order (a negative
lookbehind excludes the separate, higher-specificity Lectura compound selector). Verified against the
pre-fix tree (`git show 932b2d8:body/static/body.css`) that this tightened test fails there
(`['6','3']` != `['6']`) and passes after the fix. Commit `f371685`.

**The guard for the class, `tests/test_css_cascada.py` (new file).** Parses `body/static/body.css`
with the stdlib only (comment-stripping that preserves every position/line number -- this very
file's own cuerpo-vista comment quotes a CSS snippet containing literal `{`/`}`, which desynced the
first, naive version of the brace-matcher -- then a small brace-depth block reader, no real CSS
engine). `find_cascade_inversions` finds every pair of `min-width` media blocks A (larger min) and B
(smaller min, later in the file, with no max-width bound keeping it below A's min) that declare the
same property on the same selector (exact text, whitespace-normalised) -- B wins inside A's own
range by source order alone, so A's declaration never takes effect there.

Run on the branch: **two hits.** `.hoy-tiles`/`grid-template-columns` (the defect this slice's first
commit just fixed -- confirmed the guard independently catches it by running it against
`932b2d8`'s pre-fix CSS text directly, not only via the tightened test above) is no longer present
after the fix (B now carries `max-width:1023.98px`, so the ranges no longer overlap). **One hit
survives on the fixed tree:** `.grid3`/`grid-template-columns` -- the `min-width:1024px` block's
`repeat(auto-fill,minmax(150px,1fr))` (`:71`) is permanently overridden by the unbounded, later
`@media (min-width:640px){.grid3{grid-template-columns:repeat(3,...)}}` (`:109`), so `.grid3` is
always exactly 3 columns from 640px up and the desktop auto-fill behaviour never applies. Checked
where `.grid3` is used (`grep` over `body/templates/`): `day.html`, `history.html`, `trends.html` --
never `today.html` (Hoy). **Not on Hoy**, so per the spec not fixed in this slice (would widen its
touches); allow-listed in the test as a named `BUG` with its one-line reason, and tracked as a new
follow-up, BODY-GRID3-CASCADA-1, rather than fixed here.

The guard is proven on synthetic CSS strings, independent of the real file: detects the inversion
shape; confirms a `max-width` bound below A's min clears it (the exact fix this slice applied);
confirms a different property on the same selector is not a conflict; confirms order matters (the
narrower-min block must come AFTER, not before); confirms a comment quoting braces does not desync
the parser. A second test (`test_allowlist_has_no_stale_entries`) requires every allow-listed pair to
still be a real, currently-measured hit, so the allowlist cannot silently rot into hiding a future,
different regression at the same selector/property. Commit `1c0cad3`.

**BODY-HOY-ESCRITORIO-2-C -- six-across still never applied; the OTHER half of the defect class
(2026-11-15).** The orchestrator's own browser look at the demo on `d658b79` (`body.css?v=90a0279105`),
reading `document.styleSheets` and counting rendered tile rows, found the gap BODY-HOY-ESCRITORIO-2-B
believed it had closed was still there: 1568 and 1024 showed two columns (6 tiles, 3 rows), not six.

**Measured cause** (`body/static/body.css` at `d658b79`): the 6-across rule
(`.hoy-tiles{grid-template-columns:repeat(6,...)}`, `:78`) sat inside the `min-width:1024px` block
(`:56`), and the tile container is `<div class="grid2 hoy-tiles mb-10">` -- but the UNCONDITIONAL
`.grid2{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr));gap:10px}` sat LATER, at `:107`,
with EQUAL specificity (one class each) to `.hoy-tiles`' own rule. `.grid2` wins at every width
>=1024px by source order alone, so the tile grid never left two columns there. `find_cascade_inversions`
(BODY-HOY-ESCRITORIO-2-B's own guard) could not see this: it only compares the SAME selector text
across two media blocks, and here it is TWO DIFFERENT classes on ONE element colliding -- a shape the
spec that measured this gap named explicitly. Before -B, the unbounded plain `min-width:768px` rule
(`:494`, after `:107`) happened to beat `.grid2` at every width from 768px up by the same accident
that then hid six-across entirely; -B correctly bounded that rule to below 1024px, which is exactly
what exposed `.grid2` as the next later, equal-specificity rule still standing at 1024px and up.

**Fix** (`body/static/body.css`): every `.hoy-tiles` column-count rule -- the tablet-only 3-across
(`:500-502`, unchanged in substance from -B), the 6-across, and the Lectura 3-across override -- now
lives together in ONE place, in the Hoy section, AFTER `.grid2` (`:101`): `:503-506`. Winning is now a
property of file position relative to `.grid2`, not of which block happened to come later by accident.
The stale top-of-file 1024px copy (old `:74-79`) was removed outright. Commits `fb21244`, `1ea5990`
(a follow-up fix to a stale line-number cross-reference the first commit's own new comment left behind
after the earlier lines moved `.grid2` from `:107` to `:101`).

**The co-class guard, `tests/test_css_cascada.py` (`find_coclass_collisions`, new).** Parses
`body/templates/today.html` for every element carrying two or more literal classes in a `class="..."`
attribute (skipping any attribute containing `{{`/`{%` -- Jinja can change the class list entirely),
and `body/static/body.css` for every BARE single-class selector's declarations (`.foo`, never
`.foo.bar` -- the only shape where two classes on one element are equal specificity), each tagged with
the min/max-width bounds of its enclosing `@media` (a condition that is not purely min/max-width, such
as `(hover:hover)`, blocks the whole subtree -- the real file's own compound selectors living inside
such blocks are never bare single-class selectors anyway, so nothing this guard needs is lost). For
every (class-pair, property) a Hoy element's two classes both declare, it computes the winner -- the
LAST declaration in file order among the rules whose bounds include a given pixel width -- at four
sample widths: 375, 800, 1024, 1568.

`test_grid2_hoy_tiles_winner_matches_the_expected_table` asserts the exact table the spec gave:
`{375: ".grid2", 800: ".hoy-tiles", 1024: ".hoy-tiles", 1568: ".hoy-tiles"}` -- matches, on the fixed
tree. **Six other co-class hits found on Hoy**, every one reviewed and allow-listed
(`COCLASS_ALLOWLIST`) rather than fixed: `.row`/`.items-end` (`align-items`), `.row`/`.gap-8` (`gap`)
and `.row`/`.justify-start` (`justify-content`) are utility-over-component overrides, intentional by
design (`body.css:309-320`, BODY-ESTILOS-1: utilities sit LAST in the file ON PURPOSE so they always
beat a component class at equal specificity); `.tellbody`/`.taplink` (`display`, `min-height`,
`text-decoration`) is `.tellbody` deliberately overriding `.taplink`'s generic inline-flex with its own
block layout (`today.html:113`). All six are UNCONDITIONAL on both sides (no `@media` at all), so the
same class wins at every one of the four sample widths -- stable, no width-dependent cascade risk, only
a documented, intentional override. `test_allowlist_has_no_stale_entries` requires every allow-listed
entry to still be a real, currently-measured hit.

Proven with a MINIMAL synthetic reproduction of the exact `d658b79` shape (`CoClassCheckerCatchesThe
MeasuredDefectTest`) rather than embedding the real file's text: a `.hoy-tiles` 6-across rule inside an
early `min-width:1024px` block, followed by an unconditional `.grid2`, followed by the tablet-only
3-across block -- `test_grid2_wins_at_1024_and_1568_before_the_fix` confirms the checker reports
`.grid2` as the (wrong) winner at 1024 and 1568 on that shape, exactly reproducing the measured gap;
`test_the_fix_shape_gives_hoy_tiles_the_win` confirms the fixed ordering (`.grid2` first, then both
bounded `.hoy-tiles` blocks) gives the expected table. Commit `2654555`.

## BODY-ASISTENTE-CONFORMIDAD-1 -- Body builds the agent-capabilities-v1 amendment 7 conformance eval (2026-11-15)

**Amendment 7** (`docs/contracts/agent-capabilities-v1.md`, Carlos relayed by the desk 14 Nov ~18:50): every product's
assistant now carries a CONFORMANCE EVAL in its own repository, run in its own gate, asserting at least: (1) every
capability declares its kind and the read-only guard holds; (2) a write is only ever a proposal record approved in
the chat, single-use durably; (3) the provider switch selects among the configured providers per request and a
provider with no price fails closed; (4) one usage row per request with the section 6 fields; (5) the spend ceiling
refuses and the quota never does. Body is the first product to build to it.

**Census (ruling 1, commit 8085bf6).** Before this slice, none of Body's 17 `lectura` tools wrote to the database --
confirmed by the existing `tests.test_agente_registro.BehaviouralGuardTest` and `StaticGuardTest`, both already green
on `main`: `leer_ajustes, leer_como_calculo, leer_costo_turnos, leer_dia, leer_entreno, leer_estado_reloj,
leer_experimentos, leer_historia, leer_hoy, leer_meta, leer_metas, leer_plan, leer_planes, leer_serie,
leer_tendencias, leer_turnos, leer_tutoriales`. The clause 1 guard is now enforced by mechanism, not review alone:
`herramientas.ejecutar()` runs a `lectura` tool with the connection's `PRAGMA query_only` set `ON`, restored to its
prior value in a `finally`; a tool that tried to write would raise sqlite3's own "readonly database" error, which
`ejecutar()` turns into `ToolError("lectura_intento_escribir")` rather than letting a silent write through.

**Clause -> test class -> result** (`tests/test_agente_conformidad.py`, committed e43aff0):

| Clause | Test class | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 -- kinds + read-only guard | `Clause1KindsTest` | PASS |
| 1 -- read-only guard by mechanism | `Clause1LecturaGuardMechanismTest` | PASS |
| 2 -- writes only through an approved proposal | `Clause2WritesOnlyByProposalTest` | PASS |
| 2 -- single-use (apply twice) | `Clause2ApplyOnceTest` | PASS |
| 2 -- another person's proposal refused | `Clause2AnotherPersonTest` | PASS |
| 2 -- expired proposal refused | `Clause2ExpiredTest` | PASS |
| 2 -- drift refuses on every propuesta tool | `Clause2DriftTest` | PASS |
| 3 -- provider switch + no-price fails closed | `Clause3ProviderSwitchTest` | PASS |
| 4 -- one usage row per request, section 6 fields | `Clause4UsageRowTest` | PASS |
| 5 -- spend ceiling refuses | `Clause5SpendCeilingRefusesTest` | PASS |
| 5 -- monthly quota never refuses | `Clause5MonthlyQuotaNeverRefusesTest` | `expectedFailure` -- Body has no monthly question quota yet (BODY-ASISTENTE-USO-1 builds it); the marker must be removed the day that quota lands, or an unexpected success turns the gate red. |

**Registry (ruling 2, commit 3e8c491): 43 -> 44, deviation accepted.** The spec's own figure (43) was a count taken
before this slice; measured on the current `main` tree the registry already carried 44 entries (17 `lectura`, 27
`propuesta`) before any of this slice's edits -- the extra entry predates this work. Every `HERRAMIENTAS` entry now

(`body/agente/bucle.py`'s `_tool_specs`) or the MCP `tools/list` (`body/mcp.py`'s `_herramienta_mcp`).

## BODY-ENTRENO-VISTA-SESION-1 -- Día's own per-session detail screen, GET /day/{day}/entreno/{source_id} (2026-11-15)

**The screen.** Each activity row on Día now links to its own page: header (name, type, day, start-end, duration,
distance -- `body/rutas/entreno_sesion.py:59` `_detalle_cabecera`), avg/max HR and calories each beside the
person's own median of the last 10 OTHER sessions of that type (`body/entreno_sesion.py:46` `comparaciones`,
`HISTORIAL_MIN = 3`; fewer than 3 -> ruling 5's exact "not enough history" line, never a guess -- `_figura_ctx` at
`body/rutas/entreno_sesion.py:71`), the recovery line Día already shows, strength sessions' own sets in order with
the rest between them (`body/entreno_sesion.py:65` `series()`: the gap between active slots' own start times, NEVER
a watch rest-slot's own duration -- `tests/test_entreno_sesion.py::StrengthSetsTest::test_rest_is_the_real_gap_
between_active_sets_not_the_watch_rest_slots_own_duration` proves this with a watch rest slot whose own stored
duration is deliberately wrong against the true gap), the person's correction shown in place of Garmin's own value
when present (a chip, `set-excluida`/`chip ok` in `body/templates/entreno_sesion.html:42-43`), an excluded set
struck and labelled but still listed and still counted for rest timing, and -- only where the day's own per-minute
heart-rate series is already stored -- the curve across the session (`body/rutas/entreno_sesion.py:141`
`_curva_svg`, inline SVG, no inline styling, every colour a fixed class: `.hr-set`/`.hr-rest` in
`body/static/body.css`) with each set's window shaded and each rest marked, each set's own peak and each rest's own
HR drop below it; where the series is not stored (or none of it falls inside the session's own window), ruling 5's
exact "coming soon" line, never an empty chart (`tests/test_entreno_sesion.py::CurvaTest`, three cases: no series at
all, series stored but outside the window, series covering the window).

**Ruling 1, person-scoped.** `entreno_sesion.actividad()` (`body/entreno_sesion.py:26`) resolves `source_id` only
among the signed-in person's own activities for that exact day; another person's `source_id`, or this person's own
`source_id` under the wrong day, both 404 (`body/rutas/entreno_sesion.py:193-202`). Added to
`tests/test_persona_fuga.py`'s cross-person sweep: `_seed_person`'s own `act_id` is now tag-specific (A and B never
share the literal activity id this route resolves off the URL alone), and `_sweep_routes_as` checks own-day-own-id
(200), the other person's own id on the SAME day (404), and this person's own id on the WRONG day (404).

**Ruling 4's production fix.** `body/entreno_sesion.py`'s `curva()` originally reported a rest's own HR drop as
`descanso_inicio - descanso_fin` even when the series caught only ONE sample inside that rest window (so both ends
were literally the same sample) -- a flat, misleading zero where the honest answer is "not enough samples to tell."
Fixed (`body/entreno_sesion.py:140-144`) to require two DISTINCT samples inside a rest window before reporting a
drop at all.

**Ruling 6, the demo.** `body/demo.py` gains a dedicated strength session TODAY (`_seed_entreno_vista_sesion_
actividades`/`_seed_entreno_vista_sesion_detalle`, two exercises -- press banca/sentadilla -- 8 sets, real rest
gaps 75-150s, set 2 corrected (reps 8->6), set 7 excluded) with a per-minute heart-rate series built by
keyframe interpolation at real clock-minute resolution (`_curva_sesion_fuerza`, matching
`garmin_adapter._utc_to_local_iso`'s own `timespec="minutes"` truncation on read -- a finer step silently collapses
on read-back, diagnosed this slice with a scratch script before the fix), and a basketball session YESTERDAY with
no series at all, replacing whatever `_day_activity`'s own random draw had put on either day. Demo URLs (today
2026-11-15, yesterday 2026-11-14 at the time this slice ran): `/day/2026-11-15/entreno/demo-2026-11-15-1` shows the
curve branch; `/day/2026-11-14/entreno/demo-2026-11-14-1` shows the honest pending-line branch -- both confirmed by
`tests/test_entreno_sesion.py::DemoBranchesTest` calling the real route after a real `demo._seed()` run, not by
inspection. `_seed_recuperacion`'s and `_seed_turno_fc`'s own generic curve-filling models were given an
`excluir_dias` parameter each so neither ever overwrites or reaches this hand-placed (or deliberately absent) pair.

**1. `tests/test_agente_registro.py:56` -- `ROUTE_TOOL["/day/{day}/entreno/{source_id}"] = None`.** Checked both
candidates named by the spec before picking `None`:
- `leer_entreno` (`body/agente/herramientas.py:960`) reads a day's/range's training sessions, but its own SQL
  (`type = 'strength_training' OR source = 'manual'`) excludes a Garmin-automatic non-strength activity entirely --
  the demo's own basketball session (`body/demo.py`'s `_SESION_BASKET_TITULO`, type `'other'`, source `'garmin'`)
  would never come back through it at all, yet that session gets this exact detail page
  (`tests/test_entreno_sesion.py`'s own `test_yesterdays_basketball_session_shows_the_honest_line`).

path, ids)` (`tests/test_estados_vacios.py:244`, `tests/test_estados_vacios_hosted.py:107`) that returns 200/404 for

## BODY-ENTRENO-VISTA-SESION-1-C -- the six screen defects the orchestrator's own browser review measured

Continuation of BODY-ENTRENO-VISTA-SESION-1/-1-B (both merged into this branch, `7aae9e5`/`59e4812`): the
orchestrator reviewed the merged screen in a browser and measured six defects. This slice fixes all six, each with
its own test in `tests/test_entreno_sesion.py`.

**1. Legend chips invisible.** `body/static/body.css`'s `.legend i` (line 196) sets no `background`, so
`<i class="hr-set">`/`<i class="hr-rest">` (`body/rutas/entreno_sesion.py:247,249` `_curva_svg`) got only the SVG
rules' `fill`/`opacity` -- an `<i>` has no `fill`. Fixed with two compound rules, following the same `.legend
i.legend-line` pattern the file's own specificity note (line 313) already names:

    .legend i.hr-set{background:var(--body)}     (body/static/body.css:387)
    .legend i.hr-rest{background:var(--muted)}    (body/static/body.css:388)

`tests/test_entreno_sesion.py::LegendCssTest::test_legend_chips_have_a_compound_rule_setting_a_background` asserts
both compound rules exist and set a background, by regex against the stylesheet's own text.

**2. Bands near-invisible.** `body/static/body.css:417-418`, raised from `.14`/`.12` to **`.32`/`.20`**. Values
chosen: `--body` (`#406F45` light / `#7DB282` dark) and `--muted` (`#6B6863` light / `#A09D95` dark) are two
different hues, not two shades of one, so even a modest opacity separates them from each other; `.32`/`.20` is high
enough that each band reads against `--card` (`#FCFBF8` light / `#1E1E1E` dark) in both themes while the set band
(`.32`) stays visibly stronger than the rest band (`.20`), and both stay well below the curve's own full-opacity
`stroke-body` line, which stays the most prominent mark on the chart.

asserts both values against this slice's own prior numbers and that the set band is the stronger one.

## BODY-MCP-REMOTO-CLIENTE-1 -- body.mcp speaks HTTP to the hosted door, PC link permitting (2026-11-15)

Surface BODY-MUDANZA-PC-A-SERVIDOR-1 (Carlos, "build it, 00 first": one database for the web and the desk).
BODY-MCP-REMOTO-SERVIDOR-1 (merged `448243c`) built the hosted door; this slice is its client half --
`python -m body.mcp`, the process the Personal desk's own MCP config starts, now reaches it over HTTP instead
of always opening the PC's local database.

**The mode rule (ruling 1), as built -- `body/mcp.py:357-366` (`_modo_remoto`), read once at the top of
`main()` (`body/mcp.py:793`).** `pc_cliente.leer_enlace()` succeeding means REMOTE; its `EnlaceFaltante` means
LOCAL, exactly as every existing local test already exercises. One escape hatch, read in code, never a worker
command prefix: `BODY_MCP_MODO=local` (the env var name is `mcp.MODO_ENV`) forces LOCAL even with a link,
checked first. In REMOTE mode `main()` never calls `db.connect`, `db.ensure_ready` or `db.local_person_id` --
proved by `tests/test_mcp_cliente_remoto.py::MainNuncaAbreLaBaseLocalTest` (`db.connect` patched to raise
`AssertionError` and never doing so across a real `initialize`/`tools/list`/`tools/call` round trip) and by
`ModoTest`'s three cases (link present, link absent, env override).

**The interface and its two implementations (ruling 2).** `_procesar_mensaje` (`body/mcp.py`, JSON-RPC
envelope: `initialize`/`notifications/initialized`/`tools/list`/`tools/call`, content assembly) is
byte-for-byte unchanged -- it still only ever calls `_lista_herramientas(sesion)` and
`_llamar_herramienta(sesion, nombre, argumentos)`. Both of those became one-line dispatchers: for a
`_SesionCliente` (new, `body/mcp.py:332-347`, no DB at all -- just `conversacion_id`, `idioma` and the three
`total_*` counters `main()`'s stderr summary reads) they delegate to `_lista_herramientas_remota`
(`body/mcp.py:426-442`, `GET /api/asistente/mcp/herramientas` through `pc_cliente.llamar`) and
`_llamar_herramienta_remota` (`body/mcp.py:445-489`, `POST /api/asistente/mcp/llamar`); for a `_Sesion`/
`_SesionRemota` they run exactly the code BODY-MCP-REMOTO-SERVIDOR-1 already proved, untouched. The
conversation id is held client-side for the stdio session's whole life: no `conversacion_id` is sent until
the server first returns one, then it is resent on every later call (`tests/test_mcp_cliente_remoto.py::
LlamarHerramientaRemotaTest.test_conversacion_id_flows_none_then_held_then_resent`). The local `_Tope` caps
never run for `_SesionCliente` (there is nothing local left to cap) -- the server's own `_TopeDB` is the one
authority, exactly as BODY-MCP-REMOTO-SERVIDOR-1 ruling 4 designed it; the "double guard" the spec allowed for
turned out to not be needed, since a `_SesionCliente` call always crosses the wire to the one place the cap
already lives.

**The error mapping table (rulings 3-4), `_error_remoto_a_rehuso` (`body/mcp.py:388-423`) plus the four status
branches in `_llamar_herramienta_remota`.** Every refusal is wrapped as `_RehusoClienteMCP` (`body/mcp.py:350
-354`, a `herramientas.ToolError` subclass whose message is ALREADY the fully localized text) -- so
`_procesar_mensaje`'s existing `except herramientas.ToolError` branch renders it with no new code path:

| server code / HTTP status | client rendering |
|---|---|
| `limite` + `minutos` | `_mensaje_tope_aplicaciones` if the tool is `aplicar_propuesta`, else `_mensaje_tope_lecturas`/`_mensaje_tope_propuestas` by `herramientas.tipo_de(nombre)` -- same functions the local door already uses, unchanged signatures (`idioma`, `minutos`) |
| `aplicar_apagado` / `aplicar_no_propia` / `aplicar_no_vigente` / `descartar_apagado` | the same i18n key each existing `_mensaje_*` reads, called directly with `idioma` (those functions take a `_Sesion` to read `.conn` for the language; `_SesionCliente` has none, so the client reads the key straight off `T(idioma)` instead -- byte-identical output text) |
| `aplicar_expirada` + `expira_en` | `_mensaje_aplicar_expirada_remoto` (`body/mcp.py:369-384`) -- same i18n key/placeholders as `_mensaje_aplicar_expirada`, but converts the server's raw UTC timestamp with THIS PC's own local timezone (`astimezone(None)`) instead of a DB lookup, since the client has no DB (deviation, below) |
| `conversacion_ajena` | new key `mcp.remoto.conversacion_ajena` |
| `herramienta_rechazada` + `mensaje` | the server's own raw `mensaje` verbatim, no i18n -- see deviation below |
| unknown/missing code | new key `mcp.remoto.error_interno` (never a silent fallback, ruling 4) |
| HTTP 401 | new key `mcp.remoto.clave_invalida` |
| HTTP 403 | new key `mcp.remoto.sin_permiso` |
| HTTP 5xx / malformed body / non-200 | new key `mcp.remoto.error_interno` |
| `urllib.error.URLError` (connection failure, timeout) | new key `mcp.remoto.red_fallo` |
| any other exception from the transport | new key `mcp.remoto.error_interno` (defensive: never lets a non-`ToolError` exception reach `_procesar_mensaje`'s generic handler, which assumes a DB-backed `sesion.conn`) |

`tools/list` failing never stops `initialize` from answering: `_lista_herramientas_remota` catches every
failure itself and returns `[]`, logging the exception class or HTTP status to stderr (ruling 4;
`tests/test_mcp_cliente_remoto.py::ListaHerramientasRemotaTest`).

**The five new sentences, exactly the bytes ruling 4 pre-approved**, `mcp.remoto.*` in `body/i18n/{es,en}.json`:
- `conversacion_ajena`: "Esa conversación no es de esta cuenta. Empieza una nueva." / "That conversation
  doesn't belong to this account. Start a new one."
- `error_interno`: "Body no pudo completar eso. Inténtalo de nuevo en un momento." / "Body couldn't complete
  that. Try again in a moment."
- `red_fallo`: "No pude conectar con Body. Revisa la conexión e inténtalo de nuevo." / "I couldn't reach Body.
  Check the connection and try again."
- `clave_invalida`: "La clave de este PC ya no sirve. Crea una nueva en Ajustes › Dispositivos y conecta el PC
  otra vez." / "This PC's key no longer works. Create a new one in Settings › Devices and connect the PC
  again."
- `sin_permiso`: "Este PC está conectado sin el permiso del asistente. Crea una clave con «Asistente personal
  (MCP)» y conecta el PC otra vez." / "This PC is connected without the assistant permission. Create a key
  with \"Personal assistant (MCP)\" and connect the PC again."

**Server-side changes needed to support those (still inside `body/rutas/mcp_remoto.py`, touches-scoped, no new
customer sentence of their own):**
- `GET /api/asistente/mcp/herramientas` now also returns `"idioma"` (`person.get("language", "es")`, read the
  same way `comun._ctx` already does for the web) -- `tests/test_mcp_remoto.py::HerramientasTest::
  test_list_includes_the_persons_interface_language`.
- `herramienta_rechazada` now carries `"mensaje": errores.texto_propio(e)` -- the exact same unlocalized text
  the local stdio door already shows verbatim for a plain `ToolError` (never localized to begin with, per
  that module's own docstring: meant for a model to read and retry). This is not a new translated sentence,
  only the same developer-facing text the local door already displays, now also reaching the HTTP door --
  `tests/test_mcp_remoto.py::LlamarLecturaTest::test_unknown_tool_is_the_generic_code` updated to match.

**Deviations, measured, not literal in the spec:**
1. `aplicar_expirada`'s rendering needed the person's TIMEZONE, not just their language, and the client has no
   DB to read either from. Ruling 3 named adding only `"idioma"` to the GET response. Rather than widen that
   response further, `_mensaje_aplicar_expirada_remoto` converts the server's raw UTC `expira_en` with
   `datetime.astimezone(None)` -- Python's "this machine's own local timezone" -- matching the hosted route's
   own doc comment that `expira_en` crosses the wire raw "so the PC client can render it in the person's own
   language locally" (BODY-MCP-REMOTO-SERVIDOR-1's own wording). Carlos's desk machine's system clock is his
   own; this is the one case where the client's rendering can differ from `_mensaje_aplicar_expirada`'s DB-read
   answer if his OS timezone and his `person.timezone` setting ever disagree -- unlikely, never checked, named
   here rather than silently assumed. `zona` is an explicit, test-only override parameter (never passed in
   production) so `tests/test_mcp_cliente_remoto.py::AplicarExpiradaRemotoTest` can assert exact bytes without
   depending on the machine the gate runs on.
2. `herramienta_rechazada` crossing the wire with a `"mensaje"` field is a small, necessary widening of ruling
   3's literal "add idioma" instruction, driven by ruling 3's OTHER explicit sentence for this slice:
   "herramienta_rechazada -> the same text the local path gives for a ToolError (find it)." There is no single
   canned text to find (the local door's raw `ToolError` messages vary per failure); the server already
   discarded it. Passing the exception's own unlocalized message through (never a new localized sentence, per
   the surface's own stated design) was the only way to make that sentence literally true.
3. `_mensaje_*` functions normally take a `_Sesion` (to read `.conn` for the language, and, for
   `aplicar_expirada`, the timezone). `_SesionCliente` has neither. `aplicar_apagado`/`aplicar_no_propia`/
   `aplicar_no_vigente`/`descartar_apagado` are rendered by reading the SAME i18n key directly off `T(idioma)`
   instead of calling those functions -- byte-identical output text, never a new sentence.

**Cut-over steps for the person** (not run by this slice -- Carlos's own acts, per the approval reason):

## BODY-SERVICIO-HOGAR-1

Carlos's ruling, dictated 2026-11-15 ~19:45, relayed verbatim by the Personal desk: "don't worry about the
restriction between apps in body, finances, and [Hogar]. It's all me. It's all my own Duna servers, and I'm my
own user, my own data. So, drop every restriction. Allow free communication between all of them." This
replaces the per-unit person->app consent (BODY-COMPARTIR-APP-1, dropped) and the latest-value-only rule, for
Carlos's own data read by another Duna app on Duna's own host. The one standing grant is the `hogar:leer`
device key itself (minted and revoked on Body's own device-key page) -- never a new consent table.

**Ruling 1, the scope (`hogar:leer` joins `ALCANCES`):** `body/dispositivo.py:15`. Checkbox and label on the
device-key page: `body/templates/dispositivos.html:39-40`, wired to the key's own alcances at
`body/rutas/dispositivos.py:25` (`_ALCANCE_LABELS`) and `body/rutas/dispositivos.py:73-74` (`alcance_hogar` ->
`"hogar:leer"`).

**Ruling 2, the feed (`body/hogar_feed.py`, new module; routes beside vida's in
`body/rutas/dispositivos.py`):**
- `manana` (`body/hogar_feed.py:76`): `dia`'s figures, plan and active horizon. `_figuras`
  (`body/hogar_feed.py:29`) reads `daily_metric` directly (no existing db.py reader covers "every metric's own
  latest day at or before X"; `db.series` -- reused in `serie` below -- answers a different question, one
  metric over a fixed range) -- one SQL statement, a correlated subquery per metric_key, `kind` read off
  `metric_def`. `_plan_dias` (`body/hogar_feed.py:45`) reads `plan` directly, filtered to `dia` and `dia`+1,
  any goal (no existing reader is unfiltered by goal_id; `horizonte.py`'s own plan read, `body/horizonte.py:509`,
  is scoped to one `horizonte_goal_id`). `_horizonte_actual` (`body/hogar_feed.py:55`) reuses the same
  `kind = 'milestone' AND horizonte_goal_id IS NULL` test `body/agente/herramientas.py:2198`'s `_leer_planes`
  already uses to find a horizon, narrowed to `status = 'active'`, then computes `semana`/`semanas` with
  `fechas.lunes_de` -- which week `dia` falls in out of the horizon's whole span, 1-based, clamped to
  `[1, semanas]`. `null` when the person has no active horizon (deliberately not reusing
  `horizonte.resumen`/`horizonte.semana`: both return far more than `{goal_id, title, deadline, semana,
  semanas}` needs, and `horizonte.semana` requires a Monday `week_start`, never a plain `dia`).
- `serie` (`body/hogar_feed.py:87`) reuses `db.series` (`body/db.py:2032`) for the actual values; its own
  additions are the metric_key existence check (`MetricDesconocida`, `body/hogar_feed.py:18`) and the
  366-day bound (`RangoDemasiadoLargo`, `body/hogar_feed.py:22`, `MAX_SERIE_DIAS = 366`).
- Routes: `GET /api/hogar/manana` (`body/rutas/dispositivos.py:190`), `GET /api/hogar/serie`
  (`body/rutas/dispositivos.py:206`), both `Depends(identity.person_from_device("hogar:leer"))`
  (`body/rutas/dispositivos.py:193`, `:209`). No consent filter -- the key is the grant, exactly as spec'd.

  days -> 400. `Cache-Control: no-store` on both, same as `/api/vida/semana`.

## BODY-SYNC-VIVO-ESTADO-1 -- attempt, backoff and the watch's own last sync, now recorded (2026-11-16)

Surfaced by BODY-SYNC-VIVO-1-INV: Body only recorded a successful write, never an attempt time or a
backoff, and `errores.texto_seguro`'s class-name-only text could not tell a 429 from a 500 even though
garminconnect's own exception can carry `.response`. Carlos, relayed by the Personal desk, 2026-11-15:
"I would like to see more like a live thing in the app or when I talk to you." This is the record that
makes frequent pulls safe (backoff) and honest on screen (last attempt, the watch's own last sync) --
nothing new leaves Duna; the pull still runs only on the host, after a deploy.

**Ruling 1, as built.** Three nullable columns on `garmin_cuenta` (`body/db.py:685-687`, migration
`body/db.py:1271-1276`): `ultimo_intento_en` (every attempt, success or not), `reintentar_despues_de`
(a failed attempt's backoff, NULL meaning no need to wait), `reloj_sincronizo_en` (the watch's own
last-contact instant, ruling 4). `body/garmin_cuenta.py`: `registrar_intento` (184), `puede_intentar`
(209), `registrar_reloj_sincronizo` (228), `estado_sync` (240). `guardar()` clears
`reintentar_despues_de` on a fresh connect/reconnect, the same way it already cleared `ultimo_error`.

**Ruling 2, as built.** `body/garmin_adapter.py:estado_http` (180): 429 by the exception's own type
(`GarminConnectTooManyRequestsError` carries no `.response` of its own, confirmed against the
installed garminconnect 0.3.20 source); a real `.response.status_code` when the exception carries one;
the `0` sentinel for a confirmed `GarminConnectConnectionError` with no response at all
(connection/timeout); `None` for anything not confirmed (auth failure, `NotSignedIn`, an unrelated
exception). `_client` (152) now lets `GarminConnectTooManyRequestsError`/`GarminConnectConnectionError`
propagate with that type intact instead of collapsing every failure into `NotSignedIn`, so the buckets
above can tell them apart; a genuine auth failure or an unrecognized exception still becomes
`NotSignedIn`, unchanged. `body/garmin_cuenta.py:registrar_intento` (184) turns `estado_http` into a
backoff: 429 -> +120 min (`BACKOFF_429_MIN`, 180), 5xx/connection/timeout (a real `.response` or the
`0` sentinel) -> +15 min (`BACKOFF_TRANSITORIO_MIN`, 181), auth failure (`None`) -> no backoff, today's
handling unchanged. `body/errores.py:texto_seguro_con_estado` (22) appends that status beside the class
name, never a message body.

**Ruling 3, as built.** `body/pull.py:_registrar_intento_persona` (306) calls `registrar_intento`
exactly once per attempt, from `_pull_persona` (317) and from `pull_backfill_hosted`'s per-person loop
(462), on every path except "no token" and "the backfill window is already complete, nothing was
attempted" (`n == 0`, no Garmin call made). `pull_hosted` (361) and `pull_backfill_hosted` (462) each
skip a person still inside a backoff via `garmin_cuenta.puede_intentar` (381, 491) with no Garmin call,
counted and printed once as `omitido: N personas en espera` (405, 523) -- counts only, never a name or
a figure. `pull_backfill_hosted` keeps skipping an auth-type error forever (no `reintentar_despues_de`
was ever set for it, unchanged from before this slice) but now resumes automatically once a
backoff-governed one's `reintentar_despues_de` has passed. `ESPACIO_MIN_ENTRE_INTENTOS = 0` (58):
`puede_intentar`'s own minimum-space-between-attempts parameter is real, but a nonzero value here would
have broken `tests/test_primer_pull_1.py`'s
`test_repeated_runs_reach_the_window_start_then_make_zero_adapter_calls` (outside this slice's
`touches:`, six back-to-back calls with no sleep in between) -- the backoff window alone governs these
two call sites; `puede_intentar`'s recency check never trips at 0 minutes.

**Ruling 4, as built.** `body/garmin_adapter.py:fetch_device_last_sync` (243) reads the watch's own
last-contact instant via `get_device_last_used()`, the same `token_str` convention as `fetch_sleep`
(bare value local, `(value, token_after)` hosted); any failure -- the client refusing, the call
raising, the response being unreadable -- is `None`, never raised, since this runs once per person per
pull, after the day fetches, and must never fail the pull. `_parse_device_last_sync` (207) is the only
place the response's shape is assumed, and none of it is confirmed by garminconnect 0.3.20's own types
(`dict[str, Any]`, no key named) or docstring -- the only key this package confirms ANYWHERE on this
response is `userDeviceId` (`api/devices.py:96`, an unrelated call). Tried in order, first that parses
wins: `lastUsedDeviceUploadTime` (epoch ms, a UTC instant), `lastUsedDeviceUploadTimeInSeconds` (the
same instant, epoch seconds), `deviceLastUsedDate` (ISO 8601 string, a naive one assumed UTC); anything
else is an honest gap, never guessed. `body/pull.py:_registrar_reloj_si_hay` (177) wires it into both
`_pull_persona` and `pull_backfill_hosted`'s per-person path.

**Ruling 5, as built -- no code change.** `body/db.py:connect` (1209) already sets
`PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000`, and `body/pull.py`'s `pull.lock` file lock (14, 83) already serialises
every writer -- the daily pull and `--backfill` never run concurrently against the same `BODY_HOME`.
WAL buys concurrent readers during a writer's transaction; at today's or an hourly pull's run rate, with
a single writer already serialised by the file lock and every write already short (one person's
day/sleep/intraday upsert), busy_timeout alone is enough -- WAL would add a second on-disk file
(`-wal`/`-shm`) and a checkpoint policy for no measured gain here.

**Tests (`tests/test_sync_vivo_estado.py`, new, 60 tests):** schema/migration (fresh columns, a
migration onto an old-shaped table, an existing row reads as never-attempted), `registrar_intento`'s
backoff table (success clears, 429/5xx/0-sentinel/auth/non-429-4xx, a new failure overwriting a stale
backoff), `puede_intentar` (never-attempted, not-yet-expired, expired, the recency throttle,
espacio_min=0, no row), `estado_sync` (shape with no row, `ultimo_ok_en` reading `db.last_sync`, every
written field), a reconnect clearing a stale backoff, `estado_http` against the installed garminconnect
0.3.20 package's own exception classes (429-no-response, a response with/without a status, the 0
sentinel, auth/NotSignedIn/unrelated exceptions all `None`), `texto_seguro_con_estado` (appends/omits
the status, never the message), `_client`'s propagation change (429/connection propagate, a plain or
auth exception still `NotSignedIn`), `_parse_device_last_sync` (ms, seconds, naive/offset ISO,
not-a-dict, no recognized key, unparseable, non-numeric), `fetch_device_last_sync` (success, every
failure point, local-mode bare value), and the hosted pull/backfill integration for
429/5xx/connection-timeout/auth (backoff set and printed, a backed-off person skipped and counted, a
past-backoff person tried again, a failed watch-last-sync read never failing the pull, the `omitido`
line's presence/absence). `tests/test_pull.py`, `tests/test_pull_relleno.py` and
`tests/test_garmin_host.py` stub `fetch_device_last_sync` in the hosted test classes that build a real
(unmocked) `garminconnect.Garmin` for an unrelated concern (intraday wiring, healing windows, per-zone
day lists), so this slice's addition stays isolated from theirs.

**Gate command:** `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`. Run as 9 sequential
alphabetical chunks of 20 dotted test modules (19 in the last), each in the foreground, read from the
process:
- chunk 1 (`test_accesibilidad`..`test_baselines`): `Ran 377 tests in 102.076s ... OK (skipped=1,
  expected failures=1)`
- chunk 2 (`test_baselines_lote`..`test_dispositivo`): `Ran 481 tests in 479.916s ... OK`
- chunk 3 (`test_ejes_fechas`..`test_fechas_semana`): `Ran 318 tests in 126.477s ... OK`
- chunk 4 (`test_fit`..`test_host_backup`): `Ran 502 tests in 498.916s ... OK`
- chunk 5 (`test_host_deploy`..`test_metas_semana_tira`): `Ran 414 tests in 81.504s ... OK`
- chunk 6 (`test_mock_r2_hoy`..`test_primer_dia_1`): `Ran 530 tests in 248.945s ... OK`

## BODY-SYNC-VIVO-2 -- the on-demand pull and the "Tu reloj" freshness read-out (2026-11-16)

Carlos, relayed by the Personal desk, 2026-11-15: "I would like to see more like a live thing in the
app or when I talk to you." BODY-SYNC-VIVO-ESTADO-1 (merged above) built the watch's own last-sync
tracking and the attempt/backoff columns but no on-demand pull and no screen reads them yet. This
slice adds both: a pull that fetches TODAY alone, two triggers that never make Carlos wait for it,
and a plain-worded freshness line on Hoy and through the assistant.

**Ruling 1, as built.** `body/pull.py:pull_hoy_ahora` (389): hosted mode only (`cuenta.hosted()`
false -> `"sin_cuenta"`); the shared per-person lock `_PULL_EN_CURSO` (102, lifted out of
`body/rutas/garmin.py`, which now does `from .. import pull` and reads `pull._PULL_EN_CURSO` --
`body/rutas/garmin.py:_lanzar_pull_conexion` (23) takes the same set, so a live pull and a
connect-triggered one for the same person never overlap); `ESPACIO_MIN_HOY = 15` (86) through
`garmin_cuenta.puede_intentar`; the quiet hours below (ruling 4); records the attempt exactly as the
daily pull does (`garmin_cuenta.registrar_error`/`_registrar_intento_persona`); fetches the one day
through `_pull_one_person` (the SAME fetch path `pull_persona_ahora`'s healing loop uses for one day,
never a copy) -- NOT `_dias_pendientes_relleno`'s healing set, since a live trigger asks for today,
once. After a successful fetch, recomputes ONLY `_recalcular_sueno_fc_seguro` (454): it is the one
post-pull derivation that lands in `daily_metric`, the table `leer_hoy`/`leer_estado_reloj`/Hoy's own
card read; `recuperacion` and `turno_fc` both write to their own tables, read only by the Día and
Turnos screens, neither of which this trigger ever reaches (ruling 2 names the trigger sites), so
recomputing them here would cost real work for a card that never reads their result. Never raises:
the Garmin call sits inside its own try/except that records the error and returns `"iniciado"`
either way; the whole body sits inside a second try/except that catches anything else unexpected
(a DB or timezone failure) the same way, printing a counts-only, class-name-only line
(`errores.texto_seguro`). Opens its own connection with a bare `db.connect()` immediately followed by
the try/finally that closes it (462) -- the same shape `pull_persona_ahora` already uses, and the
shape `tests/test_conexiones_cerradas.py`'s static guard requires of every direct-connect function
under `body/`. Returns `"iniciado"` / `"en_curso"` / `"espera"` / `"sin_cuenta"`, exactly as named.

**Ruling 2, as built.** Hoy: `body/rutas/hoy.py:_debe_lanzar_pull_hoy` (159) checks hosted + connected
+ `puede_intentar`; `today()` (618) takes `background_tasks: BackgroundTasks` and calls
`background_tasks.add_task(pull.pull_hoy_ahora, person_id)` (624) when that check passes, checked
before the "no data yet" early return so the very first live pull can start from the empty state.
The assistant: `body/agente/herramientas.py:HERRAMIENTAS_HOY = frozenset({"leer_hoy",
"leer_estado_reloj"})` (2761, named explicitly as the ruling asked); `_lanzar_pull_hoy_en_hilo` (2764)
checks `cuenta.hosted()` cheaply first (so a local-mode tool call spawns no thread at all), then
`threading.Thread(target=pull.pull_hoy_ahora, args=(person_id,), daemon=True).start()`, never
awaited; `ejecutar()` calls it (2848) right before the `PRAGMA query_only` read, for every tool
named in `HERRAMIENTAS_HOY` -- the answer uses whatever is stored right now and says how fresh it is

TestClient's portal thread needs, so this test waits on the real thread instead, same as

The existing «Reloj sincronizado HH:MM» card (`today.garmin_sync.*`) is unchanged -- this is a second,

## BODY-SYNC-VIVO-TIMER-1 -- a scheduled "today" sweep and a `pull` verb (2026-11-16)

Carlos, relayed verbatim by the Personal desk, 2026-11-15: "I would like to see more like a live
thing in the app or when I talk to you." BODY-SYNC-VIVO-1-INV (OBSERVED) measured that
`body-pull.timer` ran only once a day and that `duna-deploy-body` had no `pull` verb, so a relayed
"pull now" (BODY-DEPLOY-9EEF504) could not run. This slice, on ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1's
approval: a daytime "today" sweep, its own timer, and the `pull` verb.

**Ruling 1, as built.** `body/pull.py:pull_hoy_todos` (417): loops `garmin_cuenta.every_person_id`,
sequential, `time.sleep(PAUSE_S)` before every person after the first. Each person is skipped, no
Garmin call, when `_en_horas_quietas` (the SAME 06:00-23:00-in-their-own-zone check BODY-SYNC-VIVO-2
ruling 4 already uses) is true -> `fuera_horario`, or when `garmin_cuenta.puede_intentar` is false
-> `en_espera`; `puede_intentar` is called with `ESPACIO_MIN_HOY` (15, not the scheduled pulls' own
`ESPACIO_MIN_ENTRE_INTENTOS=0`) so the sweep shares one floor with the on-demand trigger -- the
floor the README's ruling-4 ceiling math relies on. Otherwise runs `_pull_hoy_persona` (394), the
fetch+record+recalc sequence factored OUT of `pull_hoy_ahora` so both callers share one path (never
a copy) -- `pull_hoy_ahora`'s own body (`body/pull.py:510-515`) now just takes `_PULL_EN_CURSO` and
calls it. `python -m body.pull --hoy` (argparse at `body/pull.py:855`; hosted branch at `895`, with
the SAME non-blocking `_try_lock()` --backfill already uses -- a daily pull or a backfill holding
`pull.lock` is a quiet, successful skip, `"another pull is already running; skipping this run."`
at line 888; local-mode refusal at `909`) prints `hoy: N ok, M en espera, K fuera de horario, F
fallidas` (`body/pull.py:897`) -- counts only.

**Ruling 2, as built.** `deploy/host/body-pull-hoy.service` (new): the same `User=duna-body`,
`EnvironmentFile=`, `Type=oneshot` and hardening lines (`NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem=strict`,
`ProtectHome=yes`, `ReadWritePaths`, `PrivateTmp`, `UMask=0077`) as `body-pull.service`, only
`ExecStart=` changed to `python -m body.pull --hoy`. `deploy/host/body-pull-hoy.timer` (new):
`OnCalendar=*-*-* *:00,30:00 UTC` (line 5), `Persistent=false` (6), `RandomizedDelaySec=120` (7) --
every 30 minutes, no catch-up run, spread by up to 2 minutes. Both added to
`deploy/host/body-deploy.sh`'s `UNITS`/`TIMERS` arrays (lines 25-26), so the next `deploy` installs
and `systemctl enable --now`s the new timer with no hand step -- the daily 09:30 full pull and the
backfill timer are unchanged.

**Ruling 3, as built.** `deploy/host/duna-deploy-body`: a `pull` case arm (line 136, no extra args
accepted) and handling block (169-178) that runs `run systemctl start --wait body-pull.service`
(175, masked with `|| estado=$?` so `set -e` cannot swallow a non-zero exit before it is captured --
measured necessary: a bare `estado=$?` after an unmasked failing call would exit the script on that
line, under `set -Eeuo pipefail`, before the journal print ever ran), then
`journalctl -u body-pull --since "$inicio" -o cat` (176, counts and dates only -- the job's own
print lines), then `exit "$estado"` (177) -- the service's own exit status. `usage()` updated (line
28). No sudoers change: the existing line has no argument restriction (confirmed unchanged by
`SudoersTest`).

**Ruling 4, as built.** `deploy/host/README.md`, new "## Pull now" section: Carlos's one-time
reinstall step for the entry script (the same `sudo install -o root -g root -m 755 ...` line as the
existing one-time install, since `duna-deploy-body` itself changed) and the orchestrator's own line,
`sudo -n /usr/local/sbin/duna-deploy-body pull`. The ceiling paragraph: the 30-minute timer lands
inside one person's own 17-hour daytime window at most 34 times a day (17 x 2); the on-demand
trigger can also fire inside that window at most once every 15 minutes (`ESPACIO_MIN_HOY`) -- at
most 68 times a day (17 x 4); both write the same `ultimo_intento_en` column and, after ruling 1,
share that same 15-minute floor, so the two never simply add -- the combined ceiling is the
15-minute floor's own bound over 17 hours, **~68 "today"-pulls a day**, never 34+68. Each
"today"-pull makes 7 Garmin calls (the 6 feeds `garmin_adapter.fetch_day` reads, plus one read of
the watch's own last-sync instant) and a person inside a recorded backoff (2h after a 429, 15min
after a 5xx) makes none until it expires -- ceiling ~68 x 7 = 476 Garmin calls/day/person, a worst
case the window, the shared floor and any backoff keep well under in practice.

**Tests:** `tests/test_sync_vivo_timer.py` (new, 11 tests) -- `pull_hoy_todos`'s branching (outside
the daytime window with no Garmin call, too-soon-since-the-last-attempt and a live backoff both

--, a free person pulled and counted `ok`, a Garmin failure counted `fallidas` and recorded, each
person checked in THEIR OWN configured zone, a pause between people, no connected person is a

`tests/test_host_deploy.py` (9 new tests across `SystemdUnitTest`, a new `PullVerbTest` and a new

## BODY-SYNC-VIVO-2-B -- one "Tu reloj" card, not two (2026-11-16)

The orchestrator's review of BODY-SYNC-VIVO-2 (merged `d04994b`, the only report for that ID) on a
clean `git archive d04994b`: `body/templates/today.html` rendered TWO cards titled "Tu reloj" when
both applied for a hosted person -- the gap card (`garmin_sync`, `today.garmin_sync.titulo`, a chip
and a link to `/garmin`) and the live-freshness card (`reloj_vivo`, new in that same slice,
`reloj_vivo.titulo`, also "Tu reloj"). VIVO-2's own ledger entry had flagged this itself as "a
deliberate, flagged-for-browser-review choice ... can look like two headings saying the same thing
on the same screen." Once a hosted person's watch has ever reported a last-sync time, `pull.
texto_estado_vivo` returns a line on nearly every visit, so a person with any Garmin gap saw both
cards. This slice merges them into one.

**Ruling 1, as built.** `body/templates/_reloj.html` (new shape) is now THE "Tu reloj" card: one
title (`reloj_vivo.titulo`, line 9), then -- when `garmin_sync` applies -- its own chip
(`today.garmin_sync.chip`) right after the title on the same line, then `garmin_sync.texto` (line
10), then `reloj_vivo.texto` beneath it when `reloj_vivo` applies (line 11), then the gap's own link
to `/garmin` (`today.stale_link`, line 12) last. When only one half applies, the other's lines
simply do not render (each wrapped in its own `{% if %}`); when neither applies, nothing inside the
wrapper renders, and `today.html`'s own include is gated on `garmin_sync or reloj_vivo` (line 13)
so the whole card is absent, not a title with no body. `data-sincronizando` (line 8, unchanged)
still names the SAME wrapper element the poll script replaces, so `body/static/reloj-sync.js`
needed no change at all -- its `[data-sincronizando]` selector and swap logic are untouched.
`today.html` (13-14, was 13-21): the old, separate `garmin_sync` card block is gone; one `{% if
garmin_sync or reloj_vivo %}{% include "_reloj.html" %}{% endif %}` line replaces the old
include-plus-separate-card pair, and the poll-script line is unchanged (still gated on `reloj_vivo
and reloj_vivo.sincronizando` alone -- the script only ever needs to run while a pull is actually in
flight, regardless of whether the gap half is also showing).

`body/i18n/es.json` and `en.json`: `today.garmin_sync.titulo` ("Tu reloj" / "Your watch") retired --
the template no longer calls it anywhere, and `tests/test_i18n_paridad.py`'s own literal-key scan
(a static grep over every template and module) confirms nothing else does either. `reloj_vivo.
titulo` is the one surviving title key, read by both halves' own wrapper now.

**The poll route, also ruling 1.** `body/rutas/garmin.py`'s `/garmin/estado-vivo` (`garmin_
estado_vivo`, 143) renders the SAME `_reloj.html` fragment Hoy's `/` does, and the existing
`_reloj_vivo_ctx` docstring (126) already claimed "the two can never render a different card for
the same state" -- true for the freshness half alone, but false for the gap half before this slice,
since the poll never computed `garmin_sync` at all. A new `_garmin_sync_ctx` (106), duplicated from
`body/rutas/hoy.py`'s own function of the same name (the same no-cross-module-import rule this
file's `_reloj_vivo_ctx` already follows for its own duplicate), gives the route the gap half too:
`garmin_estado_vivo` now computes `person`, `today_local` and `day` once (reusing `comun._ctx`'s own
already-fetched `person` instead of the previous second `db.person` call `_reloj_vivo_ctx` used to
make on its own -- `_reloj_vivo_ctx`'s signature changed to take `person` and `today_local` as
params, same shape `hoy.py`'s version already has) and passes both `garmin_sync` and `reloj_vivo`
into the fragment. This closes the one real gap the merge would otherwise have left: without it, a
poll response taken mid-backoff (gap showing, pull not yet re-tried) would have swapped in a card
that silently dropped the chip and the `/garmin` link the instant the fragment re-rendered, even
though the gap state had not changed. `day=None` (a person who has never once had a stored day) is
handled as "not stale" rather than crashing on `date.fromisoformat(None)` -- an edge case Hoy's `/`
can never reach (it returns `soon.html` before ever asking), but this route answers the poll either

## BODY-PLAN-HOY-1 -- Today shows this week of the person's plan (2026-11-16)

**Ruling 1 -- the ONE definition of a plan, in body/horizonte.py.** `es_horizonte(conn, goal_id) ->
bool` and `horizontes(conn, person_id, hoy, *, solo_activos=False) -> list[int]`: a goal is a plan
(a horizon) when it is a `milestone` with no `horizonte_goal_id` of its own AND it carries at least
one plan row -- a child goal, a `horizonte_regla`, a `horizonte_semana`, a `horizonte_meta_semanal`
or a `horizonte_checkpoint`. Both fold the check into one bounded statement via a shared UNION
(`_PLAN_ROW_HORIZONTES`) of the five plan-row tables, never a per-row count. Every caller that used
to decide this on its own now shares it: `body/agente/herramientas.py`'s `_leer_planes` (:2197,
replacing its own `kind = 'milestone' AND horizonte_goal_id IS NULL` query with
`horizonte.horizontes(conn, person_id, hoy)`) and `body/rutas/metas.py`'s goal-detail route (:678,
`g["kind"] == "milestone" and horizonte.es_horizonte(conn, goal_id)` in place of the local
`_es_horizonte`, now removed). `horizonte.resumen` also carries `start_day` in its returned dict
(additive, zero extra cost -- the goal row is already fetched), which Today's own week-count card
needs and no existing caller's behaviour depends on its absence. A plain milestone with no plan row
is not listed as a plan anywhere; `ampliar_plan`'s own target check (herramientas.py `_ampliar_plan`
:2374, `kind = 'milestone'` only) is unchanged, so a milestone still grows into a plan the same way.
Tests: `tests/test_horizonte.py`'s `EsHorizonteTest` (9 tests: each of the five plan-row kinds makes
it a horizon, a metric goal never is, a horizon's own child is not itself a horizon even carrying a
plan row of its own, an unknown id is false) and `HorizontesTest` (6 tests: excludes a plain
milestone, lists a real horizon, excludes another person's private one, includes a shared household
one, active-then-newest ordering, `solo_activos`'s status+span filter) plus `ResumenHouseholdTest`'s
new `test_start_day_is_carried_through`.

**Ruling 2 -- "Tu plan esta semana" / "Your plan this week".** `body/rutas/hoy.py`'s `today()`
route, right after the day-ahead card (`today.plan_title`), shown only when
`horizonte.horizontes(conn, person_id, today_local, solo_activos=True)` is non-empty. One block per
active plan, at most `PLANES_HOY_MAX = 2` (a named constant); beyond it, one line "y N planes más" /
"and N more plans" linking to `/goals`. Each block, built ONLY from `horizonte.resumen` (`_plan_
semana_bloque`, `_plan_semana_ctx` -- the route queries no `horizonte_*` table and recomputes
nothing): the plan title linking to `/goals/{id}`; "Semana N de M" (Monday-based, from `resumen`'s
own `start_day` to `deadline`) and "faltan D días" / "{n} days left" (singular "falta 1 día" / "1
day left", or "termina hoy" / "ends today" at zero); this week's weekly lines as counts by estado
(`cumple`/`en_curso`/`no_cumple`/`sin_dato`), non-zero estados only, each a `<span class="chip
{ok|warn|low|off}">` reusing the existing chip colours (`_PLAN_ESTADO_CLS`, duplicated from
metas.py's own private mapping rather than imported, since `body/rutas/comun.py` -- the shared-
plumbing home -- is outside this slice's touches), singular via the repo's own `_one` key
convention, every key a literal `t(...)` call (never an f-string) so `tests/test_i18n_paridad.py`'s
scan sees each one; the next checkpoint only within 7 days ("Chequeo el 7 dic: <título>" /
"Checkpoint on Dec 7: <title>", reusing `_dia_mes`'s existing "D mon" formatter); the honest gap --
a week with no weekly lines says "Sin metas del plan esta semana" / "No targets in the plan this
week" (reworded from the spec's own suggested "...no tiene metas" wording: `tests/test_registro_tu.py`,
outside this slice's touches, correctly flagged third-person "tiene" with no allow-list entry, and
rewording stayed inside `es.json` rather than widening touches to add one). No figure of the person
beyond the counts; the detail stays on goal detail (BODY-PLAN-PANTALLA-1). 17 new i18n keys per
language (`today.plan_semana.*`).

**Ruling 3 -- bounded, proven, and a performance correction found along the way.** `tests/
test_rendimiento.py`'s new `PlanHoyCostIndependentOfSpanTest` (2 tests) proves "/" costs the
identical statement count for a 1-week vs. a 12-week horizon, and for a 1-line vs. an 8-line current
week -- `horizonte.semana`/`checkpoints`'s own per-week scoping (BODY-PLAN-MODULO-1) carries
through unchanged. **The "at most one extra statement for a person with no plan" requirement
surfaced a real cost bug while building `horizontes()`:** following ruling 1's own description
("the goals the person can see by `goals.goal_scope_sql`") literally -- calling
`household.household_of` then `goals.goal_scope_sql` the way every other caller does -- cost TWO
statements even for a person with no household (the household lookup, then the listing), measured
directly by calling `hoy._plan_semana_ctx` against a minimal no-plan fixture before this fix: 2
statements, not 1. Fixed by folding the household-visibility check into the SAME statement as a
scalar subquery (`hogar_id = (SELECT hogar_id FROM hogar_miembro WHERE person_id = ?)`) instead of
a separate `household.household_of` round trip -- a person with no `hogar_miembro` row makes the
subquery NULL, and `hogar_id = NULL` is never true, so the household branch drops out on its own,
the identical net effect `goal_scope_sql` gets by omitting that SQL text entirely. Re-measured after
the fix: exactly 1 statement for a no-plan person (confirmed directly against `hoy._plan_semana_ctx`
on a minimal fixture: person 1, no horizon, no household row). `tests/test_horizonte.py`'s
`HorizontesTest.test_shared_household_horizon_is_included` still passes unchanged, proving the
inlined subquery is behaviourally identical to the two-call form for the case that matters (a real
shared household horizon).

**Measured ceiling.** `/`'s own ceiling moved from 112 to 155 (`tests/test_rendimiento.py`): with
this file's own `_seed()` fixture (one active plan, the demo's own horizon from BODY-PLAN-PANTALLA-1),

**Ruling 4 -- the demo's existing plan is active today; no demo change needed.** The demo's horizon
(BODY-PLAN-PANTALLA-1's `_seed_plan_horizonte`) spans `anchor_monday - 3 weeks` to `anchor_monday +

filter passes without any seed change. Confirmed directly: the demo fixture's "/" renders "Tu plan
esta semana" with the seeded horizon's own title, "Semana 4 de 9" and its weekly-line counts, with
no change to `body/demo.py` (outside this slice's touches, and not needed).

**New tests**, invented demo data only, never a real figure:
