## BODY-PLAN-SESION-HECHA-1 -- a done planned training session counts once (2026-11-16)

**The gap, as measured.** BODY-PLAN-PANTALLA-1's own merge (queue/pending.txt, 2026-11-12) flagged
it and it was still open on main `732d731`: the plan's `sesiones_fuerza` count read only `activity`
rows (`body/horizonte.py`'s `_real_medida`, the branch at the then-line 263-265, backed by
`entreno_racha.sesiones_fuerza` via `_recopilar_datos`'s `"fuerza"` key, :198/:240 before this
slice), so a `plan` row the person marked done (`status = 'done'`, `body/db.py:536`) with no watch
or manual `activity` behind it counted 0 beside its own "Hecho" chip -- true on main even for the
demo horizon's own Tuesday session (`body/demo.py`'s `_seed_plan_horizonte`, title "Entrenamiento
de fuerza" / "Strength training", `status = 'done'`, no `ejercicios_json` at all, so it would still
count 0 after this slice too -- `demo.py` is outside this slice's `touches`; the exact shape is
reproduced instead in this slice's own test,
`test_the_demo_horizons_hecho_row_now_counted`, with `ejercicios_json` added so it demonstrates the
fix). Body's rule: "measured first, the person's word second, never twice."

**Ruling 1/2 -- the union, in `body/entreno_racha.py`'s new `con_plan_hecho(sesiones, dias_plan)`
(:89-101).** Pure function, no database: `sesiones` is this module's own measured classification
(`sesiones_fuerza`'s own return shape, `{'day': date, 'start_local': str | None}`); `dias_plan` is
every day carrying a done `plan` row with exercises. A day already in `sesiones` is left exactly as
measured -- the watch's record standing as given, never doubled; a day with no measured session
gets one synthetic entry per such plan-row day, so two done rows the same day with no watch session
count twice (`dias_plan` is a plain list, one entry per row, not a set). The docstring states
ruling 2 verbatim: a plan row with no exercises, or any plan row at all for a cardio measure, never
reaches this function -- it has no exercises to say what was done, and a plan row can only ever
stand in for a STRENGTH session.

**Ruling 3 -- one place, in `body/horizonte.py`.** Chosen over `entreno_racha.py` because the
union needs the `plan` table (horizonte.py's own domain -- `plan_vs_real` already reads it for
`planes_por_dia`) alongside the measured classifier; `entreno_racha.con_plan_hecho` stays a pure,
database-free function so `entreno_racha.py` itself never reads `plan`. New `_planes_hechos_fuerza`
(:226-236): one statement, `SELECT day FROM plan WHERE person_id = ? AND status = 'done' AND
ejercicios_json IS NOT NULL AND day BETWEEN ? AND ?` -- never scoped to one horizon's `goal_id`,
the same way a measured session isn't (a done session is a fact about the person's day, regardless
of which plan, or none, it was written under). `_recopilar_datos` (:239-262) now also returns
`"fuerza_con_plan"`: `entreno_racha.con_plan_hecho(fuerza, _planes_hechos_fuerza(...))`, computed
once per call alongside the existing `"fuerza"` (left unchanged, still measured-only -- the day-
level rule chequeos `sin_sesion`/`sesion_antes_de` keep reading it as before, out of this slice's
rulings). `_real_medida`'s `sesiones_fuerza` branch (:283-288) now sums over `datos["fuerza_con_
plan"]` instead of `datos["fuerza"]` -- its only change. Since `plan_vs_real`, `semana`,
`checkpoints` and `resumen` all go through `_recopilar_datos` -> `_real_medida` for this measure,
and Today's "Tu plan esta semana" card (`body/rutas/hoy.py`'s `_plan_semana_ctx` ->
`horizonte.resumen`) is itself built only from `resumen`, every one of them sees the union with no
change of its own. `entreno_racha.racha_semanal` (the watch's own weekly streak,
`BODY-ENTRENO-RACHA-SEMANAL-1`) reads no `plan` row at all, before or after this slice -- a
separate subject, confirmed by a new test
(`tests/test_entreno_racha.py::RachaSemanalTest::test_a_done_plan_row_with_exercises_never_feeds_the_racha`).

**Ruling 4 -- cost.** Exactly one extra statement per `_recopilar_datos` call (the new
`_planes_hechos_fuerza` read), the same one call `plan_vs_real`/`semana`/`checkpoints` already made
once per range before this slice. `tests/test_rendimiento.py`'s ceilings (all relative-count or
margin-based, none an exact statement count for this path) and its two
`CostIndependentOfSpanTest` classes (equal-statement-count assertions, both sides of each
comparison paying the identical +1) all stayed green unmodified.

**Tests.** New `tests/test_plan_sesion_hecha.py` (15 tests): done+exercises alone -> 1
(`DonePlanRowCountsAsAStrengthSessionTest`, including the demo-shape reproduction above);
done-without-exercises, skipped-with-exercises, proposed-with-exercises and accepted-with-
exercises -> 0; a measured session plus a done plan row the same day -> still the measured count,
not +1 (`MeasuredSessionWinsTest`, 4 tests, including two done rows with no measured session -> 2
and a done plan row on a different day adding its own count); a done plan row never counts toward
`sesiones_cardio` (`CardioStaysMeasuredOnlyTest`); `con_plan_hecho` exercised directly with no
database (`ConPlanHechoUnitTest`, 4 tests). One addition to `tests/test_entreno_racha.py` (the
racha-isolation test above). `tests/test_horizonte.py`, `tests/test_plan_pantalla.py` and
`tests/test_plan_hoy.py` needed no change -- none of their existing fixtures carry a done `plan`
row with `ejercicios_json`, so the union is additive and silent for them; they are listed here
because they were read and re-run green, not because they changed.

## BODY-CONSENTIMIENTO-V4 -- consent widens to v4, names each activity's full detail and minute-by-minute (2026-11-16)

Carlos, typed in the Body orchestrator 2026-11-15, asked whether Body should keep every activity's full
heart-rate curve and laps, and every night minute by minute: "Yes, everything, man." BODY-MINUTO-A-MINUTO-1-INV
(OBSERVED) found that the v3 clause (`privacidad.consentimiento.que`, widened by `7a3047e`
BODY-EXPERIMENTOS-CONSENTIMIENTO-1) covers set detail always but per-minute pulse/stress ONLY on experiment
days, and nothing per activity -- storing per-activity curves, laps, zones and per-minute nights needs a
consent widening first.

**Ruling 1, the version.** `CONSENT_VERSION = "consentimiento-v4"` (`body/privacidad.py:17`). Every hosted
person who accepted v3 or earlier is asked once by the existing gate (`body/identity.py:60`, unchanged) --
nothing in `body/identity.py` changes. Accepted rows of older versions stay in the `consentimiento` table as
history; export and delete-all already cover it.

**Ruling 2, the new clause, verbatim** -- `privacidad.consentimiento.que` (`body/i18n/es.json:525`,
`body/i18n/en.json:525`):
- es: "Guardamos las cifras de tu reloj. Cada día: sueño (con el oxígeno en sangre y la respiración de la
  noche), pulso, variabilidad del pulso, estrés, Body Battery y actividades. De cada actividad, su detalle
  completo: la curva de pulso de principio a fin, las vueltas (laps), el tiempo en cada zona de pulso y, en la
  fuerza, las series, repeticiones y peso. De cada noche, el sueño minuto a minuto: pulso, variabilidad, fases,
  movimiento y oxígeno. Y de cada día, tu pulso y estrés minuto a minuto, para poner junto a ellos lo que
  hiciste. Si los agregas, también tu calendario de turnos, tus metas, tus hábitos, tus experimentos, los
  momentos que anotas (como una ducha fría o una respiración) y las medidas que registras tú, como la
  flexibilidad o el ronquido."
- en: "We keep your watch's figures. Every day: sleep (with blood oxygen and breathing at night), heart rate,
  heart rate variability, stress, Body Battery and activities. For each activity, its full detail: the
  heart-rate curve from start to finish, the laps, the time in each heart-rate zone and, for strength, the
  sets, reps and weight. For each night, sleep minute by minute: heart rate, variability, stages, movement and
  oxygen. And for each day, your heart rate and stress minute by minute, so what you did can sit beside them.
  If you add them, also your shift calendar, your goals, your habits, your experiments, the moments you log
  (like a cold shower or a breathing round) and the measures you record yourself, like flexibility or
  snoring."
  `por_que`, `donde`, `derechos`, `no_medico`, `aceptar`, `no_aceptar`, `al_no_aceptar` are byte-for-byte
  unchanged.

**Ruling 3, "what changed, said once."** `privacidad.consentimiento.cambio` (`body/i18n/es.json:526`,
`body/i18n/en.json:526`):
- es: "Actualizamos lo que guardamos: ahora también el detalle completo de cada actividad, y tu sueño y tu
  día minuto a minuto. Léelo y acepta de nuevo para seguir."
- en: "We've updated what we keep: now also each activity's full detail, and your sleep and your day minute
  by minute. Read it and accept again to continue."
  `body/privacidad.py:114` `acepto_version_anterior(conn, person_id)` is True when the person has an accepted
  row of any version OTHER than the current one. `body/rutas/privacidad.py:46-47`'s `consentimiento_form`
  calls it and passes a bare `cambio` flag; `body/templates/consentimiento.html:18` reads only that flag,
  styled with the existing `.aviso` notice class (used already by `day.html`/`today.html`) -- no inline style,
  no new CSS. A first-time person (no prior row at all) sees no notice.

**Ruling 4, `guarda_detalle`.** `body/privacidad.py:124` `guarda_detalle(conn, person_id)`: True in local mode
(`cuenta.hosted()` false), else `has_consented(conn, person_id, "consentimiento-v4")` -- pinned to the
literal string, never to `CONSENT_VERSION`, so a later v5 widening never silently changes what v4 already
granted. Nothing calls it yet; BODY-ENTRENO-DETALLE-1 will.

**Tests, `tests/test_consentimiento_v4.py` (new, imports `tests/_isolate.py` first):**
`ConsentPageChangeNoticeTest` -- a v3-only hosted person sees the `cambio` line on the consent page; a

`GuardaDetalleTest` -- false for a v3-only hosted person, true once v4 is accepted.
`GuardaDetalleLocalModeTest` -- true in local mode with no consent row at all.

`tests/test_privacidad.py`'s `ConsentTextNamesTheNewDataTest` (the test the spec named at its old line 218)

## BODY-ENTRENO-DETALLE-1 -- each activity's full heart-rate curve, laps and zones; the day and night minute by minute (GATE_RED, not merged)

Carlos's two quotes, typed in the Body orchestrator, verbatim. 2026-11-15: "Remember my idea of matching my
heart rate to every activity that I did in the day, to match it exactly, to see the metrics on how I perform
in each training session or cardio session." Asked the same day whether Body should keep every activity's
full heart-rate curve and laps, and every night minute by minute: "Yes, everything, man."

**BODY-MINUTO-A-MINUTO-1-INV's findings, in brief.** `activity` is a summary only (`body/db.py:395-415` on
main); a day's per-minute HR/stress lived in `raw_payload` under kinds `intradia_fc`/`intradia_estres`
(`db.py:2175-2243` on main), fetched only for days an experiment needed. garminconnect 0.3.20 offers
`get_activity_details` (maxchart default 2000), `get_activity_splits` (laps) and
`get_activity_hr_in_timezones` (zones), one call each. It recommended a raw-blob activity-detail table parsed
on read (the intradia precedent: a parser fix never needs a re-pull) and found `privacidad.guarda_detalle`
already built by BODY-CONSENTIMIENTO-V4 (merged before this slice ran, verified at Step 0:
`body/privacidad.py:124`) with "nothing calls this yet" -- this slice is its first caller.

**Ruling 1, storage.** `body/db.py:434` `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS activity_detail` -- `(person_id,
activity_source, activity_source_id, kind, fetched_at, payload)`, PRIMARY KEY on the first four, `kind` CHECK
IN ('detalle', 'vueltas', 'zonas'), added to `SCHEMA`'s own `executescript` (runs on every `init()` call,
`IF NOT EXISTS`, so an existing home gains the table with no `_migrate` step needed -- the same route
`horizonte_regla` and friends used, BODY-PLAN-ESQUEMA-1, the newest prior table addition). Functions:
`guardar_detalle_actividad` (`db.py:2304`), `detalle_actividad_almacenado` (`:2321`, true once all three
kinds are present, including as an explicit empty marker), `detalle_actividad` (`:2334`, parsed on read
through the adapter's own parser), `actividades_sin_detalle` (`:2356`, `source = garmin_adapter.SOURCE` only
-- a manual session has no Garmin id and is never listed -- newest day first). `body/privacidad.py:75` adds
`"activity_detail"` to `FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES` (full export, unlike `raw_payload`'s own
PARTIAL_EXPORT_TABLES: this is the person's own per-activity detail, the thing BODY-CONSENTIMIENTO-V4's "yes,
everything, man" named); `export_person` gains `detalle_actividades` (`:231`); `delete_person` deletes it
(`:456`) before `activity`/`workout_set`, the same FK-order reasoning those two already carry.

**Ruling 2, the fetch.** `body/garmin_adapter.py:416` `fetch_activity_detail(activity_id, token_str=None)`:
`get_activity_details`, `get_activity_splits`, `get_activity_hr_in_timezones`, one call each, the
`fetch_intraday` `_errors` pattern (one failing call never loses the other two), the same dual-return token
shape as `fetch_exercise_sets`. `ActivityDetailData` (`:112`).

**Ruling 3, the parsers (pure, in the adapter -- every assumed key named).**
`parse_activity_hr_series(payload, zone)` (`:874`): `metricDescriptors` (the SAME `{"key", "index"}` shape
the day-level intraday descriptors already use -- reuses `_descriptor_index`/`_heart_rate_valid` unmodified,
never a positional fallback for this unconfirmed endpoint) and `activityDetailMetrics[].metrics[]`; the
timestamp is a GMT instant via `_utc_to_local_iso`. `Lap` (`:124`) and `parse_laps(payload, zone)` (`:941`):
assumed keys `lapDTOs`, `lapIndex`, `startTimeGMT`, `duration`, `averageHR`, `maxHR` -- `startTimeGMT` through
the new `_gmt_value_to_local_iso` (`:917`, epoch-ms tried first, then a GMT string with no offset).
`parse_hr_zones(payload)` (`:968`): assumed keys `zoneNumber`, `secsInZone`, `zoneLowBoundary`, a bare list or
one wrapped under `hrTimeInZones`. None of these six endpoint-and-key assumptions is confirmed by the
installed garminconnect 0.3.20 package (typed only as `dict[str, Any]`, no docstring naming a key) -- same
unconfirmed-shape documentation style as `parse_exercise_sets`/`_weight`/`_start_local`. Malformed input is
always the empty tuple, never an exception (tested in `tests/test_entreno_detalle.py`).

**Ruling 4, the fill.** `body/pull.py:856` `traer_detalle_actividad(conn, person_id, source_id,
token_str=None)`: stores only the kinds `ActivityDetailData.raw` actually holds (a failed call's kind is
simply absent, retried by a later run). `body/pull.py:879` `_pull_detalle_pendientes`: `privacidad.
guarda_detalle` false -> no Garmin call, returns 0; else up to `DETALLE_MAX_POR_CORRIDA = 10` (`:96`) of
`db.actividades_sin_detalle(conn, person_id, hoy - DETALLE_ALCANCE_DIAS)` (`DETALLE_ALCANCE_DIAS = 90`,
`:101`), a failure on one logged with `errores.texto_seguro` and never stopping the others, token persisted
the `_pull_intradia_pendientes` way, prints `detalle: N actividades traídas, M pendientes`. Called right
after `_pull_intradia_pendientes` in `pull_hosted` (re-reading the token first, since that call may just have
refreshed and persisted it) and in the local CLI `_run`.

**Ruling 5, the day minute by minute, every day.** `body/pull.py:798` `_dias_intradia_necesarios_todos` --
lives in `pull.py` (not `experimentos.py`): it needs `pull`'s own `INTRADIA_ALCANCE_DIAS` and `privacidad`,
and its only caller, `_pull_intradia_pendientes`, already lives here. Unions `experimentos.
dias_intradia_necesarios`'s own experiment days with, only when `guarda_detalle` agrees, every day from
`hoy - INTRADIA_ALCANCE_DIAS` to yesterday not yet `db.intradia_almacenado`, sorted newest-first as one
combined set (not two concatenated newest-first parts, which would not be globally sorted).
`_pull_intradia_pendientes` itself is otherwise unchanged -- still just caps at `INTRADIA_MAX_POR_CORRIDA` and
fetches. A person with neither an active experiment nor agreement makes no intraday call
(`tests/test_pull.py`'s `test_no_active_experiment_and_no_agreement_makes_no_intraday_garmin_call`, local and
hosted).

**Ruling 6, nights.** `body/garmin_adapter.py:1016` `parse_sleep_series(payload, zone)`: five assumed arrays
(`:1007` `_SLEEP_SERIES_SPECS`) -- `sleepHeartRate`/`hrvData`/`sleepLevels`/`sleepMovement` each keyed
`startGMT`+its own value field, `wellnessEpochSPO2DataDTOList` keyed `epochTimestamp`/`spo2Reading` (a
different underlying sensor pipeline, hence the different key names) -- none confirmed by garminconnect
0.3.20's `typed.py:229-236`, which names no per-sample key at all, only that these arrays "are large and
rarely needed in typed form." Returns only the arrays actually present and non-empty. `body/db.py:2371`
`sueno_minuto_a_minuto(conn, person_id, day, zona)` reads the day's already-stored `kind='sleep'`
`raw_payload` row -- no fetch of its own. No screen.

**Ruling 7, cost (synthetic data, sizes only).** One 60-minute activity's three payloads at 2000 samples:
`detalle` alone is 70,130 bytes at a minimal 2-column shape (timestamp + heart rate, what this slice's own
parser reads) or 226,465 bytes at a more realistic ~15-column shape (speed, distance, elevation, cadence,
etc., commonly present on an outdoor activity but not read by any parser here); `vueltas` (8 laps) 1,213
bytes; `zonas` (5 zones) 320 bytes -- one activity totals 71,663 to 227,998 bytes. A full day's two intraday
kinds (~720 heart-rate + ~480 stress samples, the existing minute-ish sampling convention): 15,240 +
10,208 = 25,448 bytes. 90 days: intraday alone (every day) is ~2.18 MiB; activity_detail alone (one
activity/day) is 6.15-19.57 MiB; combined, ~8.34-21.75 MiB added to the database, and the same to a backup of
it.

## BODY-MCP-HTTP-1

Carlos, relayed by the Personal desk, 2026-11-16: *"I don't want you to connect with the body version
local. I want you to fully build a real connection to all my production apps ... you'll be the brain of
the smart home ... So you should live with the apps."*

A new, real MCP-over-HTTP endpoint -- `https://body.duna.solutions/mcp` -- that any MCP client (a Claude
session, not only Body's own PC) adds by URL plus a Cuenta Duna assistant key, with no Body code running
on the client's own machine at all.

**Ruling 1 -- the endpoint itself**, `body/rutas/mcp_http.py` (new, 232 lines), `POST /mcp` (`:176-232`):
the MCP "Streamable HTTP" transport (spec 2025-03-26) in its stateless form -- one JSON-RPC request or
batch per POST, one `application/json` response, no SSE, no session id. `GET /mcp` answers 405 with
`Allow: POST`, Starlette's own default since the router registers POST only. `initialize` (`:137-147`),
`notifications/initialized` (`:148-149`), `ping` (`:150-151`), `tools/list` (`:152-155`), `tools/call`
(`:156-170`) in `_procesar_uno` (`:126-173`). Registered in `body/web.py:30,125`
(`app.include_router(mcp_http.router)`, directly after the existing device-key door's own router).

**Ruling 2 -- auth, and one dispatch for two doors.** Auth is Cuenta Duna introspection
(`body/llave_asistente.py`, new, 139 lines), never `body/dispositivo.py`'s device-key table, which stays
the existing hosted door's own auth unchanged. `verificar()` (`:102-138`) posts to
`{cuenta.issuer()}/oauth/introspect` (`_post_introspect`, `:89-93`) with Body's own client credentials,
caches only a positive answer for `CACHE_TTL_SEGUNDOS = 60.0` seconds keyed by the key's own sha256
(`:83-87`, never the key itself), and raises `LlaveInvalida` / `PersonaSinBody` / `CuentaNoDisponible`
(`:39-62`) for every other case -- wrong `producto`, unknown `permiso`, no `person.cuenta_sub` match
(`_resolver_person_id`, `:95-100`), Cuenta unreachable or answering 401/429/5xx. A resolved key's
`permiso` (`lectura`/`escritura`) governs everything downstream: `puede_escribir = permiso ==
"escritura"`, and that SAME boolean stands in for `puede_aplicar` here (`mcp_http.py:207-208`) -- the
person's own `aplicar_mcp` setting never gates this endpoint; a write the escritura permission allows
applies directly (`auto_aplicar=puede_escribir`, `mcp_http.py:165`), with no separate "tap Aplicar" step
this caller cannot take anyway. One dispatch, two doors: the existing hosted door's own logic was lifted
into two shared functions in `body/rutas/mcp_remoto.py` -- `listar_herramientas` (`:45-60`) and
`llamar_herramienta` (`:62-97`, the `auto_aplicar` parameter is new) -- and both `mcp_remoto.py`'s own
routes and the new `/mcp` now call them, so the existing door's wire shape is unchanged (its own tests,
untouched, still pass).

**Ruling 3 -- read fresh, never cached on a long-lived session.** `body/mcp.py`'s `_Sesion.puede_aplicar`
is now a `@property` (`:224-226`) reading `db.get_aplicar_mcp` on every access rather than once at
construction, so turning the setting off takes effect on this process's very next `tools/list` or
`tools/call`. `_SesionRemota` gained the same property (`:331-335`), with its constructor's new
`puede_aplicar: bool | None = None` parameter (`:312-313`) defaulting to "read the DB fresh" so the one
pre-existing 3-arg call site (`tests/test_sync_vivo.py:326`) stays unchanged.

**Ruling 4 -- the contract doc.** `docs/contracts/mcp-http-v1.md` (new, 92 lines): what the endpoint is,
the `claude mcp add --transport http body https://body.duna.solutions/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer
<key>"` command, the auth outcomes (401/503/404), the lectura/escritura table, the method table, what
stays unchanged on the existing device-key door.

**Ruling 5 -- the test list.** `tests/test_llave_asistente.py` (new, 206 lines, 16 tests):
`_post_introspect` request shape, every outcome (active/inactive/wrong-producto/unknown-permiso/
non-string persona_id/unparseable JSON/no matching `person`), Cuenta faults (timeout/500/401/429, never
cached), the 60s cache TTL and revocation. `tests/test_mcp_http.py` (new, 322 lines, 31 tests): local
mode 404, GET→405+Allow, every auth failure with its own message, the full JSON-RPC surface including
batches and parse errors, the lectura/escritura split (a lectura key never sees write tools; an escritura
key's write calls apply directly with `aplicar_mcp` off), parity with the stdio door's own tool list,
cross-person isolation, and a log-capture test proving no key, hash, or persona_id ever reaches a log
line. `tests/test_persona_fuga.py` (`_seed_person` now links `person.cuenta_sub` and carries an assistant
key, `:114-120,326-336`; the foreign-marker sweep now also calls `POST /mcp`, `:543-...`).
`tests/test_web_entry.py:100` adds `/mcp`'s own row to the route census -- never exempted.

**Two measured corrections during the gate**, neither changing any ruling above:

1. `tests/test_conexiones_cerradas.py` (outside `touches:`, read-only) requires every router module
   with a route to call `comun._ctx(` under its own `@comun._cierra_conexion_async`, or sit in a
   hardcoded allowlist this slice could not extend. `/mcp` genuinely has no `person_id` before Cuenta
   answers, so it closes one short-lived `db.connect()` for the auth step alone (`mcp_http.py:192-204`,
   satisfying the file's OTHER guard, `DirectConnectClosesInFinallyTest`), then uses `comun._ctx(
   person_id)` for everything after (`mcp_http.py:209`). Commit `29d405f`.
2. `tests/test_mcp_cliente_remoto.py` (outside `touches:`, read-only) calls
   `mcp._error_remoto_a_rehuso(sesion, nombre, data)` directly with a real `_SesionCliente`. An earlier
   version of this slice had changed that function's signature to take a bare `idioma` string, which
   broke those 11 tests (wrong-language text). Reverted `_error_remoto_a_rehuso` to its original
   signature (`mcp.py:408`, unchanged); `mcp_http.py`'s own `_mensaje_error` instead builds a throwaway
   `_SesionCliente()` just to carry `.idioma` (`mcp_http.py:100-102`). Commit `516637b`.

## BODY-MCP-HTTP-1-M

Resolves `BODY-MCP-HTTP-1`'s AWAITING_APPROVAL stop above on the customer-facing-bytes condition, for the
two 401 message strings only (the wire-contract condition on `docs/contracts/mcp-http-v1.md` is unchanged
and not touched by this slice). Merge authorisation: the orchestrator, under
`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`, reviewed the person-facing text on the branch
(`body/rutas/mcp_http.py:49-54` at the time) and supplied the approval itself, with two wording fixes --
`_MENSAJE_401` said "Clave" where Cuenta Duna's own screen says "Llaves de asistente" (one word for one
thing across Duna), and `_MENSAJE_401_SIN_PERSONA`'s Spanish half spoke about "nadie" in the third person
instead of to the reader, against Body's tu register. Carlos's go for the deploy that will carry this
(`BODY-DEPLOY-2`; this slice does not deploy), relayed verbatim by the Personal desk 2026-11-16: "Push
everything, deploy everything, and keep working on everything. See you in a couple of hours."

**The two strings, before and after** (`body/rutas/mcp_http.py:49` and `:50-54`):

Before:
```
_MENSAJE_401 = "Clave de asistente inválida o ausente. / Missing or invalid assistant key."
_MENSAJE_401_SIN_PERSONA = (
    "Esta clave es válida, pero nadie ha iniciado sesión todavía en Body con esa misma cuenta: "
    "entra a Body una vez con Cuenta Duna para enlazarla. / This key is valid, but nobody has "
    "signed in to Body yet with that same account: sign in to Body once with Cuenta Duna to link it."
)
```

After:
```
_MENSAJE_401 = "Llave de asistente inválida o ausente. / Missing or invalid assistant key."
_MENSAJE_401_SIN_PERSONA = (
    "Esta llave es válida, pero todavía no has entrado a Body con esa cuenta: entra una vez a "
    "Body con Cuenta Duna para vincularla. / This key is valid, but you haven't signed in to "
    "Body with that account yet: sign in to Body once with Cuenta Duna to link it."
)
```

No test asserted the old wording; the contract doc does not quote either string, so neither needed a
follow-on change.

## BODY-HOGAR-TURNOS-1

The Personal desk, 2026-11-16, for Hogar (duna-hogar `ee37577`): Hogar's app runs on the host and has no
shifts, because his schedule lives on his PC; Body's server already holds them (the `shift` table,
`body/db.py:446-455`). The ask: the shifts in the Hogar feed, same `hogar:leer` scope, in the ~18 Nov deploy.
Carlos's standing rule, relayed verbatim by the desk 2026-11-16 and recorded as
`BODY-APPS-SIN-RESTRICCIONES-1` (Main: `ORCH-CARLOS-SUS-DATOS-ENTRE-APPS-1`): "It's all me. It's all my own
Duna servers, and I'm my own user, my own data. So, drop every restriction. Allow free communication between
all of them." -- so no new consent and no new scope, the `hogar:leer` key is the one standing grant
(`BODY-SERVICIO-HOGAR-1`, `docs/contracts/hogar-feed-v1.md`).

**BODY-HOGAR-EJERCICIOS-1 folded in:** Hogar, 2026-11-16, for its TV page (duna-hogar `472527d`), relayed
verbatim by the desk: "knowing the plan of the workout for today ... leg day or chest day or back day,
showing there the exercises, maybe through body app interface, if possible showing the TV."

**Ruling 1, `turnos` on `manana` (`body/hogar_feed.py:85` `turnos_alrededor`, wired at `:142`):** every shift
touching `dia` -- rows with `day` = `dia` or `dia`+1, plus a row with `day` = `dia`-1 whose `end_local` is
`>= dia` (last night's shift still running this morning; ISO-formatted local datetimes compare correctly as
plain text for this test). One SQL statement, `person_id` in the WHERE, `ORDER BY day, start_local` (SQLite
sorts NULL before any value in ascending order, giving "nulls first" with no extra expression). Empty list
when none, never omitted or null.

**Ruling 2, `GET /api/hogar/turnos?desde=&hasta=` (`body/rutas/dispositivos.py:227-242`, new):** same
`hogar:leer` dependency, same `Cache-Control: no-store`, same validation as `/api/hogar/serie` (bad date or
`hasta < desde` -> 400, over 366 days -> 400). `hogar_feed.turnos` (`:112`) does the range-length check and
shapes `{"desde", "hasta", "turnos"}`; `turnos_rango` (`:101`) is the one-SQL read, same ordering as
`turnos_alrededor`. No shift in range is not an error -- an empty list.

**Item shape, everywhere (`turnos_alrededor`/`turnos_rango`'s own `SELECT`):** `{"day", "kind", "code",
"start_local", "end_local"}` -- the `shift` row's own column names, values as stored, null stays null. No
`source`, no person id.

**Ruling 5 (BODY-HOGAR-EJERCICIOS-1), `ejercicios` on plan rows (`_plan_dias`, `body/hogar_feed.py:46-60`):**
each row's own `ejercicios_json` (`body/db.py:558`) parsed with `json.loads` and passed verbatim -- the exact
list `planear_entreno` stores (`ejercicio`/`series` always present, `reps`/`categoria` when given,
`body/agente/herramientas.py:226-231`) -- or `null` when the column is null. No reshaping, no renaming, no
added keys; the five existing plan-row keys (`id`, `day`, `time`, `title`, `status`) are unchanged.

**Contract doc (`docs/contracts/hogar-feed-v1.md`):** an additive "Turnos" section (item shape, both routes,
the `dia`-1 night rule, `kind`'s vocabulary, ordering) plus a line under the plan-row keys for `ejercicios`.
Says explicitly this is still v1: a new key or a new route is not a breaking change.

**Tests (`tests/test_hogar_feed.py`, 46 tests total, 21 new):** `MananaTest` -- `ejercicios` verbatim vs.
null with the other plan-row keys checked exactly; a `dia`-1 night shift ending on `dia` included, one ending
before `dia` excluded; `dia`+1 included, `dia`+2 not; an `off` row with null times included; empty list when

## BODY-HOGAR-ESCRIBE-1

The Personal desk, relayed verbatim 2026-11-16, for a Hogar feature that detects who is cooking or
eating and registers meals and training-session feedback into Body, asking for missing data per
person. Carlos's standing rule `BODY-APPS-SIN-RESTRICCIONES-1` applies: "It's all me ... drop every
restriction. Allow free communication between all of them." This slice is the schema and tool half
only -- routes and screens are BODY-HOGAR-ESCRIBE-2.

**Ruling 1, origin 'hogar' (`body/db.py`):** `propuesta_agente.aplicada_via` and
`conversacion_agente.origen` both widen their CHECK from `('mcp')` to `('mcp', 'hogar')`, via the
existing guarded table-rebuild pattern -- `_rebuild_conversacion_agente_table` (`body/db.py:1453`),
and `propuesta_agente`'s already-reusable `_rebuild_propuesta_agente_table` triggered by the new
`_propuesta_agente_needs_hogar_rebuild` (`body/db.py:1623`). `db.marcar_aplicada_via(conn,
propuesta_id, via)` (`body/db.py:1218`) replaces the mcp-only writer; `marcar_aplicada_via_mcp`
(`:1229`) is now a thin caller over it. New i18n: `asistente.propuesta.origen_hogar` (es "Desde
Hogar" / en "From Hogar"), `asistente.propuesta.aplicado_hogar` (es "Aplicado desde Hogar" / en
"Applied from Hogar"), rendered by `_tarjeta_propuesta`'s `origen_etiqueta` (`body/rutas/
asistente.py:849-856`) alongside the existing mcp labels, same precedence (an apply THIS caller
made itself beats the conversation's own origin label).

**Rulings 2 and 3 (meal moments as per-person data; a meal can say its moment) -- NOT BUILT, see
the ruling below.**

**Ruling 4, a training note on a planned session (`body/db.py`, `body/agente/herramientas.py`,
`body/agente/propuestas.py`, `body/rutas/asistente.py`):** `plan` gains nullable `nota_sesion TEXT,
nota_sesion_en TEXT` (`body/db.py:564-565`, additive ALTER in `_migrate` for an old database). New
tool `anotar_sesion(plan_id, nota, hecha?)` (`body/agente/herramientas.py:1489` `_anotar_sesion`,

this person's own by name (`"plan desconocido: {plan_id!r}"`), proposes the resolved `antes`/

**A migration bug this slice's own fixture caught (`body/db.py`):** `_rebuild_conversacion_agente_
table`'s call site originally sat inside `_migrate()` AFTER that function's first DML statement
(the `person`/`timezone` UPDATE at the time). Python's `sqlite3` module opens an implicit
transaction before that UPDATE and never closes it before DDL, so `_rebuild_with_fk_off`'s own
`BEGIN` collided with it ("cannot start a transaction within a transaction") -- but only on an
install old enough to actually need this specific rebuild; every test anywhere else in the suite
builds a fresh database, whose `conversacion_agente` is created with `'hogar'` already in its CHECK
by `SCHEMA` itself, so the rebuild branch is never entered and the bug was invisible until
`tests/test_migraciones.py`'s pre-migration fixture exercised it. Fixed by moving the ALTER+rebuild
block earlier in `_migrate()`, beside `metric_def`'s own rebuild, before any DML statement in that
function -- the same position every other rebuild call already in `_migrate()` holds.

### BODY-HOGAR-ESCRIBE-1-W -- rulings 2, 3, 6

Dispatched on this same branch (`feat/body-hogar-escribe-1`, at `616bd10`) with the orchestrator's
own ruling on this entry's RULING_NEEDED above, verbatim:

> ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1, on BODY-HOGAR-ESCRIBE-1-INV's findings and BODY-HOGAR-ESCRIBE-1's
> RULING_NEEDED: the same additive schema the original spec approved (one per-person table with
> defaults, one nullable column, one optional tool argument, undoable), now with the two registry
> files that classify every per-person table, following the ajuste_agente precedent line for line.

And its own new ruling (6), copied from this slice's spec:

> **Register `momento_comida` the way `ajuste_agente` is registered.** In body/privacidad.py, add it
> beside `ajuste_agente` in the same structure (`FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES` or whichever set
> `ajuste_agente` sits in): it is the person's own data, exported and deleted with them. In
> body/mudanza.py, add a `TableSpec` for it shaped like `ajuste_agente`'s entry (match on `person_id`,
> `clave`). Read both `ajuste_agente` entries first and mirror them; if `ajuste_agente`'s shape cannot
> carry `momento_comida` (a different key, a different posture), STOP RULING_NEEDED with the
> measurement rather than inventing a third shape. Seed one `momento_comida` row wherever the
> persona_fuga / privacidad / mudanza tests seed `ajuste_agente`, so the export, deletion and move are
> proven on a real row.

Why this is a ruling and not a cleanup: classifying a new per-person table's privacy export/delete
behaviour and its account-migration copy shape is the judgment call this entry's own RULING_NEEDED
raised above -- it needed widening this slice's `touches:` to the two registry files, which the
original slice was told not to do unilaterally.

**Ruling 2, meal moments as per-person data (`body/db.py`, `body/comidas.py`,
`body/rutas/asistente.py`):** new table `momento_comida (person_id, clave, desde_hora, hasta_hora,
esperado, orden, PRIMARY KEY (person_id, clave))` (`body/db.py:583-592`), `clave` CHECK-constrained
to lowercase ascii (letters, digits, underscore), `desde_hora`/`hasta_hora` CHECK 0-24,
`esperado` CHECK 0/1 -- additive, created once via `SCHEMA`'s own `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`
(no rebuild needed, a brand-new table). New `body/comidas.py`: `DEFAULT_MOMENTOS` (the one
constant: desayuno 5-11 esperado 1 orden 1, almuerzo 11-16 esperado 1 orden 2, merienda 16-19
esperado 0 orden 3, cena 19-23 esperado 1 orden 4 -- today's display rule, now data),
`momentos(conn, person_id)` (`:20`, a person's own rows when they have any, the defaults otherwise)
and `momento_de(conn, person_id, ts_local)` (`:31`, the clave whose window contains `ts_local`'s own
hour, or `None`). The hour-to-moment display helper in `body/rutas/asistente.py`,
`_momento_ingesta_txt` (`:342`), is rewired to call `momento_de` instead of its old hardcoded
if/elif ladder; a new `_momento_clave_txt` (`:335`) renders one of the four default i18n labels (the
same four keys `_momento_ingesta_txt` already used, reused unchanged -- no new i18n key needed) or
the clave capitalised when it is a custom one with none. `momento_de`/`momentos` tolerate
`conn is None` (falling back to `DEFAULT_MOMENTOS`, `body/comidas.py:31-44`) because several
existing card-rendering tests call `_tarjeta_propuesta` with no live connection (the same default
every `TARJETAS` helper's own `conn`/`person_id` parameters already carry) -- discovered by the
gate, fixed in the second commit below. No screen writes a person's own custom rows in this slice
(`BODY-MOMENTOS-AJUSTES-1`, open follow-up, unchanged from the original entry).

**Ruling 3, a meal can say its moment (`body/db.py`, `body/agente/herramientas.py`,
`body/agente/propuestas.py`, `body/rutas/asistente.py`):** `comida` gains nullable `momento TEXT`
(`body/db.py:807`, additive `ALTER TABLE comida ADD COLUMN momento TEXT` in `_migrate` for an old
database, `:1383`). `db.crear_comida`/`db._crear_comida_tx` gain a trailing `momento: str | None =
None` parameter, stored on insert -- positional-call-compatible (appended last, so
`tests/test_mcp.py`'s existing positional `db.crear_comida` call is untouched). The tool
`registrar_comida` gains an optional `momento` argument (`_PARAM_REGISTRAR_COMIDA`,
`body/agente/herramientas.py:389`, typed as a plain string -- no static JSON-schema enum, since the
person's own claves are read live from `comidas.momentos` at call time, the same per-person-live-
source template `registrar_medida`'s own `metric_key` already uses). `_registrar_comida`
(`:1849`) validates it against `{m["clave"] for m in comidas.momentos(conn, person_id)}` before
building `despues`, refusing an unknown clave by name (`f"momento desconocido: {momento!r}"`,
`:1893`); `despues["momento"]` is always present (`None` when not given). Apply
(`_aplicar_registrar_comida`, `body/agente/propuestas.py:977`) passes `despues.get("momento")` to
`db.crear_comida` on the plain (non-shared) path only -- `compartida_con`'s own
`comida_compartida.compartir_comida` path is untouched, outside this slice's `touches:`. Undo is
unchanged (`db.borrar_comida` removes the whole row, `momento` included). The proposal card
(`_tarjeta_registrar_comida`, `body/rutas/asistente.py:415-419`) shows the person's own stated
moment when they gave one (via `_momento_clave_txt`), falling back to the hour-derived one
(`_momento_ingesta_txt`) otherwise -- so a stored `momento` is not silent data nobody sees. Two
people at one dinner are still two calls under two identities; Hogar's own writes never touch
`comida_compartida` (unchanged, its own `origen`/`origen_ref` columns stay unused by this slice).

**Ruling 6, registered like `ajuste_agente` (`body/privacidad.py`, `body/mudanza.py`):**
`body/privacidad.py`'s `FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES` gains `"momento_comida"` beside `"ajuste_agente"`

`body/mudanza.py`'s `REGISTRY` gains `TableSpec("momento_comida", match_cols=("person_id",
"clave"))` beside `TableSpec("ajuste_agente", match_cols=("person_id",))` (`:125-127`) -- the same

## BODY-HOGAR-ESCRIBE-2

The second half of BODY-HOGAR-ESCRIBE-1 (Carlos, relayed verbatim to Hogar 2026-11-16: "register
all that into the body app ... for each user, knowing like if any data is missing, you can ask
for it ... asking about the training session to see how it matched the plan"; his standing rule
`BODY-APPS-SIN-RESTRICCIONES-1`: "drop every restriction. Allow free communication between all of
them." and "I want everything to be automated as much as possible."). Routes and screens for the
schema and tools BODY-HOGAR-ESCRIBE-1/-1-W already built.

**Ruling 1, scope `hogar:escribir` (`body/dispositivo.py:15`, `body/rutas/dispositivos.py:22-28,
73-79`, `body/templates/dispositivos.html`, `body/i18n/es.json`, `body/i18n/en.json`):** a separate
checkbox from `hogar:leer` -- `dispositivo.ALCANCES` gains `"hogar:escribir"`, the Ajustes form
gains its own `alcance_hogar_escribir` checkbox right after `hogar:leer`'s, same template pattern.
New i18n: `dispositivos.scope.hogar_escribir` (es "Hogar: registrar comidas y notas de entreno" /
en "Hogar: log meals and workout notes") and `dispositivos.scope.hogar_escribir_explica` (es
"Hogar anota en Body lo que le cuentas en casa: qué comiste y cómo te fue en el entreno. Se aplica
directo y puedes deshacerlo en Body." / en "Hogar logs in Body what you tell it at home: what you
ate and how your workout went. It applies directly and you can undo it in Body."), exactly the
strings the spec named.

**Ruling 2, two routes, one registry (`body/rutas/dispositivos.py:261-320`, `body/rutas/
mcp_remoto.py:62-120`):** `GET /api/hogar/herramientas` (`api_hogar_herramientas`, `:270`) calls the
shared `mcp_remoto.listar_herramientas(conn, person_id, idioma, puede_aplicar=False)` -- the SAME
function `/mcp` and the hosted MCP door already use for `tools/list` -- then filters its own
`"herramientas"` list down to `_HOGAR_ESCRIBIR_HERRAMIENTAS = {"registrar_comida",
"anotar_sesion"}` (`:265`) by name; never a copied schema. `POST /api/hogar/registrar`
(`api_hogar_registrar`, `:295`) reads `{"herramienta", "argumentos"}`, refuses any name outside
those two with `404` and a malformed body with `400`, then calls `mcp_remoto.llamar_herramienta(...,
auto_aplicar=True, origin="hogar")`.

`llamar_herramienta` gained the `origin` parameter (`body/rutas/mcp_remoto.py:62-64`, default
`mcp.ORIGEN` i.e. `"mcp"` -- the door's own route and `/mcp` both call it with no `origin` argument,
so their own behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged). Rather than touching `body/mcp.py`'s
`_SesionRemota` (outside this slice's `touches:`, and the ledger's own BODY-HOGAR-ESCRIBE-1-W entry
already widened `conversacion_agente`'s CHECK to accept `'hogar'`), the function pre-creates the
conversation itself when the caller sent none and `origin` differs from `"mcp"`, through the already
general `agente_conversacion.crear(conn, person_id, origen=origin)` (`:96`) -- `_SesionRemota`'s own
`conversacion()` then just returns that id, never creating a second one. On `auto_aplicar`, the
apply call now reads `db.marcar_aplicada_via(conn, propuesta_id, origin)` (`:118`) in place of the
mcp-only `db.marcar_aplicada_via_mcp` -- that general writer already existed (BODY-HOGAR-ESCRIBE-1
ruling 1), so no change to `body/db.py` was needed either. A tool-level refusal

## BODY-CORREGIR-MEDIDA-ENTRENO-1

Three orchestrator rulings for correcting what the assistant already logged: a same-day measurement
should replace, never double; a second training-day call should correct the same session, never
create a duplicate; and a dedicated `corregir_entreno` tool should let a specific set be fixed by
position. Tier 2, `approved: no`.

**Ruling 1, `registrar_medida` replaces a same-day, same-metric pending proposal
(`body/agente/propuestas.py:1467-1548`):** `ACCIONES_REEMPLAZABLES` changed from a plain set of
action names to a dict mapping each one to the extra `despues_json` keys (beyond `day`) that must
also match before a pending sibling is discarded -- empty for the original four
(`registrar_entreno`, `registrar_comida`, `registrar_ingesta`, `registrar_checkin`, unchanged
behaviour), `("metric_key",)` for the new entry, `registrar_medida`. A day can carry several
different self-measured metrics (weight, soreness, resting HR) that are each real, never a
same-day replacement of each other -- `_reemplazar_pendientes_mismo_dia` now takes the applied
proposal's own `despues_json` dict and a `claves_extra` tuple, and skips a pending sibling whose
value differs on any of those extra keys. `registrar_medida`'s own tool `descripcion`
(`body/agente/herramientas.py:2696-2699`) gained a sentence telling the model to call the tool
again with the corrected value rather than add a second measurement (es: "Si la persona corrige un
valor que ya registró ese día, llama a esta misma herramienta con el valor correcto: reemplaza el
anterior, nunca suma un segundo registro." / en equivalent). Tests:
`tests/test_propuesta_vigencia.py`'s new `ReemplazoRegistrarMedidaTest` -- two pending proposals
for the same day and metric leave only the newer one, a pending sibling of a *different* metric the
same day is left alone, and a pending sibling of the *same* metric a *different* day is left alone.

**Ruling 2, `registrar_entreno` corrects an existing manual session instead of duplicating it
(`body/agente/herramientas.py:1400-1450`):** new helper `_resolver_sesion_entreno_dia(conn,
person_id, day)` looks up the day's own training session for a correction -- the watch's own
strength activity (`type = 'strength_training'`) when there is one, else the person's existing
manual session for that day, told apart by exactly what `db.create_manual_session` writes
(`source = 'manual'` with `type IS NULL`) -- never any other watch activity (a run, a ride).
`_registrar_entreno` now calls this helper in place of its old Garmin-only inline query, and the
watch-set fetch (`pull.traer_series`) now only runs when `source == "garmin"`, so a manual-session
correction never attempts a network call. `registrar_entreno`'s own tool `descripcion`
(`body/agente/herramientas.py:2656-2660`) gained a sentence telling the model to call the tool
again to correct an already-registered training day rather than create another one (es: "Si la
persona corrige un entreno que ya registró ese día, llama a esta misma herramienta: corrige ese
entreno, nunca crea otro." / en equivalent). Tests: `tests/test_agente_entreno.py`'s new
`RegistrarEntrenoSegundaVezManualTest` -- a second call corrects the same session with no duplicate
activity row, undoing the second call restores the first call's own corrections, and a day with
only a run (`source='garmin'`, `type='running'`) is not mistaken for a manual session.

**Ruling 3, `corregir_entreno` -- BLOCKED, Tier 1.** The spec asked for a new id-addressed
`propuesta` tool (`dia`, `orden`, at least one of `ejercicio`/`reps`/`peso_kg`) applying through
`db.correct_exercise_set` with exact undo, like `corregir_ingesta`. The full tool, its drift/undo
writers, its card, both languages' strings, and tests across six files were built once to confirm
the design, then every value it needs. Both correct in production but `propuesta_agente.accion`
carries a hardcoded SQL `CHECK` constraint (`body/db.py:93-101`) enumerating every valid action
name -- widened 12 times before through the established `_migrate_propuestas` ->
`_propuesta_agente_needs_X_rebuild()` -> `_rebuild_propuesta_agente_table()` pattern -- and it does
not list `corregir_entreno`. Inserting a row for the new action trips
`sqlite3.IntegrityError: CHECK constraint failed: accion IN (...)`. `body/db.py` is Tier 1 and this
slice's `approved: no` confirms no Tier-1 build authorization exists here, so the build stopped and
every ruling-3 change was reverted: `body/agente/herramientas.py` (`_corregir_entreno`, its
`_PARAM_CORREGIR_ENTRENO` schema, its registry entry), `body/agente/propuestas.py` (the
`_CAMPOS_SLOT_ENTRENO`/`_entreno_set_estado`/drift/apply/undo functions, the `TABLA` entry, the
`_restaurar_slot_entreno` helper un-extracted back to its original inline form in
`_deshacer_registrar_entreno`), `body/i18n/es.json` and `en.json` (the four new keys), `body/rutas/
asistente.py` (`_tarjeta_corregir_entreno` and its `TARJETAS` entry), and the test additions in
`tests/test_series_orden.py` (`CorregirEntrenoOrdenTest`), `tests/test_mcp.py`
(`test_corregir_entreno_is_offered_and_callable`), `tests/test_agente_conformidad.py` (the fixture
row and docstring count), `tests/test_agente_registro.py` (the census set/count), and
`tests/test_agente_bucle.py` (the `ofrecidas` set) -- plus the new file
`tests/test_corregir_entreno.py`, deleted outright. Grepping the whole tree for `corregir_entreno`
after the revert returns nothing.

**Gate command:** `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`. Run as 10 sequential
alphabetical chunks of 190 dotted test modules (~19 each), each read from the process, on the final
tree (rulings 1 and 2 only, ruling 3 fully reverted):
- chunk 1 (`test_accesibilidad`..`test_backup`): `Ran 379 tests ... OK (skipped=1, expected
  failures=1)`
- chunk 2 (`test_baselines`..`test_despertar`): `Ran 386 tests in 604.211s ... OK`

### BODY-CORREGIR-MEDIDA-ENTRENO-1-W

The follow-up this branch's own entry above asked for: ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1, on
BODY-CORREGIR-MEDIDA-ENTRENO-1-INV's findings and BODY-CORREGIR-MEDIDA-ENTRENO-1's BLOCKED report --
"one more value in the propuesta_agente.accion CHECK, through the same reusable rebuild used for
the twelve prior widenings, so the already-specified corregir_entreno tool can store its
proposal" -- finishing ruling 3 of the original spec on this same branch, so all three rulings land
in one merge.

**Ruling A, the thirteenth widening (`body/db.py:93-102`):** `'corregir_entreno'` added to the
`accion IN (...)` list of `_PROPUESTA_AGENTE_COLUMNS`. `_propuesta_agente_needs_corregir_entreno_rebuild`
(`body/db.py:1655-1659`), shaped exactly like `_propuesta_agente_needs_hogar_rebuild`, and a call to
`_rebuild_propuesta_agente_table(conn)` for it at the end of `_migrate_propuestas`
(`body/db.py:1717-1718`), with the one-line comment `# BODY-CORREGIR-MEDIDA-ENTRENO-1: a thirteenth
widening (corregir_entreno), same reusable rebuild.`. Nothing else in `db.py` changed. Tests in
`tests/test_migraciones.py`'s new `PropuestaAgenteCorregirEntrenoMigrationTest` (a database whose
propuesta_agente predates `corregir_entreno` keeps its two existing rows' ids and count, then
accepts a `corregir_entreno` row; running the migration twice is a no-op) and
`PropuestaAgenteCorregirEntrenoFreshDbTest` (a fresh database accepts it directly).

**Ruling B, `corregir_entreno` built on top of A** -- a propuesta tool addressed by position, like
`corregir_ingesta`, beside `registrar_entreno` in the one registry (in-app, stdio MCP, `/mcp`):

- **Arguments** (`_PARAM_CORREGIR_ENTRENO`, `body/agente/herramientas.py:264-277`): `dia` (required,
  ISO date), `orden` (required, integer, minimum 1 -- the set's raw `set_order`, the same number
  already shown on `registrar_entreno`'s own card, never a renumbered ordinal), `ejercicio`, `reps`,
  `peso_kg` (each optional, at least one required).
- **`_corregir_entreno`** (`body/agente/herramientas.py:1529-1575`): refuses a future `dia`
  (`_dia_no_futuro`); refuses a non-integer or sub-1 `orden`; refuses when none of
  `ejercicio`/`reps`/`peso_kg` is given; resolves the day's session through the same
  `_resolver_sesion_entreno_dia` ruling 2 built (a Garmin strength day, else an existing manual one,
  scoped to this `person_id` by that helper's own WHERE clause -- another person's same-calendar-day
  session is never seen); refuses with `agente.error.entreno_sin_sesion` when the day has neither.
  Looks up the set at `orden` among that session's sets filtered to `set_type == 'active'` (a rest
  slot -- Garmin alternates active/rest, BODY-SERIES-ORDEN-1 -- is never a "serie" to correct, the
  same filter `_leer_entreno`/`_registrar_entreno` already apply); refuses with
  `agente.error.entreno_sin_serie` (`orden={orden}`) when there is none. `reps`/`peso_kg` validated
  through the existing `_numero_entreno` (reused, not duplicated); a blank `ejercicio` refused.
  `antes` carries that slot's full pre-correction state -- every `person_*` and `garmin_*` column
  plus `corrected_by_person` -- the identical shape ruling 2's own `sets_antes` entries already
  carry. `despues` carries `dia`, `source`, `source_id`, `set_order` and the given fields (`None` for
  the rest, read by `db.correct_exercise_set`'s own `COALESCE` as "leave unchanged").
- **Apply/undo/drift** (`body/agente/propuestas.py:519-562`, registered in `TABLA` at
  `:1472-1473`): `_aplicar_corregir_entreno` writes through `db.correct_exercise_set` --
  the SAME writer `registrar_entreno`'s own Garmin-matched path uses. `_deshacer_corregir_entreno`
  restores `antes` EXACTLY (including `corrected_by_person` back to 0 when the slot had never been
  corrected before) through the identical direct `UPDATE workout_set` SQL
  `_deshacer_registrar_entreno`'s own Garmin-matched restoration already uses -- `correct_exercise_set`
  only ever moves a slot INTO "corrected", never back out, so no new `db.py` writer was needed (the

  `_drift_deshacer_corregir_entreno` compare the slot's current `person_*`/`corrected_by_person`
  state against `antes` (on apply) or `despues` (on undo), the same shape `descartar_series`'s own

  correction of the same slot is its own, separate pending proposal.
- **Registry** (`body/agente/herramientas.py:2729-2734`): `descripcion` (es, matching the registry's

## BODY-HOST-AUTOACTUALIZAR-1 -- the entry script updates itself on every deploy (2026-11-16/17)

The Personal desk, 2026-11-16, relayed Carlos's own rule that night: *"we should run this from the
agent and from the server itself"* -- the installed `duna-deploy-body` had no self-update, so every
wrapper change needed a hand `sudo install` from Carlos. BODY-HOST-AUTOACTUALIZAR-1-INV (OBSERVED)
had already measured that main's wrapper was byte-identical to the one on the host, that the deploy
arm pulls then execs `body-deploy.sh` as root with a before-sha captured before the pull, that the
sudoers rule is one line, and that README lines told Carlos to hand-reinstall the wrapper after a
pull-verb and an importar-pc/personas change. The orchestrator read Lotes' own mechanism
(`duna-deploy-lotes`) and ruled: (a) one shared helper, sourced from the freshly pulled checkout by
both the wrapper and the product script, so the validation exists once; (b) the self-update runs on
`deploy` only, since every deploy already leaves the installed wrapper equal to the repo checkout
for every other verb; (c) a failed deploy that resets the repo does not revert an already-validated
wrapper, so recovery is a `rollback-script` verb; (d) the bootstrap: the very first deploy after this
change still runs under the OLD wrapper, so `body-deploy.sh` itself installs the new wrapper and
sudoers rule through the same helper, as root, with no re-exec -- no hand install, ever, from here on.

**Built, in the rulings' own names:**

* `deploy/host/autoactualizar.sh` (new) -- sourced, never executed. Constants
  `INSTALLED_SCRIPT_PATH=/usr/local/sbin/duna-deploy-body`,
  `INSTALLED_SUDOERS_PATH=/etc/sudoers.d/duna-deploy-body`,
  `PREV_SCRIPT_PATH=/usr/local/sbin/duna-deploy-body.prev`,
  `PREV_SUDOERS_PATH=/etc/sudoers.d/.duna-deploy-body.prev` (:8-11). The sudoers install path was
  confirmed by reading the README's own one-time-install section (`README.md:11`, unchanged), not
  assumed -- it matches `INSTALLED_SUDOERS_PATH` exactly.
  `validar_sudoers_candidato` (:16-30): strips blank/comment/`\r` lines, requires exactly one
  remaining line matching `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31} ALL=\(root\) NOPASSWD: ${INSTALLED_SCRIPT_PATH}$`,
  pure string logic, no `visudo` call. `autoactualizar_comparar` (:32-42) sets `SCRIPT_CHANGED`/
  `SUDOERS_CHANGED` via `cmp -s` (a missing installed file counts as changed). `autoactualizar_plan`
  (:44-74) prints the dry-run text, calling `validar_sudoers_candidato` and a read-only `visudo -cf`
  to decide "would pass"/"would FAIL", installing nothing. `autoactualizar_instalar` (:76-118)
  validates first (refuses with `exit 1` and nothing installed on either a bad shape or a failing
  `visudo -cf`), then diffs, backs up each changed installed file to its `.prev` at mode 0440, then
  installs the new copies (0755 script / 0440 sudoers), and returns 0 having installed -- the caller
  decides whether to re-exec.
* `deploy/host/duna-deploy-body` -- header comment (:1-5) now lists every real verb. `usage()`
  (:23-37) gains the self-update note on `deploy` and a new `rollback-script` line;
  `--autoactualizado-interno` is never in it. The `deploy)` case arm (:113-148) now loops its own
  args, accepting `--dry-run`, the internal `--autoactualizado-interno` and `--before-sha <sha>`,
  and refuses (`usage`/`exit 2`) unless the two internal flags are given together and never with
  `--dry-run`. A new `rollback-script)` case arm (:177-182) rejects any argument. The bottom flow
  (:220-267): a new `rollback-script` block sources the helper, refuses if either `.prev` is missing
  or the `.prev` sudoers fails `visudo -cf`, otherwise `run install`s both back and prints
  `rollback-script: restored ... from their .prev backups`. The dry-run block now also sources the
  helper and calls `autoactualizar_plan` between the three echoed pull commands and the echoed final
  exec. The real flow: when `AUTOACTUALIZADO_INTERNO` is unset, it captures `before_sha`, fetches,
  pulls, sources the helper, compares, and -- only if either file changed -- calls
  `autoactualizar_instalar` then `exec "$INSTALLED_SCRIPT_PATH" deploy --autoactualizado-interno
  --before-sha "$before_sha"` (no `/bin/bash`: it re-execs the freshly installed entry script
  itself, the one line in this file that intentionally skips the `/bin/bash` convention, noted in
  the test that checks it); when up to date it just prints `entry script: up to date`. When
  `AUTOACTUALIZADO_INTERNO` is set, `before_sha` comes from the carried `--before-sha` and the
  rev-parse/fetch/pull/compare block is skipped entirely, falling through to the same
  `exec /bin/bash "$PRODUCT_SCRIPT" --before-sha "$before_sha"` line the first pass already used.
* `deploy/host/body-deploy.sh` (:68-76) -- right after the owner is read and before any function
  definition or the venv/pip block, sources the same helper, compares, and calls
  `autoactualizar_instalar` with no re-exec when either file changed (prints `entry script: up to
  date` otherwise). A refusal there is a plain `exit 1` from inside the sourced function -- the
  script's existing failure path, the same shape the pre-existing `python3-venv is missing` check
  already uses before `fail_step`/rollback become relevant, since nothing has been installed or
  restarted yet at that point.
* `deploy/host/README.md` -- the hand-reinstall callouts at the old `:48-51` (Pull now) and `:129-131`
  (Importar desde el PC) are gone, replaced by a new "Self-updating wrapper" section describing the
  mechanism, the `rollback-script` command, and the bootstrap guarantee; both sections above it now
  say the wrapper already carries their verbs. The "What installs where" table's two wrapper rows
  now say "Carlos, by hand, once; itself on every later `deploy`". The one-time install section is
  unchanged -- it is still how a brand-new host gets its first wrapper.
* Tests: `tests/test_host_autoactualizar.py` (new, 33 tests) -- functional tests source
  `autoactualizar.sh` into a temp directory with its four path constants reassigned there and
  `install`/`visudo` stubbed on PATH (never a real root action, confirmed by checking `install -o
  root -g root` genuinely fails un-stubbed on this dev machine before relying on the stub), covering
  `validar_sudoers_candidato`'s acceptance of the repo's own sudoers file and its refusal of two
  rules, an argument after the path, `ALL` in the command position, a `Defaults` line and another
  path; `autoactualizar_comparar`'s flags; `autoactualizar_instalar`'s up-to-date/first-install/
  changed-script/invalid-sudoers/visudo-refusal paths and install modes; `autoactualizar_plan`'s
  up-to-date/would-pass/would-FAIL text; and `bash -n` on all three scripts. Structural tests on
  `duna-deploy-body` and `body-deploy.sh` check placement by index (self-update strictly between the
  pull and the final exec; the bootstrap strictly before the venv/pip block with no `exec` in it),
  that the second pass skips the rev-parse/pull, that `--autoactualizado-interno` never appears in
  `usage()`, and the `rollback-script` refusal shape. `tests/test_host_deploy.py`'s
  `test_exec_line_uses_bin_bash_not_the_exec_bit` now excuses the one line containing
  `$INSTALLED_SCRIPT_PATH` (the deliberate self re-exec); its `PullNowReadmeTest` now checks the
  hand-reinstall line is gone from the Pull-now section instead of present.
  `tests/test_deploy_host.py`'s `ReadmeImportSectionTest.test_steps_are_in_order` drops the removed
  step-1 install-line check and asserts the remaining five steps stay in order.

**Process deviation from the spec's step list:** the helper, the wrapper, the bootstrap and the
README were committed together (`01c9926`) because the pieces are mutually dependent (the wrapper's
self-update and the bootstrap's call both need the finished helper to be meaningful to test), with
the new test module following in its own commit (`c2942b8`) rather than after each piece -- the
spec's `THE WORK` section asked for four separate commits. The end state matches what was asked;
only the commit granularity differs.

**Commits:** `01c9926` (helper, wrapper, bootstrap, README), `c2942b8`
(`tests/test_host_autoactualizar.py`, new).

**Gate**, `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .`, ten sequential alphabetical
chunks of ~20 dotted modules each, all green: 381+444+379+420+510+522+485+308+531+188 = 4168.
Reconciled against an independent collect-only count
(`unittest.TestLoader().discover('tests', top_level_dir='.')`, counted without running): `4168` --
exact match (4135 before this slice + 33 new in `test_host_autoactualizar.py`).

**No other db.py/schema change, no cross-repo contract touched.** This slice's diff is entirely
`deploy/host/` shell scripts, markdown and tests; nothing here runs on the host by itself -- every
install still waits for a `deploy` someone runs, and every install is validated first, backed up,
and reversible with `rollback-script`.

The first deploy after this merge installs the wrapper through `body-deploy.sh`; no hand install,
ever, from here on.

(`tests.test_host_autoactualizar tests.test_host_deploy tests.test_deploy_host`): `Ran 117 tests ...

## BODY-HOGAR-METAS-INGESTA-1

Hub «Para productos» from Hogar, 2026-11-17 (`hit_01m7m260nxvpnm6qfk81gbtbxy`, ref
`HOGAR-COCINA-IDEAS-1`, targets body only): "Hogar's meal ideas need the person's own intake goal to
say how much protein is still missing today. Ask: add 'metas' to GET /api/hogar/manana [...] from
goal WHERE kind='metric' AND status='active' AND metric_key IN (suma_ingesta keys). Empty list when
none, never omitted. Please confirm target_value for protein_g is grams per day. Additive to
hogar-feed-v1. Hogar side is ready (ideas.meta_de)."

**What the orchestrator measured:** Body does NOT keep a daily intake target in `goal`. It keeps it
in `nutrient_target` (`body/db.py:904-914`: person_id, metric_key, start_day, kind IN ('absolute',
'per_kg', 'off'), amount, sentido IN ('al_menos', 'como_maximo')), and the one resolver every screen
already uses is `nutriente_objetivo.estado_del_dia(conn, person_id, day)` (`body/
nutriente_objetivo.py:115`), which returns, per metric with a live target, `{total, n, objetivo:
{kind, amount, sentido, objetivo (resolved in the metric's unit, None with falta_peso), start_day,
falta_peso}, restante}` -- `per_kg` resolved against the person's latest `body_weight_kg` within
`PESO_DIAS_VENTANA` days, an honest gap without one; `restante` floored at 0 for `al_menos`, may go
negative for `como_maximo`. `protein_g`'s unit is `'g'` (`body/db.py:1095`) and its aggregation is
`suma_ingesta`, so a resolved target is grams per day -- confirming Hogar's own question.

**Ruling 1, `metas` on `manana` (`body/hogar_feed.py:163-191, 194-210`):** `hogar_feed.manana`
gains a sixth key, `metas`: a list, one item per metric with a live target on `dia` (exactly the
keys `nutriente_objetivo.estado_del_dia` returns), ordered by `metric_key`, `[]` when none -- never
omitted, never null. `_metas` (`:163`) builds each item from `estado_del_dia`'s own output and
nothing else, plus the unit read from `metric_def.unit`. `_metric_defs` (`:30-35`) is a new helper,
one query (`key, kind, unit`), shared by `_figuras` (its own `kind`, unchanged behaviour) and
`_metas` (its `unit`) so `manana`'s metric_def read stays the single one it always was -- no new SQL
for the unit lookup. Never a second computation of the target: Hogar's own guessed shape (`goal_id`,
`direction`, `target_value`, `deadline`) does not exist in Body, and a second reading of the target
would drift from what Today and Día show; Body computes `restante` so Hogar never re-derives
`per_kg` or the floor rule.

Item shape, verbatim as committed:

```
{"metric_key": str, "unidad": str, "sentido": "al_menos"|"como_maximo", "kind": "absolute"|"per_kg",
 "amount": float, "objetivo": float|null, "falta_peso": bool, "desde": "YYYY-MM-DD", "total": float,
 "registros": int, "restante": float|null}
```

`amount` is the stored figure (grams for `absolute`, grams per kg for `per_kg`); `objetivo` is the
resolved per-day target in `unidad` (null with `falta_peso` true); `desde` is the target's own
`start_day`; `total`/`registros` are `estado_del_dia`'s own `total`/`n`; `restante` is its own
`restante` verbatim. A metric whose latest target is `'off'` never appears -- `estado_del_dia`
already skips it.

**Ruling 2, the contract (`docs/contracts/hogar-feed-v1.md`):** the `manana` example gained a
`metas` array (invented numbers, one `per_kg` protein_g item and one `como_maximo` caffeine_mg item

## BODY-RENDIMIENTO-4

**The gap.** `tests/test_rendimiento.py`'s `RouteCostCeilingTest` calls every GET route with no
`Authorization` header, in LOCAL mode (no `BODY_CUENTA_ISSUER`), against this file's own `_seed()`
fixture. Every route gated on a device key (`identity.person_from_device`) or on `cuenta.hosted()`
404s before its own logic ever runs, so `_CEILINGS`' entry for each of them measures that early
refusal, not the route. The table's own comments already said so for some of them: BODY-HOGAR-
ESCRIBE-2's comment at the four `/api/hogar/*` routes and `/api/asistente/mcp/herramientas`/
`/api/vida/semana` ("measured 0 statements"), and BODY-SYNC-VIVO-2's comment at `/garmin/estado-
vivo` ("local mode's early 404, same path as /garmin's own"). Two slices found this independently
on 2026-11-17: BODY-HOGAR-METAS-INGESTA-1 (merged `801fc2c`) added `metas` to `/api/hogar/manana`,
a cost the ceiling could never see; BODY-APERTURA-AUTOMATICA-1 (merged `3a1261d`, ledger entry
above) raised `/garmin`'s own ceiling for its live-watch card but recorded that "the hosted+
connected cost path (12 statements) this slice actually added to" was never the path the ceiling
sweep exercises.

**The rulings** (quality questions; tests only, no Tier 1 path):
1. A ceiling that measures a 404 is not a ceiling -- every route the main sweep cannot reach gets a
   SECOND measurement on its real path (an authorised device key for the device-key routes;
   hosted + connected for `/garmin` and `/garmin/estado-vivo`), with its own measured-plus-30%
   ceiling, in the same file.
2. The main sweep's existing table stays as it is (it still proves the early 404 costs nothing),
   and the drift guard is extended so a NEW device-key or hosted-only GET route cannot join the app
   without a real-path ceiling too.
3. For `/api/hogar/manana`, prove the real-path count does not grow with the number of daily
   intake targets (one vs three) if `tests/test_hogar_feed.py` does not already prove it through
   the route -- check first, and do not duplicate a proof that exists (name it in the ledger
   instead).

**Measuring the gap, not guessing it.** A one-off sweep script (never committed) ran the main
sweep's own fixture and routes with no auth header, in LOCAL mode, and recorded every non-200
status. Result: 13 routes, not the 8 the spec's own surface named "at minimum" -- also
`/ajustes/dispositivos`, `/login`, `/login/cuenta/start`, `/login/cuenta/callback` and
`/privacidad/consentimiento`, every one of which 404s in LOCAL mode behind the identical
`if not cuenta.hosted(): raise HTTPException(404)` guard the named 8 use. This exact 13-route set
is `tests/test_estados_vacios.py`'s own `_ALWAYS_404_LOCAL`, confirming the measurement rather than
the spec's own partial list. Of the 13, `tests/test_estados_vacios_hosted.py`'s own
`_HOSTED_ONLY_CAN_200` already documents that only `/garmin`, `/ajustes/dispositivos` and
`/privacidad/consentimiento` can ever answer 200; `/login` and `/login/cuenta/start` always answer
303 (redirect to the issuer) and `/login/cuenta/callback` always answers 303 on a successful sign-in
(redirect to `return_to` or "/") or 400 with no real flow -- never 200, by that module's own
design. Ruling 1's "assert a 200" is read as "assert the route's own real, documented status" for
these three: 303 for all of them on their real path, never a literal 200 (deviation, below).

**`_CEILINGS_REAL_PATH`** (`tests/test_rendimiento.py`), ceiling = `ceil(measured * 1.3)`, same
margin rule as `_CEILINGS`:

| route | status | measured | ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/ajustes/dispositivos` | 200 | 7 | 10 |
| `/api/asistente/mcp/herramientas` | 200 | 18 | 24 |
| `/api/hogar/herramientas` | 200 | 17 | 23 |
| `/api/hogar/manana` | 200 | 27 | 36 |
| `/api/hogar/serie` | 200 | 13 | 17 |
| `/api/hogar/turnos` | 200 | 12 | 16 |
| `/api/vida/semana` | 200 | 47 | 62 |
| `/garmin` | 200 | 12 | 16 |
| `/garmin/estado-vivo` | 200 | 8 | 11 |
| `/login` | 303 | 7 | 10 |
| `/login/cuenta/callback` | 303 | 12 | 16 |
| `/login/cuenta/start` | 303 | 7 | 10 |
| `/privacidad/consentimiento` | 200 | 5 | 7 |

Every one of the 13 opens at most 2 connections on its real path (`_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, unchanged).
`/garmin` measured 12 statements -- the exact figure BODY-APERTURA-AUTOMATICA-1's own report named
and never measured; this slice is what measures it.

**Mechanism per group**, reusing each route's own existing test fixture (never a second mechanism):
the four `/api/hogar/*` routes plus `/api/asistente/mcp/herramientas` and `/api/vida/semana` use
`dispositivo.crear(conn, 1, name, {scope})` + `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, the same fixture
`tests/test_hogar_feed.py`, `tests/test_hogar_escribe_rutas.py`, `tests/test_mcp_remoto.py` and
`tests/test_dispositivo.py` each already build. `/garmin`, `/garmin/estado-vivo`,
`/ajustes/dispositivos` and `/privacidad/consentimiento` use hosted mode
(`BODY_CUENTA_ISSUER`/`BODY_PUBLIC_URL`/`BODY_CUENTA_CLIENT_SECRET`/`BODY_TOKEN_KEY`) plus
`identity.current_person_id` overridden to person 1, the same mechanism
`tests/test_garmin_conectar_vivo.py` and `tests/test_dispositivo.py`'s own `AjustesPageTest` use;
`/garmin` and `/garmin/estado-vivo` are measured connected with a registered sync error (the
richest state those routes' own tests exercise). `/login`, `/login/cuenta/start` and
`/login/cuenta/callback` take no `identity.current_person_id` dependency at all (checked in
`body/rutas/sesion.py` -- neither route declares it), so a dependency override cannot reach their

**The drift guard** (`RouteCostRealPathTest.test_the_main_sweeps_404_set_matches_this_tables_keys`):
asserts, on a fresh LOCAL-mode fixture, that `{route.path for route in every GET route if the main

**Ruling 3.** `tests/test_hogar_feed.py`'s `MetasTest.test_cost_does_not_grow_with_the_number_of_
targets` already proves the flat-cost claim, but at the `hogar_feed.manana()` function level, never

**Deviation from the spec's literal wording.** The spec's surface named only 8 routes "at minimum"

`/login/cuenta/start`, `/login/cuenta/callback`) never answer 200 on any path, by
