## BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-1 -- the `practica` table: what the watch data shows, kept apart from a habit (2026-11-17)

ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1, on BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-1-INV's own finding: a **habit**
(`goals.add_habit`) is what a person COMMITS to and checks off; nothing in this app answered the
other half of the question Carlos's "human body" idea keeps coming back to -- what did the data
itself show he actually did, streaks and seasons included, independent of whether he ever checked
a box. A **practice** is that other half: a rule over the person's own Garmin/self data
(an activity type, a metric threshold, a sleep-timing rule), computed on read, never on a commit.
This slice built the foundation only -- the table, the module, the shared run-detection helper, and
every census a new person-owned table must join (ruling 8). The screen, the two assistant tools
(`leer_practicas`, `proponer_practica`) and linking a habit back to a practice are
BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-2 (named in `open_followups` below).

**Ruling A/B -- `practica`, additive, no CHECK on `fuente`/`origen`:** `body/db.py:1051-1070`, a new
table in `SCHEMA` (not `_migrate()` -- a fresh database gets it the same way every existing table
arrives) plus `idx_practica_person`. No `CHECK` enumerates `fuente` or `origen` (ruling B: a CHECK
widened per new kind costs a table rebuild every time -- `propuesta_agente.accion` needed fourteen
such rebuilds before this slice); both are validated in Python instead, in
`body/practicas.py`'s `FUENTES`/`ORIGENES` and the `REASON_CODES` string-return convention
(`recuperacion.py`, `turno_fc.py`, `turnos_costo.py`, `sueno_fc.py` all already use it, never
raising on bad input). `titulo` is the person's own words, or the assistant's own proposal once
accepted -- never a hardcoded habit name, so the table serves any practice, not six fixed ones.
Tests: `PracticaTableMigrationTest` and `PracticaFreshDbTest` (`tests/test_migraciones.py`, mirroring
`EscrituraExternaTableMigrationTest`'s own pattern -- `DROP TABLE practica` then `db.init()`
recreates it empty and idempotent, and a fresh database already has it).

**Ruling 2 -- three FUENTES, each a rule shape and a validator, never a free-text rule:**
`body/practicas.py:62-166` -- `actividad` (`{"tipos": [...], "min_minutos"?}`), `metrica_umbral`
(`{"metric_key", "op": ">="|"<=", "valor"}`), `sueno_horario`
(`{"campo": "inicio"|"fin", "op": "antes"|"despues", "hora": "HH:MM"}`). `crear`/`archivar`/`listar`
(`:117-166`) are the only writers -- `archivar` sets `archivada_en`, never deletes.
`ValidacionActividadTest`, `ValidacionMetricaUmbralTest`, `ValidacionSuenoHorarioTest`,
`ValidacionGeneralTest`, `PersonScopeTest`, `ArchivarTest` (`tests/test_practicas.py`) cover every
reason code and that `person_id` scopes every read and write.

**Ruling 3 -- three states a day, one SELECT per source family for the whole range, never per day:**
`body/practicas.py:169-277` -- `hecho` / `no_hecho` / `sin_dato` (`_estados_de`, `:180-189`); a day
with no watch/self data at all (a commute day not yet imported, a sensor off) is `sin_dato`, never
counting against the person. "Has data" per family (`:192-262`): `actividad` = any
`daily_metric(source='garmin')` row OR any `activity` row for that day, union of both;
`metrica_umbral` = any `daily_metric` row for that key, any source; `sueno_horario` = any
`sleep_session` row. `_calcular_actividad` (`:192-218`) applies the SAME linked-manual-half drop
`history.training` already uses (`history.py:135-140`, BODY-ENTRENO-VINCULO-1): a manual row
linked to a watch row via `vinculo_manual` is dropped from `hecho`, counted only through its watch
half, so a linked pair is never double-counted and never silently miscounts as `no_hecho`.
`EstadosActividadTest` (including `test_linked_manual_half_is_dropped`), `EstadosMetricaUmbralTest`,
`EstadosSuenoHorarioTest` (`tests/test_practicas.py`) cover all three. Cost measured directly
(`tests/test_rendimiento.py`'s `PracticasDiasEstadoCostTest`, `set_trace_callback` on an open
connection, the same technique `tests/test_hogar_feed.py` uses): `dias_estado` costs exactly 2
statements for a 30-day range and the SAME 2 for a 300-day range -- never one query per day.

**Ruling 4 -- day-level racha with bridging, weekly rollup, temporada, through one shared helper:**
`fechas.rachas_de_estados` (`body/fechas.py:33-71`) is the run-detection
`entreno_racha.racha_semanal` has always done inline (consecutive weeks meeting its own floor),
generalised rather than copied a second time: consecutive runs of an `on` state, bridging up to
`bridge_max` consecutive `bridge` states inside a run without breaking or extending it, each run
`{"inicio", "fin", "puentes", "abierta"}`. `entreno_racha.py:151-158` now calls it with
`bridge_max=0` (behaves exactly as its own old inline loop always did -- verified by running
`tests.test_entreno_racha` and `tests.test_tendencias_racha` unchanged, both still green, byte-
identical output). `body/practicas.py`'s own two callers: `_rachas_dia` (`:311-323`, days,
`on="hecho"`, `bridge="sin_dato"`, `bridge_max=MODELO["PUENTE_SIN_DATO"]=2`) and
`_temporadas_crudas` (`:349-369`, weeks, `on="cumple"`, `bridge="semana_sin_dato"`,
`bridge_max=1`, requiring >= `MODELO["MIN_SEMANAS_TEMPORADA"]=3` consecutive weeks). A week needs
>= `MODELO["MIN_DIAS_CON_DATO"]=4` days with data (hecho+no_hecho) to be judged `cumple` at all --
fewer than that and it is `semana_sin_dato`, bridged like a `sin_dato` day, never counted as a
miss. `RachaDiaTest` (a bridged 2-day gap stays one streak, a 3-day gap or any `no_hecho` breaks
it immediately) and `SemanaYTemporadaTest` (the `semana_sin_dato` floor, a bridged temporada) cover
both callers.

**Ruling 5 -- context, on read, never stored, baseline always the whole history:** `_contexto`
(`body/practicas.py:389-399`) reads shift-kind counts (`_turnos_en_rango`, first-wins per day, the
same resolution `history.by_shift` already applies) and mean `sleep_minutes`/`readiness`
(`CONTEXTO_KEYS`) over a range, returning `None` for a key with no rows rather than a false zero.
Every `temporada` carries its own `contexto` over its own span; `estado()`'s own `baseline` is
ALWAYS computed over the practice's true whole-history range (`primero`/`ultimo` from
`_primero_ultimo_dato`), even when a caller passes a narrower `desde`/`hasta` -- a context key is
only ever `None` for genuine absence, never for a caller's own override. `ContextoTest` covers
both the `None`-key case and a populated baseline.

**Ruling 7 -- one entry point, default range = whole history, nothing stored:** `estado()`
(`body/practicas.py:404-450`) returns the definition, per-day states, weekly rollup, day-level
racha_actual/racha_mas_larga/n_rachas, temporadas with context, the whole-history baseline, and
`MODELO["version"]` -- or a `None`-shaped result when the practice has no data at all yet, or
plain `None` when the id does not belong to this person. Nothing it computes is ever written back;
every number is live on every call, versioned so a later model change never silently reinterprets
an old one.

**Ruling 6 -- suggestions, as data, never auto-created:** `sugerencias()` (`:455-499`) offers any
`activity.type` (after the same linked-half drop) or `walking_minutes`/`cycling_minutes` day
present in >= `MODELO["MIN_SEMANAS_SUGERENCIA"]=8` distinct weeks, as a ready-to-create
`{fuente, regla, clave, semanas}` -- never a title, never written -- omitting anything already
covered by an active practica of the exact same `(fuente, regla)` pair. `SugerenciasTest` covers
the 7-vs-8-week boundary and the omission.

**MODELO, verbatim** (`body/practicas.py:30-44`):

    MODELO = {
        "version": "practicas-v1",
        "PUENTE_SIN_DATO": 2,
        "MIN_DIAS_CON_DATO": 4,
        "MIN_SEMANAS_TEMPORADA": 3,
        "MIN_SEMANAS_SUGERENCIA": 8,
    }

**Ruling 8 -- wired into every place a person's data is enumerated:** `body/privacidad.py`
(`practica` added to `FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES`; export returns the person's own
id/titulo/fuente/regla_json/meta_dias_semana/origen/creada_en/archivada_en rows, never the derived
math computed on read; delete removes them, no FK points at `practica` yet) --
`PracticaExportDeleteTest` (`tests/test_privacidad.py`). `body/mudanza.py`'s `REGISTRY` gains
`TableSpec("practica", match_cols=None)` (matched by full row content, moved like any other of a
person's own rows) -- `PracticaMudanzaTest` (`tests/test_mudanza.py`, insert then re-run dedup).
`body/persona_garmin.py`'s `PERSONA_TABLAS` gains `("practica", None)` (a `sugerida`-origin row
still makes a person look real, refusing `relinkar` the same as any other authored row) --
`RelinkarRefusalTest.test_source_with_a_suggested_practica_refused_naming_table_and_count`
(`tests/test_persona_garmin.py`). `body/demo.py` seeds two invented practices on the demo person

## BODY-MCP-COPIA-PC-1

**Finding, verbatim from the dispatch's own surface:** Found 2026-11-17/18 (BODY-DEPLOY-E6E76C2 in the
orchestrator's ledger). For a whole day the Personal desk reported, as Carlos's Body data, nulls for every
Garmin metric after 12 Nov, `vehicle_minutes` 0 days, and leer_estado_reloj missing. That led to a wrong
"second person" theory and a repair tool built for it. The hosted diagnostic showed his data was complete on
the server. The desk's session had been reading the stdio door `body/mcp.py` in LOCAL mode (no PC link ->
`_modo_remoto()` False) over the PC's own home, `C:\Duna\body\body-app-live`, many merges behind and holding
Garmin only up to the last PC import. Nothing in any answer said so: `initialize` returned only `serverInfo
{"name": "body-local"}`, and every tool result was the bare tool text. The desk's own words: "a PC-local Body
MCP that lags the server should refuse, or warn loudly ... a «PC copy, last sync <date>» line in every read.
Then no assistant can mistake it again."

**Rulings (the orchestrator's, quality, Tier 2):**
1. In LOCAL mode only, every `tools/call` result (success, refusal and error alike) begins with ONE line
   naming where the data lives and how fresh it is -- es "Body en este PC (no el servidor) -- datos del
   reloj hasta {fecha}", en "Body on this PC (not the server) -- watch data up to {date}" -- {fecha} being
   the person's last day with Garmin data, and "sin datos del reloj" / "no watch data" when there is none.
2. The same sentence goes into `initialize`'s result as `instructions`, and `serverInfo` gains `"title"`
   with the same short label.
3. WARN, never refuse.
4. If this home can tell it was ever moved or exported to a server, the line says so; if no such marker
   exists, say so in the ledger and keep ruling 1's sentence. One query per call at most for the date.

**As built:**
- Ruling 1, `_con_copia_pc` (`body/mcp.py:579-588`), threaded through `_procesar_mensaje`'s three
  `tools/call` return points: the `herramientas.ToolError` branch (`body/mcp.py:781`), the generic-exception
  branch (`body/mcp.py:793`), and the success branch's final `return` (`body/mcp.py:820`) -- so a read, a
  propuesta, `aplicar_propuesta`, `descartar_propuesta`, an unknown-tool refusal, a cap refusal and an
  internal error all begin with the line. `isinstance(sesion, _Sesion)` (`body/mcp.py:586`) is the LOCAL-mode
  gate: a `_SesionCliente` (REMOTE stdio client, BODY-MCP-REMOTO-CLIENTE-1) returns `contenido` unchanged.
  The hosted `/mcp` (`body/rutas/mcp_http.py`) never reaches `_procesar_mensaje` at all -- it carries its own
  `_procesar_uno` and its own `SERVER_INFO` (BODY-MCP-HTTP-1) -- so it was not touched and needed no check.
- Ruling 2, `_procesar_mensaje`'s `initialize` branch (`body/mcp.py:753-764`): for a `_Sesion`,
  `serverInfo` gains `"title"` (`_titulo_copia_pc`, `body/mcp.py:560-563`) and the result gains
  `"instructions"` (`_linea_copia_pc`, `body/mcp.py:566-577`); a `_SesionCliente` falls through to the
  original, unchanged branch.
- Ruling 3: every path is a WARN, never a refusal -- `_con_copia_pc` only ever prepends a line, it never
  raises or blocks a call; the same `_Sesion` that gets the line is the one the PC-only home already serves
  reads and propuestas from.
- Ruling 4, the marker census (read, nothing new built): `body/mudanza.py`'s `importar` runs reading a PC's
  database as the READ-ONLY *source* and writing into the DESTINATION (the host's own database, per
  `db.connect()`) -- it never writes anything back onto the PC-side file it read from, so a PC that was once
  migrated to the server carries no trace of that on itself. `body/conectar_pc.py --olvidar` /
  `pc_cliente.borrar_enlace()` deletes `dispositivo.json` outright, leaving no file or row behind once a link
  is forgotten. No `fuente_importacion`-like row, no `exportado_en`-like column, and no other marker exists
  anywhere in this home's own schema (`body/db.py`) or code that would let LOCAL mode tell it was ever moved
  or exported to a server. So ruling 1's sentence is the only one built; no "copia del PC; la fuente es el
  servidor" / "PC copy; the server is the source" variant exists, since nothing could ever select it.
  `_dia_mas_reciente_garmin` (`body/mcp.py:551-557`) reads `garmin_cuenta.dias_garmin_con_valor` (one query,
  no window -- this person's whole history), never `db.days_with_data` (counts an all-NULL/empty Garmin day
  as data) -- the ceiling is proven by `tests/test_rendimiento.py::McpCopiaPcDateCeilingTest` (one query, with
  30 days of Garmin history and with none).

**Both sentences, as committed** (`body/i18n/es.json:1178-1180`, `body/i18n/en.json:1178-1180`):
- `asistente.mcp.copia_pc_titulo`: es "Body en este PC (no el servidor)" / en "Body on this PC (not the
  server)".
- `asistente.mcp.copia_pc_con_fecha`: es "Body en este PC (no el servidor) -- datos del reloj hasta {fecha}"
  / en "Body on this PC (not the server) -- watch data up to {fecha}".
- `asistente.mcp.copia_pc_sin_fecha`: es "Body en este PC (no el servidor) -- sin datos del reloj" / en
  "Body on this PC (not the server) -- no watch data".
- The date itself goes through `body/rutas/comun.py`'s own `_short_date` (day, abbreviated month, year --
  the same helper `body/seguridad.py` and every route module already import for this), never a new date
  formatter.

**Tests (`tests/test_mcp_copia_pc.py`, new, 13 tests):** `initialize`'s own `instructions`/`title` with and
without Garmin history, and in English; a lectura result with and without data; a propuesta result;
`aplicar_propuesta`; `descartar_propuesta`; an unknown-tool refusal; a cap refusal; an internal error
(a patched `herramientas.ejecutar` raising `IntegrityError`); REMOTE mode (`_SesionCliente`) adding nothing to

`RegistrarEntrenoRelojFalloTest`'s two tests, `ToolCallInternalErrorTest`'s test, `VentanaRotanteTest`'s
language test, `AplicarExpiradaTest`'s test, `DescartarPropuestaTest::test_refuses_an_in_app_proposal_naming_
why`) and `tests/test_mcp_aplicar.py` (2 tests: `test_applies_its_own_mcp_origin_proposal`,
`test_cap_reached_is_a_tool_error`). `tests/test_mcp_cliente_remoto.py`, `tests/test_mcp_visible.py` and
`tests/test_i18n_paridad.py` needed no edit: the first two exercise REMOTE mode or the web screen, neither

## BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-2 -- the screen, the two assistant tools, habit-practica linking (2026-11-17/18)

ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1, the open follow-up BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-1 named in its own ledger
entry above: the "Tus prácticas" screen section, `leer_practicas`/`proponer_practica`, and linking
a habit back to a practice so a person can "bring a habit back" once the watch data shows it
slipped. Built over four commits on `feat/body-historia-vida-2` (`8e9eb09`, `1a0b251`, `8f7db09`,

## BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-2-R2 -- `practicas.resumen()`, the raised ceiling, the privacy sweep closed, merged (2026-11-18)

ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1, continuing BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-2-R's BLOCKED report: a
performance-shape fix inside `body/practicas.py`'s own module, a ceiling raised by its measured
cost, and a privacy sweep extended to the new route and tool.

**Ruling 1 -- `practicas.resumen(conn, person_id)`, one SELECT per source family for every active
practice together:** `body/practicas.py`. The three day-state calculators
(`_calcular_actividad`/`_calcular_metrica_umbral`/`_calcular_sueno_horario`) were split into a
fetch half (unchanged, still used by `estado()`) and a pure-compute half shared with the new
function -- `_estados_actividad` (`:62-80`), `_estados_metrica_umbral` (`:97-102`),
`_estados_sueno_horario` (`:245-260`). `resumen()` (`:494-563`) lists active practicas once
(`listar`), then for the whole set together: activity rows + `daily_metric(source='garmin')` days
ONCE for every `actividad` practica regardless of its own `regla`; `daily_metric` rows ONCE PER
DISTINCT `metric_key` any `metrica_umbral` practica actually uses (never once per practica sharing
a key); `sleep_session` rows ONCE for every `sueno_horario` practica -- then runs the SAME pure
calculators plus the SAME `_rachas_dia`/`_semanas` helpers `estado()` uses, in Python, for each
practica's own `{id, titulo, meta_dias_semana, racha_actual, ultima_semana}`. `estado()` itself is
untouched. `body/rutas/historial.py`'s `_practicas_resumen_ctx` (`:218-232`) now calls `resumen()`
instead of `estado()` per practica. Byte-identity: `tests/test_practicas.py`'s `ResumenTest`
(`:379-417`) -- one practica of every fuente plus one with no data at all, `resumen()`'s
`racha_actual`/`ultima_semana` compared field-for-field against `estado()`'s own
`racha_actual`/`semanas[-1]` for the same id.

## BODY-IDIOMA-HOGAR-1 -- one-tap language switch in the shared header, the assistant's own answer-in-my-language sentence (2026-11-18)

Two Hogar (Main) `para_productos` principles, read against Body by this orchestrator: `HOGAR-
IDIOMA-1` (hub `hit_01m7p4bvnyne4pgx8rzp9639kw`) -- "Each person picks their language with one
tap": es/en catalogs, the language stored per person, a second person's default from their
browser, one-tap English/Español in the header with `<html lang>` following, data never
translated. `HOGAR-IDIOMA-2` (hub `hit_01m7p735wdza6artajrjax4r0z`) -- "the in-app assistant gets
one line telling it to answer in the person's chosen language", while what is stored for or sent
to another system stays as it is.

**The orchestrator's census, verbatim from the spec's surface:** Body already stored
`person.language` (`body/db.py:346`), took a new person's language from Accept-Language on first
sign-in (`body/cuenta.py:439`, `body/rutas/sesion.py:64`), and rendered `<html lang="{{ t.lang
}}">` (`body/templates/base.html:49`); the switch existed only on `/settings`
(`body/rutas/ajustes.py:139-146`, `settings.html:7`, which always redirected to `/settings`); and
the assistant's system prompt `agente.sistema` carried no sentence telling the model which
language to answer in, so a message typed in the other language could pull the answer into it.

**Ruling 1 -- the one-tap switch, as built:** `body/templates/base.html:76-86`, inside
`<main><div class="wrap">`, gated by `{% if tab %}` (every real screen passes a `tab`; the one
base.html page rendered with no signed-in person -- `body/rutas/sesion.py`'s `_cuenta_down_page`,
Cuenta Duna unreachable mid sign-in -- passes `tab=None`, so the switch never renders there; the
other rejected-access pages, `sin_acceso.html`/`acceso_rechazado.html`/
`origen_rechazado.html`/`consentimiento.html`, never extend base.html at all). It shows only the
OTHER language's button (`t.lang=='es'` shows "English", else "Español") and posts a real `<form
method="post" action="/settings/language">` with a `<button type="submit">` -- no script, so it
works with JavaScript off. Its hidden `volver` field is the current tab's own root path, read off
the SAME tab->path map the nav links beside it already use literally (`today`->`/`,
`shifts`->`/shifts`, `trends`->`/trends`, `goals`->`/goals`, else `/settings`) -- `comun.py` is not
in this slice's `touches:`, so the exact sub-path (e.g. `/history`) is not threaded through a new
Jinja global; the ROUTE itself (next paragraph) accepts any same-site path regardless of where the
rendered button sends it, proven directly by `tests/test_idioma_hogar.py`'s
`LanguageSwitchRedirectTest.test_volver_to_a_same_site_path_is_honoured` (`volver=/history` ->
`/history`). CSS: `body/static/body.css:150-151` (`.idioma-switch`/`.idioma-switch-btn`, the same
`.ayuda-ctx`/`.foot-logout-btn` shapes already used for a top-right, 44px, underlined tap target).

`/settings/language` (`body/rutas/ajustes.py:139-160`): a new `_safe_volver` (`:139-149`) --
starts with `/`, not `//` or `/\` (a browser reads a backslash as a forward slash), and never
carries a `://` scheme separator, else `/settings` -- the same allow-list idea
`set_trabaja_turnos`'s own `volver` (`:157-159`, unchanged) uses, broadened from `{'/',
'/settings'}` to any such same-site path. `set_language` (`:152-160`) now reads `volver` from the
POST body and redirects there instead of always to `/settings`. `settings.html`'s own
Español/English pair (unchanged, no `volver` field) still redirects to `/settings` -- an absent
`volver` is the same "falls back to `/settings`" case `_safe_volver` already covers.

**Ruling 2 -- the assistant's own sentence, as built:** appended to `agente.sistema` in each
catalog (`body/i18n/es.json:1076`, `body/i18n/en.json:1076`), as committed:

    es: "Responde siempre en español, aunque la persona te escriba en otro idioma; los nombres de
    herramientas y los datos se quedan como están."
    en: "Always answer in English, even if the person writes in another language; tool names and
    data stay as they are."

Nothing else in `agente.sistema` changed; the sentence lands at the end, after the existing
`marcar_habito` sentence. `tests/test_registro_tu.py` flagged the Spanish sentence's own
"escriba" as an usted-register word-list hit (`_USTED_WORDS` includes it as the formal-imperative
spelling) -- a false positive: here it is third-person subjunctive ("aunque LA PERSONA te
escriba"), never a command to the reader. Fixed by a new `_USTED_WORD_ALLOW` dict
(`tests/test_registro_tu.py`, next to `_USTED_PHRASES`) with a reasoned
`"agente.sistema"` entry, mirroring the existing `_THIRD_PERSON_ALLOW` pattern one guard down, plus

## BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-3 -- the drill-down's weekly strip, an edit form, the weekly-target and baseline sentences, the header switch's real `volver` (2026-11-18)

The orchestrator's own review of BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-2 (merged `8e4a78b`) and BODY-IDIOMA-HOGAR-1
(merged `72564fb`), six problems found on `/history/practica/{id}` and the header language switch.

**Measurement, verbatim from the dispatch's own surface:**

(a) the drill-down's day grid (`practica.dias_title`, `_PRACTICAS_DIAS_RECIENTES = 90`) painted
every `no_hecho` day `--danger` red, so a 5-day/week practice looked like constant failure for the
other two days every week -- the same "never a colour of failure" rule BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-2's own
`ruling 1 UNKNOWN` gap (above, `specs/body-historia-vida-2.md` not in this repository) should have
covered for this screen, had it been found there; (b) no way to retitle or retarget a practica once
created; (c) `practica.meta_dias` ("Meta: {n} días por semana") read as a command, not a label; (d)
`practica.baseline_title`/the context sentence under it had no subject or units ("En general" alone,
then a bare metric-only sentence) and the shift list had no plural agreement ("1 noches"-shaped
output); (e) `base.html`'s `idioma_volver` was a fixed tab-root map (`history`->`/history`), so
posting the language switch from `/history/practica/1` sent the person back to `/history`'s own
root -- actually `/trends` per the dispatch's own wording -- never the page they were reading; (f)
`goals.retomar_nota` used straight quotes (`"X"`/`"X"`) instead of the project's own guillemets/curly
pair.

**Ruling 1 -- the weekly strip replaces the day grid as the drill-down's own main visual, as
built:** `body/practicas.py`'s existing `_semanas` rollup (unchanged) already carries `hecho`,
`semana_sin_dato` (`hecho+no_hecho < MODELO["MIN_DIAS_CON_DATO"]`, i.e. 4) and `cumple` per week --
no new SQL. `body/rutas/historial.py:347-359`'s `_semana_clase(semana, meta)` maps each week to
exactly one of four classes, never a failure colour: `w-gap` (too little data to judge),
`w-met` (`hecho >= meta`), `w-partial` (`hecho > 0`), `w-empty` (0 days). `:334-345`'s
`_semanas_en_temporada` turns each temporada's own `[desde, hasta]` into the set of Mondays it
covers, so a season's own weeks can be outlined. `:327-332`'s `_mes_anio_corto` labels each row with
a 3-letter month + year (`t('date.months')[...][:3]`). `:361-382`'s `_semanas_strip_ctx` builds rows
of `_SEMANAS_POR_FILA = 13` (`:26`, a quarter) weeks, each cell carrying `clase`, `en_temporada`
and an `aria` string (`practica.semana_aria`/`semana_aria_gap`). `:384-414`'s `_practica_detail_ctx`
exposes the result as `practica.semanas`. `body/templates/practica.html:21-35` renders it under
`practica.semanas_title` ("Tu historia, semana a semana" / "Your history, week by week"); the
recent-days grid below it (`:37-50`) is now explicitly the SECOND, more granular view, bounded to
`_PRACTICAS_DIAS_RECIENTES = 28` days (`:24`, was 90) under its own renamed heading
`practica.semanas_recientes_title` ("Últimas 4 semanas" / "Last 4 weeks"). `body/static/body.css`:
every `--danger` reference on a practice/day-grid rule removed -- `.strip-cell.p-no_hecho`'s
`::after`/legend dot now use `var(--muted)` (`:313,317`), `.strip-cell.p-sin_dato` is dimmed AND
dashed (`:314-315,318`, an honest gap, never a failure); the new `.week-cell` states
(`:325-333`): `w-empty` transparent, `w-partial` a `color-mix` of `var(--ok)` at 40%, `w-met` solid
`var(--ok)`, `w-gap` dashed, `w-season` an inset outline -- no `--danger` anywhere in either block.
Tests: `tests/test_practicas_web.py`'s `WeeklyStripTest.test_met_partial_empty_and_gap_weeks_each_
render_their_class` (`:215-241`, all four classes present from one fixture), the pre-existing
`DetailTest.test_seasons_section_lists_a_season_with_context_and_day_links` (`:191-208`) extended
to assert `w-season`, `NoFailureColorInPracticeStylesTest.test_no_danger_variable_in_practice_or_
weekly_styles` (`:247-254`, reads `body.css`, fails if any actual rule line -- `"{" in line` --

`DetailTest.test_detail_bounds_the_recent_day_grid_to_the_last_4_weeks` (`:157-...`, asserts "Últimas

**Ruling 5 -- the header switch's `volver` is the request's own path, as built:**
`body/rutas/comun.py:91` -- `env.globals["ruta_actual"] = lambda: _RUTA_ACTUAL.get()`, next to the
existing `env.globals` entries (`static_url`, `hosted`, `es_demo`, `tarea_en_contexto`). This is a

targeting another module, so `tests/test_guardia_parches.py`'s `NoReverseShimGuardTest` does not

(`body/rutas/comun.py:51`) is set in `body/web.py`'s middleware from the raw ASGI `scope["path"]` --
the concrete path actually requested, never a route template -- so `GET /goals/new?practica_id=5`
carries `/goals/new` with no query string at all (FastAPI/Starlette separate `path` from

## BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-4 -- the day-shift noun reads as a shift, the day grid's Monday-first header and pad cell, the weekly strip's own legend (2026-11-18)

**Measurement, from the dispatch's own surface** (`specs/body-historia-vida-4.md`, not in this
repository; reconstructed here from the commit that built it, `4d9cbfc`, since the slice that ran it
stopped BLOCKED before writing this entry -- BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-4-R below closes that gap):

Three rulings against `/history/practica/{id}`: (1) the English baseline sentence's shift nouns
("1 morning", "3 nights") read as calendar words, not shifts -- every working kind needed 'shift' in
its own noun, and Spanish's `día` noun alone needed the same fix (`mañana`/`tarde`/`noche` already
read as shifts); (2) the drill-down's recent-days grid had no weekday header and its leading pad cell
(a short first week) drew as a visible empty cell; (3) the weekly strip (BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-3 ruling
1) had no legend for its four classes, and no fifth swatch for a season.

**Ruling 1 -- the day-shift noun, as built:** `body/i18n/en.json:1050-1061` -- every
`shift.kind.noun.*`/`noun_plural.*` English string gains the word "shift" (`"morning"`->`"morning
shift"`, `"afternoon"`->`"afternoon shift"`, `"night"`->`"night shift"`, `"day"`->`"day shift"`, and
their plurals), `shift.kind.noun.off`/`noun_plural.off` ("day off"/"days off") unchanged -- already
reads as a shift. `body/i18n/es.json:1050-1061` -- only `shift.kind.noun.day`/`noun_plural.day`
change (`"día"`->`"turno de día"`, `"días"`->`"turnos de día"`); `mañana`/`tarde`/`noche` already read
as shifts in Spanish. Tests: `tests/test_practicas_web.py`'s `BaselineSentenceTest` (`:351-427`) --
`test_baseline_sentence_uses_turno_de_dia_for_day_shift_counts`,
`test_english_baseline_sentence_uses_shift_nouns_for_day_and_night`, plus the pre-existing
plural-agreement and no-shift-clause cases re-run against the new nouns.

**Ruling 2 -- the Monday-first weekday header and the transparent pad cell, as built:**
`body/rutas/comun.py:154-157`'s new `_week_letters(t)` reads `t('date.days')` into Monday-first
initials -- lifted out of `body/rutas/metas.py`'s habit week strip (`:97-123`, `_week_strip` now
calls `comun._week_letters(t)` at `:104` and indexes it at `:123` instead of hand-typing
`name[:1].upper()` a second time) so the habit week strip and the practice day grid header share one
helper, never two hardcoded letter lists. `body/rutas/historial.py:410`'s `_practica_detail_ctx`

## BODY-INSTALL-DESDE-VIVO-1

**The incident (2026-11-17):** the installer was run from the LIVE tree (`body-app-live`, a linked
worktree that BODY-LIVE-CHECKOUT-1's installer itself creates, detached at `main`) instead of from
`body-app`. `scripts/install-daily-sync.ps1:32` takes `$repo = Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent`, so
`$repo` became the live tree: `$py`/`$pyw` pointed at a `.venv` that does not exist there, every
scheduled task was registered on that missing interpreter, and `$LiveDir` defaulted to `"$repo-live"`,
so a second worktree `body-app-live-live` was created. Nothing refused. The preamble already measured
worktree identity for `$LiveDir` (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`) but never for `$repo` itself.

**The rulings (Tier 2, quality; "anything off the normal flow raises a flag"):**

1. Before anything else runs -- before `$LiveDir` is defaulted, before any `git worktree add`, before
   any `Register-ScheduledTask` -- the installer checks that `$repo` is the MAIN working tree of its
   repository: `git -C $repo rev-parse --git-dir` and `--git-common-dir`, both resolved to full paths,
   must be the same directory; if they differ, it prints one line in Spanish naming the main tree's
   path (the common dir's parent) and the exact command to run instead, and `exit 1`, registering
   nothing.
2. Right after, it checks that `$py` exists; if not, one line naming the missing interpreter path and
   `exit 1` -- a scheduled task is never registered on an interpreter that is not there.
3. The messages follow the script's existing ASCII-Spanish style; no absolute personal path is written
   into the script.

**Built, file:line:**

* Ruling 1 -- `scripts/install-daily-sync.ps1:34-44`: `$repoGitDirRaw`/`$repoCommonDirRaw` from
  `git -C $repo rev-parse --git-dir` / `--git-common-dir`, resolved to full paths with
  `Join-Path`/`Resolve-Path`; a mismatch sets `$mainTree = Split-Path $repoCommonDirFull -Parent` and
  exits. This sits before the `$LiveDir` default (`:46`), before `git -C $repo worktree add --detach`
  (`:63` after the insertion) and before the first `Register-ScheduledTask` (hosted branch, well
  after).
* Ruling 2 -- `scripts/install-daily-sync.ps1:48-51`: `if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $py))`, right
  after `$py` is assigned (`:47`) and before `$pyw` (`:52`) -- also before the first
  `Register-ScheduledTask`.

**The exact messages as committed:**

* Main-tree mismatch (`:42`): `"Este es el arbol vivo (una copia que el instalador mantiene), no el
  repo. Corre el instalador desde: $mainTree\scripts\install-daily-sync.ps1"`
* Missing interpreter (`:49`): `"No encuentro el interprete Python en $py. No registro nada."`

Both are plain ASCII (no accents), matching the script's existing style (`:54`, `:60`, `:65` as they
stood before this slice). No absolute personal path (`C:\Duna`, `C:\Users`) appears in either block --
`$mainTree` and `$py` are runtime variables, never literals.

**Tests added**, `tests/test_installer.py` (read the script as text, like the existing classes):
`InstallerMainTreeGuardTest` (order before `$LiveDir` default, before `worktree add`, before the first
`Register-ScheduledTask`; the mismatch block has `exit 1`, names `arbol vivo` and
`install-daily-sync.ps1`; no absolute personal path), `InstallerPyExistsGuardTest` (same order/exit/no-
personal-path checks for the `$py` guard), and `InstallerMainTreeVsWorktreeGitBehaviourTest` -- runs
ONLY `git rev-parse --git-dir` / `--git-common-dir` against a throwaway repo and a
`git worktree add --detach` of it under the test's own temp dir, proving the two values match on the
main tree and differ on the worktree; it never invokes the script itself.

**Gate, exact command:** `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .` -- run as 11
sequential alphabetical chunks of dotted modules (20 modules each except the last, 209 modules total):

1. `test_accesibilidad`..`test_baselines`: `Ran 385 tests in 63.104s` -- OK (skipped=1, expected
   failures=1)

## BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-2 -- leer_intradia: a few hours of one day, local time, refreshed on demand (2026-11-18)

**Ruling 1** -- a new `lectura` tool, `leer_intradia` (`body/agente/herramientas.py:2921-2928`, function
`_leer_intradia` at `:932` plus helpers `_hora_local` at `:914` and `_motivo_intradia_sin_datos` at
`:921`), gated at `nivel: "completo"`, the same gate `leer_dia` itself enforces. Parameters `fecha`
(a day), `desde`/`hasta` (local HH:MM, normalized via `strftime("%H:%M")` after parsing so an
unpadded `"6:00"` still compares correctly against a stored `"06:05"`). The window is capped at
`_LEER_INTRADIA_MAX_MIN = 4 * 60` minutes; longer is refused with the cap stated in the message
(`"leer_intradia admite hasta 4 horas por llamada (...); divide el rango"`). Returns, for that window
only: heart-rate and stress points as `[hora_local, valor]` via `db.intradia`, and -- for the part of
the window inside Garmin's own sleep session (`sleep_session.start_local/end_local` for that day) --
the sleep minute arrays via `db.sueno_minuto_a_minuto` plus that start/end. A minute with no stored
value is simply absent, never a 0 (both db functions' own contract; `_leer_intradia` never fills a
gap). An empty window explains why via `MOTIVOS_INTRADIA_SIN_DATOS = ("fuera_de_alcance",
"reloj_apagado", "no_traido")`: out of Garmin's own 130-day retention (`pull.INTRADIA_ALCANCE_DIAS`),
the watch never connected, or it is connected but that part of the day was not fetched yet.

Offered wherever `leer_dia` is offered with no separate wiring: the in-app assistant and both MCP
tool lists (local `body/mcp.py`, hosted `body/mcp.py`'s same path) all derive their listings from the
static `HERRAMIENTAS` registry this entry extends, confirmed by `tests/test_mcp.py`'s new
`test_leer_intradia_is_offered_and_callable`. The tool's own description (committed verbatim, Spanish,
`es.json`-register-guard-clean) tells the model this is for a few hours of one day and points
elsewhere for a range of days: *"El pulso y el estrés minuto a minuto en una ventana de hasta 4 horas
dentro de un día (...), con el sueño minuto a minuto para la parte de la ventana que cae dentro de esa
noche. Para un rango de varios días usa leer_serie; para el resto de ese mismo día usa leer_dia. Pasada
la ventana de 4 horas se rechaza sin leer nada: divide el rango."* A `lectura` permission key sees it
like any other lectura tool (`tests/test_llave_asistente.py`, unchanged -- it derives its own list the
same dynamic way).

**Ruling 2 (freshness on demand)** -- `body/pull.py`'s new `actualizar_intradia_si_corresponde(person_id,
day)` (added after `_pull_intradia_pendientes`). When `day` is today or yesterday in the person's own
zone and `db.intradia_almacenado` is false, it refreshes that one day through
`traer_intradia(..., forzar=True)` using the SAME per-person Garmin-session path the scheduled pull
already uses for that mode: hosted (`garmin_cuenta.leer`/`.guardar`) or local (the adapter's own stored
token) -- never a new token path. Called from `ejecutar()` in `body/agente/herramientas.py` (the
`necesita_actualizacion` branch), never from `_leer_intradia`'s own body: a `lectura` tool must never
write (enforced both by `PRAGMA query_only` and the static writer-guard that walks every lectura tool's
own call graph), the same place `HERRAMIENTAS_HOY`'s own `_lanzar_pull_hoy_en_hilo` already runs its
write trigger from -- but SYNCHRONOUS here, since the just-asked-about window must already be filled
before the read that follows in the same tool call.

The guard: at most one attempt per `(person_id, day)` every `INTRADIA_FRESCURA_ESPACIO_MIN = 30`
minutes, kept in an in-process dict (`_ULTIMO_INTENTO_FRESCURA_INTRADIA`) -- a worker's choice: a
restart loses the guard, which only costs one extra on-demand fetch, never a wrong answer. Deliberately
NOT `garmin_cuenta`'s own `ultimo_intento_en`/`reintentar_despues_de` (BODY-SYNC-VIVO-ESTADO-1): an
intraday refresh failure must never show up as a daily-sync backoff on Hoy's own "Tu reloj" card
(`texto_estado_vivo` reads exactly those two columns) or delay the next scheduled pull's own
`puede_intentar` check. A refresh that fails or is refused never raises -- every exception is caught
and reported back as `True` ("an attempt was made and it did not succeed"), which `ejecutar()` threads
through as `actualizacion_fallo`, surfacing `t("asistente.intradia.no_actualizado")` ("No pude traer
los datos más recientes justo ahora; aquí tienes lo último que ya tengo guardado.") in the result with
the stored data still returned -- never an exception to the model.

**Ruling 3** -- no figure in the result belongs to anyone but the person asking (`db.person`'s own
`person_id` scoping, proven by `tests/test_persona_fuga.py`'s cross-person sweep, which now names
`leer_intradia` in `READ_TOOLS`); every time in the result is local, with the zone named once
(`out["zona"]`), never repeated per point.

## BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-3 -- the model: dormitando/despierto_quieto/levantado/sin_dato, relative to his own baseline (2026-11-18)

**Carlos's surface**, relayed by the desk, verbatim: *"I think that body should be like the app that reflects
reality in most accurate about my body so because it's the mix between the data that is stored by the watch
and and all the other info that can gather, use as my timeline, GPS, the things that I report to you, eating,
training with detail, I mean everything."*

**The orchestrator's reading** (dev-protocol DECISIONS.md `## BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-RULING`, as given in this
slice's own dispatch): the evidence decides -- dozing after Garmin's own sleep end is proposed as SLEEP, quiet
awake time in bed only as the GET-UP time, and "cannot tell" is said plainly; Garmin's own record is never
edited.

**This slice is the MODEL only** -- no screen, no tool, no schema (BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-4..7 below). New module
`body/despertar_real.py`, a pure read over a connection and a person id (no web imports, no writes, no network),
the same shape as `body/recuperacion.py`, `body/turno_fc.py` and `body/sueno_fc.py`.

**`MODELO`** (`body/despertar_real.py:59-104`), every threshold a named model parameter, as committed:

| parameter | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | `"despertar-real-v1"` | |
| `horizonte_horas` | `4` | how far past Garmin's own sleep end the model ever looks |
| `ventana_base_min` | `30` | minutes before Garmin's own end used to read the baseline |
| `cobertura_min_base` | `3` | fewest baseline samples trusted before falling back |
| `margen_dormitando_bpm` | `5` | bpm over baseline still read as dozing |
| `margen_levantado_bpm` | `15` | bpm over baseline that is a CANDIDATE rise |
| `margen_estres_descanso` | `10` | stress points over baseline still the night's own rest range |
| `tolerancia_pareo_estres_min` | `5` | minutes a stress reading may sit from a heart-rate reading to be paired |
| `minutos_sostenidos` | `10` | minutes a candidate rise must hold to read as 'levantado' |
| `factor_hueco_espaciado` | `3` | gap, as a multiple of the night's own observed spacing, that is 'sin_dato' |
| `espaciado_asumido_min` | `2` | assumed spacing only when fewer than two samples exist to measure it |
| `cobertura_sin_dato_max_alta` | `0.1` | share of the horizon as 'sin_dato' still allowed for 'alta' |
| `cobertura_sin_dato_max_media` | `0.5` | share above which the evidence is thin -- 'baja' and 'ninguna' unless an event bounds it |

None are a bare constant tuned to Carlos: every margin is relative to the person's own baseline, read fresh
for each call.

**Rulings, as built:**

1. `estimar(conn, person_id, day) -> dict` (`body/despertar_real.py:286`): Garmin's own `sueno_inicio`/
   `sueno_fin` (straight from `sleep_session`), `segmentos` (each `tipo` one of `dormitando` |
   `despierto_quieto` | `levantado` | `sin_dato`, with its own `inicio`/`fin`), `primera_levantada`,
   `propuesta` (`sueno` with a later end, `levantado` with a get-up time, or `ninguna`), `confianza`
   (`alta`/`media`/`baja`), and `evidencia` by source. Honest gaps return the same shape with `segmentos: []`
   and `evidencia: {"motivo": ...}` (`sin_sesion` or `sin_linea_base`, `body/despertar_real.py:262-276`).

2. Baseline relative to the person's OWN heart rate near the end of that night's sleep
   (`_baseline`, `body/despertar_real.py:117-141`): median of `db.sueno_minuto_a_minuto`'s own
   `heart_rate` array over `ventana_base_min` minutes before Garmin's own end (preferred), falling back to
   `db.intradia`'s `intradia_fc` over the same window, falling back again to `daily_metric.resting_hr` ONLY
   where neither gives `cobertura_min_base` points -- never an absolute bpm anywhere. Stress baseline the
   same window, `intradia_estres` only (the sleep array carries no stress series),
   `body/despertar_real.py:150-164`. Classification (`_clasificar_punto`, `body/despertar_real.py:176-189`):
   dozing = heart rate within `margen_dormitando_bpm` of baseline AND stress inside `margen_estres_descanso`
   (or no paired stress at all); a CANDIDATE rise = heart rate at/over `margen_levantado_bpm` AND stress having
   left that range; everything else is `despierto_quieto`. A candidate run confirms as `levantado` only once
   it holds for `minutos_sostenidos` (`_segmentos`, `body/despertar_real.py:204-239`) -- shorter, it is a blip
   and stays `despierto_quieto`. Gaps wider than `factor_hueco_espaciado` times the night's own observed
   spacing are `sin_dato` and never classified; a horizon with no heart-rate point at all is one whole
   `sin_dato` run.

3. Every source Body already has (`_eventos`, `body/despertar_real.py:242-260`), read by one query per
   source regardless of day or event count: a logged meal (`comida.ts_local`, `body/db.py:810`), a check-in
   (`checkin.ts_local`, `body/db.py:1016`), a training session or activity start (`activity.start_local`,
   `body/db.py:406`) -- time and source name only, never the meal's words, the check-in's
   mood/energy/stress_felt, or the activity's own type. Used as an upper bound on the get-up time in
   `estimar`'s own decision (`body/despertar_real.py:316-335`): the EARLIEST of a confirmed HR rise and a
   logged event wins, and the chosen `confianza` is capped at `media` when an event is what decided it.
   **Checked and found not usable today:** `body/desplazamiento_import.py:26-28`
   (`FUENTE = "personal:commute-diario.csv"`, `COUNT_COLUMNS`) stores only a DAILY count summary
   (vehicle_minutes/vehicle_trips/walking_minutes/cycling_minutes) with no per-event departure timestamp --
   a named gap, not a source used here. **Named hook:** `_eventos_lugares`
   (`body/despertar_real.py:110-115`) returns `[]` until Lugares' own read API exists
   (BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-LUGARES-1), in the same `{"fuente", "hora"}` shape every other source uses.

4. Honest output (`body/despertar_real.py:316-357`): no baseline at all, or a `sin_dato` share of the
   horizon over `cobertura_sin_dato_max_media` with no logged event to bound it, reads `confianza: "baja"`
   and `propuesta: {"tipo": "ninguna"}` -- never a guess. An immediate rise right at Garmin's own end also
   reads `propuesta: "ninguna"` (Garmin was already right, nothing to add). Every figure the model reads is
   the one person's own (`tests/test_persona_fuga.py`'s new `DespertarRealFugaTest` below).

**Tests, `tests/test_despertar_real.py`** (10 tests, invented nights only -- a dozing tail, synthetic baseline
levels, no real figure): a dozing tail with no later rise proposes `sueno` with the later end
(`DozingTailTest`); quiet-awake-then-rise proposes `levantado` at the rise, never at the start of the quiet
stretch (`QuietAwakeThenRiseTest`); an immediate rise proposes `ninguna` (`ImmediateRiseTest`); a watch-off
gap over the whole horizon is one `sin_dato` segment with `confianza: "baja"` (`WatchOffGapTest`); a logged
meal, or a check-in/activity, before any HR-detected rise bounds the get-up time and appears in `evidencia`
by source, confidence capped at `media` (`EventoAcotaLevantadoTest`, 2 tests); the SAME night shape at two
different baselines (shifted +40 bpm) classifies identically -- same segment kinds, same relative timing
(`RelativeBaselineTest`); a heart-rate rise with stress staying in its own rest range never confirms as
`levantado` (`EstresFueraDeDescansoRequeridoTest`); `sin_sesion`/`sin_linea_base` honest gaps
(`SinSesionYSinLineaBaseTest`, 2 tests).

**Cross-person sweep, `tests/test_persona_fuga.py`'s new `DespertarRealFugaTest`:** this module has no
assistant tool yet (ruling, no tool this slice), so it is swept directly rather than through `READ_TOOLS` --
person A gets a confident rise, person B (same day) gets only a `sleep_session` row and nothing else;
`estimar(conn, PERSON_B, day)` reads `segmentos: []`, `confianza: "baja"`, `propuesta: "ninguna"`, never A's
rise.

**Bounded queries, `tests/test_rendimiento.py`'s new `DespertarRealCostTest`:** a sparse day (a handful of
points) and a dense one (120 heart-rate points, 80 stress points, one logged meal) cost the SAME number of
statements -- measured 8 on the dense fixture, ceiling `ceil(8 * 1.3) = 11` (this file's own margin rule).

**Gate, exact command:** `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .` -- run as 11 sequential
alphabetical chunks of dotted modules (20 per chunk except the last, 211 modules total, +1 over

## BODY-MCP-PENDIENTES-VIGENCIA-1 -- `pendientes_mcp` stops counting an expired proposal nobody ever opened (2026-11-18)

**The desk's surface**, 2026-11-18: Carlos's Today page showed «Your personal assistant suggests 3 changes ·
Review» and asked whether they were stale. Reading the code: the count comes from
`agente_conversacion.pendientes_mcp` (`body/agente/conversacion.py:39-52` before this slice), which counts
every `propuesta_agente` row with `estado = 'propuesta'` in an 'mcp' conversation -- but a proposal's expiry
is LAZY: it gets `expira_en` at creation (`body/agente/propuestas.py:133-135`, `EXPIRA_MINUTOS = 15` at
`:86`, or the end of the next local day for an mcp-origin one) and is only marked 'expirada' when something
touches it (`:156`, `:1707`). So a proposal nobody opened stayed 'propuesta' forever and Today kept
announcing it, and its link opened a panel full of proposals that could no longer be applied.
`pendientes_mcp`'s own docstring already said both Hoy's line and the assistant panel's default read it.

**The orchestrator's rulings** (Tier 2, quality; "anything off the normal flow raises a flag -- and a stale
flag is a false one"), each as built:

1. **`pendientes_mcp` counts only proposals still in force** -- `estado = 'propuesta' AND expira_en >
   <now>`, now in the same ISO form `_ahora()`/`_iso()` already write elsewhere in this codebase, one
   statement, the same cost; the newest conversation id comes from the same filtered set (one `WHERE`
   clause feeds both the `COUNT` and the `MAX`); `ahora` is an injectable parameter for tests, real UTC
   `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` by default -- as built: `body/agente/conversacion.py:39-56`. Its only two
   callers, `body/rutas/hoy.py:219` (`_mcp_pendientes_ctx`, Hoy's own line) and
   `body/rutas/asistente.py:1082` (the panel's `pendiente` sentinel), needed no change: both call it with no
   `ahora`, so both pick up the real-clock filter for free.

## BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-1-INV (findings) -- superseding the placeholder, restated with file:line evidence (2026-11-18)

The placeholder entry above says truthfully that this slice's own sandbox (scoped to `C:\Duna\body\body-app`
alone) could never read `logs/worker-body-despertar-real-1-inv-body-app-20261118T091720.json`, the
investigation's own report, and that remains true today -- this entry is not a transcription of that report
either. What follows is the investigation's own findings restated from what BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-3's model and
this slice's own schema work independently confirm against the live Garmin adapter, intraday storage and
commute importer -- each one a fact about this repository's own data, checked again directly here, not
copied from a report nobody in this lineage has been able to open.

**Finding 1 -- Garmin's own intraday heart-rate interval is 2 minutes**, the fallback spacing
`despertar_real.MODELO["espaciado_asumido_min"]` is set to when fewer than two samples exist to measure the
night's own spacing directly (`body/despertar_real.py:95-97`).

**Finding 2 -- Garmin's own intraday stress interval is roughly 3 minutes**, wider than the heart-rate one,
which is why `MODELO["tolerancia_pareo_estres_min"]` (5 minutes) has to cover at least one full stress cycle
to pair a stress reading with a heart-rate one (`body/despertar_real.py:80-84`).

**Finding 3 -- the sleep array carries no stress series.** `db.sueno_minuto_a_minuto`'s own per-minute arrays
(parsed from Garmin's `sleep` raw payload) hold heart rate and movement, never stress -- `_baseline_estres`
reads `intradia_estres` instead, over the same window (`body/despertar_real.py:150-153`).

**Finding 4 -- `save_day`'s own `sleep_session` write is a fixed 4-column `INSERT OR REPLACE`** (`person_id`,
`day`, `start_local`, `end_local`, `body/db.py:2221-2226`): any column added as a sibling on that table would
be silently blanked on the day's next sync. This is the finding this slice's own ruling 1 acts on directly
(`body/db.py:1509-1514`): the person's own correction lives in its own table, `despertar_correccion`, never a
sibling column.

**Finding 5 -- the commute importer stores no per-event timestamp.** `body/desplazamiento_import.py:26-28`
(`FUENTE = "personal:commute-diario.csv"`, `COUNT_COLUMNS = ("vehicle_minutes", "vehicle_trips",
"walking_minutes", "cycling_minutes")`) is a DAILY count summary only -- no departure or arrival time per
trip -- so it cannot bound a get-up time the way a logged meal, check-in or activity start can
(`despertar_real._eventos`, `body/despertar_real.py:242-260`). Checked and found not usable today, not a
source this slice or BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-3 before it ever reads for this purpose.

**Finding 6 -- Lugares has no read API yet.** `despertar_real._eventos_lugares` (`body/despertar_real.py:110-
115`) is a named hook returning `[]` until BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-LUGARES-1 gives GPS-derived timeline events a
read path, in the same `{"fuente", "hora"}` shape every other source already uses.

**Unknown, still:** the investigation's own report may hold findings beyond these six -- about activities,
training detail or other evidence Carlos named in his own surface (*"my timeline, GPS, the things that I
report to you, eating, training with detail, I mean everything"*) that neither BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-3 nor this
slice needed to act on. Whoever next has access to `logs/worker-body-despertar-real-1-inv-body-app-20261118T091720.json`
from the dev-protocol side should still reconcile it against this entry rather than trust this one alone.

## BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-4 -- corregir_despertar: the person's own correction beside Garmin's own sleep, never a sibling column on it (2026-11-18)

**Carlos's surface**, relayed by the desk, verbatim (same surface BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-3 quoted): *"I think
that body should be like the app that reflects reality in most accurate about my body so because it's the
mix between the data that is stored by the watch and and all the other info that can gather, use as my
timeline, GPS, the things that I report to you, eating, training with detail, I mean everything."*

**The orchestrator's rulings** (dev-protocol DECISIONS.md `## ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`, as given in
this slice's own dispatch): a new `despertar_correccion` table, additive, NEVER a sibling column on
`sleep_session` (Finding 4 above); a 16th `propuesta_agente.accion` widening, `corregir_despertar`, offered
wherever `corregir_entreno` is; `leer_dia`/`leer_intradia` show the correction next to Garmin's own sleep,
both labelled as which is which.

**Ruling 1 -- `despertar_correccion`** (`body/db.py:1509-1527`), guarded `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, one
row per `(person_id, day)` (`UNIQUE` constraint), columns `tipo` (`'sueno'`|`'levantado'`), `hora_local`,
`modelo_version`, `origen` (`'persona'`|`'asistente'`), `creada_en`. Three functions right after
`sueno_minuto_a_minuto`: `despertar_correccion` (read, `body/db.py:2635-2642`), `guardar_despertar_correccion`
(upsert via `ON CONFLICT(person_id, day) DO UPDATE`, `body/db.py:2645-2657`), `borrar_despertar_correccion`
(delete, quiet no-op when absent). Wired into census: `body/mudanza.py`'s `TableSpec("despertar_correccion",
match_cols=("person_id", "day"))`, `body/privacidad.py`'s `FULLY_HANDLED_TABLES` plus an
`despertar_correcciones` list in `export_person()` and a delete in `delete_person()`,
`tests/test_persona_fuga.py`'s `_seed_person()`, `body/demo.py`'s `_seed_despertar_correccion` (one invented
correction, 25 minutes after the demo person's own last Garmin sleep end).

Proven in `tests/test_migraciones.py` (`DespertarCorreccionTableMigrationTest`,
`DespertarCorreccionFreshDbTest`): an old-shape database gains the table on its next `init()` keeping every
other table's row untouched, idempotent, enforces one row per day. Proven again in the new
`tests/test_despertar_correccion.py` (11 tests): read/save/delete round trip; saving twice replaces, never
duplicates; different days each get their own row; deleting an absent row is a quiet no-op;
`sleep_session`'s own row is byte-identical before and after a correction is saved; a re-sync of the same day
(`db.save_day` with the same `sleep_start`/`sleep_end`) leaves the correction in place; `leer_dia` shows the
correction next to Garmin's own sleep (or omits the key when there is none), and never shows one for a day
with no Garmin sleep even if a stray row exists.

**Ruling 2 -- `corregir_despertar`**, a `propuesta` tool (`body/agente/herramientas.py:1021-1056`, registry
entry at the end of `HERRAMIENTAS`), parameters `fecha`, `tipo` (`'sueno'`|`'levantado'`), `hora` (local
HH:MM). Validates: the day has a Garmin `sleep_session.end_local`
(`agente.error.despertar_sin_sueno`/"That day has no sleep recorded by Garmin."); `hora` is strictly after
that end (`agente.error.despertar_hora_no_posterior`/"The time must be after the sleep end Garmin
recorded."); `hora` is within `despertar_real.MODELO["horizonte_horas"]` (4 hours) of it
(`agente.error.despertar_hora_fuera_horizonte`/"The time is too far past the sleep end Garmin recorded.");
`tipo` is one of the two JSON-schema enum values (malformed input never reaches the function body). The
proposal's `despues_json` carries `despertar_real.estimar`'s own `confianza` and `evidencia` for that day, a
snapshot taken at proposal time, never recomputed live at card render.

Card text (`body/rutas/asistente.py:858-884`, titles and strings committed verbatim):
- Title: es `"Corregir despertar"`, en `"Correct wake-up"`.
- `'sueno'`: es `"Contar como sueño hasta las {hora} (Garmin marcó {fin})"`, en `"Count as sleep until {hora}
  (Garmin recorded {fin})"`.
- `'levantado'`: es `"Te levantaste a las {hora} (Garmin marcó tu despertar a las {fin})"`, en `"You got up
  at {hora} (Garmin recorded waking at {fin})"`.
- Evidence line, appended only when `despertar_real.estimar`'s own `evidencia.eventos` named a source: es
  `"Según: {fuentes}."`, en `"Based on: {fuentes}."`, each source named by a dict-lookup key
  (`_FUENTE_EVIDENCIA_KEYS`, never a hand-typed i18n-key concatenation) -- `asistente.propuesta.despertar_fuente.comida`
  ("una comida registrada" / "a logged meal"), `.checkin` ("un check-in" / "a check-in"), `.actividad`
  ("una actividad o entrenamiento" / "a logged activity or training session").

Apply (`body/agente/propuestas.py:898-935`) writes through `db.guardar_despertar_correccion` with `origen =
'asistente'` -- Garmin's own `sleep_session` row is never touched either way, proven directly in
`tests/test_corregir_despertar.py::ApplyUndoTest::test_apply_writes_the_correction`. **Undo choice:** when the
day had no prior correction, undo deletes the row (`db.borrar_despertar_correccion`); when a prior correction
existed (whether from a previous `corregir_despertar` apply or set directly), undo restores that exact prior
row (`tipo`, `hora_local`, `modelo_version`, `origen`) rather than deleting it -- the same "restore what was
there, or remove what was not" shape every other `propuesta` action in this registry already uses. Drift is
checked both ways by comparing the live row against the proposal's own `antes`/`despues` snapshot
(`_drift_aplicar_corregir_despertar`, `_drift_deshacer_corregir_despertar`); `corregir_despertar` is NOT in
`ACCIONES_REEMPLAZABLES` -- a second correction of the same day is its own separate pending proposal, the
same precedent `corregir_entreno` set.

Offered wherever `corregir_entreno` is: `body/mcp.py` needed no code change (confirmed directly,
`tests/test_corregir_despertar.py::CatalogParityTest::test_listed_over_stdio_mcp`) since its tool listing and
dispatch are fully generic over the static `HERRAMIENTAS` registry.

**Ruling 3 -- `leer_dia`/`leer_intradia` show the correction beside Garmin's own sleep**
(`body/agente/herramientas.py:811-818` and `:1004-1009`): only when Garmin's own sleep exists for that
call (a correction cannot exist without one, ruling 2's own refusal at creation), the tool's own `sleep`/
`sueno` dict gains a `correccion` key carrying the row exactly as `db.despertar_correccion` returns it --
Garmin's own `start_local`/`end_local` (or `inicio`/`fin`) stay exactly as they were, never merged with or
overwritten by the correction. Proven in `tests/test_leer_intradia.py`'s new `CorreccionTest` (2 tests) and
`tests/test_despertar_correccion.py`'s `LeerDiaMuestraCorreccionTest` (3 tests, including the stray-row case
above).

## BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-7

Carlos's own surface, relayed by the desk 2026-11-18, verbatim: *"I think that body should be like the app
that reflects reality in most accurate about my body so because it's the mix between the data that is
stored by the watch and and all the other info that can gather, use as my timeline, GPS, the things that I
report to you, eating, training with detail, I mean everything."* Until this slice, `despertar_real.estimar`
(BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-3) and the `corregir_despertar` propuesta tool (BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-4) existed only for
chat/MCP -- no screen showed either one. This slice is that screen, built to the orchestrator's own rulings
(`BODY-DESPERTAR-RULING` in dev-protocol's own DECISIONS.md: the evidence decides, Garmin's record is never
edited, the correction is Body's own layer applied only on the person's own tap, undoable) and to five
specific rulings given in the dispatch.

**Ruling 1 -- Día's own line and button** (`body/rutas/hoy.py:_despertar_dia_ctx`, wired into `day_view()`;
rendered in `body/templates/day.html` right after the `sueno_fc_linea` paragraph in the sleep card): when
`despertar_real.estimar` returns a `propuesta` other than `'ninguna'` at `confianza` `'alta'`/`'media'` and
the day has no correction yet, shows one line (`day.despertar.sueno_linea` or `day.despertar.levantado_linea`,
both es/en below) plus a "¿Corregir?"/"Correct it?" button (`day.despertar.corregir_boton`). The button posts
to the new `/day/{day}/despertar/proponer` route, which raises the SAME `corregir_despertar` propuesta a
chat/MCP call would, through `agente_herramientas._corregir_despertar` -- the exact precedent
`/settings/nutriente/proponer` (`body/rutas/ajustes.py`) already sets: a conversation created, the tool
function called directly, `ToolError` swallowed. Confianza `'baja'` or `propuesta.tipo == 'ninguna'` -> no
line, matching the ruling. The pending proposal's own card (once raised) shows inline with its own summary
text (`_despertar_propuesta_txt`, duplicating the `asistente.propuesta.despertar_sueno_resumen`/
`despertar_levantado_resumen` wording already used by the chat card -- read, never written, by this slice)
and Aplicar/Descartar buttons. **The card-reuse choice, recorded as the dispatch asked:** Aplicar/Descartar
post to two new routes (`/day/{day}/despertar/propuestas/{id}/aplicar|descartar`) that both delegate straight
to the existing, accion-agnostic `_entreno_propuesta_resolver` (no new resolver logic written) -- the same
function `/day/{day}/entreno/propuestas/{id}/aplicar|descartar` already uses for a different accion, proven
accion-agnostic by this reuse.

**Ruling 2 -- once a correction exists** (same `_despertar_dia_ctx`, the `correccion is not None` branch):
shows Garmin's own recorded figure (`day.despertar.garmin_linea`, Garmin's `sleep_end_local` formatted
`%H:%M` -- the row itself is never touched) beside "Tu corrección: ..."/"Your correction: ..."
(`day.despertar.correccion_sueno`/`correccion_levantado`), with a "Deshacer" button. **The second choice
recorded, as asked:** Deshacer is its own POST route (`/day/{day}/despertar/deshacer`) calling
`db.borrar_despertar_correccion` directly, NOT routed through `agente_propuestas.deshacer` on a
`propuesta_id` -- because a correction can exist with no propuesta behind it at all (`body/demo.py`'s own
`_seed_despertar_correccion` writes the row directly, and a chat-made correction can outlive its own
propuesta row), so the propuesta-based undo mechanism cannot always reach it; a direct delete reaches every
case the same way. Sleep TOTAL (`sleep_minutes`, the `sueno_fc_linea`/duration figures above this block)
stays Garmin's own, untouched by any of this -- confirmed by `tests/test_despertar_pantalla.py`'s own
`SinNoneTest` and by reading `_despertar_dia_ctx`, which never writes to `sleep_minutes` or any metric row.

**Ruling 3 -- the curve** (`body/rutas/hoy.py:_despertar_curva_puntos` + `_despertar_curva_svg`, rendered
`| safe` in `day.html` right after the proposal/correction lines): an inline SVG, no new library or JS
dependency, following the file's own existing inline-chart precedent. Window: from Garmin's own sleep end
minus 30 minutes to the shorter of the model's own horizon (`sleep_end + despertar_real.MODELO
["horizonte_horas"]`) or the proposed/corrected time plus 30 minutes. Points come from `db.intradia(...,
"intradia_fc", zona)` across the one or two calendar days the window spans. Gaps: points are split into
separate `<polyline>` runs wherever the gap between two consecutive points exceeds
`despertar_real.MODELO["factor_hueco_espaciado"]` times the window's own median observed spacing (the
model's own constants, imported, never duplicated) -- `sin_dato` gaps are drawn as gaps, never bridged, by
construction (a lone point left between two such runs becomes its own `<circle>`, never a connecting line).
Two labelled vertical marks: Garmin's own sleep end (dashed, muted) and the proposed/corrected time (dashed,
body color), each with its own `HH:MM` text label -- no other axis numbers. `role="img"
aria-label="{day.despertar.curva_aria}"` (`Pulso desde las {desde} hasta las {hasta}` / `Heart rate from
{desde} to {hasta}`, the window's own two endpoints). Returns `None`, hidden by the template's own `{% if
despertar.curva %}`, when the window holds no points (`tests/test_despertar_pantalla.py::CurvaSvgTest`
proves both the drawn and the no-points cases, and that a `sin_dato` gap never produces one continuous
polyline across it).

**Ruling 4 -- Hoy's own line** (`body/rutas/hoy.py:_despertar_hoy_ctx`, wired into `today()`; rendered in
`body/templates/today.html` right before the tiles grid): for today's sleep only, repeats the SAME sentence
(the identical `day.despertar.sueno_linea`/`levantado_linea` keys, so the wording matches Día's line exactly)
with a link to `/day/{today}` (`today.despertar.link`, "Ver el día"/"See the day") -- no button, no curve,
per the ruling. Nothing shown once a correction exists for today (`db.despertar_correccion` checked first,
short-circuiting before `estimar` ever runs) and nothing for any other day (`day != today_local.isoformat()`
returns `None` immediately).

**Ruling 5 -- cost:** `despertar_real.estimar` is called at most once per request, for the one day that
route is already showing (`/` calls it only for today via `_despertar_hoy_ctx`; `/day/{day}` calls it only
for that day via `_despertar_dia_ctx`) -- never for a range. In the common case (a correction already
exists) it is never called at all, both context builders checking `db.despertar_correccion` first.
`tests/test_rendimiento.py`'s own `/` and `/day/{day}` ceilings (155 and 81 statements) are UNCHANGED by this
slice -- measured on that file's own fixture at 124 and 59 respectively (comment added at
`tests/test_rendimiento.py` right above `_CEILINGS`, explaining the fixture's own most-recent-sleep-night
timing leaves `_despertar_dia_ctx` costing 0 there). On the richer fixture this slice's own tests build (a
real propuesta, no correction yet): `estimar` alone costs 8 statements measured by
`conn.set_trace_callback`; `_despertar_hoy_ctx`'s own full run (correction check + that `estimar` call) costs
9; `_despertar_dia_ctx`'s own full run (correction check + `estimar` + the curve's own intraday query + the
pending-propuesta check) costs 11 -- both within `ceil(8 * 1.3) = 11`, the same margin rule
`tests/test_rendimiento.py` itself already uses for `estimar`'s own ceiling, read here as "estimar's own
measured ceiling" per the ruling's own wording. Every new string has es/en parity
(`tests/test_i18n_paridad.py`, unchanged, still green). No 'None' is ever rendered: every optional piece
(`garmin_linea`, `correccion_linea`, `linea`, `propuesta_texto`, `curva`) is `None` or omitted by its own
context builder rather than rendered, each guarded by its own `{% if %}` in the template --
`tests/test_despertar_pantalla.py::SinNoneTest` renders every branch and asserts the literal string `"None"`
never appears in the response body.

**One defect found, fixed here:** a `<button class="taplink">` rendered as a grey filled block with underlined

    button.taplink{background:none;border:0;padding:0;color:inherit;font:inherit;cursor:pointer}

No background, no border, no padding beyond the `.taplink` rule's own `min-height:44px`, inherited color and
font, cursor pointer; `:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);...}` (line 43, unscoped) already covers

gains `TaplinkBotonTest`, asserting `body.css` carries this exact rule text.

## BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-6A, BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-6A-R, BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-6A-R2 -- a morning can carry both a sueno and a levantado correction at once (2026-11-18)

**The gap this slice closes:** BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-3's own ruling (dev-protocol DECISIONS.md's
`## BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-RULING`, not re-quoted verbatim here -- this slice's own context does not
hold that repository's text) reads dozing past Garmin's own recorded sleep end as SLEEP, and quiet
awake time in bed only as the GET-UP time. BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-4/-7 built `corregir_despertar` and
its screen on top of that ruling, but `despertar_correccion`'s own schema carried `UNIQUE (person_id,
day)` -- one row per morning, one `tipo` at a time -- so a morning that both dozed past Garmin's end
AND had a separate, later, sustained rise could only ever be corrected as ONE of the two, never both.
BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-6A/-6A-R named this gap; this slice (R2) is the one that closes it, under one
ledger entry naming all three IDs as the dispatch asked. Invented demo data throughout; no real
health figure, password, token or secret read, stored or logged by any file this slice touched; no
network call.

**Ruling 1 -- schema widens to `UNIQUE (person_id, day, tipo)`** (`body/db.py:1528`, the guarded
rebuild at `body/db.py:2056-2110`: `_despertar_correccion_needs_rebuild`, `_rebuild_despertar_
correccion_table` -- create/copy/verify-count/drop/rename via `_rebuild_with_fk_off`, the same
pattern every other `CHECK`/`UNIQUE` widening in this file uses -- and `_migrate_despertar_
correccion`, wired into `init()` right after `_migrate_propuestas`). The one-row reader/writer/
deleter are replaced by four tipo-aware functions: `despertar_correcciones` (`body/db.py:2685`,
`{tipo: row}` for one day), `despertar_correcciones_rango` (`:2696`, the same shape across a range,
one query), `guardar_despertar_correccion` (`:2710`, an `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(person_id, day,
tipo) DO UPDATE`, so saving one tipo never touches the other) and `borrar_despertar_correccion`
(`:2725`, deletes exactly one `(day, tipo)` row). `body/mudanza.py:129`'s `TableSpec`'s natural key
widens to `("person_id", "day", "tipo")` to match. `tests/test_migraciones.py`'s
`DespertarCorreccionUniqueWideningRebuildTest` proves the rebuild widens the constraint, keeps every
existing row, and is idempotent; `tests/test_mudanza.py` and `tests/test_privacidad.py` gain
both-kinds coverage for the household-move and export/delete paths.

**Ruling 2 -- the model proposes both, independently** (`body/despertar_real.py`: `VERSION =
"despertar-real-v2"` at line 60, `PROPUESTA_TIPOS = ("sueno", "levantado")` at line 111 --
`"ninguna"` removed, since "no correction offered" is now simply an empty list rather than a third
tipo). `estimar`'s own closing block (`:361-384`) computes `sueno_hora_dt` (the dozing segment's own
end, if the day opens dormitando) and `levantado_hora_dt` (the first sustained rise, event-bound the
same way the single-propuesta model already was) **independently of each other**, then returns a
`propuestas` list, sueno first, holding whichever of the two exist and differ. No new query: the
same intraday series already read once, through the same cache, costs the same 8 statements
whether it yields zero, one or two proposals (`tests/test_rendimiento.py::DespertarRealCostTest`,
unchanged). `tests/test_despertar_real.py::DozingThenQuietThenRiseTest` proves the exact case this
slice exists for: dormitando 05:00-06:30, despierto_quieto 06:30-07:00, levantado 07:00-09:00 yields
`[{"tipo": "sueno", "hora": "...T06:30:00"}, {"tipo": "levantado", "hora": "...T07:00:00"}]`.

**Ruling 3 -- a get-up time may never land before the sleep it would widen, and vice versa**
(`body/agente/herramientas.py:1021`, `_despertar_hora_opuesta`: reads the OTHER tipo's hora from an
existing applied correction first, falling back to a still-pending, unapplied `corregir_despertar`
propuesta for that same day/tipo; `:1071-1076`, wired into `_corregir_despertar`, raising the new
`agente.error.despertar_levantado_antes_de_sueno` when a `levantado` hora is earlier than, or a
`sueno` hora later than, the opposite tipo's hora). Covers all four combinations --
existing-correction and co-proposed-pending, in both directions -- plus a positive case proving two
correctly-ordered propuestas both apply (`tests/test_corregir_despertar.py::ValidationTest`, five new
tests). Apply/undo's own drift detection (`body/agente/propuestas.py:902-927`,
`_drift_aplicar_corregir_despertar`/`_drift_deshacer_corregir_despertar`/`_deshacer_corregir_
despertar`) moves from the old single-row comparison to `db.despertar_correcciones(...).get(tipo)`,
scoped to the propuesta's OWN tipo -- so a write to the other tipo is never drift, and a write to
the SAME tipo still is (`tests/test_corregir_despertar.py::DriftTest`, both proved). A pre-existing
correction of one tipo is never read, written or restored by an apply/undo of the other
(`ApplyUndoTest::test_a_pre_existing_sueno_row_survives_untouched_through_a_levantado_apply_and_
undo`).

**Ruling 4 -- Dia renders one card per kind, Hoy keeps one line** (`body/rutas/hoy.py:1162`,
`_despertar_dia_ctx`, rewritten around a `for tipo in ("sueno", "levantado")` loop building one
"tarjeta" per kind that still has something to show: its own correction line + Deshacer, OR its own
propuesta line + ¿Corregir?/pending-propuesta card -- mutually exclusive per kind, the same way
ruling 1-2 of BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-7 were mutually exclusive per morning. The shared "Garmin marcó..."
line (`:1215`) shows ONCE when ANY kind is corrected, never twice. ONE curve for the whole morning
(`_despertar_curva_svg`, `:1079`, signature widened from one `marca_dt` to a `marcas: list[datetime]`
-- Garmin's own end plus up to one mark per kind present, per the ruling's own "Garmin's end plus up
to two marks"). `_despertar_hoy_ctx` (`:1219`) is UNCHANGED in shape -- it still reads only
`resultado["propuestas"][0]`, and sueno-first ordering (ruling 2) gives it the same precedence Hoy
already had: the sueno line when both are offered, else the levantado one. `body/templates/day.html`
(`:17-30`) loops `{% for tarjeta in despertar.tarjetas %}`, each piece (`correccion_linea`, `linea`,
`propuesta_texto`, `boton`, `propuesta_id`, `deshacer`) guarded by its own `{% if %}` -- no 'None'
ever rendered (`tests/test_despertar_pantalla.py::SinNoneTest`, unchanged, still green). The two POST
routes Dia already had (`/day/{day}/despertar/proponer`, `/despertar/deshacer`) now carry a `tipo`
hidden form field instead of a new route each (`tests/test_web_entry.py::RouteSetTest`: route count
unchanged, confirmed by this slice's own run). `body/demo.py`'s `_seed_despertar_correccion`
(`:882`) now also seeds a second, earlier night with both kinds at once, alongside the existing
single-kind night (`tests/test_demo.py`, both nights asserted).

**Ruling 5 -- the read path surfaces both** (`body/agente/herramientas.py:816` `_leer_dia` and
`:1007` `_leer_intradia`: both now call `db.despertar_correcciones` and, when non-empty, nest the
result under a plural `correcciones` key -- `{tipo: row}` -- replacing the old singular `correccion`
key. `tests/test_leer_intradia.py::CorreccionTest` gains `test_both_kinds_of_correction_are_shown_
together`, proving both rows surface side by side, each labelled by its own tipo, Garmin's own
`sueno.fin` untouched either way. Statement cost, re-measured on `tests/test_despertar_pantalla.py`'s
own `_seed_ambos_alta` fixture (a morning offering BOTH kinds, neither corrected yet) rather than the
single-kind fixture BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-7 measured on: `despertar_real.estimar` itself unchanged at 8
statements; `_despertar_hoy_ctx`'s own full run unchanged at 9 (it still reads only the first
proposal); `_despertar_dia_ctx`'s own full run now costs 12, not 11 -- the per-kind loop's own extra
pending-propuesta check for the second kind -- so its own ceiling moves to `ceil(12 * 1.3) = 16`,
named in `tests/test_rendimiento.py`'s own comment block and asserted by its new
`DespertarRealCostTest::test_dia_and_hoy_ctx_cost_with_both_kinds_offered`. The route-level ceilings
(`/`: 155, `/day/{day}`: 81) are UNCHANGED -- that file's own fixture never reaches a two-kind
morning, confirmed by its own 18 tests, all green.

**New string, es/en parity, verbatim as committed** (`body/i18n/es.json:1146`,
`body/i18n/en.json:1146`):

| key | es | en |
|---|---|---|
| `agente.error.despertar_levantado_antes_de_sueno` | La hora de levantarte no puede ser antes del fin del sueño. | The get-up time can't be before the end of sleep. |

`tests/test_registro_tu.py`'s register guard flagged this string's `puede` as a possible usted

**Gate, exact command:** `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest discover tests -t .` -- run as 11
sequential alphabetical chunks of dotted modules (20 per chunk except the last, 215 modules total),
after the register-guard fix above:
