## BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-6B, BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-6B-R -- the sleep TOTAL itself becomes corrected, through one view, never by editing Garmin's record (2026-11-18)

**Carlos's words, verbatim, relayed by the desk 2026-11-18:** "I think that body should be like the
app that reflects reality in most accurate about my body so because it's the mix between the data
that is stored by the watch and and all the other info that can gather, use as my timeline, GPS, the
things that I report to you, eating, training with detail, I mean everything."

**The orchestrator's reading (dev-protocol DECISIONS.md's own `## BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-RULING`, not
re-quoted verbatim here -- this slice's own context does not hold that repository's text):** dozing
after Garmin's recorded sleep end is SLEEP; quiet awake time in bed changes only the GET-UP time;
Garmin's record is never edited; the correction is Body's own versioned layer, applied with the
person's tap.

**The gap this pair closes:** BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-6-INV (OBSERVED) found that `save_day`'s own
`INSERT OR REPLACE` into `daily_metric` per `(person, day, metric_key)` rules out ever storing a
corrected value there -- the next sync would silently overwrite it, and it would edit Garmin's own
record, which the product ruling above forbids. Readiness was computed live and stored after sync,
carrying the same problem one layer up. BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-6B built rulings 1-4 and landed them on
this branch (commits below); 6B-R is the continuation that verified ruling 5, re-measured the
statement ceilings, ran the full gate in 11 chunks, wrote this entry and merged. Invented demo data
throughout; no real health figure, password, token or secret read, stored or logged by any file this
pair touched; no network call.

**The orchestrator's rulings (ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1):**

**Ruling 1 -- ONE SEAM, IN THE SCHEMA** (`body/db.py:2115-2134`, `_migrar_vista_daily_metric_
efectiva`, run LAST in `init()` at `:2171`, after `despertar_correccion` and every other table/
column already exist; dropped FIRST at `:2144`, before any guarded table rebuild could otherwise
break on a stale view referencing a table mid-rename -- this slice's own `d5111d5`). The view's exact
SQL, as committed:

```sql
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS daily_metric_efectiva;
CREATE VIEW daily_metric_efectiva AS
SELECT dm.person_id AS person_id, dm.day AS day, dm.metric_key AS metric_key,
CASE WHEN dm.metric_key = 'sleep_minutes' AND dc.hora_local IS NOT NULL
          AND ss.end_local IS NOT NULL
     THEN dm.value + MAX(0, CAST(ROUND(
              (julianday(date(ss.end_local) || ' ' || dc.hora_local)
               - julianday(ss.end_local)) * 1440.0) AS INTEGER))
     ELSE dm.value END AS value,
dm.source AS source,
CASE WHEN dm.metric_key = 'sleep_minutes' AND dc.hora_local IS NOT NULL
          AND ss.end_local IS NOT NULL
     THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS corregido
FROM daily_metric dm
LEFT JOIN despertar_correccion dc ON dc.person_id = dm.person_id AND dc.day = dm.day
    AND dc.tipo = 'sueno' AND dm.metric_key = 'sleep_minutes'
LEFT JOIN sleep_session ss ON ss.person_id = dm.person_id AND ss.day = dm.day;
```

Every `daily_metric` row as stored, `corregido` 0, except a `sleep_minutes` row whose person/day
carries a `sueno` correction AND a `sleep_session` row with a non-NULL `end_local`: its `value`
becomes Garmin's own value plus the whole minutes from `end_local` to that day's own date (the date
`end_local` itself falls on) at `hora_local`, rounded, never negative (`MAX(0, ...)`, SQLite's
2-argument scalar form). A `levantado` correction changes no figure -- the join only matches
`tipo = 'sueno'`. `daily_metric`, `sleep_session` and every Garmin row are never written by this
view (proved byte-identical before/after, `tests/test_sueno_corregido.py::ViewBehaviourTest::
test_garmins_raw_rows_are_byte_identical_before_and_after`). `tests/test_sueno_corregido.py::
MigracionVistaTest` proves a database missing the view gains it additively on the next `init()`,
and that `init()` is idempotent.

**Ruling 2 -- READERS MOVE** (census re-run at the start of this continuation, `git grep -n
"daily_metric" -- body/ tests/`, confirming the moved set matches what 6B already built): `db.series`,
`db.day_values`, `body.lector.Lector` and `body/baselines.py:61` now read `daily_metric_efectiva`;
`db.series_garmin` (new, named) keeps `body/vida_dia.py` on Garmin's own figure, through
`db.series(..., registro=True)`'s sibling, until BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-6C. Every other direct SQL
reader of a `daily_metric.value` figure from the dispatch's own census (`body/agente/herramientas.py`,
`body/compartir.py`, `body/despertar_real.py`, `body/desplazamiento_import.py`, `body/history.py`,
`body/hogar_feed.py`, `body/horizonte.py`, `body/nutriente_objetivo.py`, `body/practicas.py`,
`body/profile.py`, `body/recuperacion.py`, `body/sueno_fc.py`, `body/turno_fc.py`,
`body/rutas/tendencias.py`) moved to the view. `tests/test_sueno_corregido.py::AllowListCensusTest`
is the new census test: it enumerates every `(FROM|JOIN)\s+daily_metric\b(?!_efectiva)` occurrence
under `body/*.py` and fails on any one not named in its own `ALLOW_LIST`, each entry with its
one-line reason -- the allow-list, verbatim as committed (`tests/test_sueno_corregido.py:211-243`):

| file | reason |
|---|---|
| `body/db.py` | `save_day`'s own INSERT OR REPLACE -- the one writer |
| `body/db.py` | `set_metric`'s own INSERT OR REPLACE / DELETE -- the one writer |
| `body/db.py` | `series_garmin` -- a caller that names it wants Garmin's own record, uncorrected |
| `body/db.py` | `days_with_data` -- a Garmin-day existence check, reads no value |
| `body/agente/herramientas.py` | `_registrar_medida`'s own antes-snapshot for `registrar_medida`'s undo, which calls `db.set_metric` directly on the raw table |
| `body/agente/propuestas.py` | `registrar_medida`'s own drift-on-apply/drift-on-undo, comparing against exactly what `db.set_metric` wrote or will restore |
| `body/garmin_cuenta.py` | existence check, reads no value |
| `body/persona_garmin.py` | count/scrub specs, read no value |
| `body/tutoriales.py` | existence check, reads no value |
| `body/practicas.py` | `_calcular_actividad`/`_primero_ultimo_dato`/`resumen`'s own 'has data' day existence and MIN/MAX(day) range reads -- no value column |
| `body/sueno_fc.py` | `recalcular`'s own idempotency check (NOT EXISTS, a different metric_key, `sleep_hr_avg`) -- reads no value |
| `body/rutas/tendencias.py` | `_trend_days_have`'s own COUNT(*) per metric_key -- a count, never a figure (the worker's own choice, ruling 2) |
| `body/privacidad.py` | export (the record as stored), deletes, and `person_tables`'s own `type='table'` schema scan (a view is never a table) |

**Ruling 3 -- READINESS** (`body/readiness.py:136-146`, `recompute_desde`: re-stores readiness for
`day` itself and every later day within `baselines.WINDOW_DAYS` after it that has data, since only
those days' own trailing baseline window can reach back far enough to include `day`'s now-corrected
sleep figure. `compute`'s own weights and `VERSION` are UNCHANGED -- the model is the same, its input
is truer. Wired into `body/agente/propuestas.py:921-928` (`_aplicar_corregir_despertar`) and

**Ruling 6 -- COST, re-measured this continuation** (`.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest
tests.test_rendimiento tests.test_rendimiento_red tests.test_rendimiento_turnos
tests.test_agente_leer_serie`): `Ran 51 tests in 36.169s` -- `OK`. No ceiling moved; none re-measured

**Three deviations, accepted by the orchestrator as built (named in this continuation's own

(a) `body/agente/herramientas.py:2038` and `body/agente/propuestas.py:735,744` stay on the raw

## BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-LUGARES-1

**Carlos, relayed by the desk (his words):** «remember that I want in body all my historical
data...», and on 2026-11-18 he ruled what Body is for: «I think that body should be like the app
that reflects reality in most accurate about my body so because it's the mix between the data that
is stored by the watch and and all the other info that can gather, use as my timeline, GPS, the
things that I report to you, eating, training with detail, I mean everything.»

**Main built Lugares' read API** (LUGARES-VIDA-VIAJES-LECTURA-1, duna-lugares main `e5f5cdc`). **THE
WIRE, verbatim from Main's message of 2026-11-18**, quoting `src/app/api/vida/eventos/route.ts` +
`src/lib/store/servicioVida.ts`: REQUEST `GET /api/vida/eventos?person=<cuenta sub>&desde=YYYY-MM-DD&hasta=YYYY-MM-DD`
with header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; hosted base `https://lugares.duna.solutions`, local
`http://127.0.0.1:3060`; token: env `DUNA_LUGARES_TOKEN_BODY` on the Lugares side, Body holds the
same value. RANGE: desde and hasta are INCLUSIVE calendar dates; a trip appears if its [start, end]
intersects [desde, hasta]; max hasta - desde = 3660 days; reversed, missing or invalid dates -> 422.
200: `{"eventos":[{"id","person","hogar_id":null,"kind":"trip","starts_at":"YYYY-MM-DD","ends_at":"YYYY-MM-DD","all_day":true,"timezone":"America/Bogota","source":"lugares","ref":<viaje id>,"data":{}}]}`
-- one event per trip on the person's lists; a trip with no end date has ends_at = starts_at; trips
with no start date are left out; data is always {}. ERRORS: 401 `{"motivo":"token_invalido"}`, 422
`{"motivo":"rango_invalido"}`, 503 `{"motivo":"vida_no_configurado"}` when Lugares has no token set.
No coordinates, no place names.

**Main's answer on the person (2026-11-18):** `person` is ONE value everywhere (Cuenta's single
issuer); a local Body calls the HOSTED Lugares; if no sub is configured Body sends nothing and shows
Lugares as «sin conectar», and never falls back to vida-v1's local key.

**The orchestrator's rulings (ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1), as built:**

(1) **PERSON** -- the sub sent to Lugares is `person.cuenta_sub` and nothing else: never a config
value, never an email, never `BODY_PERSON_KEY` or vida-v1's local key. Built `body/lugares.py:57`
(`_cuenta_sub`, one read of `person.cuenta_sub`); a person with no `cuenta_sub` is «sin conectar» and
no request is made (`body/lugares.py:103-105`).

(2) **CONFIG** -- `config.lugares_token()` reads env `BODY_LUGARES_TOKEN` (`body/config.py:22,25-29`;
`None` when unset, never logged, never stored in the DB, never in a URL); the base URL is the one
`enlaces` already owns, exposed as a public `enlaces.origen("lugares")` (renamed from `_origin`,
`body/enlaces.py:38-43`; both internal callers in `url_de` and `ref_desde_entrada` moved) so the one
override `DUNA_LUGARES_ORIGEN` serves both the trip links and this client; `deploy/host/body.env.example`
names `BODY_LUGARES_TOKEN=` empty with a one-line comment. No token -> «sin conectar», no request.

(3) **CLIENT** -- new module `body/lugares.py`, the ONLY module that talks to Lugares (its own
docstring says so, like `garmin_adapter.py`): network seam `_get_json(url, token) -> (status, dict)`
(`body/lugares.py:41-55`), patched in every test; `sincronizar(conn, person_id, hoy) -> dict`
(`body/lugares.py:95-150`) asks ONE range `[hoy - 3650 days, hoy + 365 days]`
(`VENTANA_PASADO_DIAS`/`VENTANA_FUTURO_DIAS`, `body/lugares.py:32-33,110-111`), validates each event
(`_validar_evento`, `body/lugares.py:65-83`: `kind == "trip"`, ISO dates, `starts_at <= ends_at`, `ref`
present -- an invalid event is skipped and counted, never stored), and on 200 REPLACES that person's
cached rows in one transaction (`body/lugares.py:139-146`, DELETE then INSERT inside `with conn:`); on
401/422/503, a network error (`estado_http == 0`) or a malformed body it keeps the cache as-is and
records only the error's own class in `lugares_sync.motivo` via `_registrar_intento`
(`body/lugares.py:85-93`): `red` for network, `formato` for a malformed body, or the wire's own
`motivo` string (`token_invalido`/`rango_invalido`/`vida_no_configurado`) via `_MOTIVO_POR_ESTADO`
(`body/lugares.py:62`). Returns counts only.

(4) **STORAGE** -- two additive tables, `body/db.py:1081-1098`:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS viaje_lugares (
    person_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES person(id),
    ref        TEXT NOT NULL,
    starts_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
    ends_at    TEXT NOT NULL,
    fetched_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (person_id, ref)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS lugares_sync (
    person_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES person(id),
    intento_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    ok_at      TEXT,
    motivo     TEXT
);
```

Nothing Lugares did not send: no names, no coordinates. db readers: `viajes_lugares(conn, person_id,
desde, hasta)` (`body/db.py:2525-2534`, trips intersecting the range, one statement) and
`lugares_estado(conn, person_id)` (`body/db.py:2536-2544`). Census: both tables in

(`body/pull.py:493-511`), beside `_recalcular_turno_fc_seguro`: skips silently once

(`lugares: N viajes` / `lugares: sin conectar` / `lugares: <motivo>`), catching every exception and

GET routes write nothing. No other screen reads trips in this slice (BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-LUGARES-2,

## BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-LUGARES-1-WINDOW -- the one-range window corrected to two requests inside Lugares' own cap (2026-11-18)

**Surface, verbatim:** BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-LUGARES-1 (merged `765010b`) built `lugares.sincronizar`
asking ONE range `[hoy - 3650, hoy + 365]` because the orchestrator's spec said so; its worker
measured and flagged that this span is 4015 days, OVER Lugares' own maximum (Main's wire, verbatim:
"desde and hasta are INCLUSIVE calendar dates; a trip appears if its [start, end] intersects [desde,
hasta]; max hasta - desde = 3660 days; reversed, missing or invalid dates -> 422"), so every live sync
would get 422 `rango_invalido`. The orchestrator's arithmetic error, not the worker's own.

**The orchestrator's ruling (ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1), as built:** Carlos asked for «all my
historical data», so the past is not shortened. `sincronizar` (`body/lugares.py:104-167`) now makes
TWO requests, each inside the maximum -- the past `[hoy - 3650, hoy]` (3650 days) and the planned
`[hoy + 1, hoy + 365]` (364 days) (`body/lugares.py:123-124`) -- with the same `person`, Bearer header
and seam (`body/lugares.py:98-101`, `_url`, asserts `desde <= hasta` and `hasta - desde <=
MAX_SPAN_DIAS` on every URL it builds). The two answers are checked in order
(`body/lugares.py:128-135`): any failing call (401/422/503, a network error, or a malformed body
without an `eventos` list) keeps the cache as it is and records THAT call's own `motivo`
(`body/lugares.py:129-142`), same mapping as BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-LUGARES-1
(`_MOTIVO_POR_ESTADO = {401: "token_invalido", 422: "rango_invalido", 503: "vida_no_configurado"}`,
`body/lugares.py:65`). Only when BOTH answers are 200 and valid are the events merged by `ref` into a
dict (`body/lugares.py:145-153`, a trip whose ref appears in both -- one spanning today -- stored
once, its dates as Lugares sent them) and the person's cache REPLACED in one transaction
(`body/lugares.py:155-166`). A module constant names the maximum, citing Main's wire:
`MAX_SPAN_DIAS = 3660` (`body/lugares.py:36`, comment at `body/lugares.py:35`). The comment at the old
`body/lugares.py:25-30` (the one-range-is-over-cap deviation note) is replaced by the ruling's own
reason (`body/lugares.py:26-31`). The statement count, the once-per-day rule
(`body/pull.py::_sincronizar_lugares_seguro`) and the pull wrapper's printed line (counts only) are
unchanged -- this slice touched only `body/lugares.py` and `tests/test_lugares.py`.

**Tests, verbatim (all in `tests/test_lugares.py`):**

- `RequestShapeTest.test_makes_exactly_two_requests_with_the_exact_ranges` (line 167): asserts
  exactly two `_get_json` calls, the first `[hoy - VENTANA_PASADO_DIAS, hoy]`, the second
  `[hoy + 1, hoy + VENTANA_FUTURO_DIAS]`, same token on both.
- `RequestShapeTest.test_every_request_stays_inside_the_maximum_span_and_desde_le_hasta` (line 194):
  parses `desde`/`hasta` back out of both built URLs and asserts `desde <= hasta` and
  `hasta - desde <= lugares.MAX_SPAN_DIAS` for each.
- `MergedWindowTest.test_a_trip_present_in_both_answers_is_stored_once` (line 216): a trip spanning
  `HOY` present in both the past and planned answers is stored once; `viajes: 3` for 101+999+202, not
  4.
- `MergedWindowTest.test_both_200_replaces_the_cache` (line 228): two disjoint trips, one per
  answer, both stored.
- `MergedWindowTest.test_past_401_planned_200_keeps_cache_and_records_past_motivo` (line 248) and
  `test_past_200_planned_401_keeps_cache_and_records_planned_motivo` (line 257): either call failing
  with 401 keeps the previously cached trip and records `token_invalido`, regardless of which call
  failed.
- `MergedWindowTest.test_network_error_on_past_keeps_cache` (line 266) and
  `test_network_error_on_planned_keeps_cache` (line 274): a `(0, {})` network error on either call
  keeps the cache and records `red`.
- Two pre-existing tests were updated for the new two-call shape, not re-specified:
  `SafeWrapperTest.test_second_call_the_same_day_makes_no_second_request` now expects
  `m.call_count == 2` (one `sincronizar`, two requests) on the first call and none on the second
  (once-per-day unchanged); `SyncSuccessTest.test_an_invalid_event_is_skipped_and_counted` now feeds
  the invalid-event batch to only the past call (`side_effect=[...]`) so the four-invalid count is not
  doubled by the planned call's own identical mock return.

**Gate, exact command:** `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest tests.test_lugares tests.test_pull
tests.test_privacidad tests.test_mudanza tests.test_persona_fuga tests.test_demo` -- `Ran 291 tests in
400.021s` -- `OK`. No password, token, Cuenta sub or real health figure was read, printed or written;
no network call was made (`lugares._get_json` patched in every test).

**Deviation, measured, carried forward rather than silently dropped:** `VENTANA_PASADO_DIAS = 3650`
and `VENTANA_FUTURO_DIAS = 365` are unchanged in name and value from BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-LUGARES-1; what
changed is that they now drive TWO separate windows (`[hoy-3650, hoy]` = 3650 days, `[hoy+1,
hoy+365]` = 364 days) instead of one combined `[hoy-3650, hoy+365]` = 4015-day window. Both new
windows are inside `MAX_SPAN_DIAS = 3660`. This is a Tier 2 build per the dispatch's own ruling, not a
new product-shape question -- the previously open "which direction to narrow" ruling from
BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-LUGARES-1's own open follow-ups is answered: neither direction narrows, both
requests happen.

**customer_bytes: none.** No `settings.lugares.*` string, no route, no schema change. Only
`body/lugares.py`'s internal request shape and `tests/test_lugares.py` changed.

**Open follow-ups carried forward:** BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-LUGARES-2 (season context, Tendencias
shading, a Día line on a trip day, and whether `despertar_real._eventos_lugares` should stay empty --
unchanged by this slice). Carlos's three deploy-time hand steps from BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-LUGARES-1
(set `BODY_LUGARES_TOKEN`, run `python -m body.vincular_cuenta` once, Lugares' own
LUGARES-VIDA-VIAJES-LECTURA-1 deploy) are still the gate to anything going live; nothing here changes
them.

## BODY-HOGAR-PLAN-RANGO-1 -- `manana` gains `plan_bloque`, the whole training block to the horizon (2026-11-19)

**Hogar's ask, verbatim, hub ref HOGAR-PIDE-BODY-PLAN-RANGO-1 (2026-11-19):**

> Asked 17 Nov: GET /api/hogar/serie (or manana) to return the training plan rows from today up to
> the horizon deadline (or 28 days), same fields as today's plan rows. Hogar's high-mountain hike
> pilot (HOGAR-PILOTO-MONTANA-1, building now) shows the whole training block toward the hike date;
> today Body sends only dia and dia+1, so the block shows two days plus an honest note. Please reply
> with a slice id and ETA, or the field you prefer.

Carlos's own direction behind it, HOGAR-PLAN-VIVO-1, his words relayed by Main: Hogar should «know my
plans ... so we can schedule weekly events ... reducing the friction».

**The orchestrator's ruling (Tier 2, build; the field was Body's to choose, Hogar said so):**
`manana` gains ONE new key, `plan_bloque`; `plan` stays exactly as it is. `plan_bloque` =
`{"desde": dia, "hasta": <date>, "hasta_por": "horizonte" | "28_dias", "filas": [...]}` where `hasta`
is the active horizon's `deadline` when `_horizonte_actual` returns one and that deadline is on or
after `dia` (`hasta_por` "horizonte"), else `dia` + 27 days (`hasta_por` "28_dias"); the span is
capped at `MAX_SERIE_DIAS` counting `dia` (a farther deadline is cut there and `hasta_por` stays
"horizonte" -- `hasta` says where it was cut); `filas` are every plan row with `day` in
`[desde, hasta]`, any goal, ordered by day then time, in exactly `_plan_dias`'s item shape -- one
shared row reader over a range, no second copy of the field list. No health figure added. Body's own
copy of the wire, `docs/contracts/hogar-feed-v1.md`, documents `plan_bloque` with the same words. The
route's statement ceiling is re-measured and named.

**As built:**
* `body/hogar_feed.py:53` -- `_plan_filas(conn, person_id, desde, hasta)`: the one shared SQL
  reader (`day BETWEEN ? AND ?`), replacing the old `day IN (?, ?)` query -- same field list (`id`,
  `day`, `time`, `title`, `status`, `ejercicios`, `nota_sesion`), same `ejercicios_json` parse, in
  exactly one place.
* `body/hogar_feed.py:75` -- `_plan_dias(conn, person_id, dia)`: now a thin call into `_plan_filas`
  over `[dia, dia+1]` -- unchanged output.
* `body/hogar_feed.py:80` -- `_plan_bloque(conn, person_id, dia, horizonte)`: `horizonte` is passed
  in (`manana`'s own `_horizonte_actual` result, never re-queried). `tope = dia + (MAX_SERIE_DIAS -
  1)`; `deadline` is parsed from `horizonte["deadline"]` when `horizonte` is not `None`. When
  `deadline is not None and deadline >= dia`: `hasta_por = "horizonte"`, `hasta = min(deadline,
  tope)`. Otherwise: `hasta_por = "28_dias"`, `hasta = dia + 27 days`. `filas` is `_plan_filas` over
  `[dia, hasta]`.
* `body/hogar_feed.py:222` -- `manana`: computes `horizonte` once, adds `"plan_bloque":
  _plan_bloque(conn, person_id, dia, horizonte)` alongside the unchanged `"plan": _plan_dias(...)`.
* `MAX_SERIE_DIAS` (`body/hogar_feed.py:27`, unchanged at 366) is the one cap `serie`, `turnos` and
  now `plan_bloque` all read.

**Tests, `tests/test_hogar_feed.py` (synthetic home, invented plan, no real health figure):**
new `PlanBloqueTest` class -- an active horizon 40 days out covers `dia..deadline`, `hasta_por`
"horizonte", rows in order, item shape equal to `plan`'s own keys; no horizon defaults to
`dia..dia+27`, "28_dias"; a deadline already past also answers "28_dias"; a deadline 500 days out is
cut at `dia + (MAX_SERIE_DIAS - 1)`, `hasta_por` still "horizonte"; another person's plan rows never
appear in `plan_bloque.filas`; `plan` stays byte-for-byte identical with `plan_bloque` present;
`plan_bloque`'s own statement cost does not grow with the number of matched rows (one query, not
one-per-row). `MananaTest.test_four_old_keys_unchanged_with_turnos_present`'s own key-set assertion
was updated to include `plan_bloque`.

**Wire doc, `docs/contracts/hogar-feed-v1.md`:** the `manana` example response gained a `plan_bloque`
example; a new bullet documents `desde`/`hasta`/`hasta_por`/`filas` under the `plan` bullet; the
"Still v1" additive paragraph now names `plan_bloque` as additive, `plan` unchanged.

**Statement ceiling, re-measured and named:** `/api/hogar/manana`'s real path
(`tests/test_rendimiento.py`'s `_CEILINGS_REAL_PATH`) measured 28 statements (was 27 before this

## BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-6C

**Carlos's own words, relayed by the desk 2026-11-18, carried into this slice verbatim (surface):**
«I think that body should be like the app that reflects reality in most accurate about my body so
because it's the mix between the data that is stored by the watch and and all the other info that
can gather, use as my timeline, GPS, the things that I report to you, eating, training with detail,
I mean everything.»

**Main's contract ruling, vida-v1, verbatim (hub `hit_01m7r7f4wh1w4zq01e1crvny0k`, 2026-11-18,
`contracts/vida-v1.md`):** «`kind` = `measured` | `estimated` | `corrected` (`corrected`, added
2026-11-18 by Main for Body: a device's measured figure that the person themself corrected, for
example «I was still asleep until 8:00». It shows as «tu corrección» wherever it appears. The app
that holds the correction keeps the device's original figure, and `source` stays the app that wrote
the value.»

**The defect this slice fixes (BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-6-INV, OBSERVED):** BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-6B's seam
(`daily_metric_efectiva`) turned `db.series`'s sleep figure into the person's own corrected value

**Carlos's own words, relayed by the desk, carried into this slice verbatim (surface):** «remember

like the app that reflects reality in most accurate about my body so because it's the mix between
the data that is stored by the watch and and all the other info that can gather, use as my
timeline, GPS, the things that I report to you, eating, training with detail, I mean everything.»

**What this slice built on:** BODY-HISTORIA-VIDA-LUGARES-1 (MERGED `765010b`) and -1-WINDOW

slice started.

0. **The one helper** -- `viajes.dias_de_viaje(conn, person_id, desde, hasta) -> set[str]`
   (`body/viajes.py:14`), one statement over `db.viajes_lugares`, every day of a trip whose own
   span (`ends_at - starts_at + 1`) is 2 or more days, clipped to `[desde, hasta]` -- a 1-day trip

6. **Día polish** (found by the orchestrator in the browser, BODY-DESPERTAR-REAL-6B) --

## BODY-TURNOS-DESHACER-LOTE-2

**Surface (dev-protocol queue BODY-TURNOS-DESHACER-LOTE-1, 2026-11-17):** an APPLIED shift batch
could not be undone -- `confirmar_turnos` is explicitly SIN_DESHACER
(`body/agente/propuestas.py:283`) and `/shifts` showed only "last confirmed on \<date\>". Every
other write Body makes on the person's own tap has an Undo, and Carlos's standing rule is that
anything off the normal flow is shown and reversible.

**BODY-TURNOS-DESHACER-LOTE-1-INV's findings (OBSERVED, dev-protocol logs/worker-body-turnos-
deshacer-lote-1-inv-body-app-20261119T040251.json), as relied on here:** `confirm()` per day keeps
a manual row (outcome `'manual_kept'`), keeps a row from a higher-order batch (`'newer_kept'`), else
DELETEs the prior `personal:`/`patron:` row(s) for that day and INSERTs a shift row with
`source = f'{personal|patron}:{file_name}'` and `batch_id` = this batch (`'applied'`); every apply
path funnels through `confirm()`/`confirm_all()` in `body/shift_import.py`; `shift.batch_id`
identifies exactly the rows a batch wrote; `shift_batch_item` keeps every batch's full per-day
record forever; batch precedence is `(received, extracted_at)`; the one STORED derived data that
goes stale is `turno_fc`.

**ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1's rulings, as built:**

1. **Status** -- a fifth value, `'undone'`, in `shift_batch.status`'s CHECK (`body/db.py:474`),
   through the same guarded, row-preserving rebuild shape every other CHECK widening in this file
   already uses (`_shift_batch_needs_undone_rebuild`/`_rebuild_shift_batch_table`, `body/db.py:
   1603-1653`; wired into `_migrate` at `body/db.py:1396-1397`, placed before this function's first
   DML the same way `_rebuild_conversacion_agente_table`'s own call is -- `_rebuild_with_fk_off`'s
   own `BEGIN` collides with the already-open implicit transaction otherwise). `shift.batch_id` and
   `shift_batch_item.batch_id` both reference this table's id by FK; the rebuild runs with foreign
   keys off, every row and id preserved. No `undone_at` column: `shift_batch` has no existing column
   that column's own name would reuse (its closest sibling, `decided_at`, already serves confirm/
   dismiss's own decision moment and is reused for undo too, see ruling 2 below) -- the ruling's own
   "only if a column for it already exists" bar is not met, so no new column; the status value
   itself is enough (tests/test_turnos_esquema_1.py's own `UndoneStatusMigrationTest`).
2. **Undo** -- `shift_import.undo(conn, person_id, batch_id) -> dict` (`body/shift_import.py:240`,
   counts only). Refused (`UndoRefused`, `body/shift_import.py:34`, nothing written) unless the
   batch is this person's own and its status is `'confirmed'` or `'superseded'`
   (`body/shift_import.py:269-275`), and refused the same way when an affected day carries a legacy
   `shift` row -- a `personal:`/`patron:` source with `batch_id IS NULL` -- the INV's own unknown,
   never silently skipped (`body/shift_import.py:282-292`). In one transaction
   (`body/shift_import.py:297-342`): (a) the affected days are read from `shift.batch_id` itself,
   never from `shift_batch_item`'s own historical outcome (which can list a day this batch never
   actually wrote to -- a `manual_kept`/`newer_kept` day is exactly a day `confirm()` skipped, so it
   is never in this set to begin with); (b) `DELETE FROM shift WHERE batch_id = ?`
   (`body/shift_import.py:298`); (c) each day falls back to the most recent OTHER batch of this
   person by `confirm()`'s own `(received, extracted_at)` precedence, among `'confirmed'`/
   `'superseded'` batches only -- never `'undone'`/`'dismissed'`/`'proposed'` -- whose
   `shift_batch_item` has that day, written with the exact `source`/`batch_id` shape `confirm()`
   itself uses (`body/shift_import.py:306-328`), unless a manual row exists for that day (the same
   query `confirm()` uses, manual always wins, nothing written, counted separately as
   `days_kept_manual`); (d) a day with no such batch ends with no shift row at all -- what the
   person had before this batch was ever confirmed (`days_emptied`); (e) a fallback batch that
   regains a row this way, and is currently `'superseded'`, flips back to `'confirmed'`
   (`body/shift_import.py:330-333`) -- the exact mirror of `_mark_superseded`'s own check
   (`body/shift_import.py:228-237`), which flips `'confirmed'` -> `'superseded'` the moment a
   batch's own rows all disappear; only a batch that actually gained a row this run is touched, so
   this never reaches a batch superseded for an unrelated reason; (f) the undone batch moves to
   `'undone'` with `decided_at` stamped now, the same convention `confirm()`/`dismiss()` already use
   for their own decision moment (`body/shift_import.py:335-337`); its own `shift_batch_item` rows
   marked `'applied'` are reset to `NULL` (`body/shift_import.py:338-341`) -- ruling 1 widens only
   `shift_batch.status`, never `shift_batch_item.outcome`'s own CHECK (`'applied', 'manual_kept',
   'newer_kept'` only, `body/db.py:496`), so there is no `'undone'` value to set there; `NULL`
   already reads as "not currently applied," and the parent batch's own status is what says
   `'undone'` -- no screen reads this field standalone in this slice (ruling 3) to disagree with
   that choice; (g) `turno_fc` rows for every affected day are deleted through the new
   `turno_fc.eliminar_dias(conn, person_id, days)` (`body/turno_fc.py:213`, every `modelo_version`,
   a no-op on an empty list) -- the one place outside `body/privacidad.py`'s own person-wide wipe
   that touches this table, so `undo()` never issues a raw DELETE against it itself. `confirm()`
   additionally refuses an already-`'undone'` batch (`body/shift_import.py:179-180`): undo then
   re-confirm of the same batch is refused -- a new import is the way back, never a second undo of
   the same batch either (status is `'undone'`, not `'confirmed'`/`'superseded'`,
   `body/shift_import.py:274-275`).
3. **No screen, no assistant in this slice** -- the button, the history list and the assistant's own
   undo of `confirmar_turnos` (removing it from SIN_DESHACER) are BODY-TURNOS-DESHACER-LOTE-3, next.
4. **Census** -- `body/mudanza.py`'s `shift_batch` `TableSpec` (`body/mudanza.py:141-142`) and
   `body/privacidad.py`'s `shift_batches` export/delete (`body/privacidad.py:184-185`, `:529-532`)
   both already copy/export rows by column, never by an enumerated list of status values, so no
   code change was needed in either file; `tests/test_turnos_esquema_1.py`'s own
   `CarriesTheUndoneStatusTest` proves an `'undone'` batch moves through `mudanza.importar()` and
   `privacidad.export_person()`/`delete_person()` untouched.

**Tests (invented rosters only, no real health figures):** `tests/test_turnos_esquema_1.py` --
`UndoneStatusMigrationTest` (a database at the previous shape, batches in all four old statuses
plus `shift`/`shift_batch_item` rows pointing at them, migrates with every row and id kept, every
`PRAGMA foreign_key_check` clean, the widened CHECK accepts `'undone'` and still rejects a bogus

`UndoTest`: the overlap/empty/flip-back scenario (batch A applied two days, batch B overlapping

A back to `'confirmed'`, deletes exactly the four affected `turno_fc` rows, and a `recalcular()`

for the named person, every `modelo_version` for a day, and a no-op on an empty list.

| # | Range | Ran | Result |

## BODY-NOCHE-LECTURA-1

**Note on sourcing:** the worker that ran this entry's own merge slice (BODY-NOCHE-LECTURA-1-M)
could not read `../dev-protocol/specs/body-noche-lectura-1.md` or
`../dev-protocol/logs/worker-body-noche-lectura-1-body-app-20261119T094644.json` -- both outside
this repository's sandbox, permission denied on every attempt (`Read`, `Grep`, direct and via `..`).
Carlos's own words for this slice and the report's own first-gate-line text are therefore not
reproduced verbatim here; what follows is built from the two commits this slice itself left on
`feat/body-noche-lectura-1` (`6e34f8a`, `9e343ff`) and the dispatching merge spec's own account of
the stop, re-measured against the repository rather than copied blind.

**Surface:** Garmin's own sleep payload spans two calendar dates, and `leer_intradia`'s window
filter (`_en_ventana` in `body/agente/herramientas.py`) checked only the clock-time slice
`ts[11:16]` against `[desde, hasta)`, with no date check -- a sleep-array minute from the day BEFORE
the requested `fecha` could pass as if it belonged to that day's own evening window whenever its
clock time happened to land inside the range. Separately, no single tool call returned a whole
night's own readings (HR, stress, sleep stages, corrections, derived facts) in one shot; the
assistant had to stitch `leer_intradia` calls across midnight itself.

**Ruling 1 (cross-midnight leak in `leer_intradia`, verdict: REAL), as built:** `_en_ventana`
(`body/agente/herramientas.py:1018-1019`, comment at `:1011-1017`) now requires the FULL local
timestamp, `ts[:10] == fecha and desde <= ts[11:16] < hasta`, not clock time alone -- closing the
leak for every series it filters (fc, estres, every `sueno_minuto_a_minuto` array), at no cost: all
of them already carry `fecha` as their own date (`BODY-INTRADIA-SPOTCHECK-1`'s day-scoped fetch).
`tests/test_leer_intradia.py::CrossMidnightSleepTest` (added by `6e34f8a`) proves the defect and the
fix.

**Ruling 2 (new tool `leer_noche`), as built:** a `tipo: lectura, nivel: completo` tool
(`body/agente/herramientas.py:1118` `_leer_noche`, registry entry `:3196-3206`) returns a whole
night in one call -- Garmin's own sleep start minus 60 min to its own end plus 120 min, capped at
16h, crossing midnight -- carrying the HR/stress minute points (full local timestamp, both calendar
dates), the sleep minute arrays, the person's own corrections, and five derived facts
(`fc_minima`, `fc_minima_vs_rango`, `vfc_noche`, `despertar_modelo`, `minutos_despierto_tras_fin`),
each null when its own input is missing. `tests/test_leer_noche.py` (new, 444 lines, 32 tests --
re-run alone on this slice's own final tree: `Ran 32 tests in 11.127s` -- `OK`) covers the window
shape, the 16h cap, `sin_datos`, a future `fecha`, all five derived facts, persona isolation and a
bounded statement-count ceiling. `9e343ff` additionally censused every registry/MCP/`persona_fuga`
test that enumerates tool names (`tests/test_mcp.py`, `tests/test_agente_registro.py`,
`tests/test_persona_fuga.py`) so each names `leer_noche` explicitly, never "at least".

**NOCHE's own first gate (the dispatching merge spec's account, not re-read from the original
report):** its own work green -- ruling 1 confirmed and fixed, `leer_noche` built with 32 tests,
every targeted module passed alone and inside its chunk; 11 of 12 chunks `OK` and the total
reconciled (4902 collected = 4902 run). The one red: `tests/test_host_autoactualizar.py`, 8 errors
in chunk 5b, every one a `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` from the module's own `_run_bash` helper
(`timeout=30` on a `bash run.sh` subprocess) on a busy machine -- reproduced on `main` too, not a
regression, and neither `body/host_autoactualizar.py` nor that test is in this slice's own diff.
That flake, and this slice's own full gate re-run, are BODY-NOCHE-LECTURA-1-M's entry below.

**Deviation:** none in NOCHE's own work. The merge slice's inability to read the original spec/report
files (above) is its own deviation, not this slice's.

**Open follow-ups:** none beyond the flake BODY-NOCHE-LECTURA-1-M fixes.

**Commits:** `6e34f8a` (step 1-2: ruling 1 fix, `leer_noche` built) -- `9e343ff` (step 3: ruling 5
census) -- merged `4256c83` into `main` (BODY-NOCHE-LECTURA-1-M below covers the merge and its
post-merge finding).

token/reset (`:91-92`). Run in the same process AFTER `test_mcp` but BEFORE
`test_agente_registro.DisponiblesTest`, that leaked `False` value hides the three shift tools from
`disponibles()`. **Confirmed pre-existing on bare `main` (406ecfc, before this slice and before
BODY-NOCHE-LECTURA-1 touched either file):** a temporary local branch at `406ecfc` running only
`.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m unittest tests.test_mcp tests.test_agente_registro` (that exact order,
the minimal reproduction) fails identically -- `Ran 72 tests in 17.175s` -- `FAILED (failures=3)`,
same three tests, same missing names. Neither `tests/test_mcp.py:71` nor the `_TURNOS_ACTUAL`
pattern is in this slice's `touches`; NOCHE's own edit to `tests/test_mcp.py` (`9e343ff`, +17 lines
at `:437-453`) only adds a new test method after the existing ones and never touches line 71. The
mandated gate command itself (`unittest discover tests -t .`, alphabetical module order) never
triggers this leak -- `test_agente_registro` runs in chunk 1, long before `test_mcp` in chunk 7, each
chunk its own process -- which is exactly why this slice's 12-chunk gate above was green. The smoke
command's own module order (not alphabetical) is what exposed it. Not re-ordered to dodge it, per
"a reproducing failure is never re-run into green" -- reported as found instead.

**Open follow-up coined here: `BODY-TURNOS-ACTUAL-CONTEXTVAR-LEAK-1`** -- give `_TURNOS_ACTUAL`
test isolation (a `contextvars.Token`-based reset in `tests/test_mcp.py`'s own
tearDown/fixture, or a context-manager wrapper around `fijar_turnos_actual` in
`body/agente/herramientas.py:91-92`) so one test module's call can never leak into a module that
runs after it in the same process. Not fixed here: outside `touches`, pre-existing on `main`, and
this slice's own mandated gate (the thing merge policy actually gates on) is green.

**Verdict: merge stands.** The failure is not a regression from this slice's or NOCHE's diff, it
reproduces identically on `main` before either existed, it is outside `touches`, and the full
mandated gate (alphabetical, reconciled 4902=4902) found nothing. Reverting a proven-safe merge over
a pre-existing, order-dependent flake in an unrelated file would not make the tree any more correct.

## BODY-HISTORIA-MINUTO-2

**Surface, Carlos's words, relayed by the desk 2026-11-19:** *"that same detail in minute by minute
measurements is the thing that we have to build to reconstruct my whole history that body already
has."* The read-only investigation BODY-HISTORIA-MINUTO-1-INV found the keeper already backfilling
minute HR/stress for every day in reach (`body/pull.py`), the night's richer minute arrays (HR, HRV,
stages, movement, SpO2) coming from the `sleep` raw payload with five keys that have never been
confirmed against a real payload (`body/garmin_adapter.py:994-1043`), the export supplying HR/stress
only, and no coverage command. The orchestrator added: every daily pull also stores the
`body_battery` feed raw, whose `bodyBatteryValuesArray` is an intraday series the adapter only
reduces to high/low (`body/garmin_adapter.py:572-578`). This slice builds the count, not the guess.

**Ruling 1 (`body/cobertura.py`), as built:** `python -m body.cobertura [--cuenta-sub <sub>]
[--json]` opens the database read-only (`backup.open_readonly`, `body/cobertura.py:255`) and never
writes, migrates, calls Garmin or opens a plain `sqlite3.connect`. `recopilar` (`:195-204`) resolves
one person (`_resolver_persona`, `:30-37`: a `SELECT id FROM person WHERE cuenta_sub = ?` only --
the same lookup `cuenta.resolve_person` runs before it would ever consider creating a row, never the
create-on-first-sign-in half of it, since a read-only connection could not write that row anyway;
required when `cuenta.hosted()`, else `db.default_person_id()`) and prints, per stream:

* `intradia_fc`/`intradia_estres` per source (`garmin`, `garmin_export`), `_bloque_intradia`
  (`:46-68`): days with a row, first/last day, and days whose payload parses to at least one valid
  minute point via the existing `db._INTRADIA_PARSER_NAMES` parsers -- a payload that will not parse
  as JSON, or parses but has the wrong shape, is caught and simply never counted toward
  `dias_validos` (never raises, never guessed).
* `sleep` (`_bloque_sleep`, `:92-108`): nights stored, first/last, and for EACH of the five raw keys
  `garmin_adapter.parse_sleep_series` reads (`sleepHeartRate`, `hrvData`, `sleepLevels`,
  `sleepMovement`, `wellnessEpochSPO2DataDTOList` -- named from `garmin_adapter._SLEEP_SERIES_SPECS`,
  the single source of truth, never a duplicated list) the nights where it is present and non-empty
  plus the median sample count across those nights. A night whose payload is not even a dict is
  still counted as a night stored; it contributes to none of the five keys, exactly like a key that
  is simply absent.
* `body_battery` (`_bloque_body_battery`, `:124-142`, `_body_battery_muestras` `:111-121` --
  the same extraction `garmin_adapter.py:572-578` already uses, counted rather than reduced to
  high/low): days stored and days with a non-empty `bodyBatteryValuesArray`, plus its median sample
  count per such day.
* `keeper` (`_bloque_keeper`, `:145-169`): of the days from `hoy-130` (`pull.INTRADIA_ALCANCE_DIAS`)
  to yesterday that have a daily pull (a stored `sleep` row from the live API -- the same "already
  pulled by every day's ordinary sync" signal `db.sueno_minuto_a_minuto`'s own docstring relies on),
  how many have NO live-API intraday row, fc and estres counted separately, plus the oldest such
  missing day.

Sample on an invented test home (counts and dates of invented data only; no real figure anywhere in
this entry):

    intradia_fc.garmin: dias=2 primero=2026-07-01 ultimo=2026-07-02 dias_validos=1
    intradia_fc.garmin_export: dias=0 primero=None ultimo=None dias_validos=0
    intradia_estres.garmin: dias=0 primero=None ultimo=None dias_validos=0
    sleep: noches=1 primero=2026-11-10 ultimo=2026-11-10
    sleep.sleepHeartRate: noches=1 mediana_muestras=2
    sleep.hrvData: noches=0 mediana_muestras=None
    sleep.sleepLevels: noches=1 mediana_muestras=1
    body_battery: dias=1 dias_con_datos=1 mediana_muestras=2
    keeper.intradia_fc: dias_con_pull_diario=1 dias_sin_intradia=1 dia_mas_antiguo_faltante=2026-11-10
    keeper.intradia_estres: dias_con_pull_diario=1 dias_sin_intradia=1 dia_mas_antiguo_faltante=2026-11-10

**Ruling 2 (host verb), as built:** `duna-deploy-body cobertura --cuenta-sub <sub> [--json]` --
`deploy/host/duna-deploy-body`'s usage text and its `cobertura)` case arm (no bash-level arg
validation; forwards `"$@"` to `body-import-pc.sh`, the same shape `importar-pc`/`relinkar-garmin`

**Surface, Carlos's words, relayed by the desk 2026-11-19:** *"it's not that serious injury. You can

brings the days back at once with nothing lost; and `corregir_periodo` already lets a person change
an open period's kind. The orchestrator's ruling (ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1): two properties of
a kind, as data, and a new kind 'molestia' seeded from them.

**Ruling 1 (two properties of a kind, as data), as built:** `period_kind` gains
`excluye_del_rango INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (excluye_del_rango IN (0,1))` and

## BODY-PLAN-FASES-5

**Surface, Carlos's words, relayed by the desk:** *"it's not that serious injury. You can have in
detail the push session that I did having this, so it's not that bad ... if it were that bad, I
couldn't have that session. However, next week when I'll do next time push session, we'll get into
detail into my sensations."* The desk's own ask: at the end of a training session, for each
exercise that loads the injured zone, ask pain 0-10 during and after, plus which movement or angle
hurt; the next morning, ask how it feels. The orchestrator's ruling (ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1):
a new person-scoped record, carried by mudanza and privacidad, written only by the person (form) or
through a proposal card he confirms; never medical advice.

**Ruling 1 (the record), as built:** `entreno_dolor` (`body/db.py:1017-1033`, additive, guarded by
`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`) -- `id`, `person_id`, `day`, `sets_source`, `sets_source_id`,
`ejercicio`, `zona`, `dolor_durante`/`dolor_despues`/`dolor_manana` (each `INTEGER CHECK (... IS NULL
OR ... BETWEEN 0 AND 10)`), `movimiento` TEXT, `manana_registrado_en`, `creado_en`, with
`UNIQUE(person_id, sets_source, sets_source_id, ejercicio)` so a second save for the same exercise
edits the same row, never a second one. The one named 0-10 scale constant,
`db.DOLOR_ESCALA_MIN`/`DOLOR_ESCALA_MAX` (`body/db.py:36`), is the single source every CHECK and
every template select shares; i18n anchor labels `dolor.escala.min`/`max` (es *"sin dolor"*/*"el peor
dolor"*, en *"no pain"*/*"the worst pain"*). Writers: `db.registrar_dolor_entreno` (`:4015-4033`, the
upsert), `db.dolor_de_sesion` (`:4035-4044`, one session's own rows), `db.pendientes_dolor_manana`
(`:4046-4062`, ruling 4's own reusable read, bounded by `MANANA_VENCE_DIAS = 2` at `:4012`),
`db.registrar_dolor_manana` (`:4064-4074`, fills every still-open row of a zona/day in one UPDATE).
Mudanza: `TableSpec("entreno_dolor", match_cols=(person_id, sets_source, sets_source_id, ejercicio))`
(`body/mudanza.py:144-145`). Privacidad: a `PARTIAL_EXPORT_TABLES` entry (`body/privacidad.py:106`) --
every column exports except `movimiento`, the one free-text column that never leaves the host
(`:243` the export SELECT, `:537` the delete).

**Ruling 2-3 (which exercises are asked, session screen), as built:**
`entreno_sesion.ejercicios_con_zona_abierta` (`body/entreno_sesion.py:114-123`) intersects a
session's own exercise categorias with `db.zonas_en_recuperacion`'s open-period zonas for that day
-- direct set intersection, the same vocabulary and the same join an exercise's `categoria` and a
period's `zonas` already share (precedent: `body/rutas/asistente.py`'s own `categorias & zonas_dia`);
no open zona period, no question. `body/rutas/entreno_sesion.py`'s `_dolor_ctx` (`:271-294`) builds
the card's context and `entreno_dolor_registrar` (`:364-`) is the one POST
(`/day/{day}/entreno/{source_id}/dolor`) that upserts every exercise's row through
`db.registrar_dolor_entreno` in one call and redirects with a result line (`role="status"`). The
form uses indexed field names (`ejercicio_0`, `durante_0`, ...) plus a count field, never repeated
names -- `comun._form`'s own `parse_qs` keeps only the first value per key, so a repeated-name
design would have silently dropped every exercise past the first. `entreno_sesion.html`'s card title
`entreno_sesion.dolor_titulo` is `"¿Cómo respondió tu {zona}?"`/`"How did your {zona} respond?"`;
saving again for the same exercise prefills and edits the same row (ruling 3's own instruction).

**Ruling 4 (next morning, on Hoy), as built:** `body/rutas/hoy.py`'s `_dolor_manana_hoy_ctx`
(`:306-`) reads `db.pendientes_dolor_manana` and renders one card per (day, zona) still open, up to
`MANANA_VENCE_DIAS` days back; `dolor_manana_registrar` (`:1470-`) is the one POST
(`/day/{day}/dolor-manana`) that fills every exercise that zona named that day through
`db.registrar_dolor_manana`. `today.html` gets one card per pendiente, before the despertar card.

**Ruling 5 (the assistant), as built:** `registrar_dolor` (`body/agente/herramientas.py:2327-2366`,
catalogue entry `:3542`), a `propuesta`-kind tool following `registrar_medida`/`corregir_entreno`'s
own template exactly: resolves the day's session through the same `_resolver_sesion_entreno_dia`
`corregir_entreno` uses, and `zona` comes from that session's own matching set -- never freely typed,
so it can only name an exercise the person actually trained that day; refuses an unknown day/
exercise, an empty call (none of durante/despues/movimiento given), and an out-of-range number, each
in the person's own language (`agente.error.dolor_sin_sesion`/`dolor_ejercicio_desconocido`/
`dolor_nada_que_registrar`/`dolor_fuera_de_rango`, es/en). `body/agente/propuestas.py`'s
`registrar_dolor` entry (`:1770-1771`, writers `:839-874`) is update-shaped like `registrar_medida`:
`antes` carries the existing row's own durante/despues/movimiento (or None), so `deshacer` restores

`propuesta_agente.accion`'s CHECK widens to include `'registrar_dolor'` (`body/db.py:114`, the
seventeenth such widening, through the existing reusable `_rebuild_propuesta_agente_table`
-- `:1943-1947` detects it, `:2020-2021` runs it -- additive, every existing row survives

one tool; it now carries each session's `dolor` list (durante/despues/manana numbers only) --

(`body/agente/cliente.py`, the only module allowed to send anything to one) and `movimiento` is the

## BODY-NOCHE-LECTURA-3 -- leer_noche compares like with like, leer_dia groups meals, cobertura names the real sleep keys (2026-11-20)

Three defects the desk's real reads surfaced (relayed 2026-11-20, no figures here) plus one measurement gap, all in
assistant read paths (ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1):

**(A) Apples to oranges in leer_noche.** `fc_minima` is the single lowest heart-rate minute inside Garmin's own sleep
window (`_fc_minima_noche`, by design), but the removed `fc_minima_vs_rango` compared it against the range of
`sueno_fc.CLAVE_MIN` ('sleep_hr_min'), a ROBUST LOW -- a percentile of the window's samples, never a single sample.
A single minute reads systematically below a percentile, so nearly every night read "below the usual range" -- the
desk reported a night as well below his range when it was the comparison itself that was biased, and `leer_serie`/
`leer_dia` showed that same night's `sleep_hr_min` (the robust figure, tagged estimated) while `leer_noche` showed a
lower single minute, so the tools seemed to disagree.

**(B) Meals lost their description in leer_dia.** `registrar_comida` stores the meal's own description on the
`comida` row and its amounts as `ingesta` children with `descripcion` NULL; `leer_dia` listed only the `ingesta`
rows (through `db.load_day`), so a logged meal's description read null. `db.comidas_del_dia` already grouped
children under their meal with its description and time -- `leer_dia` simply never called it.

**(C) SpO2 key unknown.** The first coverage run on the host (dev-protocol BODY-COBERTURA-HOST-1) found the assumed
SpO2 array key `wellnessEpochSPO2DataDTOList` present on 0 of 884 stored sleep payloads, while the other four
assumed keys were present on 141-142 -- whether the watch records no overnight SpO2 or the key is simply named
differently could not be told without seeing the payload's own key NAMES.

**Ruling 1 (like with like) -- `bbdc06b`.** `_derivados_noche` (`body/agente/herramientas.py:1193`) keeps `fc_minima`
{valor, hora} with no range of its own. It adds `fc_baja_robusta` (`herramientas.py:1214`) -- that night's own
`sleep_hr_min` as stored in `daily_metric_efectiva` for the wake day (`db.day_values`, the same figure `leer_serie`/
`leer_dia` already return) -- and the range comparison moves to `fc_baja_robusta_vs_rango` (`herramientas.py:1215,
1218-1219`), the same `rango_30_dias`/`rango_historia`/`motivo`/`z`/`z_base` shape BODY-NOCHE-LECTURA-2 built, reused
unchanged via `_rango_doble_y_z`. The old key `fc_minima_vs_rango` is removed; a census
(`git grep -n fc_minima_vs_rango -- body/ tests/`) found no caller outside the tool and the test module, both now
updated. The tool's own `descripcion` (`herramientas.py:3378-3379`) now names the two facts in one sentence: the
single minute is the lowest moment; the robust low is what compares with the usual range. Tests:
`tests/test_leer_noche.py` -- `fc_baja_robusta` equals the stored `sleep_hr_min` and its own range reuses it (renamed
from `test_fc_minima_vs_rango_reuses_baselines_baseline_on_sleep_hr_min`); `fc_minima` carries no range

**Ruling 2 (meals as meals) -- `81f36b0`.** `_leer_dia` (`herramientas.py:870`) adds `data["comidas"] =
db.comidas_del_dia(conn, person_id, day)` -- one SQL statement, the same grouping `body/rutas/hoy.py`'s own Día

## BODY-MINUTO-ANALISIS-1 -- leer_serie gains a minute step, and the remote MCP door gets its own read budget (2026-11-20)

Carlos, relayed by the desk 2026-11-20, his own words: *"I want between you and body design specialized tools to
analyze in full detail every minute of the metrics."* First of a series (BODY-MINUTO-ANALISIS-*); this slice (-1) is
a read step plus a read-budget fix, measured by the orchestrator (ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1): (A) `leer_serie`
only read daily/weekly/monthly steps, so a question about one stretch of a night or a day cost a whole `leer_noche`
or several `leer_intradia` calls; (B) the remote MCP's own read cap, `LIMITES["lecturas"]` = `bucle.MAX_LECTURAS` = 5
per window, was written for the IN-APP assistant's own per-question budget (a model call per round) and reused,
unchanged, for the remote door, whose reads cost Body only database time -- the desk hit "reading limit is reached,
try again in 15 min" while analysing nights.

**Ruling 1 (a minute step) -- `55c9980`.** `leer_serie` (`body/agente/herramientas.py`) gains `paso='minuto'`
(`LEER_SERIE_PASOS`, line 129) for a window given by full LOCAL timestamps `desde`/`hasta` (never a plain date, since
the window may cross midnight), at most `_LEER_SERIE_MAX_MIN_PASO_MINUTO` = 360 minutes (line 137), over the six
minute streams in `LEER_SERIE_MINUTO_METRICAS` (line 138: fc, estres, etapa, vfc, movimiento, body_battery) --
`_PARAM_LEER_SERIE`'s own `metricas` enum (line 144) is the union of these and the existing daily `TENDENCIA_
METRICAS`, the paso-dependent split enforced in Python, the same way its bounds already were; `desde`/`hasta` lose
their old `"format": "date"` (paso-dependent shape, never checked by the JSON-schema layer). `_leer_serie` dispatches
to the new `_leer_serie_minuto` (line ~1215 at the time of writing; function body unaffected by the ledger's own line
drift) before any of the date-only parsing that would reject a full timestamp (line 989: `if paso == "minuto":`).
`_leer_serie_minuto` needs `nivel_datos='completo'`, the same rule paso='dia' already enforces, and returns ONE row
per minute present on at least one requested stream (`_filas_leer_serie_minuto`, line 1099), built by:
- `fc`/`estres`/`movimiento`: minute-exact joins against `db.intradia`/the night's own `arrays["movement"]`
  (`db.sueno_minuto_a_minuto`, the exact date-safe reader `leer_noche` already uses for both calendar dates a window
  touches).
- `etapa`: the Garmin stage segment covering that minute (`ETAPAS_SUENO_GARMIN`, the same label `leer_noche` already
  shows), each segment's own end being the next segment's start or the night's own stored `end_local`.
- `vfc`/`body_battery`: the sparser streams, matched with two small helpers (`_mas_reciente_dentro`, line 1071: the
  latest sample at or before the minute, within `_LEER_SERIE_MINUTO_TOL_VFC_MIN` = 5 minutes -- HRV's own
  forward-fill; `_mas_cercano_dentro`, line 1083: the nearest sample on EITHER side, within `_LEER_SERIE_MINUTO_
  TOL_BB_MIN` = 15 minutes -- body_battery's own looser sampling), both bisect-based over a pre-sorted sample list.
  `body_battery` is parsed on read from its own stored raw_payload by a NEW, small parser kept here, `_bateria_
  corporal_minuto` (line 1031) -- the SAME extraction `garmin_adapter.py:572-578`'s own high/low fallback uses
  (`[timestamp_ms, value]` pairs, `garmin_adapter._num`/`garmin_adapter._utc_to_local_iso` called from outside the
  module exactly as `body/cobertura.py` already does for `_num`, `garmin_adapter.py` itself never edited).
  A window may touch TWO nights' own arrays (Garmin files a night under its WAKE day, which can sit on either side
  of the calendar dates a window's own clock time touches): the candidate wake days are read in ONE `sleep_session`
  statement (an `IN` clause over a small, fixed set), never one query per candidate, so the statement count stays
  independent of window length -- bounded by the number of CALENDAR DATES and NIGHT CANDIDATES the (capped) window
  can ever touch, never by how many minutes it spans. Each key is present on a row only when that stream actually
  has a usable sample there -- never a 0 or an invented value, and a minute with no stream data at all gets no row.
  The registry's own `descripcion` (near line 3679) now names the minute step and says when to use it (a window
  inside a night or a day) versus `leer_noche` (the whole night once) and `leer_intradia` (kept, unchanged).
  Tests (new module `tests/test_leer_serie_minuto.py`, 18 cases): a 40-minute window crossing midnight returns one
  row per minute with full timestamps from both calendar dates and the half-open `[desde, hasta)` convention
  `leer_intradia` already uses; `etapa` covers every minute of its own segment and an unmapped code reads
  'desconocido' (never dropped); `vfc` forward-fills within its 5-minute tolerance and never reads from a sample
  still in the future; `body_battery` matches the nearer sample on EITHER side within its 15-minute tolerance, and
  is absent past it on both sides; a stream with no stored data never appears on any row; a window over 360 minutes,
  `hasta <= desde`, a malformed timestamp, a future window, an unknown paso='minuto' metric and nivel='resumen' are
  all refused with a `ToolError`; another person's minutes never appear; statement count is identical for a 10-
  minute and the full 360-minute window (`StatementCountTest`). `tests/test_agente_leer_serie.py` (20 cases) reruns
  green unchanged -- the existing paso='dia'/'semana'/'mes' path is untouched by the dispatch added at line 989.

**Ruling 2 (the remote door's own read budget) -- `a893f53`.** `body/mcp.py` adds `MCP_MAX_LECTURAS = 120` (line 148)
as its own named constant, with the reason in its own comment: remote reads cost Body only database time, not a
model call, and the person's own key already reaches every figure a read could return. `_SesionRemota.__init__`
(the hosted HTTP door, backed by `_TopeDB`, the audit-table-counted cap) now builds `tope_lecturas` from
`MCP_MAX_LECTURAS` instead of `LIMITES["lecturas"]` (line 335-336) -- `LIMITES["lecturas"]` itself is UNCHANGED
(still `bucle.MAX_LECTURAS` = 5), so the LOCAL stdio door (`_Sesion`, backed by the in-memory `_Tope`) keeps its own,
unchanged cap, exactly as `propuestas`/`aplicaciones` on either door are unchanged. `tests/test_mcp_remoto.py`'s own
`CapsTest` updated: `test_lectura_cap_reached_then_allowed_again_after_the_window` now loops `mcp.MCP_MAX_LECTURAS`
(120) remote calls instead of 5 before asserting the next one is refused; `test_local_calls_count_toward_the_same_
remote_cap` now loops 119 LOCAL calls through `mcp._llamar_herramienta` (swallowing the `ToolError` each one raises
past the local door's own, still-5 in-memory cap -- every attempt is audited BEFORE that check, per `_TopeDB`'s own
docstring, so the shared count keeps growing through the refusals) before showing the remote door accepts the 120th
shared read and refuses the 121st -- the same "one shared budget, not one per door" fact ruling 4 (BODY-MCP-REMOTO-

## BODY-MCP-INICIO-SIN-LLAVE-1 -- the remote MCP handshake answers initialize/ping/notifications without calling Cuenta (2026-11-20)

Main's hub item hit_01m7vs9tpsfvzwt372r246srg1 (principle for every Duna product), quoted: *"answer the methods
initialize, ping and every notifications/* WITHOUT calling Cuenta (they return only server name, version and
capabilities, nothing personal). Require and check the Bearer key on tools/list, tools/call and every data-
returning method; those run under the client's longer request timeout. Keep the unauthenticated methods in ONE
explicit allow-list with a test that fails if a data-returning method joins it. Keep the positive-answer
cache."* Measured on the live host 2026-11-19/20: when Cuenta is slow or cold, every remote MCP call waited on
`llave_asistente.verificar`'s own 5 s introspection budget (`body/llave_asistente.py:33`) before the body was
even parsed, and returned a bare HTTP 503 after ~5 s (Body's journal: 23 x `POST /mcp 503 5030-5105ms` on 19
Nov); Claude Code's own `initialize` probe gives up at 5000 ms, so a cold Cuenta made the client report "Version
negotiation probe timed out after 5000ms" and never connect, even though a retry a minute later would work. This
slice also closes Body's own queued candidate BODY-MCP-CUENTA-CAIDA-1.

**Ruling 1 -- one allow-list, checked before any Cuenta call.** `body/rutas/mcp_http.py:56`:
`METODOS_SIN_LLAVE = frozenset({"initialize", "ping"})`, plus the `notifications/` prefix rule inside
`_metodo_sin_llave` (`:143-147`), with the comment at `:48-55` naming why (Main's hub item, and that
`AllowListCensusTest` fails the moment a data method joins it). `mcp_http()` (`:211-294`) parses the JSON-RPC
body FIRST (`:223-228`) -- a parse failure can never be classified as "every message is in the allow-list", so it
always falls through to full verification, same precedence as before: an auth failure still wins over a parse
error. The `Authorization: Bearer` header is still required unconditionally before any of this (`:214-216`, 401
at once with no header, unchanged); it is just never introspected when every message in the body (a lone object
or every item of a batch, `_todos_sin_llave`, `:150-156`) is in the allow-list (`:230-247`). A batch mixing
`initialize` with `tools/list` (or anything else) answers `False` and goes through full verification unchanged,
cache included (proven by `AllowListCensusTest.test_a_batch_mixing_initialize_and_tools_list_is_not_sin_llave`,
`tests/test_mcp_http.py:171-175`).

**Ruling 2 -- nothing personal moved, because nothing personal was there.** Census (file:line, as built): the
unauthenticated `initialize` branch of `_procesar_uno` (`mcp_http.py:170-180`) answers `protocolVersion`,
`serverInfo` (name + version only, `SERVER_INFO = {"name": "body", "version": "1"}`, `:40`) and
`capabilities: {"tools": {}}` -- no `instructions`, no `title`, no person-derived text, before this slice and
after it alike. `ping` (`:183-184`) answers an empty result object; `notifications/initialized` (`:181-182`)
answers nothing (`None`, a 202). **Nothing moved out of the unauthenticated `initialize`, because there was
nothing in it to move** -- proven, not assumed, by the new `McpInitializeCarriesNoPersonTest`
(`tests/test_persona_fuga.py:929-954`): with three different keys (person A's, person B's, and a never-granted
one), the unauthenticated `initialize` response is byte-identical regardless of which key rode along or which
language the underlying person has set, and carries neither person's own markers, no `instructions` key and no
`title` on `serverInfo`.

**Ruling 3 -- a JSON-RPC reason on 503, not a bare status.** `_503()` (`mcp_http.py:86-95`): besides the existing
transport-level 503 and its `Retry-After` header (unchanged), the response body is now a JSON-RPC error object
(`_responder(None, error={"code": _CUENTA_NO_DISPONIBLE_CODE, "message": mensaje})`,
`_CUENTA_NO_DISPONIBLE_CODE = -32001` at `:45`) carrying the localized sentence
`asistente.mcp.cuenta_no_disponible` -- `"Cuenta no responde; reintenta en {n} s"` (es) /
`"Cuenta is not responding; retry in {n} s"` (en) -- `body/i18n/es.json:1327`, `body/i18n/en.json:1327`. Raised
from `llave_asistente.verificar`'s own `CuentaNoDisponible` (`mcp_http.py:259-262`); the language is read off the
caller's own `Accept-Language` header or the default, since no person is resolved yet at the point introspection
itself is failing.

**Ruling 4 -- the allow-list census and no-leak tests.** `AllowListCensusTest`
(`tests/test_mcp_http.py:139-175`, 7 tests): the allow-list is exactly `{initialize, ping}` plus the
`notifications/` prefix, every method the dispatcher answers is classified correctly, an unlisted
`notifications/*` message is still allow-listed by prefix, an unknown method and a non-dict/methodless item are
not, an empty batch is not, and a batch mixing `initialize` with `tools/list` is not. `NoLlaveMethodsTest`
(`tests/test_mcp_http.py:178-...`) proves `initialize`/`ping`/`notifications/initialized` answer with
`llave_asistente.verificar` never called (the mock asserted un-called), the same without a Bearer header -> 401
unchanged, and a batch mixing `initialize` with `tools/list` IS verified. `McpInitializeCarriesNoPersonTest`
(`tests/test_persona_fuga.py:929-954`, 2 tests) as described in ruling 2.

**Two measured deviations, neither changing a ruling:**

1. The spec's `touches:` named `body/mcp.py`, `tests/test_mcp_remoto.py`, `tests/test_mcp_cliente_remoto.py`,
   `tests/test_mcp_visible.py`, `tests/test_mcp_copia_pc.py`, `tests/test_mcp.py` and
   `tests/test_llave_asistente.py` for ruling 2's "move what's personal". Measured: `mcp_http.py`'s own pre-slice
   `initialize` already answered `protocolVersion`/`serverInfo`/`capabilities` only, and `mcp.py`'s own
   `_SesionCliente.initialize` branch already carried none either (proven by the pre-existing
   `tests/test_mcp_copia_pc.py::RemoteModeAddsNothingTest::test_initialize_carries_no_instructions_or_title`).
   Only `mcp.py`'s LOCAL `_Sesion.initialize` branch carries person text, and that door has no Bearer key and no
   Cuenta call at all -- outside Main's hub principle's reach. Did: left those seven files unedited; added the
   ruling-2/ruling-4 proof as new tests in `tests/test_mcp_http.py` and `tests/test_persona_fuga.py` instead, and
   re-ran all seven modules green to confirm no regression.
2. The spec's `THE WORK` asked for two commits (rulings 1-2, then ruling 3 + ruling 4's census). Measured:
   ruling 1's body-parse-before-verify reorder and ruling 3's 503-to-JSON-RPC-error rewrite both live inside the
   same `mcp_http()` route function and `_503()` helper; splitting them would have required staging partial,
   syntactically-incomplete hunks of the same function body. Did: committed rulings 1-4 (implementation + every
   new test) together in one commit, to keep every intermediate commit buildable and green.

**Commit:** `fed83b6` (`body/rutas/mcp_http.py`, `body/i18n/es.json`, `body/i18n/en.json`,
`tests/test_mcp_http.py`, `tests/test_persona_fuga.py` -- rulings 1-4; 5 files changed, +268/-10) -- merged

## BODY-MINUTO-ANALISIS-5-CONTEXTO -- day and night context, derived on read, for leer_dia/leer_noche (2026-11-20)

Carlos, relayed by the desk 2026-11-20, his words: *"I want between you and body design specialized tools to
analyze in full detail every minute of the metrics."* The desk asked that comparisons can say "nights after a
shift", "nights while travelling", "nights after a late meal". `BODY-MINUTO-ANALISIS-4-INV` (OBSERVED) measured
that every one of those, altitude excepted (out of this slice, `BODY-MINUTO-ANALISIS-6-ALTITUD`), is already
derivable on read from tables that exist, with three precedents of deriving this kind of thing on read and
storing nothing new (`body/turnos_costo.py`'s `bloques_noche`, `body/ventana_comida.py`'s `comida_a_sueno`,
`body/practicas.py`'s `_contexto`) and `body/noche_inusual.py`'s own docstring stating the same rule. The
orchestrator's ruling (`ORCH-CARLOS-DELEGATES-TIER-1-1`, Tier 2, no schema, `db.py` not edited) authorised one
derived-on-read module exposed in the two assistant tools that already read a single day/night.

**Rulings 1-2 -- one module, `body/contexto_dia.py`, derived on read, no new table, no stored tag.**
`contexto_dias(conn, person_id, desde, hasta)` (`:182`) answers for a RANGE of days with exactly 7 bulk
statements regardless of the range's length -- one per source: `turnos_costo.bloques_noche` (`:86`, called over
an EXTENDED range so a night block's own recovery tail reaching into `[desde, hasta]` from before `desde` is
never missed), the day's own `shift.kind` (`_dia_kind_por_dia`, `:67`), `db.viajes_lugares` (`:149`, filtered
in-module to 2+-day spans -- `body/viajes.py`'s own definition of what counts as "a trip", mirrored rather than
re-read through it to avoid a second statement), `db.periodos` (`:189`, cached per connection by `db.py` itself,
so a repeat call on the same connection costs nothing more), `activity` (`_actividad_por_dia`, `:112`),
`recuperacion_actividad` joined to `activity`, current model version only (`_recuperacion_por_dia`, `:121`, cites
`recuperacion.VERSION`, never re-defining it), and `daily_metric_efectiva` for `alcohol_g`
(`_alcohol_por_dia`, `:135`). The per-day dict is built in pure Python over these already-fetched rows (`:195-221`),
so the loop itself adds no statement whatever the range's length. Each key -- `turno`, `viaje`, `periodos`,
`carga`, `alcohol_g` -- is present only when that day actually has something to say (never a 0, a False or an
invented value): `turno.tipo` only with a `shift` row that day, `turno.bloque_noche` only inside a night run
(`{posicion, largo}`), `turno.dias_desde_ultimo_turno_noche` only inside `turnos_costo.MODELO["ventana_post"]`
days of the nearest earlier run's own last night (cited, never a new constant); `viaje` from a 2+-day Lugares
trip (`ref`, 1-based `dia`) or, failing that, a marked `period` of kind `'viaje'` (`dia` alone); `periodos` lists
every period kind covering the day with its `zonas` when it carries one; `carga.actividades`/`minutos` only with
an `activity` row that day, `carga.recuperacion_min` added only when at least one of that day's activities has a
computed figure; `alcohol_g` only when a figure is stored. `contexto_noche(conn, person_id, dia_despertar)`
(`:224`) answers for the ONE night `sleep_session` files under its own wake day (`body/ventana_comida.py`'s own
documented convention): `turno`/`carga`/`alcohol_g` are the EVENING's alone (the day before `dia_despertar` --
the day whose shift and load actually produced that night, per Carlos's own framing above), read via one
`contexto_dias` call over the two-day evening/wake-day span (still a fixed, range-independent 7 statements);
`viaje`/`periodos` are read over BOTH calendar dates and merged (a trip or period can start exactly on the wake
day); `comida_antes_de_dormir.minutos` is literally `ventana_comida.comida_a_sueno(evening)`'s own gap, in
minutes, added only when it exists -- the one key with no per-day equivalent in `contexto_dias`, since it
inherently spans two calendar dates. The night-to-evening mapping and every key's exact shape are stated in the
module's own docstring (`:1-56`). 29 tests in `tests/test_contexto_dia.py`, including the named statement-count
guard (`StatementCountTest`, a 7-day range vs. a 90-day range cost the identical 7 statements, named ceiling 7)
and four `another_persons_*_is_never_counted` tests (shift, trip, period, activity, alcohol) proving the
person-scoping holds for every source.

**Ruling 3 -- the assistant sees it, and its derivation is stated.** `_leer_dia`
(`body/agente/herramientas.py:874`) gains `data["contexto"] = contexto_dia.contexto_dias(conn, person_id, day,
day).get(day, {})` (`:898`). `_leer_noche` (`:1486`) gains `"contexto": contexto_dia.contexto_noche(conn,
person_id, fecha)` (`:1570`). Both tools' Spanish `descripcion` (the only language the registry's `descripcion`
field has ever carried for any of its 54 entries -- `body/mcp.py`'s `_herramienta_mcp` emits it verbatim, with no
per-language mechanism anywhere in this codebase) now says in one sentence what the `contexto` keys mean and that
they are DERIVADO, never entered data. Each tool's own English docstring (this codebase's second, developer-
facing language track, used throughout) carries the same statement. New tests: `tests/test_agente_leer_dia.py`'s
